author: dongshunyao
body:
## Why

Moving the UI stack to MUI v9 left every style block still written for tss-react. That was deliberate: keeping the style objects untouched is what made that diff mechanical enough to read. tss-react is a bridge, though, and the tree currently has two ways of writing the same thing.

This burns down fifteen of the twenty-three blocks that use it - everything in `src/components` and `src/pages`. The remaining eight are the editor widgets, and the dependency comes out with them.

## What changed

Fifteen files, six commits, one per group of files so that each can be measured on its own. Nothing here is meant to change what the app looks like: every conversion is an equivalent move, and a visual change would be a defect rather than an improvement.

The default target is `styled`. These blocks came from `makeStyles` and are all static - a styled component generates its class once at creation, the way the old one did, while `sx` serialises on every render, which matters for the note cards in a list and the tree rows in a drawer. `sx` is used for the conditional cases only, where the condition reads better at the call site than as a prop forwarded into a styled component.

Three kinds of rule needed more than a rename:

- **Slot classes.** `TreeItem` took four of them from every one of its ten call sites, `Drawer` took one from two, and `InputBase` took two. Each becomes one styled component addressing those slots by their own class names. That is a more specific selector than hanging a class on the slot, which cannot make a rule stop applying.
- **Descendant selectors into DOM the app does not render.** Thirty-four of them: CodeMirror's gutters and code area, flexlayout's tab strip and popup menu, d3's nodes and arrows. `styled` keeps the class on the same element, so they address the same nodes.
- **Conditional classes.** Thirteen call sites combined a class conditionally through `clsx`; they become `sx` with the same condition.

Twenty-one rules are deleted rather than carried over, because they have no consumer - most of them in `Home`, left behind when earlier rounds removed the toolbar search field and the mobile menu. Inside a style object an unread key is invisible; as a module-level styled component each one would be a lint warning. That accounts for the net 305 lines removed.

The CodeMirror rules are copied character for character rather than tidied. The editor gets replaced next round and CodeMirror 6 shares none of these class names, so all eighteen get rewritten then; reworking them now would only widen this round's regression surface.

## Test results

Five gates on every commit: `format:check`, `lint` (135 warnings, 0 errors, unchanged from the 136 baseline apart from one dead `classes` binding this removes), `typecheck`, `test` (39/39), `build`.

The style objects are where the compiler stops helping - TypeScript checks property names and value types, not which element a selector lands on. So each commit was also measured against a build of the previous `main`: both versions served side by side, driven through the same interactions, with every element's rectangle and computed styles serialised and compared. Seven such comparisons, covering the notes list, the settings page, the note cards, the notebook tree, the app shell at 1280 and at 375, the flexlayout chrome, the graph view, and the note panel in both edit and preview mode. All identical, including the tree row measurements that a rule silently going no-op cost last round.

Two mutation checks confirm the comparison can actually fail: changing one spacing step moved a popover 8px and flagged it, and renaming one CodeMirror selector turned the hidden gutters visible and flagged that. Both were reverted and re-measured back to matching.

E2E is 7/7 with no locator changes, which is the expected result - this PR should not move any DOM structure or role.

The six commits touch disjoint sets of files; nothing was reworked.

  * Simplified styling implementation across dialogs, popovers, previews, search controls, and navigation elements.

author: asithade
body:
Two documented endpoints could not work as written. Both are copy-paste examples, so anyone following the guides hits an error rather than a result.

## `webhook-testing.md` — wrong auth

Verifies a stored release with `Authorization: Bearer lfx_…`. `authorize()` rejects API-key requests on any route that declares no scope, so this returns **403**, not a release list.

This is not fallout from #201 moving the route under `/api/github` — the old `/api/releases` declared no scope either, so the example was already failing. The move just made the reason legible.

Corrected to a session cookie. Also dropped the "Public API" heading, which described an endpoint that has always required authentication.

## `changelog-views.md` — wrong path

Documents the endpoints as `/api/changelog-views/unseen` and `/api/changelog-views/mark-viewed`. The router mounts at `/api/changelogs` and declares `/views/*`, so the real paths are `/api/changelogs/views/*`. Every path in that file was off by one segment and returns **404**. Nine references corrected.

The auth in those examples was already correct — both routes declare `changelogs:read`, so API keys genuinely work there. Only the paths were wrong.

## Verification

Documented paths cross-checked against the route definitions; no other guide has either problem. Docs only, no code changes.

body:
## Purpose

Redesign `effect-text` as a coherent Effect v3-native library, with canonical concern ownership across public declarations, implementation, exports, tests, examples, and application consumers.

## API and behavior

- Expose matching root namespaces and PascalCase subpaths for `Text`, `TextMeasurer`, `MeasurementCache`, `Hyphenation`, `CanvasTextMeasurer`, `CanvasProfile`, `PreparationKey`, and `Calibration`.
- Keep preparation effectful and layout projections pure, with measurement tables and cursor hints private to prepared handles.
- Use native Effect models, collections, control flow, services, and scoped resources throughout the package and migrated consumers.
- Preserve scoped measurement sharing, cancellation, failure/retry behavior, and dictionary hyphenation. Add Unicode 17 grapheme conformance coverage and correct emoji compensation for graphemes with combining marks.
- Migrate application consumers, examples, benchmarks, and documentation. Supporting changes cover study-storage composition, API-source discovery, docs state and browser checks, and repository modeling guidance.

## Breaking changes

Remove the old `Browser`, `React`, `contracts`, and `experimental` entrypoints without compatibility aliases. Consumers use the canonical concern APIs, including `Text.summary`, `Text.lines`, `Text.layout`, incremental projections, and `new PreparationKey.PreparationKey(...)`.

Includes an `effect-text` minor changeset for the pre-1.0 breaking redesign and an `effect-search` patch changeset for study-storage composition.

## Verification

- `bun run check:all` — passed.
- `bun run lint` — passed.
- `bun run test` — 407 files, 2,200 tests passed.
- `bun run build` — passed.
- `bun run effect:diagnostics` — 957 files, zero errors, warnings, or messages.
- `bun run docs` — 35 README snippets and 39 authored API examples verified.
- Local Worker dry-run build and `test:worker test/worker/docs.test.ts` — 16 Chromium tests passed.
- Strict built-package consumer compilation using root and `/Text` imports passed; three examples executed against the distribution.
- Browser inspection exercised wide/narrow text layout, line details, and docs search.

An additional full Bun-host declaration check exposed the existing incompatibility between `@effect/platform-bun@0.91.2` and current Bun declarations. The isolated `effect-text` declaration check and repository gates pass; this PR does not change Bun dependency versions or `skipLibCheck`.

body: ## Summary T04-02 — capture and edit notes with an honest save state. Adds a thin desktop note editor over already-audited, unchanged `fehrest::project::{create_note,update_note}` -- no `src/` (Core) change. ## What's built - Three new typed commands (`list_notes`, `note_create`, `note_update`, `desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs`), each opening/creating a `CanonicalStore` and calling an already-tested Core function unchanged. `NoteInfo` exposes each note's current `revision_id` so the frontend always knows what to send back as `expectedRevisionId`. - `desktop/src/NoteEditor.tsx`: a five-state save machine (`Saved`/`Unsaved`/`Saving…`/two distinct not-saved states/`outcome-unknown`), Ctrl/Cmd+S keyboard save, native undo/redo (relies on the browser's own per-field edit history -- the buffer is never force-reset except on an explicit note switch), and explicit, owner-chosen (never automatic) conflict-review actions. - `desktop/src/markdown.tsx`: a dependency-free Markdown-subset preview (headings/bold/italic/code/lists) -- no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere; links/images render as inert plain text, never a clickable ``/loaded ``, by construction, so the preview issues zero network/process activity. - `desktop/src/App.tsx`: project-detail navigation wiring (open a project, list/open/create its notes). ## Verification A scripted E2E (`docs/evidence/flake-v1/T04-02/e2e-test/run-e2e-test.mjs`) reuses T04-01's established CDP-driven pattern to drive the real compiled `flake-desktop.exe` through its exact real typed-IPC bridge (`window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke`). Every claimed save is independently cross-checked by reading `canonical.sqlite` directly (`independent_read_note.py`, a thin wrapper around T02-07's unmodified `sqlite_reader.py` -- no Flake binary/library/Rust source imported), never by trusting the IPC response alone: 1. Create a note (Markdown + multi-byte UTF-8: CJK, emoji, combining diacritic) -- saved body byte-exact, independently re-read. 2. Update -- byte-exact, independently re-read, revision advanced. 3. **Conflict**: save against a stale revision id is refused with Core's own `"expected revision conflict"`, and the independently-re-read canonical payload is confirmed **unchanged** -- never a silent overwrite. 4. **Large body**: ~900 KB (near Core's 1 MiB limit) saves and is preserved byte-exact. 5. **Over limit**: 1.1 MB is refused by Core's own existing `check_len`, and the prior large body is confirmed still intact afterward. All 16 steps pass: `docs/evidence/flake-v1/T04-02/e2e-test/results/run-2026-09-16T03-18-03-851Z.{json,log}`. Two earlier harness-bug dry runs are preserved on record rather than deleted. A real accessibility gap (no `aria-live` on the save-state announcement) surfaced while drafting the manual native-composition checklist and was fixed during this task, not merely noted. Native IME/screen-reader confirmation across profiles is this task's own contract's explicit `T04-06` cross-platform gate, not this task's -- recorded honestly as not yet performed: `docs/evidence/flake-v1/T04-02/MANUAL_COMPOSITION_CHECKLIST.md`. ## Test plan - [x] `cargo fmt -- --check` / `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` -- clean - [x] `cargo audit` -- 0 vulnerabilities (unchanged from T04-01, no new dependency) - [x] `npm run build` (`tsc && vite build`) -- clean - [x] `npm audit` -- 0 vulnerabilities - [x] `git diff --check` -- clean - [x] `git diff --stat origin/main -- src/` -- empty (no Core change) - [x] Scripted E2E against the real compiled app, independently cross-verified against `canonical.sqlite` directly (see above) Full evidence: `docs/evidence/flake-v1/T04-02/REPORT.md`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_017y9yraFkEzskx96yEgLPuG --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a desktop note editor for creating and editing notes within a project. It calls the existing Core `create_note` and `update_note` functions unchanged, so there is no `src/` change. **What changed** - Adds `list_notes`, `note_create`, and `note_update` commands; `NoteInfo` exposes each note's current `revision_id` so the frontend can send it back as `expectedRevisionId`. - The editor distinguishes saved, unsaved, saving, conflict, error, and outcome-unknown states, with Ctrl/Cmd+S save and manual conflict review instead of silent overwrites. - Adds a dependency-free Markdown preview that renders links and images as inert plain text and never uses `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. - Adds `aria-live` to the save-state label so screen readers announce save changes. - Advances `specs/CURRENT.md` to T04-03. **Verification** - A scripted E2E drives the compiled app through its real IPC bridge and independently confirms saved bodies by reading `canonical.sqlite` directly. - E2E covers byte-exact create/update, UTF-8 content, stale-revision conflict refusal, ~900 KB body preservation, and rejection of a >1 MiB body. - Native IME/screen-reader confirmation is recorded in the manual checklist but not yet run; that remains T04-06's cross-platform gate. Written for commit 17d1a2c1a9d062f31f951fc48e4a7cb73d0d06f0. Summary will update on new commits.

## Summary
- Fixes a visual bug from #39: the current part's label in the sidebar (e.g. "Part 13") was rendering white text with no background, making it invisible against the page background.
- Root cause: `#site-nav .nav--series a { background: none; }` and `#site-nav .nav--series a[aria-current='page']`'s blue-background rule were tied in CSS specificity (id + class + type vs id + attribute + type). The plain rule appeared later in the file and won the tie, stripping the background while the white text (set by a separate, correctly-higher-specificity rule) stayed — white-on-page-background.
- Fix: give the `aria-current='page'` rule enough specificity (adds the class selector too) to win outright, restoring the blue background behind the white text.

author: nextroad-dev
body:
The web app's design tokens had drifted: the single `@theme` source in `apps/web/src/assets/index.css` was bypassed by Tailwind's default palette (16 sites), by hardcoded brand/canvas RGB literals inside the canvas background components, and by raw `bg-black*` / `text-white*` primitives (115 sites) — while `--color-overlay` sat unused and four other tokens had zero consumers. This PR routes every color through tokens, makes the token set self-cleaning, and adds a lint guard so the drift cannot come back.

Single commit: `6a862a2` — 36 files, +402 / −998.

## What changed

### Token layer (`apps/web/src/assets/index.css`)

| Token | Value | Replaces |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-foreground-inverse` | `#ffffff` | `text-white*` / `bg-white*` / `border-white*`, `--color-primary-foreground` |
| `--color-credit` | `#F59E0B` | `amber-500` |
| `--color-positive` | `#10B981` | `emerald-500` |
| `--color-negative` | `#F43F5E` | `rose-500` |
| `--color-danger-hover` | `#B91C1C` | `red-700` (redefines a dead alias that was `#dc2626`) |
| `--color-danger-active` | `#991B1B` | `red-800` |
| `--color-danger-border` | `#FECACA` | `red-200` |

Removed as unused: `--color-primary-foreground` (renamed, 2 call sites), `--color-muted`, `--color-surface-dark{,-muted,-border}`. `--color-overlay` is kept and is now the only scrim/media-backdrop token. Every replacement is value-identical, so the palette work is a pure refactor — the danger family now has the same base/hover/active/soft ladder as the brand family.

### Consumption

- **Palette bypasses** — Coins icon → `text-credit` (4 sites); account ledger deltas → `text-positive` / `text-negative`; reserved quota delta → `text-credit`; `BaseButton` danger → `hover:bg-danger-hover active:bg-danger-active`; `SurfaceCard` danger → `border-danger-border`.
- **Black/white primitives** — 115 replacements across 19 files: `bg-black*` → `bg-overlay*` (scrims, lightbox, letterboxed media, gradient masks) and `text-white*` / `bg-white*` / `border-white*` → `*-foreground-inverse*`. Values unchanged.
- **`IdleConsole`** — `rgba(22,138,73,0.15)`, `rgba(255,255,255,0.25)` and the `#fff` mask placeholder become `color-mix()` over `--color-primary` / `--color-foreground-inverse`.

### Canvas components

New `apps/web/src/shared/lib/css-color.ts` (`readCssVar`, `resolveCssColor`) replaces the two hand-rolled parser copies in `FlowLinesBg`/`MatrixBg` and resolves `var()`, named colors and modern color spaces (`CSS.supports` + canvas normalization). The hardcoded `#168A49` / `{ r: 22, g: 138, b: 73 }` fallbacks are gone: an unresolvable token now renders nothing instead of fabricating the brand color. `MosaicBg.vue`, `ParticleBg.vue` and `MosaicProgress.vue` are deleted — they were never imported (no `defineAsyncComponent`, no `import.meta.glob`, no reference anywhere in the repo).

### Guard

`apps/web/scripts/check-design-tokens.mjs` (zero new dependencies) rejects:

1. default Tailwind palette utilities with numeric steps (`bg-red-500`, `border-slate-300`, …)
2. raw `black`/`white` utilities (`bg-black/60`, `text-white/90`, …)
3. hex color literals
4. numeric `rgb()` / `rgba()` literals
5. `--color-*` tokens with no consumer (dead tokens)
6. any second `@theme` block

`GoogleIcon.vue` (third-party brand marks) is the only literal allowlist. Wired into the web `lint` script and exposed as `lint:tokens`.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` — clean across all 8 workspace projects.
- `pnpm lint` — clean; guard reports `design tokens: ok (31 color tokens, 111 source files checked)`.
- `pnpm --filter @musecanvas/web build` — ok (6.2s).
- `pnpm test` — **225 passed / 0 failed** (api 83, providers 91, worker 25, domain 16, database 10).
- Built CSS inspected: all new tokens are emitted inside `:root,:host`, and every migrated utility resolves (`bg-overlay/{0,30,40,50,60,65,70,75,80}`, `text-foreground-inverse{,/20,/70,/90}`, `bg-foreground-inverse{,/10,/20,/90}`, `border-foreground-inverse/30`, `from-overlay/80`, `via-overlay/30`, `text-credit`/`positive`/`negative`, `border-danger-border`). No trace of `--color-muted:` / `--color-surface-dark*:` / `--color-primary-foreground:`.
- Guard verified against planted violations: all six rule families fire and exit 1, while token-based classes (`bg-neutral-soft`, `border-border-strong`, `bg-primary`, `bg-overlay/60`) produce no false positives.
- Dev-server smoke: `/` returns 200 and every touched module (including `css-color.ts` and the two canvas components) compiles.
- Reverse grep across `apps/web/src`: only the token definitions themselves and the allowlisted Google brand hexes remain.

## Notes

- **One intentional visual shift:** the legal notice banner on `/terms` and `/privacy` moves its border/fill from `amber-500` (`#F59E0B`) to `--color-warning` (`#B45309`) — a 40%-alpha hairline border and a 5%-alpha fill, so the visible difference is negligible, and the banner now shares one hue with its own text color (which was already exactly `--color-warning`). Say the word if you want pixel-identical output there and I'll add a bright-amber token instead.
- **The guard is not enforced in CI yet.** `pnpm lint` runs it, but `.github/workflows/media-quality.yml` only runs typecheck/tests/build. Adding `pnpm --filter @musecanvas/web lint` as a step there would close the loop; left out here because CI changes were outside the approved plan.
- **Out of scope:** the 33 numeric `z-*` literals (`z-10` / `z-20` / `z-50`, …). Most are component-local stacking for image overlays and modal panels, so converting them to the semantic scale needs per-site judgement and carries z-order regression risk. The guard's rule table is structured so a `z-<number>` rule can be appended later; `DataTable.vue`'s sticky header (`z-10` → `z-sticky`) is the first candidate.
- The repo now contains zero dead color tokens and `apps/web` has no unused canvas components. `apps/web` still has four `node:test` files that nothing runs (no `test` script in that package, which needs a `tsx` devDependency) — separate follow-up.
- Deliberately left untouched: an unrelated local `.gitignore` edit (adds `.zcode`) that was already in the working tree before this branch.

body:
> **Prompt:** Then let's fix the bug first

> [!NOTE]
> The following content was generated by AI.

Closes #1652. A self-map — `rep_of: {columns: {snapshot: snapshot, rep: snapshot}, key: snapshot}`, the language's own example of the form — passed `check` and then raised: polars' `DuplicateError` relationally, linopy's coordinate mismatch eagerly, and on `sum(by=)` the two lanes disagreed, one raising where the other built.

The walk named its value column after the dimension it lands on, which for a self-map is the name the key column already holds. The mapping table names its columns **by side** now — `__walk key__`, `__walk value {relation}__` — and the join names its sides (`left_on` / `right_on`), so the landing is aliased to its dimension at the end rather than colliding at the start. On the eager lane the pullback puts the fine labels back as the coordinate: a row lands at the snapshot that *read* a value, not at the one it read.

<details><summary>What the probe says, before and after</summary>

| | `lps.check` | relational | eager |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at(price, by=rep_of, over=rep)` before | passes | `DuplicateError` | `ValueError: Coordinate mismatch` |
| `sum(p, by=rep_of, over=snapshot, into=rep)` before | passes | `DuplicateError` | builds, unchecked |
| both, after | passes | builds | builds, and the two agree |

</details>

<details><summary>Mutation table</summary>

Baseline for this environment: 10 failures, all `gurobi`/`xpress` not installed.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| the one-value-column-per-relation guard (`compiler.py:703-706`) | **caught** |
| the walk selects its landing by the dimension's own name (`compiler.py:845`) | **caught** — 218 failed |
| the eager pullback keeps the labels it read (`operators.py:120`) | **caught** — 11 failed, 1 beyond the baseline |
| the join renames the mapping onto the fragment's dims instead of naming both sides (`compiler.py:846`) | **not caught** — recorded rather than hidden: it is an equivalent implementation, since what the bug needed was the *landing* to keep a name of its own, which the row above is the guard for |

The first through `python -m tools.mutate`, which reported the tree clean afterwards; the rest by hand (changed lines, which the tool does not express), each with the same three precautions.

</details>

<details><summary>Verified</summary>

`ruff check` · `ruff format --check` · `pyrefly check` · `pytest -q -n 4` — the suite reaches the same 10 failures as `main` in this environment, all a solver that is not installed. Run in a `uv` venv rather than pixi (no pixi here).

**Not run**: `pixi run test-floors` and `test-bench` — no pixi environment here.

author: ramizloki
body:
Closes #122

## Implementation sketch — before UI changes

The following compact wireframes preserve the existing Fastify/Postgres writers, RLS, revision and domain contracts. They describe only hierarchy and interaction; no user-study or performance claim is implied.

### 1. Shared internal shell

**Before:** public header / marketing navigation → broad admin links / counters / filters → tasks below the fold.

**After:**
```text
+ Brand | current account | language | legal | View public site +
| Tasks | Garages | Users | Privacy | Audit | Settings       |
+----------------------------------------------------------+
| Tasks / To do                    [more filters] [reset] |
| [Review queue 3] [Garage checks 2] [Requests 1]          |
| ► Review: visit evidence    High · unassigned · now      |
| ► Garage: submitted profile  Medium · owner missing      |
+----------------------------------------------------------+
```
Desktop uses the persistent narrow rail. At 390px it becomes one labelled section switcher; the first task or the explicit empty state remains in the first viewport. Existing `/admin`, `/moderation`, locale prefixes and public link stay canonical.

### 2. Review case

**Before:** choose generic action → then checklist; content, evidence, action and history are one long vertical form.

**After:**
```text
< Back to filtered tasks                     Assigned: Me
Review · appeal / original decision and reason (when relevant)
+ Content and rating        | Evidence (open on demand) |
+ Check: garage [ ] work [ ] visit month [ ]               |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| [Publish review]  [Reject…]  [Request information] [Escalate] |
| Result status → [Next eligible case] (never automatic)   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```
The three controls are always visible before direct choices. Reject reason and escalation reason are action-local. Missing/revoked evidence and own-appeal conflict show the permitted safe route. Leaving changed checks asks to discard; reload/back/language reauthorizes the case.

### 3. Garage review and secondary work

**Before:** verification, coordinate editing, photos, team, transfer and support share one long form and one remote reason field.

**After:**
```text
Garages / submitted profile                   [Review] [Photos] [Team & ownership] [Support]
+ Evidence | neutral contact/location (read-only) | blockers +
| Company [ ] Contact [ ] Location [ ] Owner [ ]             |
| [Save review]                         [Review and publish] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Position correction is deliberately opened from the review context. Known evidence/owner/location/conflict blockers disable publish with explanation. Combined review + publication uses the existing single domain transaction; saving remains secondary. Team transfer presents source → target consequences and one confirmation.

### 4. Privacy requests

**Before:** policy configuration appears before pending requests.

**After:** requests first, each with state, object counts, policy version and a contextual blocker/return link; policy moves to secondary settings. Pending physical file deletion stays explicitly pending.

### Target sequences

1. Open an actionable queue → open case → compare content/evidence → consciously check → direct decision → observe result → optionally choose next case.
2. Admin opens task → self-claims or assigns → stays in the same refreshed case.
3. Open garage review → satisfy four checks → one final combined publish confirmation, or save review only.
4. Open Team & ownership → search/select an existing active account → verify consequence → one confirmation.
5. Open a privacy request → follow exact blocker to permitted context → return to the request → confirm the shown policy version.

Baseline and after screenshots use only the existing signed synthetic OIDC helper plus a new isolated test database. They will be attached through the existing test artifact route and not committed.

## Implementierung und Abnahme

Der gemeinsame Arbeitsplatz ist umgesetzt. Die bisherigen öffentlichen Seiten behalten ihre Navigation und Lucide-Icons; interne Admin-/Moderationsseiten verwenden die ausdrücklich beauftragte reduzierte Shell. Die Header-/Routing-Konflikte mit `main` wurden zusammengeführt, nicht durch pauschales Übernehmen einer Branchversion gelöst. Lazy Loading bleibt erhalten.

Die technische Dokumentation und der reproduzierbare Vergleich stehen in [`docs/architecture/STAFF-WORKSPACE-UX.md`](https://github.com/ramiz4/autokosova/blob/d069c5e96f614ab3fb05a930a1b91c22e6651d5a/docs/architecture/STAFF-WORKSPACE-UX.md). Die kanonische Rollenreferenz wurde im selben PR aktualisiert.

### Umgesetzter Umfang

- Aufgabenansichten mit wirksamen Status-/Bearbeiter-/Fallart-/Prioritätsfiltern, korrekten begrenzten Zählern und direkten Werkstatt-/Löschauftragszielen. Fallübernahme bleibt im geöffneten, neu autorisierten Fall. Eskalation entfernt den entzogenen Fall aus der URL und lädt die verbleibende eigene Arbeit mit einer einmaligen Rückmeldung neu.
- Bewertungsprüfung vor der Entscheidung: drei bewusste Kontrollen, objektgebundener Nachweis, direkte Veröffentlichung/Ablehnung, passender lokaler Grund, unabhängiger Widerspruch und ausdrücklicher nächster Fall. Bloßes Öffnen einer Option ist kein ungespeicherter Entwurf.
- Werkstattprüfung mit vier sichtbaren, getrennten Prüfungen (Telefon, Kontaktperson, Unternehmensdokument, Standort); aktiver Eigentümer bleibt ein zusätzliches Server-Gate. Geänderte Prüfung/Position und Veröffentlichung verwenden genau eine bestehende Domaintransaktion. Teilprüfung bleibt optional; Fotos, Team/Eigentum und Support sind getrennt. Keine versteckten globalen Gründe, kein scheinbarer Gesamterfolg nach fehlgeschlagenem Fresh Read.
- Suchbares aktives Zielkonto, konkrete Eigentumsfolgen, Schutz des letzten Eigentümers, Membership-Direktlinks und bewusst geöffnete Sicherheitsaktionen. Löschaufträge stehen vor der Policykonfiguration und zeigen gebundene Version, Objektarten/Anzahlen, konkrete Eigentumsblocker und den Rückweg zum Auftrag.
- Technische Detailnavigation, Filter-/Seiten-/Rückkehrfokus, RAM-only Entwürfe, Verwerfenschutz, sperrender 409-Konflikt bis zum bewussten aktuellen Read und Invalidierung nach Kontowechsel/Rechteentzug. Keine Freitextsuche, privaten Nachweise oder Grants in neuen URLs/Browserstorage.

### Ausgeführte Prüfungen

| Prüfung | Ergebnis |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e` | erfolgreich |
| `npm run test:dev` | 20 bestanden |
| `npm test -- --watch=false` | 393 bestanden in 36 Dateien |
| `DATABASE_URL=<isolierte lokale Test-DB> npm run test:server` | 130 bestanden, 0 fehlgeschlagen, 2 separate seed-gesteuerte Tests im Sammellauf übersprungen; CI führt deren dedizierte Seed-Kommandos aus |
| `npm run verify` | vollständige Kette einschließlich Build und Smoke erfolgreich; Smoke prüft 45 lokalisierte SSR-Seiten |
| `npm run test:e2e:policy` | erfolgreich; vollständiges Pflichtinventar bleibt erzwungen |
| `AUTOKOSOVA_E2E_DATABASE_URL=<isolierte lokale Kontroll-DB> npm run test:e2e` | 30/30 bestanden: alle 15 Pflichtfälle jeweils Desktop und Mobil, `retries: 0`; zusätzliche Konflikt-, Entwurfs-, Übernahme-, Next-Case-, Eskalations- und Kontextprüfungen |
| `npm run test:staff:browser` | endgültiger CI-Lauf siehe verlinkter Nachweis unten; Veröffentlichung/Abbruch, Ablehnung, fehlender Nachweis, Rückfrage, Hide/Restore, unabhängiger Widerspruch, Rollen-/Dateigrenzen, Seed/Neustart und 12 Sprach-/Viewportkombinationen |
| `node --import tsx scripts/staff-workspace-ux-evidence.mts` | 35 Nachher-Bilder einschließlich 320-CSS-Pixel-Reflow |
| derselbe Runner mit gepinntem Baseline-Checkout und Phase `before` | 32 Vorher-Bilder; gleiche fiktive Szenarien, eigener signierender Testprovider und eigene zufällige Testdaten

## Summary

Amit's Production smoke found that a correct password on `/invite` produced no visible change. Runtime logs show the sign-in POST returned 200 and the only follow-up request was `GET /invite`, never `GET /`.

Cause: the app shell renders the sidebar on `/invite`; its links prefetch protected routes, the proxy answers each anonymous prefetch with a redirect to `/invite`, and Next keeps those redirects in the client router cache. `router.replace("/")` after sign-in resolved from that stale cache.

Fix: perform a full navigation after a successful password sign-in via a small mockable helper (`src/lib/browser-navigation.ts`). The state file records the finding.

author: andreisavu
body:
## What changes

Every agent can participate through `say`, `seat`, `unseat`, and its domain tools during an exchange. The room no longer has a special assistant, an opening selection activation, protected assistant membership, or a separate `summarise` tool.

Define agents once and assign an optional summary writer by name:

```ts
const room = await startRoom({
  agents: [editor, inventory, scheduling],
  summary: 'editor',
});
```

The writer has ordinary membership and attention. When a human exchange closes, the room records one closing assignment if that writer is seated. Its prompt contains the fixed source discussion, recipient, and response guidance. It receives the regular `say({ text, to? })` tool. The receiving room stamps the summary's author, recipient, and source range. Ending without `say` leaves the exchange without a summary.

Membership changes use journal facts. Concurrent requests for the same membership state return a no-op. Removal invalidates pending and active work; reseating cannot revive an old activation. One agent can receive ordinary work while finishing a prior summary, with one live execution per seat.

## Migration

Replace `assistant: editor` with `agents: [..., editor], summary: 'editor'`. Choose ordinary attention through `seats` when needed. Omitted `seats` seats the whole catalog with broadcast attention; `{}` keeps it in reserve.

Composition version 2 rejects old histories explicitly. Start a new journal or migrate old history before resuming. There is no legacy assistant execution path. Public contracts, examples, release scope, and remaining work are updated together.

## Validation

Implemented and reviewed with Luna/High. Adversarial review fixes include removal followed by reseating, expired lease revocation, a new question arriving during closing work, a summary writer initially in reserve, and a summary from the wrong author.

- `pnpm format` and `pnpm check` pass: 580 core tests, 37 workspace tests, and 18 Cloudflare/workerd tests and six CLI tests, plus the remaining repository checks.
- `pnpm chaos` passes all 728 expanded recovery tests across memory and SQLite.
- Tests verify shared tool schemas, closing prompts, fixed summary boundaries, concurrent membership no-ops, self-removal, stale authority, replay, and overlapping exchanges.
- All seven GitHub checks pass on the integrated head, including Node 22/24, live-provider tests, Dafny verification, lint/types, and the CLI smoke test.
- Integrated concurrent PR #127 without dropping its CLI, release, or Cloudflare changes. The generated team uses an ordinary planner as the optional summary writer.
- The packed CLI consumer smoke passes, including generated project typechecking and the Wrangler build.

author: theciege23
body:
## What happened

A signed-in `/core` answer on 2026-09-16 produced eight data sources. Three reached the evidence block's fallback and rendered de-underscored:

- `core_surface_context` → "core surface context"
- `sports_digest_db` → "sports digest db"
- `agent_prompt_trade_analyzer` → "agent prompt trade analyzer"

## ⚠ Why they were missed — not the reason I first gave

I recorded this as *"a live response envelope is the only complete source of the slug list."* **That's wrong.** Both `core_surface_context` (route ~2143) and `sports_digest_db` (route ~3197) were in the source the whole time. My original census piped the grep through `head -20`, cut off around line 2140, and I treated the truncated result as the full list.

The live envelope didn't reveal something a grep couldn't — it revealed that **the grep had been cut short**. Re-running it unpiped found nineteen push sites, not thirteen.

## The two literals

Read from what actually gates them (`renderCoreSurfacePrompt`, `chimmySportDigestFreshness`) rather than from the slug's wording:

- `core_surface_context` → **"The screen you asked from"**
- `sports_digest_db` → **"Stored sports data (scores, injuries, news)"**

## 🛑 A prefix branch, and a second family the full census turned up

The route mints **two** slug families by concatenation:

```
dataSources.push(`agent_prompt_${specialistAgent}`)
dataSources.push(`decision_os_grounding_${grounding.outcome}`)
```

Neither can be a literal map — it goes stale the moment somebody adds a specialist, and stale in the quiet way, where the entry stops matching and the fallback takes over without telling anyone. Both now render through `SLUG_FAMILIES` (`Specialist: trade analyzer`, `Decision engine (timeout)`).

## 🛑 The literal map is checked first, and a test pins it

`decision_os_grounding_packet` is a real literal meaning *the packet arrived*, not an outcome named "packet". With the family checked first it renders **"Decision engine (packet)"** — wrong, entirely plausible, and it would outrank a correct label with nothing going red. Driven red by inverting the two lookups.

## ⚠ The existing degrade test needed its fixture moved, not its assertion

It used `agent_prompt_waiver`, which is no longer unlabelled. Left alone it would have been a test named *"unlabelled"* that only ever exercised a **labelled** slug — a guard that silently stops guarding.

It now uses a slug matching no literal and no family, and still asserts the source **renders** rather than being dropped. Hiding a source would understate what an answer touched; the label map is a readability improvement, never a filter.

## Verification

18 tests pass (was 10). The literal-beats-prefix ordering was driven **red first**.

author: omkarbhale
body:
Built a fourteen-module course teaching tas-playwright — 82 minutes, one video file. The video
is content and stays out of this repo (ADR-0002). What is here is the studio work that making
it required, and every claim below is measured on this machine.

## Speech and alignment no longer depend on an account

The OpenAI key stopped working mid-course, and it took **both** halves of the narration path
with it: `tts.mjs` for speech and `transcribe.py` for the per-word timings ADR-0003 requires.
A local voice with no local alignment is audio you cannot cue.

**[ADR-0009](docs/adr/0009-a-local-voice-and-a-local-aligner.md)** puts Kokoro-82M and
faster-whisper behind those same two paths — `--engine auto|openai|kokoro` and
`--engine auto|openai|local`. `auto` prefers OpenAI and falls back **loudly**, always printing
which engine actually spoke, because a voice that changes unnoticed is worse than one that
fails. The Kokoro path shells out to the engine's own `tts` command rather than loading a
model (ADR-0001).

`repair.py` had a transcription client of its own that would only ever have worked on OpenAI;
it now goes through `transcribe.py`. Proved by collapsing a 4.88s run of twelve words and
watching it come back — and it then fired for real on a module whose alignment genuinely
collapsed.

**Measured, not hoped for:** across six Kokoro voices on a sample built from the hardest
tokens in a real corpus, **zero deletions and zero insertions in every one**. It does not drop
clauses the way the OpenAI model does, so there is one take and a drop `verify.py` reports is a
fact about the script. It does mispronounce proper nouns and has no `instructions` control, so
`--lexicon` respells what is **spoken** while leaving the script the guards check untouched.

## Three guards, and what they each caught

**`dry_run.py`** — a composition reads its transcript, so nothing about it runs until the audio
exists, which hides the cheap faults behind the expensive one. This writes a synthetic
transcript from the script so the generator and both guards run for free. On this course it
caught **nine of fourteen modules failing before a take was spent**: two generators that raised
outright, eight cues quoting phrases no transcript could contain, four ambiguous list-built
cues.

**`id_check.py`** — a duplicate id means one element is revealed twice and another is on screen
from its scene's first frame, with `cue_check.py` still passing and the settled frame identical
either way.

**`join.py`** — refuses mismatched parts and a part that did not arrive, both of which otherwise
produce a playable file that is quietly wrong.

## What the README now says that it did not

- **The clause drop is length-driven**, and 2000 tokens is not the working ceiling: clean at
  1,398 words, never clean in ten takes at 1,663. Write ~1,200 a pass; add a module rather than
  cut content.
- **A cue is matched against the transcript, and a transcript respells your script** five ways —
  no hyphens survive at all; numbers come back as digits *inconsistently* (`Screen one` became
  `Screen 1` while `Screen two` stayed words, so the sibling cues kept passing and hid it);
  spelling is Americanised; compounds separate; and a local aligner **glues words together
  across a dash**, emitting both sides as one token.
- **`cue_check.py` cannot see a cue built from a variable.** It reads `t("literal")` calls, so a
  scene cueing a row of pills from a list passes with every one of those cues unverified — and
  those are exactly the cues a repeated row uses. Run the generator rather than scan it.

## Merged with the dubbing work

Both branches reached for the same rule from different ends: main made `words()` importable so
`dub_script.py` stops posting its own request; this branch put a second engine behind the same
file. `words(audio, key, vocab=None)` survives unchanged — its `vocab` parameter is load-bearing
for a re-voice — with `local_words()` beside it. My ADR renumbered 0008 → 0009. Both AGENTS.md
bullets and both README sections are kept: different jobs, not competing answers.

Verified after merging: every script parses, `dub_script` still imports `words`, and a line goes
through the local voice and the local aligner with no dropped words.

author: robertkill
body:
feat(lock): multi-screen — the authentication UI follows the active screen

1. Every screen now runs the same surface and exactly one of them is active:
   it compacts the clock and reveals the password field, while the others stay
   idle (wallpaper, clock, hint) and can take the lock over at any moment. The
   active screen follows the interaction — a click gives it to the screen that
   was clicked, a key press to the screen the pointer is on.
2. The pointer is the only usable signal for the keyboard case: the X11 grab
   delivers every keystroke to one window, which is not necessarily the screen
   the user is looking at. Key presses are therefore watched per lock window
   (never application-wide — Qt offers the same QKeyEvent to the window, the
   focused item and then up that item's parent chain, so an application-wide
   filter would act on one physical key press more than once). A keystroke
   aimed at another screen hands the interactive UI over there and becomes that
   screen's first password character, instead of being typed into a field the
   user cannot see.
3. Stop grabbing the pointer. With one fullscreen window per screen the clicks
   already land on the lock, and an X11 pointer grab funnels every click into
   the grab window — which is exactly what would break "click the screen you
   are looking at". Alt+Tab / Super blocking is unaffected: that is the
   keyboard grab, which now follows the password field to whichever screen owns
   it.
4. Remove a lock-out: the primary screen going away used to destroy the only
   screen with a password field and release the input grab, leaving a lock with
   nothing to type into. An active screen that disappears now falls back to
   "none", and every remaining screen can be woken again.
5. SecondaryScreen.qml is gone (every screen runs LockScreen.qml) and a video
   wallpaper now decodes on every screen; WallpaperHost drops the `playVideo`
   switch that had no caller left.

Log: Made the lock screen multi-monitor: the authentication UI follows the
screen the user interacts with.
Influence: Any screen can unlock; unplugging the primary screen no longer
wedges the session.

feat(lock): 多屏——认证界面跟随交互所在屏

1. 每个屏跑同一个 surface，同一时刻只有一块是活跃屏：它收起时钟并显示密码框，其余
   屏停在空闲态（壁纸 + 时钟 + 提示），随时可以接管。活跃屏跟随交互：点击哪块屏就
   归哪块屏，按键归指针所在的那块屏。
2. 键盘这一侧只能靠指针判断：X11 的抓取会把按键送到某一个窗口，不一定是用户在看
   的那块屏。因此按键按窗口逐个监听（绝不 application-wide——Qt 会把同一个
   QKeyEvent 依次投给窗口、焦点 item，再沿该 item 的父链上传，全局过滤器会对一次
   物理按键执行多次）。按键不属于当前活跃屏时，把认证界面搬过去，并让它成为该屏
   密码的第一个字符，而不是敲进用户看不见的那个密码框。
3. 不再抓取指针：多屏下每个屏都有自己的全屏窗口，点击本来就落在锁屏上，而抓指针
   会把所有点击灌进同一个窗口，正好破坏「点哪块屏哪块屏进认证」。Alt+Tab / Super
   的拦截不受影响——那是键盘抓取，现在跟随密码框迁到所属屏。
4. 修掉一个锁死路径：主屏消失会销毁唯一带密码框的屏并释放输入抓取，剩下的锁屏无
   处输入。现在活跃屏消失会退回「无活跃屏」，其余屏随时都能被唤醒。
5. 删除 SecondaryScreen.qml（所有屏都用 LockScreen.qml），动态壁纸在所有屏解码；
   WallpaperHost 去掉已无调用方的 `playVideo` 开关。

Log: 锁屏支持多屏，认证界面跟随用户交互所在的那块屏。
Influence: 任意屏都能解锁；拔掉主屏不再把会话卡在无法解锁的状态。

author: sivancola
body:
## Problem and behavior

A single send could render twice when optimistic messages and canonical records arrived out of order. Collapsed and expanded tool views disagreed on stopped or timed-out execution. Windows terminal redraws could corrupt shell completion markers.

This change persists optional submission receipts at the shared Controller admission boundary, reconciles transcript identities across events and history, and centralizes tool presentation. Windows Agent execution uses persistent PowerShell with a private structured completion channel and raw output boundaries. Existing message bodies, the bash tool name, and historical shell configuration remain readable.

## Compatibility and limits

- Submission identity stays in optional host events and DTOs, outside provider messages. Duplicate IDs with different requests conflict; uncertain accepted requests are not automatically replayed.
- PowerShell state is scoped to the logical session and reset after timeout, cancellation, or transport failure. Permission-specific and background calls remain isolated.
- The PowerShell tool description changes at environment binding, which can reduce cache reuse on the first upgraded request.
- Native Windows 5.1/7 tests passed on Windows 11 ARM64. Final-head packaged installer qualification is still required before merge readiness. This PR is deliberately a draft.

## Validation

- Current-base owning Go packages: control, session, serve, persistentshell, sandbox, builtin passed.
- Frontend typecheck passed on the current base.
- Earlier implementation verification passed Desktop full module tests, focused frontend transcript/composer/remote/terminal suites, DOM identity/presentation tests, browser transcript benchmark, selected race tests, live PowerShell 7 tests, and previous-reader compatibility checks.
- Broader root testing encountered ACP E2E/provider failures; these are not claimed as passing or proven unrelated.
- Windows focused PowerShell 7/5.1 coverage is added to CI. Cross-compilation is not native validation.

## Review focus

Documentation-impact: updated - Added bilingual Windows Agent shell guidance and refreshed Desktop inventory.
Cache-impact: medium - PowerShell persistence description changes stable tool bytes at environment binding; submission metadata stays local.
Cache-guard: go test ./internal/session ./internal/tool/builtin passed; submission regression excludes host identity from derived provider messages, and existing tool schema guards cover workspace stability.
System-prompt-review: Reviewed in this PR: the Windows golden system prompt is byte-identical to the existing golden; the intentional change is the platform-specific PowerShell tool description and its derived prefix hash. Approval remains on hold pending final CI and review.

Please inspect durable admission ordering, session/fork identity scope, stale async transcript updates, PowerShell error semantics and process-tree cleanup. Related open work includes #10320 and #10206 in remote/session ownership; integration order needs rechecking if either merges first.

## Additional native evidence

Windows 11 ARM64 passed persistent PowerShell 5.1 and 7.6.6 tests, Windows child-tree cancellation/cleanup, and explicit POSIX hook execution after installing official Git for Windows 2.55.0. The release-mode portable package built at final head 4fc7bdbc9 passed strict startup, renderer Version invocation, second-launch reuse, and clean shell/service shutdown. Portable SHA256: D5C0B79BB675AED30DF62736DEB0E829ECA2C5AA4E3218F26EABE6671FE8F210. The NSIS installer also built; installer UI and signing qualification were not exercised. All 378 frontend suites and final submission identity race tests passed.

Final main CI: https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/actions/runs/35062527818 (success on 4fc7bdbc9). Latest cache declaration check: https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/actions/runs/35063667010 (success). PR remains draft pending the stated qualification gaps and remaining screening status.

body:
## Summary

Add a manual hosted PR reviewer to `tlon-workflow`. It explores implemented user-facing changes on an EAS iOS simulator and posts findings with video in one comment.

## Changes

- Use Codex CLI with Sol high, agent-device, and the shared login and navigation helpers. Create ordinary test data through the app and explore the main changed paths.
- Record H.264 directly, then run an independent recording reviewer with shell tools and ffmpeg. Save its native session log so image inspection can be verified.
- Attach one complete clip per finding and the full recording with `gh --attach`. Update one canonical comment.
- Keep upfront assessment, compatible build reuse, and cached disposable backends. Exploration, recording review, and publication share one EAS Mac worker.
- Use GitHub concurrency and saved artifacts, without a custom evidence service, checkpoints, billing proxy, or publication locks.
- Let the existing PR watcher wait for QA. Keep this manual and advisory for trusted code, with no required base comparison, fixes, or merge loop.

## How did I test?

- [Full hosted run on #6521](https://github.com/tloncorp/tlon-apps/actions/runs/35185632443) passed in 15m28s using the same app build as the earlier 16m37s run. The agent covered short and long note scrolling, editing, preview, sync, and reopening with content preserved.
- The independent reviewer received 14 image sheets, including consecutive frames around both scroll transitions. It reported no substantiated findings and listed background/reopen and small-device coverage as untested.
- The action updated the [existing QA comment](https://github.com/tloncorp/tlon-apps/pull/6521#issuecomment-5683765408) with a playable full recording. This run had no findings; finding clips are covered by the synthetic test below.
- A [tooling-only run](https://github.com/tloncorp/tlon-apps/actions/runs/35183549130) skipped simulator/backend work after assessment.
- 12 automated tests pass, including real ffmpeg clipping of a one-frame change, attachment placement and repeat comment updates, source/build identity, login, backend proxy access, Codex session setup, and watcher behavior. Current PR CI passes.

Verification caught and fixed EAS checkout setup, missing Codex home creation, and frame loss from full-video conversion. This qualifies one iOS scenario, not a guarantee of reviewer quality across all features.

author: replicas-connector[bot]
body:
The five files you asked about are all samples, and all five are marked. The `ACME:` convention is sound and `AGENTS.md:8` is the right place for it. These are the four edges where it doesn't quite hold. For the record, the grep returns **ten** files, not five: the four you didn't list are `cadence/carryover.md`, `plan/company-plan.md`, `plan/outcomes.md` and `plan/strategy.md`. ## 1. `outputs/README.md` contradicted its own samples Line 12 said: > Append-only. Never rewrite or delete an existing entry; correct it with a dated addendum. Both sample entries say "Delete it." An agent reading that README as policy either refuses to delete them or appends a dated correction to fiction. Now carves out the marked entries. ## 2. One sample didn't look like one Its sibling is `2026-02-03-example-icp-list-build`. This one was `2026-07-10-signal-detection-first-run` — nothing in the path, the title or the frontmatter said it was fiction, and its frontmatter reads `outcome: 3 accounts triggered, 0 meetings yet`. Meanwhile `outputs/README.md` tells agents to *"read the recent entries here for prior art"* before starting work. The `ACME:` line on line 9 catches anything that reads the body. It does not catch a frontmatter-only consumer, and it does not catch someone scanning a directory listing. Renamed to `2026-07-10-example-signal-detection-first-run` and retitled `"Example: ..."` to match its sibling. It still satisfies the `YYYY-MM-DD-` entry rule, and nothing referenced the old path. ## 3. Nothing reported on the markers `grep -rn ACME scripts/ .github/` was empty, so the convention depended on remembering to run the grep. Adds `lint:examples`, wired into `npm run lint`: ``` worked examples: 73 files scanned, 9 still fiction (report-only; --strict to enforce) ``` **Report-only by default.** A freshly scaffolded repo legitimately carries every marker, and a scaffold whose lint fails out of the box is one nobody trusts. `--strict` turns them into errors so a repo that has finished replacing can keep fiction from coming back in CI. It matches the marker only where it *opens* a line, so prose that merely names the convention — `AGENTS.md`, and the new carve-out in change 1 — isn't itself counted. That was a real false positive on the first pass. The case this actually catches is **partial** replacement. The examples cross-reference each other: `plan/outcomes.md:34` and `plan/company-plan.md:30` both name `initiatives/outbound-motion.md`. Replace some and keep others and you get real files citing fiction, which nothing else would surface. ## 4. `outputs/` had no template The other three layers ship `_template.md` beside their example. `outputs/` shipped only the example — which is why its marker reads *"showing the shape of an outputs entry"*. So "delete it" also deleted the only shape reference. Adds `outputs/_template/`, and teaches `lint-outputs.ts` to skip `_`-prefixed directories, which otherwise fail the entry-name pattern. Same convention as `cadence/` and `initiatives/`. ## Verification Simulated both ends rather than reasoning about them: | State | Result | | --- | --- | | fresh scaffold | 9 files fiction, report-only, `npm run lint` green | | five dated samples deleted, four remaining markers stripped | 0 fiction, `--strict` exits 0, `npm run lint` green, `outputs/_template/` survives | `npm run typecheck` clean. I also confirmed the new copy carries no em dash, which `check-copy.ts` rejects repo-wide — my first draft of the change-1 wording had one. ## Not changed Two things I noticed and left alone, since they're judgement calls rather than defects: - the nine markers use five different phrasings. Harmless, since `ACME:` is the greppable part, and `lint:examples` now lists them regardless. - the dates age. A scaffold generated today ships with July history; one generated next year ships with history over a year old. Fixing that means generating dates at `cdk init` time, which is a CLI change, not a repo change. ---
Created with Replicas

author: ebarnett3
body:
first step for #17

For the full draft implementation of #17, see PR #41

A condition variable is added to the Platform interface. In the subsequent PRs, this will be used to synchronize consumers with the gripper's data exchange cycle. This will allow polling-based approaches to be replaced by event-based approaches.

Example: currently, if a consumer runs a control loop, it must be paced independently of the exchange cycle, creating an inherent desynchronization problem. With the condition variable and the subsequent PRs, such a loop can be executed in lockstep with the exchange cycle.

author: steipete
body:
Follows #149697 (merged).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing cron usage when a retry after an acknowledgement throws or is cancelled, even though the first prompt already consumed tokens.

## User Impact

Failed scheduled runs retain completed prompt usage and cost while preserving the original error. The interim acknowledgement is not delivered, and accounting cannot overwrite a replacement session. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The execution owner now records completed prompts before continuation persistence can fail. Success and error handling share one accounting settlement, so usage and diagnostics are recorded once even if later persistence or delivery fails. Final-result context adoption stays separate, and session writes retain their existing lifecycle checks.

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway baseline reproduced:** on `f7b6ec34117`, an isolated Gateway and registered synthetic harness completed a prompt with 10 input tokens, 20 output tokens, and 3 cache-read tokens, then threw `AgentHarnessPreflightError` during the retry. The cron CLI reported the original `Synthetic cron retry preparation failed.` error, but run usage was absent instead of totaling 33 tokens.
- **Runner tests passed:** 59 tests across five retry, accounting, and lifecycle suites. The final five-case regression table also passed: retry rejection, cancellation, accounting-write failure with a late abort, a competing session generation, and delivery failure after a completed retry. These checks cover original-error preservation, no interim delivery, unchanged replacement-session billing, and no duplicate usage diagnostics.
- **Checks passed:** scoped lint, formatting, diff checks, and a fresh isolated review through P2 with no actionable findings. The original-code regression failed on missing usage before the repair.
- **Candidate build and live proof passed:** full production build at final head `4f1114ee2b2385df80796e96ea6ebc9946e10a29`, followed by both registered-harness cases through the actual isolated Gateway and public cron CLI. Each retained 10 input, 20 output and 3 cached tokens (33 total), with session cost $0.0000515. The thrown error and the returned-abort diagnostic were preserved. Each emitted exactly one terminal failure webhook with the same usage, omitted diagnostic/summary fields according to the existing webhook contract, and contained no interim acknowledgement. Owned processes and isolated state were cleaned up.
- **Required CI passed:** [run 35061190786](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35061190786) completed successfully on the final head. Both live cases also passed again after the main refresh.

author: craftsamo
body:
## Summary

Hermes Engineer drove OpenCode through the same `plan`, `build` and `review`
primaries a human uses in the TUI. Those prompts assume someone is sitting at
the terminal: they ask clarifying questions, hand a plan off to build, keep a
visible todo list, and consider a reviewer pass before every commit. In a
non-interactive `opencode run` the question tool is denied outright and the
caller is another agent, so that ceremony only cost turns and context.

This adds three hidden primaries written for that transport and points the
wrapper at them.

**Hidden primaries**: `hermes-plan`, `hermes-build` and `hermes-review`
(`mode: primary`, `hidden: true`) replace the provider default prompt with a
non-interactive contract — decisions returned as numbered questions with a
default already taken, fixed report headings the caller can parse, every check
delegated to the verifier subagent so the primary keeps its context, and
reviewer passes only when the message asks for one. `debug` still shares the
human primary.

**Role mapping**: the wrapper maps the Hermes role to the installed agent at
exactly two points — the `--agent` flag and the injected per-agent permission
key. The branch gate, the appended scope lines, `--auto` and the permission
shape all keep reading the role, so renaming an installed agent stays a
one-line change.

**Model split**: plan and review run on Opus 5, build on GPT-5.6 Sol, pinned
per role instead of following whichever family Hermes itself runs on. Whether
Engineer sits on Fable or Astra, the plan it challenges and the code it QAs
never come from its own model family. Opus 5 joins the wrapper allowlist so a
Client can still name it explicitly.

**Contract docs**: the shared OpenCode reference and the plan / build / QA
entries record the new handshake — answer plan's open decisions with
`DECISION(Q<n>)`, and ask for a review pass in the message when an increment
warrants one.

## Verification

- `pytest hermes/plugins/opencode` — 35 passed, including four new cases
  covering the role-to-agent map, `--auto` placement and the injected key.
- `scripts/validate-profile-skills.py --all` — PASS.
- Live smoke on a scratch repo: all three agents resolve by name and end with a
  `stop` event; the session store confirms Opus 5 / high for plan and review
  and GPT-5.6 Sol / medium for build.
- `opencode debug config` confirms `hidden: true` and that the injected
  permission deep-merges with each file's own block rather than replacing it.

## Notes

- Nothing to restart: `opencode run` starts a fresh process per call and the
  wrapper change applies on the next Hermes turn.
- Hidden primaries stay reachable by `--agent` but are refused by
  `default_agent` and never appear in the TUI agent cycle.
- OpenCode keys its plan-mode reminder on the literal agent name `plan`, so
  `hermes-plan` gets none of it — its read-only posture comes from the prompt
  and the permission block instead.
- The read-only permission object the wrapper injects is shared by plan and
  review, so plan is technically allowed to call `reviewer`/`debugger` even
  though its prompt forbids it. Splitting that per role is a follow-up if it
  ever matters.

author: richard-epsilla
body:
Google retires gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash and gemini-2.5-flash-lite in about a month. A model the provider will refuse is not a model this product supports, so the three ids leave every place the support list is defined:

- the gemini catalog and every other backend's model list in `_MODEL_CATALOG`
- the Vercel and OpenRouter provider maps and the Google vendor table
- the runner's pinned gemini-cli id tuple
- the console's placeholder lists in `ui/src/lib/harness.ts`

Nothing is renamed or aliased. An id that is gone is refused at the send the same way any unknown id is.

**The support matrix.** It is rendered from the recorded runs, so the 81 pairs that measured those ids are dropped from `docs/support-matrix-results.json` and `docs/support-matrix.md` is rendered again from what remains. The retired rows are gone; no other row changed, only the per-column counts.

author: carnster
body:
Lets each school **author its own registration policy text** — the exact words a family reads and signs (handbook, discipline, media release, field trip, tech/internet, FERPA, etc.). Until now that text was hardcoded in `policy-content.ts`, so a school couldn't update its own annual handbook language without a developer.

## What's in it
- **Migration 00066** — `campus_policy_override` (campus_id, item_type, body_en, body_es, optional `pdf_storage_path`), RLS: enrollment_manager on the campus writes, campus staff read. **Absent row = the built-in default**, so nothing changes until a school edits a policy. (Applied to prod; migration file included.)
- **Family registration** now shows the school's own policy text, falling back to the built-in default. The text is fetched **server-side** (a family isn't campus staff, so it can't read the table under RLS), and the query is **fail-safe** — any error resolves to the built-in, so it can never block registration.
- **Settings → Registration policies** — campus picker + an **EN/ES editor per policy**, prefilled from the school's text or the built-in default, with **Reset to default** and a Customized/Using-default badge. Saving is RLS-gated and audit-logged; clearing both languages resets to the default.

## Red-team / verification
- **No cross-campus leak:** `activeCampus` is clamped to the manager's accessible campuses (URL tampering can't view another campus), and writes are independently RLS-enforced (`enrollment_manager` on that campus).
- **Migration verified in prod:** 10 columns, 2 RLS policies, RLS enabled.
- **Fail-safe read:** table-missing / error → built-in text, registration unaffected.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; **532 tests pass**.

## Next step (schema already supports it)
`pdf_storage_path` is in place so schools can attach the **official policy PDF** and **blank forms families download/fill/upload** — the file-attach half — as the immediate follow-up.

author: wwolf
body:
## The present grid follows today's rivers and paints today's lakes

Rebased onto main after #48 merged (v0.15.1). Two things the lake pictures exposed: at 0 m the Danube was not drawn, and below 0 m the Caspian vanished.

**The Danube.** The 20 km grid closes every gorge narrower than a cell. Routed on the grid alone, the Pannonian basin is a closed pit (the Iron Gates cell stands at 398 m), the fill raised it to 383 m and spilled it over its lowest rim, the Moravian Gate, into the Oder: 0.54 Mkm² went to the Baltic, the delta received 0.23 Mkm² instead of about 0.8, and the lines inside the filled basin were the fill's outlet paths, not the river. Carving narrow sills (breaching) did not help: in this grid the Moravian Gate really is the lower pass, so nothing on the grid can prefer the Iron Gates.

**What this PR does.** Where today's rivers are known they need not be guessed. `sources/present-water.json` pins Natural Earth's 10 m river and lake centrelines (public domain, 1,473 features with a size rank) and HydroLAKES v1.0 (Messager et al. 2016, CC BY 4.0, 1.4 million lakes with their mean depth, the Caspian included; the 820 MB archive is extracted with the receipt of #44 and deleted). `scripts/present_water.py` rasterises them onto the present grid's texture, cached beside the fields:

- rivers as one-texel lines carrying a size from their rank (canals left out, lake centrelines kept so a river stays continuous through its lakes), with two corrections: where two rivers touch anywhere but at the lower end of one of them they pass each other across a divide (the Guaporé and the Paraguay at the Pantanal, the Red and the Minnesota at the Traverse Gap) and the smaller is broken there, or the trenches below would join and one basin drain through the other's mouth; and a line that stops short, of the river it joins or of the grid's sea (Natural Earth ends the Amazon 250 km from the grid's coast), is carried on along the lowest path;
- lakes of 100 km² or more at their mean depth, and the texels of the lakes the grid holds at or below its datum (the Caspian, the Dead Sea).

For the present grid only, `scripts/build_rivers.py` cuts the routing surface along the lines (50 m at rank 12, 2,000 m at rank 1, so a headwater trench never reaches a main stem's pool), lets the water out of the grid where a line meets the sea and in those below-datum lakes at every sea level, then fills and routes as before. The drawn field is still the drained area; the lines only guide it. The present fields and the ice slices paint HydroLAKES's lakes in the green channel of #48 (at least 3 m so Chad's 1.5 m still passes the cut, off the ice), so the Great Lakes, Baikal and Victoria, which the grid draws as flat land, appear, and the Caspian stays a lake whatever the slider says, with the Volga ending in it rather than crossing its floor to the Manych.

**Checks on the present grid (drained area, Mkm²).** Danube delta 0.81 (0.61 through the Iron Gates, 0.01 through the Moravian Gate, Budapest 0.22); Amazon 5.7 (Óbidos 4.5); Congo 3.9 (Kinshasa 3.8); Nile 3.3; Plata 3.3; Mississippi 3.2 (Memphis 2.4); Yangtze 2.0; Volga 1.3 into the Caspian at 0, −20 and −130 m alike. Pooled ground 8.0 of 143 Mkm² (17.8 before). Known overshoots stay from the every-basin-spills rule: the Niger 6.4 (real 2.1) collects the Chad basin's and the Sahara's spill, the Amur 3.3 (1.9) Mongolia's.

**Not done, and why.** Which other basins are closed today (Chad, Balkhash, the Great Salt Lake) the data cannot say: a test on the river lines closed the Great Lakes, Kariba, Rybinsk and Lake Albert as well, which would have cut the St Lawrence, Zambezi, Volga and Nile, so only the grid's own below-datum lakes are sinks and the rest spill as before. HydroRIVERS, which has an endorheic flag, was downloaded and tried and then dropped: its licence is WWF's HydroSHEDS agreement (an end-user licence and a fixed attribution for derivative works), not CC BY like HydroLAKES's own. The Caspian's glacial levels (Atelian lowstand, Khvalynian highstand) exist only as curves in papers; today's outline stands in for them in the ice slices.

**Verified.** `tests/rivers_check.py` 10 OK, `tests/present_water_check.py` 3 OK (a line carried on to the sea, a junction kept, a divide contact broken), Django 77 OK; browser suites and the Firefox check against a development server on this branch; pictures below the fold in the devlog (wwolf 011). Only the present grid's two fields and the 32 ice slices need rebuilding for this change (`build_rivers.py paleodem-0000` and `--ice`), after `fetch_paleodem.py --manifest sources/present-water.json`; the other 138 fields are unchanged, and the `?format=river-lake-rgb-v1` URLs and the packer guard of bbe5e9e apply as before.

## Review follow-up (2026-09-16, devlog wwolf 012)

The three defects jikhanjung reproduced (devlog 090) are fixed, each with its counterexample as a regression check in `tests/present_water_check.py` (now 12 checks):

- **Path search:** the state is (cell, steps); `best`, `before` and the reconstruction follow it, ordered by highest ground then steps. The 6×8 grid returns the four-move route over ground no higher than 5.
- **Lake islands:** outer rings (clockwise) are filled, inner rings (counter-clockwise) cleared, and `closed` uses the same mask. Islands are cleared where they cover a texel's centre (`clear_island()`, drawn 8× finer): PIL fills every texel a polygon touches, and HydroLAKES has 79,791 islands among its 1,708 lakes of 100 km² or more (1,247 in Huron), so clearing every touched texel had emptied half the lake texels. Lake texels 20,547 → 19,174; closed 1,660 → 1,622.
- **Cache:** `cache_key()` hashes the elevation array (bytes and dtype), the whole manifest (with the source hashes) and the rule version `RULES` with the tunables, stored as `key` in the npz; a cache without that key, or of another key, shape or type, is not used and says so. A new cache is built only from sources verified with `fetch_paleodem.py`'s `verify`/`verify_extracted` (the Natural Earth zip hashed and read directly, HydroLAKES's extracted files checked against the receipt); without them `load()` returns None as before.

The manifest note now describes the final rule (outlets where a line meets the sea and in the below-datum lakes), and the docs record the islands, the cache key and the **deployment scope: the production series is the present grid's two fields and the ten ice slices to 25 ka (`--ice` default); the 32 slices to 80 ka exist only where `--ice-to 80` builds them and are not deployed until #59 decides the 26–80 ka policy.**

Rebuilt from the verified sources: cache (225 s), the two present fields and the 32 slices. Basin areas unchanged: Danube delta 0.81 Mkm² (Iron Gates 0.62), Amazon 5.75, Congo 3.79, Nile 3.34, Plata 3.30, Mississippi 3.16, Yangtze 1.98, Volga 1.32 into the Caspian. Checks: `present_water_check` 12, `rivers_check` 12, Django 77, `make check`; the browser suites (`river-browser`, `globe-browser`, `firefox-browser`) did **not** run here: Playwright's headless-shell download stalled twice and headless Firefox did not open its BiDi port on this machine. The change touches the processing script and the derived data only, no JS or templates, so the screen check before merge remains yours to run.

author: monsieurbon
body:
One rule throughout: a comment stays only when the fact has no trace in the code. "It documents the why" is not enough if the surrounding code already implies the reason. 1089 comment lines to 406, CLAUDE.md 266 to 124, no behaviour changes.

Two things you cannot get from the diff:

- **The SQL migrations are untouched on purpose.** Editing V1–V3 changes their Flyway checksum, and `validate-on-migrate` defaults to true, so every already-migrated database would refuse to start.
- **`TaskRepository`'s zone ordering is fragile and I did not fix it.** Its comment claimed `order by t.zone` uses the enum's declaration order; the column is a string and only sorts alike by luck. A fourth zone could break board ordering silently.

`./mvnw -Pintegration-tests verify` green from clean; `OpenApiContractIT` did not rewrite the contract.

## Summary

Step 6 of the mango-protocol monorepo import (Ref #1064, #1065, #1066): move the tree out of `mango-protocol/` into `spec/`, `packages/protocol/`, `crates/mango-protocol/`, `docs/protocol/`, and `scripts/protocol/`; resolve `@mangostudio/protocol` via `workspace:*`; add path-filtered Protocol CI and a `protocol-v*` release train; remove import fences.

The layout mirrors upstream (`spec/` at the repo root for `../../spec`; fuzz workspace nested under the crate) so source paths did not need rewriting.

## Changes

- **Relocation.** Drop `mango-protocol/` and duplicate protocol Biome/dprint/tsconfig/lefthook manifests; wire check/test/fix through root `protocol:*` lanes. Apps pin `workspace:*`; in-repo `exports` → `src/`. Published npm layout via `scripts/protocol/pack.ts` (npm does not apply `publishConfig.exports`).
- **CI / release.** `protocol-ci.yml` (Gate always reports; Rust matrix only on protocol paths). `protocol-release.yml` on `protocol-v*.*.*` with `make_latest: false` so application `latest` assets stay on app tags. Fuzz under `crates/mango-protocol/fuzz`. Dependabot for root + fuzz Cargo locks; labeler paths updated. `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.96.0` on cargo-shim. CodeQL config is name-only — protocol TypeScript and runtime-contract artifacts scan with the rest of the repo.
- **Release guards.** `resolve` requires the exact `protocol-v$version` tag (blocks unsafe `workflow_dispatch`). `github-release` uses the `protocol-release` environment (tag deployment rule provisioned). Release verify installs `cargo-hack`, 45m timeout, re-runnable GitHub assets (`gh release upload --clobber`).
- **Changelog.** Separate app vs protocol trains (`exclude_paths`, `PROTOCOL_IMPORT_TIP..HEAD` for app full-history modes; `protocol:release:prepare` prepends — never regenerates upstream 0.1.0/0.2.0). `PROTOCOL_CHANGELOG_GLOBS` includes `.github/workflows/protocol-*.yml`. Blank-line postprocessor in both cliff configs (next app release may reformat `CHANGELOG.md` only).
- **Pack / verify.** Turbo caches LICENSE and hashes external build inputs; `pack.ts` stages from manifest `files`; `verify-package` asserts non-wildcard export targets, `replaceAll` for wildcards, `withTempDir` cleanup; shallow-checkout skips for `PROTOCOL_IMPORT_TIP` tests. `--rs-only` fails when Cargo is missing. `scripts/lib/protocol.ts` in `PROTOCOL_TOOLING_FILES` (release/fuzz workflows stay out — tag/schedule triggers).
- **Docs / tooling.** `docs/protocol/` index; architecture/playbooks/releasing updates. `scripts/runtime-contract/validate.ts` reads `spec/schema/1/` directly; stricter `packages/protocol/tsconfig.json`. `bun run fix --staged` keys rustfmt on protocol surface (mirrors `check.ts`). `runSequential` coverage in `scripts/lib/exec.ts`.

## Test Plan

author: lowiesevilla-crypto
body:
## Production incident
Admin Employee workflow can fall into the global error boundary when an employee payroll configuration already has today's effective date and the administrator changes salary/rate again on the same day. The shared form always submitted today's effective date, while the server rejected any changed configuration whose date was <= the latest version.

## Fix
- allow correction of the newest compensation version on the same effective date only when no finalized/posted/paid payroll locks that period
- retain the existing locked-payroll protection and reject genuinely backdated changes
- keep EmployeeProfile legacy payroll fields synchronized
- preserve a future scheduled effective date in the edit form instead of defaulting behind it
- clarify payroll configuration UI behavior
- extend the included Employee browser E2E to reproduce: create employee -> identity edit -> same-day salary edit -> verify one compensation row and corrected rate -> verify Add Employee route remains healthy

## Safety
- no destructive migration
- no production data deletion
- tenant scoping remains unchanged
- finalized/posted/paid payroll history remains protected
- merge only after required CI/build/browser gates pass
