author: ludvignion
body:
## The bug

git moves at wall-clock speed while the runner reads the build session's stream behind it. By the time the runner is on tool result N, the builder may already have run N+1 and N+2.

`after_tool()` read the close-out from whatever `HEAD` happened to be at that instant, so `done` flipped a step or more early. The build's own remaining calls — **including the close-out commit itself** — then arrived looking like orbits after a close-out they had in fact produced. The runner terminated the session on one of them and logged `orbit after close-out` on the ticket as its own finding, against a build that did nothing wrong.

It also broke out of the stream loop on the spot, before the result envelope was read, dropping the permission denials, the turn count and the cost with it.

There was a second, narrower window inside the same function: `head_subject()` ran `git log -1` and `status_marks()` ran `git show HEAD:<ticket>` as two independent resolutions of `HEAD`, so a commit landing between them made the runner read the feat commit's subject and the close-out's status line from *different commits*.

Under load this took whichever test asserted on anything at or after the close-out. On `main` before this branch, `make ci` was red 2 runs in 4. 0.11.4 moved `green` into the close-out step to dodge one instance (E32); this is the cause behind it (E33).

## The fix

- `head_sha` is read **once** per tool result and passed to `head_subject` and `status_marks`, so both describe the same commit.
- `wrote_a_session_commit` spares a call the orbit when its text writes one of the commit subjects in `start_sha..closeout_sha`. Nothing in git can say where the stream is, and nothing in the stream can say what git holds — those subjects are the one thing present in both. The range ends at the **close-out commit**, so a builder that keeps committing after its close-out is still caught.
- `drain_envelope` reads a terminated session's output to the end of its result envelope instead of breaking immediately.

## Test plan

- `test_a_commit_after_the_close_out_is_still_an_orbit` added, pinning the upper bound of the range.
- Runner suite: 12 sequential runs green, 6 concurrent copies green.
- `make ci`: 3 consecutive full runs, 326 tests, `OK (skipped=1)`.
- No assertion relaxed and no test removed; the only test change is the one added.

Lands in the untagged `0.11.5` section, so it ships with that release.

body:
## 目的

設計書 `case_knowledge_design_20260916.md`（v2）の ①②③ のコード部分。Aico Vault の文書（提案書・報告書・施策実績）から **事例レコード**（業種・目的・商品状態・チャネル・特性・結果・出典）を抽出して構造化する層を足し、類似事例・競合事例を「構造で絞る → 意味で並べる」で引けるようにする。元文書は消さず、レコードは元 document への参照（external_id / URL / 抜粋）を持つ。

## 変更

| 区分 | ファイル | 内容 |
|---|---|---|
| schema | `src/teamagent/cases/schema.py` | `CaseRecord` v1（pydantic strict・extra=forbid）。tag 語彙は青木 事例DB.json の `_meta.tag_vocab` をそのまま定数化（purpose 7 / sector 11 / product_state 4 / channel 6 / traits 9・語彙外は `その他`）。`metrics[]` は `{name, value(文字列そのまま), unit, source_url}`。`external_use` は ok/ng/unknown。`similar_keys` は構造 4 項目から常に導出 |

| extract | `src/teamagent/cases/extract.py` | `extract_cases(document_text, *, document_meta, bedrock, model_id, request_id)`。`BedrockClient.converse` のみ。フェンス除去＋ 1 回 repair（ValidationError 文面を返して再送）。安全装置: 語彙外→その他 / 本文に無い数値は捨てる / 出典は文書に固定 / `client_masked` に社名が残れば業種表記へ / `external_use` はモデルに決めさせない |

## テスト結果

## 未実施（裁定待ち・費用）

## Build failure
The newly included `frontress_sm3_compat.h` pulls `<windows.h>` into `clientmode_tf.cpp` before its gameplay methods. Windows SDK macros rewrite `IGameEventManager2::CreateEvent` to `CreateEventA` and `vgui::ISurface::PlaySound` to `PlaySoundA`, leading to the reported 11 C2039 errors. The default broad Windows headers also trigger registry-name macro redefinition warnings.

## Fix
- Include Windows headers under `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN` to limit collateral headers; restore the macro to its prior state afterwards.
- Explicitly `#undef CreateEvent` and `#undef PlaySound` after the include, so Source's C++ API method names remain intact.
- No change to fatal SM3 check, GPU diagnostics, translations, or game rendering.

## Validation
Source inspection identifies every error in the report as the name-macro collision caused by the new Windows include. **Windows x64 compilation has not yet been rerun**; please verify with the failing build before merging. If registry macro warnings persist, isolate Win32 implementation in a dedicated compilation unit instead of including the general Windows headers in this gameplay header.

author: algorex-ph
body:
Consolidates the four open frontend PRs from this week's Epic 3 work into one. **Replaces #53, #55, #57 and #58**, which are closed in favour of this.

One real conflict in `e2e/mocks.ts`, resolved keeping both explanations (details below). The combined result is gated in full — which is the point of consolidating rather than merging four branches in sequence and hoping.

> **⚠️ Merge order: [Contracts #2](https://github.com/Bl0cksmiths/Orizon-Agents-Smart-Contract-Stellar/pull/2) must land first.** The address-parity CI job checks out the contracts repo's default branch, and the address book only exists on a feature branch until that PR merges. Until then that job is red with exit 1 — the correct signal, since it has no skip path by design.

---

## What is in here

### Correct the cold-start claim on the operator dashboard (was #53)
**My error, shipped in 2.06.** `routing-standing.tsx` told every operator *"a brand-new agent's lower bound sits below the floor."* That is false, and it is the opposite of the guarantee permissionless registration rests on:

```
prior_bps = 7000 · cold-start lower bound = 5677 · floor_bps = 5500 → clears by 177 bps
```

A never-rated agent is **routable on the day it is registered**. Telling an operator otherwise, on the one screen they read after registering, is the most discouraging thing the product could say — and it was wrong.

### Make format:check pass on a clean clone (was #55)
Frontend CI had been red on `main` for the same class of reason as the backend: CI runs `prettier --check .` over the whole repo while everyone locally runs it on source directories. Twelve tracked files failed.

Split by judgement rather than a blanket `--write`: two are genuine source files that should be formatted; nine are `Week-1-Tranche-Submission/`, added to `.prettierignore` on the same reasoning as the `docs/` entry already there — they are hand-laid-out for a grant reviewer and **frozen once submitted**, so reformatting would rewrite a record of what was actually sent.

### 3.05 — Marketplace standing (was #57)
`/app/agents` showed a score and nothing about whether an agent can be hired.

**The audit found the ticket could have been closed against a badge marking the wrong population.** `{a.real && <Badge>LIVE</Badge>}` — `real` means "backed by a real Agno worker rather than a mock", `registry_sync` sets it false for *every* on-chain agent, and the seeded catalog is a mix. The one population it could never mark is the externally registered agents this marketplace exists to make visible. **Removed, not relabelled** — leaving it beside a real provenance badge would put two contradictory provenance signals in one row.

Rows now carry provenance (`⬡ external` — not "on-chain", because the same row says "on-chain reputation" and two different "on-chain"s is an ambiguity we would have created), `⊘ not yet operational`, `⚑ below floor · not eligible`, and `⚠ provisional`. Clearing the floor renders nothing: good standing is the ordinary case, and a marker on every row is a marker on none.

**A false claim fixed in the shared badge.** `ReputationBadge` labelled every `source: "prior"` score *"no on-chain ratings yet"* — including reads that had **failed**, asserting an agent has no history when we had merely been unable to read it. Identically on three surfaces: the marketplace, the plan card, and the operator dashboard.

### 3.07 — Catch contract address drift (was #58)
Two hardcoded copies of the same ids became one shared module — the within-a-repo version of the very problem this story is about.

**The check is a script, not a unit test, and that is the interesting decision.** Its input lives in another repo, so a vitest test could only be red on every laptop without a clone, or skip. Red-everywhere is skip with extra steps: a test that is red for reasons unrelated to your change gets disabled. Taking it out of the suite is what buys the third option — **always fail when the address book is missing.** Verified by exit code:

```
missing dir -> 1    unset+no checkout -> 1    real clone -> 0
```

Extended at integration to cover `README.md`, the higher-risk surface and the one people copy ids *from*: ten ids, four contracts, both networks, every one a clickable explorer link. Matched **by shape, not position**, so reflowing a table does not break it. Proven to bite with the exact stale id story 3.07 was written about:

```
FAIL  README.md (link)  CDHDMVVER…3J63WXKV != not a deployed address    exit=1
```

---

## The one conflict

`e2e/mocks.ts` — both `fix/cold-start-claim` and 3.04's fixture work corrected the same impossible cold-start value (`5100`, which `lowerBoundBps(7000, 0)` can never produce). Resolved by keeping `main`'s fuller doc comment, which already records the `5100` history, **and** the branch's per-value explanation of why 5677 is what the arithmetic actually returns. Neither explanation was dropped.

---

## Gate, on the combined branch

typecheck · lint (`--max-warnings=0`) · `format:check` clean for CI · build · bundle budget · **873 unit tests** (37 files) · **66 e2e** including the full WCAG A/AA sweep · `check:addresses` 3/3.

The one remaining `format:check` warning is an untracked `C:\Users\Predator\AppData\Local\lighthouse.21828904/` directory in my working tree — a Windows path leaked into WSL by `npm run lighthouse`. CI clones fresh so it never sees it; worth deleting locally.

49 non-merge commits.

author: fred-labs
body:
`follow_waypoints` takes its goals as an OSC-declared `list of pose_3d`. That works while a scenario author writes the poses, and stops working when an offline planner produces them: tens to hundreds of poses, a different sequence per condition and repetition. Writing those into the scenario — or into the parameter overrides that vary it — makes either file the store for another tool's output: regenerated wholesale whenever the planner runs again, and unreadable as a scenario in between.

`follow_waypoints_from_file` is `follow_waypoints` with the poses read at execute time from where the planner already wrote them.

```
do serial:
    robot.follow_waypoints_from_file(poses_file: '/data/plan.json', rep: 3)
```

The file is shaped `{"repetitions": [{"waypoints": [[...], ...]}, ...]}` — one entry per draw of the offline step, each an ordered list of fixed-width rows.

- `x_index` / `y_index` / `theta_index` locate the pose within a row, so a producer's own column layout is read as it is rather than assumed.
- `rep` selects the entry and wraps by their number, so a deterministic planner's single recorded sequence serves every `rep` alike and several serve one draw each, without the scenario having to know which case it is in.

The subclass overrides `execute` only, so the goal message, the loop count, the namespace and the feedback message are the existing action's. A file with no `repetitions` raises rather than navigating to an empty list, since an empty goal set is a run that succeeds having gone nowhere.

`make check` (autopep8 + pylint) passes on the added files; `docs/libraries.rst` gains the action's parameter table and `docs/dictionary.txt` the two words the spelling check would otherwise stop on.

author: kratobal
body:
## What and why

Balázs asked for the sticker code to be enterable on an asset that was recorded
without one. The server was the bottleneck: `UpdateAssetDto` did not know
`labelCode` **at all**, so the phone had nothing to call. This is that half —
the mobile and web halves follow, and the order is deliberate.

## What it does

- `UpdateAssetDto` accepts `labelCode`. The shape is checked by the shared
  `normalizeAssetLabelCode`, not by a second pattern beside the first.
- The repository's update path **claims, swaps and releases in one
  transaction**, at the same `Serializable` level as create, and with the same
  guard: a conditional `updateMany` on `assetId: null`, never a read-then-write.
  Two concurrent requests for one code still cannot both pass.
- A swap writes `LABEL_ASSIGNED` carrying `previousCode`, so the journal can say
  which sticker went back into stock. **Sending the same code again is not an
  event** — the web form posts the whole record, so without that check every
  save would write a line and the journal would be unreadable in three days.

## Three decisions the brief left to me

**1. No removal in this round — and the reason is not the mechanics.** Clearing
the row is one statement. The obstacle is that the journal has *no name* for it:
the only type is `LABEL_ASSIGNED`, which says the opposite, and adding
`LABEL_RELEASED` is a schema migration for something Balázs did not ask for.

So `labelCode` is `string`, **not** `string | null` like its sibling fields —
a deliberate deviation from the file's own convention, written down where it
deviates. A `null` now fails validation loudly instead of silently doing nothing.

**2. The missing field is not an empty field.** Absent → the sticker stays;
empty string → invalid code, 400. That is why the update path calls
`normalizeAssetLabelCode` and **not** `assetLabelCreateProblem`: the latter reads
an empty string as "no sticker", which is right on create and wrong here.

**3. The editor gets the INTERNAL conflict message.** The endpoint sits behind
`SERVICE_MANAGE`, so whoever reaches it can see the issued-code list; splitting
the two cases ("not issued" vs "already on another asset") is useful to them, not
a leak. `map` takes the scope *optionally* and silently falls back to the partner
text — nothing fails, the caller just learns less than they are owed.

## Measured on the way

**A code-only save writes a row.** This decides whether the feature works at all:
`data` carries every field as `undefined` when only the label is sent, so the
question was whether `updateMany` returns count 1 or trips `STALE_UPDATE`.
`Asset.updatedAt` is `@updatedAt`, so Prisma always writes it. Count is 1, and
the concurrency token moves — which is correct, the asset did change.

## Calibration

Not "it went red", but: how many tests **ran**, and was the red the one named.

    break: drop the { kind: "internal" } scope
      2711 ran (same as unbroken)   red: "a szerkesztő ág a BELSŐS üzenetet adja"
      the sibling 400-vs-409 test stayed green

    break: remove the shape split inside `map`
      2711 ran (same as unbroken)   red: "a szerkesztő ágon a rossz ALAK 400-at ad"
      nothing else reddened

A note on the count: node:test reports each of these twice (subtest and
top level), so `# fail 2` is **one** assertion, not two.

The second calibration also turned up something worth stating: **no existing
test guarded `map`'s shape branch.** Had one existed, that break would have
reddened it too. The new assertion is the first thing holding that split.

## What this does not prove

The five integration assertions — attach, swap, sibling control, rollback,
malformed — **have not run locally**. There is no Postgres in my container, so
their first real run is CI. They are written into
`asset-label.integration.spec.ts` rather than a new file because that suite's
stated intent is to measure the label stock *on the database*, and a separate
file would assert the same things under another name.

The fourth of them is the one that matters most and is the one a unit test
cannot reach: a swap is two steps, and if the release commits while the claim
fails, an asset stands without a sticker whose old code is already back in
stock. Only the database can show that boundary holds.

## Gates

All four, from the root, forced:

    pnpm format:check                    exit 0
    turbo run typecheck --force          6/6 tasks,  0 cached
    turbo run test --force              10/10 tasks, 0 cached
    turbo run build --force              6/6 tasks,  0 cached

## A second commit, and why it is not scope creep

While wiring the mobile half I measured something the brief did not name: **no
screen anywhere shows which sticker is on an asset.** `AssetDetail` does not
carry the code, so the field cannot be pre-filled.

That was harmless while the code could only be given at creation. It is not
harmless now, because the same brief allows a **swap**: the form would show an
empty box, the technician would type a code, and a working sticker would go back
into stock with nobody the wiser. The swap decision is what makes the read
load-bearing, so it belongs to the server half rather than to the client PRs.

Three lines and a type: `AssetDetail.labelCode`, `label: { select: { code: true } }`
in `assetDetailInclude`, and `labelCode: row.label?.code` in the mapping.

**The relation is singular, and the schema decided that, not me.** I wrote
`labels` first; the compiler corrected me. It was right: a list would have
claimed an asset can carry several stickers, and `AssetLabel.assetId` is unique
precisely so it cannot.

Two assertions, and the second is what makes the first mean anything — a field
that is *always* filled would satisfy "the detail returns the code" just as well.
The sibling requires that an asset without a sticker comes back with the field
absent, and that the query does not fall over on the empty relation.

**And the type will not catch a regression here.** `labelCode` is optional, so
deleting the mapping line compiles cleanly. That is exactly why the assertion
exists rather than trusting the types.

Gates re-run after this commit: format 0, typecheck 6/6 (0 cached), test 10/10
(0 cached), build 6/6 (0 cached).

## What

**Load more (bounded window).** `search` gains an optional `limit` (default 20) and returns `candidateCount`; results are a stable prefix of the reranked candidate list, so pressing Load more fetches the next 20 with no duplicates or reordering, up to the 200-candidate rerank window. A query/sort/lane change restarts at page one, and the previous page stays on screen while the next loads (state derived during render, no set-state-in-effect). When the window is exhausted the SERP says so instead of pretending there is more.

**Why a window, not infinite scroll:** retrieval is deliberately bounded (RISKS R1: seed 1,500, per-term caps, ≤200 reranked). Widening past 200 would need a deliberate read-budget change, not a UI tweak.

author: danbarua
body:
## Bug

`Orchestrator.poll()` returns immediately once `result.json` reads OK, skipping the log-pull block that only runs in the still-running (`else`) branch. Any output the script writes between the last periodic pull and process exit was never synced to local disk -- not a rare race, the normal shape of the terminating poll tick.

Caught live during dogfooding: two otherwise-identical CPU sleep/wake/log jobs applied back to back. Job 1 happened to keep its trailing `done` line because an earlier periodic tick landed after the line was already flushed. Job 2 lost its final print and the runner's terminal status line entirely -- same code, same shape, just unlucky timing.

## Fix

Extracted the existing best-effort log-pull into `Orchestrator._pull_runner_log(transport)`. Still called every healthy poll tick (unchanged behavior). Now also called once more from `cleanup()`, through the same Contents transport (`self.job_transport()`), immediately before `client.unassign()` releases the VM that holds the file -- the true last chance to read anything off it.

## Verification

- New regression test `test_cleanup_pulls_runner_log_once_more_before_releasing_the_vm`: drives `poll()` to capture one line via a fake transport, then `cleanup()` to capture a second (different) line, asserting cleanup's own pull -- not poll's -- is what picks up the tail.
- Full repo suite: 1005 passed, 3 skipped, lint clean.
- Live end-to-end: reinstalled the global binary from this branch, ran a real CPU job on a live VM with a script engineered so its final print lands entirely in the gap window between the last poll tick and process exit (short sleep/wake script, default 15s poll interval). The final line and the runner's terminal status line both survived on disk after the fix; would have been lost before it.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Two things land together here: the **Unity Catalog governance + Lakebase control plane** implementation, and the **handoff package** (docs, plan, issue inventory, OpenSpec specs) so another agent can continue from this exact point.

### Implementation (`crates/lakeforge-api/src/uc/*`, `api/lakebase.rs`, `api/catalog_ext.rs`)

**One SQL choke point.** Every SQL surface (notebooks, jobs, SQL editor, statement API, 1.2 commands) now goes through:

```
AppState::execute_sql → prepare_sql(principal, sql, conf) → PreparedSql
   ├─ sqlguard::analyze      (sqlparser AST; text fallback when unparsable)
   ├─ authorize_sql          (reads/writes/DDL/system tables/external paths)
   ├─ grant_sql / metastore_op   GRANT | REVOKE | SHOW GRANTS | ALTER … OWNER TO | CREATE/DROP FUNCTION
   │                              → applied to UC docs, never sent to Forge
   └─ rewrite_sql            row filters, column masks, SQL-UDF inlining, current_user()/is_account_group_member()
→ Forge (gRPC) → query history + audit + observe_ddl + table/column lineage
```

- `uc/privileges.rs`: full UC privilege vocabulary, `Securable` hierarchy, ownership, `ALL_PRIVILEGES`, metastore→catalog→schema→object inheritance, `effective-permissions` with `inherited_from_*`. **UC grants are now enforced** on every UC REST route and every SQL statement (previously stored only).
- `uc/audit.rs`, `uc/lineage.rs`, `uc/system_tables.rs`: audit middleware (mutating + denied requests, secret redaction), query history, table/column lineage API, and a `system` catalog (`access.audit`, `access.*_lineage`, `query.history`, `compute.*`, `lakeflow.*`, `billing.list_prices`, `mlflow.*`, `serving.*`, `lakebase.*`, `information_schema.*`) materialised to Parquet and broadcast to running Forge clusters.
- `api/catalog_ext.rs`: tags, constraints, workspace bindings, temporary table credentials, artifact allowlists, system-schema enable/disable, row-filter/column-mask routes.
- `api/lakebase.rs`: Databricks `/api/2.0/database/*` shapes — instances (lifecycle, branching, roles), credentials, database catalogs (`CATALOG_DATABASE` UC catalogs), synced tables (UC mirrors with `data_source_format=POSTGRESQL`), database tables.

**Lakebase is metadata-only emulation.** `LAKEFORGE_LAKEBASE_POSTGRES_URL` unset → `backend=emulated`, DNS `*.lakebase.invalid`, credentials are 1-hour Lakeforge API tokens (not PG passwords), no data movement. Set → `backend=external` reports the host but does not yet provision roles/databases. `GET /api/2.0/lakeforge/lakebase/backend` discloses this; the README/parity docs say so explicitly.

**Bug fixed in this PR:** `main`/`main.default` and default grants were bootstrapped lazily only on catalog-browse routes, so a fresh workspace's first `CREATE TABLE` + `GET /tables?catalog_name=main&schema_name=default` returned `Schema 'main.default' does not exist`. `AppState::new` now calls `ensure_default_catalog()` at startup.

### Handoff package

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/handoff.md` | 15-minute orientation, exact start/smoke/gate commands, how to pick work |
| `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/development.md`, `docs/api-surface.md` | module map, governance pipeline, every REST route group, env vars |
| `docs/uc-lakebase-status.md`, `docs/parity.md` | honest Implemented / Partial / Emulated / Missing matrix |
| `docs/continuation-plan.md` | Waves 0–4 with dependencies, exit criteria, session-based estimates |
| `docs/issues.md` | **LF-001 … LF-028**, each with problem, evidence, scope, proposed implementation, acceptance criteria, tests, doc/parity implications |
| `openspec/` | `project.md`, `AGENTS.md`, 10 capability specs (`unity-catalog-{authorization,policies,audit-lineage,system-tables,models}`, `lakebase-{instances,credentials,catalogs,synced-tables,emulation}`), 2 change folders with `proposal.md` / `tasks.md` / spec deltas (`## ADDED / MODIFIED / REMOVED Requirements`) |

Known gap called out in the specs and LF-003: when `sqlparser` cannot parse a statement, `sqlguard::analyze_fallback` still privilege-checks extracted table names but **performs no policy rewrite**, so row filters/masks are skipped for that statement. The proposed fix (fail closed for policy-protected tables) is specified but not implemented.

### Verification

- `cargo test -p lakeforge-api …` 31 passed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean
- `pytest` 9 passed; `web` build OK, lint warnings pre-existing only
- `tests/smoke/platform-smoke.sh` **39/39**, `tests/smoke/uc-lakebase-smoke.sh` **50/50** on a fresh `.lakeforge/` and again on reused state (smoke `lib.sh` now skips TERMINATED clusters; `LF_DB` env selects the SQLite file for the plaintext-secret check)
- Not verified: real cloud provisioning, external PostgreSQL backend (not implemented), browser UI for new UC/Lakebase surfaces (no UI yet — LF-021/LF-022)

author: davenompozolo-blip
body:
Three things: the F-5 source report, the A3 closure, and now the **F-5 tape itself**.

---

# 1 · F-5 — the tape

`docs/F5_TAPE_BUILD_REPORT.md`. Three sprints cycling where the portfolio strip sits.

**Owner's decision applied (2026-09-16): Sprint 2 runs sector + index. EEM sits inside the index frame labelled as itself. No regional label anywhere on the tape.**

### Acceptance (F2 §5 clauses 6 and 7) — measured off the live DOM, not read off the source

| Clause | Measured |
|---|---|
| Three sprints | NAMES, GROUPS, SIGNALS — 10 / 12 / 12 items |
| Constant velocity | `linear`, 6,156 px → **111.9 s** = 55 px/s, derived from the **measured** width |
| Pause on hover / focus | hover **paused** → unhover **running**; focus **paused** → blur **running** |
| Keyboard | tab order from a cold page: **NAMES → GROUPS → SIGNALS →** out |
| `prefers-reduced-motion` | `animationName: none`, paged static list, pager **◀ 1 / 3 ▶** |
| Empty sprint skipped | holdings emptied → `["GROUPS","SIGNALS"]`; instruments emptied → `["NAMES","SIGNALS"]` — no padding |

Clause 7 ("prove they cannot diverge") is proven **structurally**, not by comparing a day's output: `nexusTapeCompute.js` imports `alignedWindow`/`buildSeries` and holds no ratio arithmetic, so the only num/den division in the repository remains the one in `nexusPairsCompute.js`. Sharing a *table* was never enough — two implementations of the same arithmetic drift.

### The framing is a column, not a map in the component

`market_instruments` had nothing able to express sector vs index: `asset_class` is `equity_etf` for XLE, SPY **and** EEM alike, and `proxies_for` is free text that parsing would misfile silently. So `tape_group` is a column — the rule `nexusPairsCompute.js` already states about pair-to-axis maps. A labelling change over existing rows: **no new series, no price backfill.**

**The fold is structural, not a carve-out for EEM.** A group with fewer than two legs gets no frame; its legs fold into the broad-market frame and the fold is recorded on the item and stated on the sprint. **Registering a second regional leg gives regional its own frame with no code change** — asserted by adding a second regional row to the test fixture, not by inspection.

**The ticker is the label for every leg**, not just EEM. XLE's own caveats say it is a large-cap-only slice "close to a two-stock series", so "Energy +2.17%" is the same overstatement one step smaller. `proxies_for` rides on the title.

### Three display defects the render caught and the build did not

1. `factor_axes.label` is a full sentence and swamped each item at ticker size (9,526 → 6,156 px). The token is now the axis key, with the sentence and `positive_means` on the title.
2. **The axis tag carried no loading sign.** RSP/SPY loads **−0.47** on concentration, so a bare `concentration` tag asserts the reverse of the loading — the misreading `nexusPairsCompute.js` warns about in its own header.
3. Sprint 2's frames were invisible, which made the EEM decision unreadable. A marker now sits at each boundary.

### One paged read of `market_prices`

`fetchPricesPaged` was local to the pair explorer; a second PostgREST pager is how the 1,000-row cap keeps returning. Extracted to `nexusMarketPrices.js`, explorer repointed, its suite unchanged.

### The gap, recorded rather than only avoided

Sprint 2 runs two frames because no regional coverage exists (§8 of the report). Closing it is an A0-style unit — register EFA/EWJ/FXI with caveats and inception, backfill, set `tape_group` — **never an aggregate computed from the book**, which is the F3 §2.1 substitution in the layer it would be easiest to reach for.

**263/263 tests pass. Build clean.** Render proven, network read not: rows read server-side and replayed by patching `window.fetch` for `/rest/v1/*`, with the real client, query builders and component running.

---

# 2 · F-5 source report

`docs/F5_TAPE_SOURCE_REPORT.md`. **Sprint 2 does have a source, and an independent one** — 19 active legs in `market_instruments`/`market_prices`, all current, priced by their own nightly loader rather than derived from the book. F3 §2.1's two-sprint contingency does not fire.

**Sprint 1 reads `nexus_holdings`, not `vw_nexus_holdings`** — the latter reads a matview that ran three positions behind the live book and its `daily_return_pct` has no staleness gate.

---

# 3 · A3 closed out

`docs/A3_CLOSURE_2026-09-16.md`. The re-run described as pending **was already done and is still writing nightly** (`v0.1-structural`, 17,706 rows, current to 2026-09-15).

**Result: 1 of 4 — report and hold.** The layer is not retired; that is the 0-of-4 branch and it did not fire.

**F-2 is dropped from the active register** on the ruling's §5/§7.4 — withheld on a standing decision, not blocked on a dependency.

Finding kept: `tariff_rebasing` fires **465 sessions** across four episodes, all 2003–2011, and is silent in both target windows — which also inverts F1 §3.1's evidential-weight sort. No action taken; retiring a seeded theme needs its own decision.

body:
`rd-n` §8 item 1 prescribed a power calculation **from the event arm's own dispersion, before any family is specified.** Applied to the series `rd-o` collected.

**It commits nothing** — no situation defined, no threshold chosen, no window designated. It measures the instrument, not the market.

## The prerequisite nobody could have inferred

KRX has three kinds of gap, measured on the real series:

| gap | count | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| **11 minutes** | **249** | the closing call auction, 15:20–15:29 — no continuous trade, so no bar |
| 17.5 hours | 186 | overnight |
| 65.5 hours | 46 | a weekend |
| 30–31 min | 9 | a late open (수능일, the year's first session) |

Within a session the series is clean — **99.998% of steps are exactly 60s.** Between sessions it is not, and neither is the close.

`stage2_event_study.forward_return` indexes **positionally**, because BTC 1m runs continuously and `open[i+1+h]` really is `h` minutes later. On KRX that is false **~490 times per symbol**, and it fails **silently** — producing entirely plausible returns that happen to span an overnight gap, which is the largest single move in an equity series.

> A KRX event study reusing the BTC machinery unchanged turns an intraday study into an overnight one **without changing a line of the write-up.**

`session_forward_return` keeps a pair only when entry and exit share a session label. It costs real sample — **37% of bars survive at h=240** against a 381-bar session — which is also why h=1440 is absent: a day-long horizon has no meaning inside one session.

This project already records gap-blindness as an open exposure on BTC, where it affects **two** signal positions in 3.66M bars. Same class of bug, three orders of magnitude more of it.

## The finding is a trade-off, not a number

| | BTC 1m, 12bp floor | KRX intraday, 30bp floor |
|---|---|---|
| events to resolve the floor | 1,099 – 15,585 | **27 – 878** (lower bound) |
| per-event effect demanded | 0.03σ – 0.12σ | **0.13σ – 0.75σ** |

`rd-l` §6 found the first half on BTC — *"a harsher cost floor makes the question cheaper to settle"* — and this attaches the second. **Cheap to settle, hard to satisfy.**

| h (min) | σ | effect/σ | n (lower bd) | n at 1.2× | n at 3.1× |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 40.9 | **0.73** | 27 | 39 | 263 |
| 15 | 66.7 | **0.45** | 73 | 105 | 702 |
| 60 | 122.7 | 0.24 | 247 | 356 | 2,376 |
| **240** | **231.3** | **0.13** | **878** | **1,264** | **8,438** |

h=5–15 demands 0.45σ–0.73σ — not a weak signal but a *different claim* from anything in the literature or this project's record. Cheap to test and almost certainly negative. **h=240 demands 0.13σ**, the size rd-b's framing calls detectable.

## Is h=240 reachable? Genuinely maybe — the first time that has been the answer

**2,493 symbol-sessions collected**, ten more every trading day, against a band of **1,264–8,438**.

The band is wide because the dispersion measured here is **unconditional** — a lower bound. rd-l §4.1 measured event returns at **1.2×–3.1×** unconditional (events are volatility bursts), which is **1.4×–9.6× in events**. Quoting the unconditional figure alone is the mistake that cost rd-l its first headline, and it is not repeated.

So the honest statement is that it **depends on a quantity nobody has measured yet** — the event dispersion for a *Korean* situation, where 1.2×–3.1× is borrowed from BTC.

Every prior arithmetic of this kind returned a number nobody could reach: 5,619 events, 49.8 more years, a detectable difference exceeding anything observed. This one returns *maybe*, and names exactly which measurement would settle it.

## What follows

1. **Any Korean family is specified at h ≥ 120, or not at all** — below that the required effect is implausible, and rd-l §8 item 2's policy half says such a family should not be run. Available *before* a specification exists, which is the point of computing it first.
2. **The first thing such a family must report is its own event dispersion.**
3. **The cross-section keeps growing** — BTC's window was fixed at 6.96 years; this one gains ten symbol-sessions a trading day. A count out of reach this quarter may not be next year.

Full suite **2,715 passed** (19 new).

author: fbumann
body:
> **Prompt:** "Continue" — the formulation annex, from "the annex is now unblocked and is the cheapest of the three".

> [!NOTE]
> The following content was generated by AI.

**The model page prints the spec with nothing bound; the dashboard prints the answer with no math beside it. The Annex page is the two joined.** Every declaration the archive holds, in the notation the symbols file declares, with what the archive says it cost underneath.

This is the artefact a reader outside the repository asks for — a regulatory annex, a client report, a paper appendix — and assembling it by hand is exactly how a formulation section drifts from the model it claims to describe.

<details><summary>What a section looks like</summary>

For `carbon` on the reference run:

> $\sum_{d \in \mathcal{D},\ h \in \mathcal{H},\ g \in \mathcal{G}} w_d \cdot e_g \cdot p_{d,h,g} \le E^{\max}$
>
> | rows | priced | largest shadow price |
> |---:|---:|---:|
> | 4 | 0 | 0.00 |

Zero on `base`, because the cap does not bind there. On `carbon_cap` the same equation reads `4 | 1 | 217.27` — which is the carbon price the pathway page leads with, and the one `clients/headline.sql` computes independently.

</details>

## `priced`, not `binding` — a test caught the difference

I wrote the column as **binding** and asserted every row of an equality constraint binds. It failed: `balance` has 288 rows and **86** with a non-zero dual.

That assertion was wrong, not the code. An equality binds everywhere by construction; its dual is still zero wherever moving the right-hand side would not move the objective — a fully-renewable hour at zero marginal cost. The column is now **priced**, the docstring says why, and the test asserts `0 < priced < rows`, which is the real economics: the price of meeting demand varies by hour. Calling it "binding" would have printed a true number under a label that hid the interesting thing.

## The boundary

`src/showcase/annex.py` imports no lpspec. The equations come from math-spec, which has no solver in it; the numbers come from the archived parquet; the join is by declaration name, the one key both sides share. It is added to `test_boundary.py`'s readers for that reason, along with the page loader.

That stitching is the argument in [`fluxopt/lpspec#1648`](https://github.com/fluxopt/lpspec/issues/1648): the typesetter renders a model, the result frames carry the answer, and holding one against the other is left to every caller that wants this page. This PR is that caller, written out.

## Verified

- `pytest` — 25 passed, 6 new plus 2 new boundary parameters.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`.
- `observable build` over seven pages; Annex is 51 kB.
- The built page rendered in Chromium: **10 KaTeX blocks, no raw TeX anywhere in the body.**

The objective row is asserted equal to `warehouse.records`, per period and in total, so no number on the page is transcribed.

## Not done: the PDF

I said CI could render a PDF through the `typst` PyPI binding. It cannot, without a cost I do not think is worth paying:

```
SchemaError: symbol table: written in latex, but this is a typst render
and nothing translates between notations — write a typst table.
```

`models/pathway.symbols.yaml` is a LaTeX table. A typst render needs a second table declaring the same symbols in typst, and two tables for one notation is precisely the copy that drifts. The alternatives are a TeX toolchain in CI, or printing the page from a headless browser — both heavier than the page itself.

**This is worth raising upstream**: a symbol table is bound to one notation, so a model documented in LaTeX cannot be rendered to typst at all without duplicating it. That belongs in the math-spec handoff rather than here.

## Deliberately not done

- **No scenario picker.** An annex is about one run; the page prints the first archive in the directory and names the command for any other. A picker would make it a dashboard, which the other pages already are.
- **No per-coordinate tables.** A constraint is one equation and thousands of rows, so each section carries the block's shape, not a row of it — the first of the three readings set out in lpspec#1648, and the one an annex wants.

author: yasyf
body:
## Context

Every kind cc-notes has models one thing an agent wrote down: a fact, a plan, a
procedure, a suspicion, a task. None of them models the many like units a long
drive is actually tracking — ninety open pull requests, a package per migration
wave, a stack per apply — where the state lives in some external system and the
agent's job is to keep a register of it current while remembering, per unit,
what only the agent knows.

Tonight a landing desk carrying ~90 concurrent pull requests hand-built that
register as a bash script writing a markdown table, because red and unrebased
PRs were going untracked. Spelled as tasks, the same register churns a hundred
entities every refresh. Spelled as a doc, it is a markdown table nothing can
query. Neither survives the thing that actually matters: a hold reason someone
typed by hand has to outlive the twenty-minute refresh that rewrites every
column the external system reports.

## Summary

Adds `ledger`, an eleventh entity kind. A ledger holds rows keyed by a string
the external system already owns, each carrying a flat map of string fields.
`ledger sync` writes a whole row set in one commit, merging each row's named
fields into the row already keyed by it, so a field the refresh does not name
keeps its value; `--prune` removes the rows the set omits. Thirteen MCP tools
and a `ledger` noun in the CLI cover the surface.

## Motivation

Field-wise merging is the whole point. It is what lets an operator's hold
reason and the head sha a triage pass last graded survive a refresh that only
re-reads what GitHub reports, and it is what lets a refresh lane and a triage
lane write the same row concurrently and converge on the union instead of
clobbering each other. Fields resolve last-write-wins one at a time, so two
replicas that touched different columns of one row agree without coordination.

`--prune` is how a unit that left the external system leaves the register, and
a pass that would change nothing writes nothing, so a twenty-minute cadence
does not append a commit per pass to a ledger nothing moved in.

## Details

`model.Ledger` carries `Rows []LedgerRow`, an advisory `Columns` display order,
and the same anchors, labels, comments, and active/archived lifecycle a runbook
has. Rows order by a fractional index (`model.PositionBetween`), so inserting
never renumbers neighbors, and each row is stamped with the actor and time of
its most recent write — which is what lets a reader see how long a row has been
parked.

Five ops carry it: `CreateLedger`, `SetColumns`, `UpsertRow`, `RemoveRow`, and
`SetLedgerStatus`. `UpsertRow` merges by default and replaces under `Replace`;
an upsert with no position leaves an existing row where it was. The folder
deep-copies a seeded checkpoint's rows, because `fold.History` re-folds
prefixes over one decoded chain and a shared field map would let one prefix
fold corrupt the next one's seed.

The notes client refuses a sync whose row set names one key twice, before it
writes anything, since the two rows would otherwise silently collapse. `--where
NAME=VALUE` narrows both `ledger show` and `ledger row list`. Ledgers project
read-only in the FUSE tree as a markdown table and rank in `relevant` and
`search` over their row keys and field values.

`model/position.go`'s error text and doc comments said "step position"; two
kinds order by it now, so they say "position".

Tests cover the fold semantics (merge, replace, position stability, the total
row order, concurrent field writes converging, checkpoint seed isolation), the
client (merge preserving unnamed fields, prune, the no-op sync, the duplicate
key refusal, archived gating), and the CLI end to end. Each was mutation-checked:
reverting the behavior reds its test.

One test-harness change rides along. `synthesizeArgs` in the MCP inventory test
could not fill an object-typed property or an array of objects, so a tool whose
handler decodes structured elements would have failed to decode and emitted no
argv — passing the vocabulary check vacuously. It now fills both, which is what
makes `ledger_sync` and `ledger_row_set` genuinely covered.

author: muhsin-k
body:
Incoming WhatsApp replies through Twilio lose their quoted-message context, leaving agents unable to tell which earlier message the customer means. This change displays the referenced message when it exists in the same conversation.

The Twilio callback now accepts `OriginalRepliedMessageSid` and passes it to the existing message reply resolver as `in_reply_to_external_id`.

### Things to know

- Applies to incoming quoted replies. Sending quoted replies through Twilio remains unchanged.
- Uses the existing same-conversation lookup; references to unavailable messages retain the existing unresolved-reply behavior.
- Previously received messages are not backfilled.

### How to reproduce

1. In a Twilio WhatsApp conversation, reply to an earlier message using WhatsApp's reply action.
2. Before this fix, Chatwoot displays the reply without the quoted message even when Twilio supplies its SID.

### How to test

1. Reply to a recent message in an existing Twilio WhatsApp conversation.
2. Confirm the incoming reply displays the original message in its quote preview.
3. Click the quote preview to navigate to the original message.

Locally verified by posting a mock Twilio webhook to the callback endpoint: the incoming message persisted both reply identifiers and displayed the original message in the conversation UI. Regression coverage checks that the controller forwards the quoted SID and the incoming-message service persists both reply identifiers. The focused Twilio suite passed with 52 examples and no failures; RuboCop and diff checks also passed.

The two pins to 0.9.0 (ephico2real2/cf2cnp v0.9.0: structured logging, the download's three answers — fork PR #6). poc1 upgraded to revision 4 with the same `chart-from-fork.sh develop` the lab runs; the pod on `ghcr.io/ephico2real2/cf2cnp:0.9.0`.

Measured on the live server: `GET /download/<never generated>` → 404 *No policy has been generated under this id…* with `refused reason=download_unknown`; a generate through the Gateway keeps Envoy's `x-request-id` into the log line; the operator's own Download-before-Generate, Generate (200) and Download (200) appear in order.

Noted, not fixed here: the observer fork's `Chart.lock` still pins the cf2cnp **subchart** at 0.7.0, whose Deployment does not know `logging.format`, so the 0.9.0 binary logs in text; bumping that dependency to 0.9.0 gives JSON.

Root cause of the "An error has occurred" toast, found today: Grafana opened over **http://** — `Origin: http://grafana.poc.local` is not in cf2cnp's allow-list (demo 33: `https://grafana.poc.local`), the preflight has no allow-origin, Chrome drops the POST (`net::ERR_FAILED`, reproduced with Playwright from the operator's exact URL). Fix in #14's plan: an http→https redirect on the Gateway, then the same-origin route.

author: alrayyes
body:
## Summary

- Adds a note to the README's Installation section: `@react-pdf/font` must
  be pinned to `4.0.11` via the *consumer's own* `overrides`/`resolutions`,
  not just by bumping `@washy-washy/pdf`.

## Why

`#109` pinned `@react-pdf/font` here via this package's own `overrides`,
but npm/Bun `overrides` declared in a dependency's `package.json` never
propagate to a downstream consumer's install — only the project that
declares them is bound. Confirmed live on `washy-washy-cli`: bumping to
`2.4.3` alone did not fix the compiled-binary crash there
(`#standard-fonts/Helvetica`); adding the same
`"@react-pdf/font": "4.0.11"` override to that repo's own `package.json`
did. See alrayyes/washy-washy-cli#234 for the fix and before/after
verification.

Without this note, the next consumer to bump past 2.4.2 has no reason to
suspect the version bump alone isn't the fix.

Closes #110

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run lint:md` / `lint:prose`
- [x] Full `bun run check` (pre-push hook): lint, build, typecheck,
      types-doc, 180 tests pass

author: tb-adbe
body:
## What

The `url-prompts` enrichment (cited / youtube / reddit analysis audits) now runs the **same shared Semrush entitlement check** the `domain-urls` source already uses, **before** minting an IMS token / doing the S2S login.

Previously url-prompts went straight to the IMS mint + S2S login for **any** brand and relied on a `401/403` to bail for non-entitled ones. Now a non-entitled (or inconclusive) brand skips the wasted auth round-trip entirely and returns an empty `Map`.

## Why

`domain-urls` (offsite-brand-presence) gates on entitlement before any Semrush call; `url-prompts` did not — the exact asymmetry flagged in the #2972 review. This closes it, keeping the "should we call Semrush at all?" decision in **one reusable check** shared across every offsite audit.

## How

- Reuses the existing `resolveSemrushEntitlement(context, { orgId, brandId })` primitive (the one `domain-urls` uses) — inserted right after brand resolution in `loadUrlPromptsFromSemrush`, before `getS2sSessionAuthorization`.
- It's a **local DB check** (serenity feature flag + Semrush workspace lookup via PostgREST / data-access), **not** a Semrush API call, with a 300 ms fail-closed budget. Adding it costs one DB round-trip, never a paid Semrush request.
- Non-entitled → skip, `reason=not_entitled`; inconclusive check → skip, `reason=entitlement_check_failed` (fails closed). Both return an empty `Map` (best-effort — enrichment never fails the audit).

## Behavior change

For a **non-entitled** brand running cited/youtube/reddit with enrichment on:
- **Before:** IMS mint → S2S login → 403 → `session_token_auth_failed` → empty.
- **After:** local entitlement check → skip → empty. No IMS mint, no login, no data call.

Entitled brands are unaffected (one extra local DB check, same as domain-urls).

## Testing

- `url-prompts-semrush.js` at 100% coverage. New tests: entitlement checked with the resolved org+brand; not-entitled and inconclusive both skip **without** minting a token or hitting the data call.
- Lint clean; affected suites green (223 passing). ADR 006 updated with the entitlement-gate section.

author: liviuciulinaru
body:
<!-- Create all pull requests in Draft. Automated checks must pass before making your pull request "Ready for review". See CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. -->

### 📝 Description

A Card holder with a good session lost it whenever `GET /v1/user` failed. The app signed them out
and asked for a whole OAuth login again, for what was often one timeout.

This is the first half of LIVE-36134. It changes the login machine and the error taxonomy only. The
panel that shows these errors is #22051, stacked on top.

**The cause.** The machine had one `error` state, and its entry published the signed-out flag. Every
failure landed there, so a card-data failure and a failed login were the same thing to everything
above the machine.

**The split.** `error` becomes two states.

| State | Publishes signed out | `RETRY` goes to | Reached by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authError` | yes | `preparingAttempt` | every OAuth failure |
| `userFetchError` | **no** | `fetchingUser` | a card fetch that is not a 401 |

`userFetchError` keeps the session. Its retry asks for the card again, and it never mints an
attempt, so a transient network error costs the holder nothing.

**Three answers, not one.** `fetchingUser.onError` now reads the error before it decides, in this
order:

1. **A finished session.** Clear the session and return to the login. The base query already asked
   `refreshCardSession` to renew, so a 401 here means finished, not stale.
2. **A stale request.** Return to the login in silence. A newer login or logout already won, and
   that session is not this one's to touch.
3. **Anything else.** `userFetchError`, with the session intact.

**`isUnauthorizedError` was too narrow.** It matched a plain `status === 401` only. RTK Query
reports the same finished session in three shapes, and two of them were falling through to branch 3.
The session then survived a 401, which is the opposite of the rule.

| Shape | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `{ status: 401 }` | a 401 |
| `{ status: "PARSING_ERROR", originalStatus: 401 }` | a 401 whose body does not parse |
| `{ status: "CUSTOM_ERROR", error: "Card session renew failed" }` | a renewal the port could not start |

`isStaleRequestError` is new. It matches `{ status: "CUSTOM_ERROR", error: "card_stale_request" }`,
which `@shared/api-services` returns when a newer session replaced the one the request carried. See
"Renewal" in the `@features/platform-card` README.

**The view model.** It treats both new states exactly as it treated `error`: the login action stays
pressable, and the intro sheet can still open. No behaviour moved into the view.

**The second commit.** `RETRY` on `userFetchError` clears the error kind as it leaves. Without that
the old message stayed on screen while the refetch ran.

**Tests.** `pay-card-auth` 259 pass. The machine suite gains cases for the two extra 401 shapes, the
stale request, a retry that loads the card without a new login, the cleared error kind, and the
signed-out flag that must stay unpublished. Both platforms typecheck.

**What this PR does not do.** The failure still renders as one red line under the login button.
#22051 replaces that with the panel from the design, and it carries the copy for each error kind.

### 🔗 Context

- **JIRA / GitHub issue**: [LIVE-36134](https://ledgerhq.atlassian.net/browse/LIVE-36134)
- **Stacked under**: #22051
- **Reference**: [`@features/platform-card` README](https://github.com/LedgerHQ/ledger-live/blob/develop/features/platform/card/README.md) — the renewal rule this PR reads against
- **ADR** (if any): —


[LIVE-36134]: https://ledgerhq.atlassian.net/browse/LIVE-36134?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

body:
### Motivation

- Stop ad-hoc, family-specific rules that let geometrically-equivalent Parallel and Perpendicular observations become simultaneous authoring authorities and cause unexpected preview/commit behavior.  
- Fix viewport-dependent candidate generation so panning cannot change which semantic references participate.  
- Make the product model explicit: raw detection (plural) → single direction authority → independent position/endpoint authority → presentation → minimal persistence.  
- Preserve existing H/V, Endpoint, Midpoint, Point-Reference, Ctrl override, and continuity invariants while removing overlapping policy layers.

### Description

- Introduced an explicit singular direction authority and rejected-redundant list on the snap channels so the resolver selects one non-axis relation to govern the authored ray and records why equivalent observations were rejected. (adds `directionAuthority` and `rejectedRedundantDirectionRelations` to the snap channels and related plumbing).  
- Normalized Parallel/Perpendicular candidates before authority selection and deterministically prefer `Parallel` when both describe the same unoriented ray; removed the previous start-incident-only Perpendicular suppression and the late persistence-time representative minimizer.  
- Made candidate generation document-semantic (use complete committed sketch) instead of viewport-culling X/Y and point-reference sources so identical document geometry yields invariant semantic candidates regardless of pan/zoom.  
- Simplified persistence to consume the already-selected authoring authority (persistence now records the selected authority rather than re-running an equivalent-demand minimizer).  
- Presentation now projects the selected authoring authority (presentation defensive projection), and diagnostics were expanded to report raw candidates, candidate roles, selected direction authority with reason, position authority with reason, rejected redundant relations, transient presentation selection, and persistent selection.  
- Files changed (key): `src/app/drawingSnapEngine.ts`, `src/app/drawingInference.ts`, `src/app/drawingGeometricDemand.ts`, `src/app/drawingLineTool.ts`, `src/app/drawingInferencePresentation.ts`, `src/app/DrawingWorkspace.tsx`, plus updated tests under `tests/` and docs `PROJECT_MASTER.md`, `PROJECT_HISTORY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Testing

- Build: `npm run build` completed successfully.  
- Unit/regression suites run: `test:drawing-line-authority`, `test:drawing-endpoint-direction-inference`, `test:drawing-inference-product-regressions`, `test:drawing-live-direction-coexistence`, and `test:drawing-parallel-marker`; all executed and passed in this environment.

author: jaysonsantos
body:
## Problem

Plex sends a late `media.stop` or `media.pause` after the `media.scrobble` that records the play.
The scrobbler wrote a new progress row for that event. The play had cleared the position, so the
row held 0%. The home page then showed the watched episode again in the "In progress" list, with
the state `paused` and 0%.

The webhook log of the report shows the sequence: `media.scrobble` -> `play` at 06:40, then
`media.stop` -> `progress` and `media.pause` -> `progress` at 06:43, all for the same episode.

## Change

- `Scrobbler::played_recently` reports a play of the same target inside the rewatch window.
  The play path and the position path share it.
- A position event (`media.play`, `media.pause`, `media.resume`, and a `media.stop` below the
  threshold) answers `already-watched` and writes nothing when that check is true.
- A stop at or above the threshold keeps the old answer, `duplicate-play`.
- `fmtDate` builds the stamp from the local values of the browser, not from `toISOString`. Every
  time in the UI now shows in the time zone of the browser. The show page compares air dates with
  the local day.

The rewatch window is 360 minutes by default. A rewatch inside that window shows no progress card.
This matches the play rule, which already counts those two plays as one.

## Test

`keeps_an_episode_watched_when_plex_stops_and_pauses_after_the_scrobble` replays the reported
sequence. It checks that no progress row comes back, that the play count stays 1, and that a play
event after 24 hours tracks progress again.

`prek run --all-files` passes (shellcheck, hadolint, and nixfmt skip: no nix in the shell, and no
files of those types change). `scripts/test-db.sh cargo test --workspace`, `pnpm test`, and
`pnpm build` pass.

## Note

PR #6 rewrites the same file with the `stale-event` rule. The two branches conflict in
`scrobble.rs`. Merge one, then rebase the other.

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [hugo](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo) | uses-with | minor | `0.162.1` → `0.166.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>gohugoio/hugo (hugo)</summary>

### [`v0.166.0`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/releases/tag/v0.166.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/compare/v0.165.0...v0.166.0)

This release is mostly about hardening and bug fixes, but there are some notable changes:

- [`.Render`](https://gohugo.io/methods/page/render/) now takes an optional context argument: `{{ .Render "view" $ctx }}`, mirroring the `partial` API. This makes it possible to pass e.g. a dict to a content view. See [#​15077](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15077).
- The [`return`](https://gohugo.io/functions/go-template/return/) keyword in templates has been reimplemented. It now works in any template (not just partials) and can be used anywhere, e.g. inside `if` or `range` blocks. See [#​15212](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15212).
- New [`resources.Publish`](https://gohugo.io/functions/resources/publish/) template function and [`IndexOf`](https://gohugo.io/methods/pages/indexof/) method on `Pages`.
- [`related`](https://gohugo.io/configuration/related-content/) config: new `tokenize` option for index values, and index creation is faster.
- Several [security](https://gohugo.io/configuration/security/) fixes; see the notes below.

#### Note

- tpl/transform: Bump fileCacheEntryVersion in transform.ToMath (note) [`8d88b8b`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/8d88b8b4) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​15267](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15267)
- resources/images: Bump formatVersionNumbers.PNG and fix version cache busting for images.Filter (note) [`d19e0a4`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/d19e0a4b) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​12536](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/12536) [#​12543](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/12543) [#​15266](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15266)
- warpc/js: Upgrade katex to 0.18.4 (note) [`ec52e63`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/ec52e638) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​15254](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15254)
- hexec: Fail on symlinks that escape the Node.js permission paths [`c05c012`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/c05c012a) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep)
- config/security: Deny text/org content by default [`e6abb9c`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/e6abb9c3) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep)
- config/security: Add http.proxyFromEnvironment and document the resolved address check [`6a2a955`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/6a2a955d) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​15301](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15301) [#​15302](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15302)
- deps: Upgrade github.com/gobwas/glob v0.2.3 => v1.0.0 [`efd2456`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/efd24562) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​15273](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15273)
- hugofs: Drop symlinked mount roots [`938c820`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/938c8206) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep)
- tpl: Improve the return keyword in templates [`8405b80`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/8405b802) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​15212](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15212)
- resources/page: Don't let a title's "/" split an auto-derived slug [`39507d5`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/39507d51) [@​ipince](https://redirect.github.com/ipince) [#​4092](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/4092) [#​3577](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/3577) [#​5571](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/5571) [#​4090](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/4090)

##### Glob patterns

The glob library used for e.g. module mounts (`includeFiles`, `excludeFiles`), `cascade` targets, `segments`, `deployment` matchers and `noVendor` has been upgraded to v1.0.0. This is a complete rewrite of the matching engine that fixes a long list of correctness bugs, but it also means that some patterns may behave differently:

- Malformed patterns (e.g. an unclosed `{`, an empty `[]` class) now fail with a syntax error instead of being silently accepted.
- `**` matches any sequence of characters including separators, but it is not the `**/` "globstar" of shells: `**/x` requires the literal `/` and does not match `x`, and `a/**/b` does not match `a/b`. Use `{**/,}x` if you need both.
- `\` is the escape character, so a literal backslash must be written as `\\`.

If a pattern that used to match no longer does (or vice versa), it was most likely relying on a bug in the old engine.

##### Security

- `text/org` content is now denied by default, as Org mode's export blocks and `@@html:...@@` snippets pass raw HTML through unescaped, making it the same XSS sink as `text/html`. Sites with Org content can opt back in via `security.allowContent`.
- Remote fetches (`resources.GetRemote` etc.) now validate the resolved address at dial time and reject loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT and similar ranges. This only applies under the default `security.http.urls` allowlist; if you have customized it, you have opted into your own hosts and the check stands down. Proxies from `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` hide the destination address from this check and are now ignored unless you set `security.http.proxyFromEnvironment = true`.
- Node.js tools (PostCSS, Tailwind CSS etc.) now fail before invocation if a symlink inside the project resolves outside the allowed read/write roots. If you have a legitimate link, add its target to `security.node.permissions.allowRead`.
- Mount roots that are themselves symlinks (e.g. `themes/mytheme/assets -> /somewhere/else`) are now dropped. This closes a gap in the `themes/` confinement; absolute mount `source` values are still allowed.

##### Other

- `{{ return <value> }}` outside a partial is now an error; it was previously silently ignored.
- A page without an explicit `slug` whose title contains a `/` (e.g. `Watch/listen to this`) now gets a single URL segment (`.../watch-listen-to-this/`) instead of a nested one (`.../watch/listen-to-this/`). Taxonomy and term pages are not affected.
- Hugo is now built with Go 1.27.

##### KaTeX

When upgrading to Hugo v0.166.0, sites using `transform.ToMath` with the `output` option set to `html` or `htmlAndMathml` must update the KaTeX stylesheet referenced in their template(s) to version 0.18.4 or higher. Using older CSS versions like 0.16.21 will cause certain mathematical or chemical expressions to render incorrectly.

Example update:

```diff
- <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.21/dist/katex.min.css">
+ <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.18.4/dist/katex.min.css">
```

See these examples:

- <https://gohugo.io/functions/transform/tomath/#step-3>
- <https://gohugo.io/render-hooks/passthrough/#example>

#### Bug fixes

- tpl/strings: Fix replaceRE with zero-width assertions [`ae07063`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/ae07063f) [@​youdie006](https://redirect.github.com/youdie006)
- common/hreflect: Fix the off-by-one in the float to int overflow guards [`5130d00`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/5130d000) [@​youdie006](https://redirect.github.com/youdie006)

body:
Suite des revues codex sur #628. **Les trois remarques étaient justes**, je les corrige ici, plus le déplacement demandé hors du fichier chargé à chaque session.

> Ne pas merger tout de suite — à relire.

## P2 — j'avais tiré la mauvaise conclusion

J'écrivais qu'un correctif multi-schémas *doit* être éclaté par pod propriétaire. C'est faux, et codex a raison de pointer `home/mcp.nix` : `postgres_staging_rw` tourne en `mcp_readwrite`, qui détient `pg_write_all_data` sur `trusk_staging` en mode `unrestricted`. Ce rôle écrit **tous** les schémas, donc un correctif multi-schémas y tient en **une seule transaction**.

J'ai inversé la hiérarchie : le rôle de maintenance est le **chemin par défaut**, et l'éclatement par pod — non atomique — n'est que le **repli** quand ce rôle *et* le VPN sont indisponibles. C'était précisément la situation du 16/09, ce qui explique que j'aie pris le repli pour la règle.

## P1 — la recette « staging sur 8899 » pointait toujours vers la prod

`proxy-up` dérive les quatre variables de `TRUSK_PROXY_PORT=8888`. Ouvrir le tunnel staging sur 8899 sans réexporter les variables laissait le `kubectl` suivant partir vers la prod, ou expirer. Export explicite des quatre casses ajouté — et surtout, la recommandation principale devient la plus simple : **fermer un tunnel avant d'ouvrir l'autre**, auquel cas les variables standard suffisent.

## P1 — l'assertion de cluster échouait en mode ouvert

```bash
kubectl --context "$CTX" get ns production >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "STOP"; exit 3; }
```

Un tunnel mort, des creds expirés, une erreur DNS ou TLS renvoient eux aussi non-zéro : le garde saute et le script continue **exactement comme si staging avait été vérifié**. Pour une assertion censée précéder une écriture destructive, c'est le pire mode de défaillance possible.

Remplacée par une fonction qui distingue « namespace absent » (`NotFound` → vraiment staging) de « impossible de demander » (tout le reste → abandon), et qui exige en plus la présence du namespace `staging`.

## Le déplacement

Le paragraphe PG et le blockquote sur la collision de ports quittent `trusk-CLAUDE.md` pour **`notes/staging-access-and-writes.md`**, avec une ligne de déclencheurs dans la table et deux pointeurs courts. Le fichier chargé à chaque session perd 25 lignes.

## Une édition locale embarquée

Le diff contient aussi une modification non versionnée qui traînait dans ton arbre de travail, sur la puce Staging/Tailscale : **deux `tailscaled` coexistent sur le Mac**, il faut interroger le socket du daemon work plutôt que de rebasculer de tailnet. Elle n'était commitée nulle part, je la sors de l'oubli — dis-moi si tu préfères que je l'isole.

Au passage, ça corrige ce que je t'ai raconté ce matin : je t'ai fait croire qu'il fallait te reconnecter à Tailscale, alors que le tailnet Trusk était bien là, sur l'autre socket.

## 의도

N5a — 네이티브 편집기에 **미니맵**을 세운다([시각 매핑 §6.1](docs/native-editor-visual-mapping.md), 계획 공격 뒤의 결정). 본문 오른쪽·세로 막대 왼쪽에 문서의 «모양»(줄 2px·글자 1px 의 색 블록 run)이 서고, 보이는 구간이 반투명 슬라이더로 덮이며, 클릭·드래그하면 그 줄이 화면 가운데 오게 굴러간다. 배치·수치는 VS Code 의 기본값(`side = right` · `size = proportional` · `scale = 1` · 폭 120px · 클릭 = 가운데)을 실측해 따랐다(MIT — 동작만).

계획 공격에서 결정한 것: **비례 스크롤**이라 프레임 비용이 문서 크기와 무관(스트립 창 ≈ 350 줄만 그리고 색도 그 창만 묻는다) — §3.0 이 미니맵을 큰 파일 축소 1단으로 둔 전제(전 문서 스팬 요구)가 사라져 그 단을 두지 않는다(문서 정정). 판의 가로 막대는 **누를 수 없으니 그리지 않는다**. 본문이 40 열보다 좁아지면 접힌다.

## 구현

- 변경한 책임 영역:
  - `chrome/components/editor_view/minimap.zig`(새, 순수): `widthPx`(설정 열 → px, 접힘 규칙 — **본문 열 수·히트 기하·보이는 열 수·Lab 이 전부 이 함수를 지난다**), `topLine`(비례), `stripRows`, `lineAtY`, `build`(run quad + 슬라이더; 저장소가 모자라면 잘릴 뿐 죽지 않는다).
  - `frame.build` — `minimap`/`minimap_px` 를 받아 본문 끝에 스트립을 그리고 세로 막대를 **그 오른쪽**에 세운다(막대 `content.w` 에 px 를 더한다). `diff_frame.buildSide` — `Side.minimap` 이 오면 폭을 먼저 떼고(`minimapPx`) 그 나머지에서 열 수·막대를 잰다. 단일 편집기만(비교·병합은 N5b).
  - 제품(`app_session/editor.zig`) — 설정 `editor.minimap`(기본 켬)·`editor.minimap-width`(기본 15 셀 ≈ 120px); 렌더·히트 기하·보이는 열 수가 같은 `minimapPxFor` 로 폭을 뺀다; 미니맵 창의 색은 본문과 **다른 저장소**(`editor_syntax.ColorBufs` 둘)로 만들고 `top` 기준으로 잘라 넘긴다; 렌더가 스트립 자리와 **그 프레임이 쓴 창**을 굳혀(`editor_minimap_rect/top/rows`) 클릭이 그것을 읽는다; 클릭·드래그는 막대 제스처 자리(`beginScrollbarGesture`)에서 잡아 `scrollbar_drag_target = .editor_minimap` 으로 이어진다 — caret 은 안 놓는다.
  - Lab 장면 `editor_minimap`(1200×720, TypeScript 픽스처) + 골든 `editor-minimap`; 판정자 `MM1~8`(컴포넌트)·`MMP1`(제품 경계 — 자리·폭·막대 위치·quad·클릭·드래그·비례·끄기·접힘·색 창·첫 프레임 클릭).
- 중요한 트레이드오프: 창(`top`)의 비례 분모는 **지난 프레임의 스크롤 상한**이라 한 프레임 늦을 수 있다 — 그 프레임의 색과 히트 기하는 같은 창을 쓰므로 어긋나지 않는다(첫 프레임은 창 0). 판이 자기 폭으로 조이지 않고 접힌다(40 열 규칙). 슬라이더는 늘 보인다(mouseover 판정 없음).
- 의도적으로 하지 않은 것: 비교 뷰·병합 Result 의 미니맵, overview 마커(검색·진단) 승격, 슬라이더 잡기·관성, `renderCharacters` 급 글자 모양 — N5b(§6.1 끝).

## 다이어그램

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  C["설정 editor.minimap · minimap-width"] --> P["minimapCols → diff_frame.minimapPx(inner_w, cell_w, cols) = minimap.widthPx"]
  P --> R["render: buildSide — body_w = rect.w − px → sideMetrics → total_cols"]
```

body:
# Description
Alternative implementation of #4880 that doesn't duplicate the stamp field, but rather introduces an enum for the different types of stamps we might find in a word. Instead of looking in a specific place (first leading bytes for Fermi, 25..31 for Metric), we search the timestamp in the entire word (either in seconds or ms representation), and replace its occurrence with the corresponding timestamp of the previous block

Note, that this could in theory cause issues if the timestamp randomly showed up in the word for other purposes than checking if the quote is stale. However, the upside is that it doesn't depend on per provider implementation details (which don't seem to be documented and subject to change). If we wanted to only search in specific locations, we could still add this "per provider specific logic" in the `stamp_fields` logic specifically.

# Context
Titan's propAMM venues (Fermi, Metric, ...) quote from pending next-block memory rather than from existing on-chain state. When we simulate settlements and verify quotes using pAMM liquidity, we use `state_overrides`, so a pAMM route simulates on-chain against the price the maker is proposing to offer in the next block.

Every venue publishes its quote into a global registry contract, one U256 storage slot per directed token pair (called `lane`). 
A lane's word holds undocumented proprietary data (depending on each propAMMs implementation detail), but most of them contain a freshness *stamp*: the timestamp of the block the quote is meant for. The venue's contract reverts unless the stamp matches the timestamp of the block the call runs in, so a quote can only be used in the block it was made for.

Our simulations run against the latest mined block, while the streamed quotes are stamped for the block after it. Applied as-is, the venue would see a stamp from the future and revert. So before overriding we *restamp* each lane for the simulated block's timestamp. Each venue uses its own format and decides how it packs price and stamp into its word. Fermi leads the word with four bytes of unix seconds; Metric keeps six bytes of unix milliseconds near the end (bytes 25..31), with sub-second precision. The logic so far only knew Fermi's layout, which is why Metric quotes were never restamped and are always failing quote verification.

# Changes
* Support ms timestamps in search
* Search for any bytes matching the quote timestamp, rather than looking in a specific location.

## How to test
Same added tests as in #4880
