`fix/umsh-qa-ux`에 쌓여 origin/main에 전혀 반영되지 않았던 27개 커밋을 main과 합칩니다. 두 계보가 56커밋만큼 병렬로 갈라져 있어 14개 파일이 충돌했습니다.

## 담긴 작업

| 슬라이스 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| T22 | 서비스 목록·초안 편집·버전 발행, 공지 버전 관리, 관리자 LNB 그룹화 |
| T22 (결제) | 천명사주 CTA → 체크아웃, 주문을 리포트 1건에 결속 |
| T23 | private 미디어 저장소 수명주기, 권리 근거, 인벤토리 |
| T24 | 콘텐츠 승인·예약 워크플로, 코퍼스·프롬프트 목록 |

## 충돌 14건 해소 방식

**결제 entitlement (가장 중요)** — main은 코퍼스 세대(lineage)를, task-022는 리포트별 주문 결속을 각각 추가했습니다. 둘 다 유지합니다. main의 지역 `orderUnlocks`는 버렸습니다: `!order.reportId → true` 분기가 바로 task-022가 고친 미결속 주문 재사용 경로입니다. 이제 `src/payment/entitlement.ts`가 유일한 판정 기준이고 테스트가 붙어 있습니다.

`findUnlockingOrder` 순서는 **정확 매칭 → 계보 → 레거시 미결속 폴백**입니다. 느슨한 폴백이 앞에 오면 미결속 주문을 현재 열람에 묶어버려, 계보로 정확히 짚었어야 할 지난 주문이 가려집니다. `refund-approval-precedence.test.ts`의 7번 테스트가 이 순서를 지킵니다.

**나머지**
- `findUnlockingOrder` / `resolvePaidAccess`가 `reportCreatedAt`과 `lineageId`를 별도 인자로 받습니다. 기존 호출부는 5번째 자리에 둘 중 하나씩을 넘기고 있었습니다.
- `admin-snapshot.ts`는 서로 다른 함수의 add/add 충돌 — 둘 다 보존.
- 관리자 셸: 공유 라우트(`/api/admin/v1/corpus`, `/prompts`, `/api/services`)는 main 구현 채택, 이 브랜치의 미디어·공지·예약 화면은 추가.
- `service-version-store.ts`는 두 초안 구현을 모두 담습니다. `stableJson`이 양쪽에 있었고 해시 결과가 달라(main 쪽은 undefined를 걸러냄) 합치지 않고 초안용을 `stableDraftJson`으로 분리했습니다 — 기존 체크섬이 깨지지 않습니다.
- `plan.md` / `status.md` / `tests.md` / integration 로그는 append-only 기록이라 양쪽 다 보존.

## 검증

```
npm test        1130/1130 pass, 0 fail (139 suites)
tsc --noEmit    0 errors
vercel-build    PASS (sitemap 19 URLs, FAQ 126)
```

## 리뷰어가 봐야 할 곳

1. `src/server/app.ts`의 `findUnlockingOrder` — 세 단계 순서가 의도대로인지
2. 공유 라우트에서 main 구현을 택하면서 이 브랜치의 프롬프트 파일 목록 패널과 `getPublicServiceDirectorySnapshot` 경로가 연결 해제됐습니다. 함수 자체는 남아 있으니, 되살릴지 지울지 결정 필요
3. `stableDraftJson` 분리가 맞는지 (합치면 기존 초안 체크섬이 전부 바뀝니다)

author: will-break-it
body:
This CPS describes a gap in how Cardano participants exchange time-sensitive messages off chain: stake pool incident alerts, pool announcements, governance updates and dApp notifications. Existing channels carry them, but no common standard combines publisher authentication against Cardano identities, integrity, and quantified resistance to targeted suppression.

It sets out four use cases and six goals, including resistance to targeted peer selection and practical per-node cost. Its open questions cover adversarial participation, delivery targets, topic populations, small topics, participation costs, and behaviour during a chain halt or fork. A proposed solution follows as a separate CIP pull request.

The statement comes out of a research workstream on trustworthy message dissemination for Cardano, including an analysis of SecureCyclon under a silent adversary and a use-case survey with population estimates to validate with operators. Both are linked from the References section.

[Rendered from this branch](https://github.com/cardano-scaling/CIPs/tree/cps-offchain-message-dissemination/CPS-%3F%3F%3F%3F) ([upstream version](https://github.com/input-output-hk/pubsub/blob/main/docs/cps/README.md))

author: thomasmichon
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #2776. After that fix, a bare anchor's activation scope (e.g.
odsp-web-harness on cloud1) no longer crashes on `repository-unavailable`
-- it correctly falls through to resolving its `requires_external_state_root`
declaration instead. But `_external_state_root` runs
`agent-worktrees state-root --json` with `cwd=root`, relying on cwd-based
project discovery (like git). A bare anchor checkout has none of the
markers walk-up discovery needs, so this call always failed there with
`unavailable` -- even though the repo is a perfectly well-known, registered
project. `companion-provider.py`'s `_active_environment` correctly treats an
uncertain external-state-root as fatal (an uncertain state must not silently
proceed) -- but that still crashed activation for every OTHER activation
scope resolved in the same request, permanently blocking the
`agent-index-service`/`-engine` companion group on cloud1.

## Fix

When cwd-based `state-root` discovery fails, reverse-lookup the calling
root's project name from `~/.agent-worktrees/repos.yaml` and retry once with
an explicit `--project <name>`, which resolves correctly regardless of
work-tree attachment.

## Testing

- Added `test_external_state_root_falls_back_to_project_flag_for_bare_repo`.
- `pytest plugins/agent-index/tests/test_effective_config.py` -- 31 passed.
- `pytest plugins/agent-index/tests/test_z_dispatch_companion.py` -- 31 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (missing `agent_index` module in this dev env), 1 skipped -- matches baseline.
- Manually verified on cloud1: `agent-worktrees state-root --json` from the bare anchor cwd fails with "Could not resolve a project"; the same command with `--project odsp-web-harness` succeeds and resolves `dotfiles` as the bound knowledge repo.
- Version bumped to `0.1.0-dev174`.

author: jiaqizho
body:
Azure input files only exposed Arrow’s regular random-access interface, so asynchronous callers had to fall back to the generic path even though the blocking Azure SDK operations could safely run on the filesystem’s IO executor. This made Azure behave differently from other providers that expose NonBlockingRandomAccessFile and prevented callers from selecting the optimized async read path at runtime.

Make the Azure input file implement NonBlockingRandomAccessFile and add asynchronous size lookup and range reads. Cached sizes return immediately, while uncached metadata requests and range downloads are submitted to the executor from the file’s IOContext. Submitted operations keep the input file alive until the blocking Azure SDK call finishes, and validation or submission failures are returned through completed Arrow futures.

Move Azure read metrics into the input file and return it directly from both OpenInputStream and OpenInputFile. This keeps read counts and byte totals unchanged while avoiding the existing metrics wrappers hiding the new runtime capability from dynamic_cast<NonBlockingRandomAccessFile*>.

author: itsjakubmazur
body:
Datová vrstva archivu: celá historie OKTAGONU od turnaje 1, ke čtení. UI (rozdělení po sezónách, sekce archivu) přijde zvlášť — do té doby je archiv v appce neviditelný, protože ho všechny výpisy filtrují pryč.

## Proč do `events`/`fights`, a ne vedle

Jinak nejde použít nic z toho, co appka kolem karty umí — plakát, `FightMatchup` s fotkami, výsledková část, statistiky. Postavit to vedle by znamenalo druhou, hloupější kopii půlky appky.

Cena je, že `events` od teď obsahuje dvě různé věci a **každý dotaz musí říct, kterou myslí**.

## Dvě nezávislé pojistky

Bodování je v bezpečí samo od sebe: žebříčky se odvozují od tipů a na `completed` galavečer nikdo tipovat nemůže (`predictions_insert_own`).

Nebezpečné jsou **notifikace**. `send_followup_notifications` vybírá podle `status <> draft` + `followup_notified_at is null` a každému profilu pošle push „galavečer je za námi" — devadesát archivních turnajů by znamenalo zhruba **devět set notifikací**. Proto:

1. **Filtr** `is_archive = false` na všech výčtových dotazech: 13 míst v `cron.py`, 5 v `/api/cron-tick`, plus seznam galavečerů, přepínač na žebříčku, sezónní statistiky, nemesis, startovné a admin přehled.
2. **Konstrukce** — importér archivnímu eventu rovnou vyplní *všechny* značky „už odesláno". I kdyby budoucí dotaz na filtr zapomněl, nezbude co poslat.

Druhá vrstva je tam proto, že spoléhat na „vypadne to samo podle stavu a data" je přesně ten předpoklad, co tady minulý týden skončil výpadkem.

## Detaily importu

- Karta se píše **rovnou s výsledky** — archivní galavečer je odehraný, psát ho jako `scheduled` a pak grade-ovat by byl zbytečný okruh přes živou výsledkovou cestu.
- **Plakát** z `coverImage` v `/v1/events/`; `import_image` scrapuje homepage a ta zná jen aktuální turnaje.
- `rounds` se u zápasu rozšíří, když skončil později (submise ve 4. kole nemůže být tříkolový zápas) — případ, co reálně existuje.
- Běží po dávkách přes workflow *Import archive*, celá historie se do jednoho běhu nevejde.

## Ověření

95 pytest testů, 7 nových. První z nich je ten nejdůležitější: **importér se nesmí dotknout galavečera, který je náš**. Dál: archivní event má vyplněné všechny notifikační značky, karta se ukládá s výsledky, opakovaný běh aktualizuje místo duplikace, budoucí turnaje se přeskakují a rozsah `--from/--to` opravdu omezuje.

Odhad velikosti: ~145 eventů, ~1 000 zápasů, ~900 bojovníků, ~2 000 řádků historie, ~450 statistik — **kolem 5 MB i s indexy**.

author: pgorbachev
body:
## Summary

Maven repositories inheriting this parent have **no quality gate at all**. The Gradle repositories get
Checkstyle, PMD, SpotBugs, coverage, detekt and ktlint from the `octopus-quality` convention plugin in
octopus-base; the eight Maven repositories get nothing, because that standard lives in a Gradle plugin and
cannot reach them.

This PR brings the Maven side to the **same rules and the same tool versions**, wired so that the gates
actually run in CI, and ships a fixture suite that proves they do.

Default is **report-only**: bumping the parent never turns a repository red. Each repository flips the
switch itself once it is clean.

Found while fixing octopusden/octopus-releng-lib#17 — a latent `equals`/`hashCode` defect in a repository
where no linter had ever run.

## What it adds

| Profile | Active when | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| `octopus-quality` | build JDK ≥ 11 | enforcer (`banDuplicatePomDependencyVersions`), Checkstyle 10.17.0, PMD 6.55.0, SpotBugs 4.9.8, JaCoCo report + line-coverage check |
| `octopus-kotlin-quality` | JDK ≥ 11 **and** the module has `src/main/kotlin` | detekt 1.23.8, ktlint 1.8.0; SpotBugs off for that module |
| `octopus-mutation` | `-Poctopus-mutation` only | PIT 1.30.0 |

- Rulesets are the files bundled in `gradle-quality-plugin`, pinned to an octopus-base tag, so a Maven and
  a Gradle repository judge code by identical rules. Engine versions match `gradle.properties`.
- Gates run at **`prepare-package`**, because the shared CI workflow invokes `mvn package`.
- `findbugs-maven-plugin` removed (dead since 2017, cannot read Java 9+ bytecode).
- `equalsverifier-nodep` added to `dependencyManagement`.
- README documents profiles, properties, report paths, known limitations and the rollout sequence.

**Nothing changes for a repository building on JDK 8** — five of eight consumers today. Bytecode target is
untouched (`maven.compiler.source/target` stay `1.8`). This PR does not pick a baseline JDK and does not
change the org's JVM policy; that decision stays open.

## The contract is tested

`mvn -Pit verify` (and `mvn -Pit package`, which is what CI runs) executes six fixtures in `src/it` as real
consumer projects. Each asserts one promise the README makes:

| Fixture | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `violation-detected` | report-only finds and reports violations without failing; the org ruleset and `includeTests=true` reach the **forked** analysis goals |
| `strict-fails` | `failOnViolation=true` fails the build |
| `skip-disables` | `octopus.quality.skip` in the consumer POM disables everything and writes no report |
| `consumer-gate-preserved` | a consumer's own PMD gate keeps its own failing semantics; the parent does not downgrade it |
| `pit-opt-in` | PIT does not execute without `-Poctopus-mutation` |
| `ratchet-allows-baseline` | strict mode with a frozen backlog passes while still reporting |
| `kotlin-gates` | ktlint scans `src/test/kotlin` with Kotlin declared only via `<sourceDirs>`; detekt reports; SpotBugs is off on a Kotlin module |

Every fixture was verified by **reintroducing its defect**, not merely by passing today. That pass found two
of them too weak and both were strengthened. CI log for the current head shows all six executing.

## Measured on two consumers (JDK 17, defaults — both builds green)

| Gate | `octopus-releng-lib` (Java + Kotlin) | `octopus-license-maven-plugin` (Java only) |
|---|---|---|
| Checkstyle | 1 | 17 |
| PMD | 1 | 13 |
| SpotBugs | — skipped (Kotlin module) | 57 |
| JaCoCo ≥ 0.10 line | pass | pass |
| detekt | 15 | — no Kotlin |
| ktlint | 166 (6 remain after `mvn initialize ktlint:format`) | — |

No consumer is clean, which is why report-only is the default.

## Why review took four rounds

Not one finding was about the rules. All nine were about wiring, and the worst would have made the whole PR
inert: every gate was bound to `verify` while CI runs `mvn package`, so `mvn package` ran **zero** analyzers
and wrote **zero** reports — the first execution would have landed inside the release job's `mvn deploy`.

The others, each reproduced before fixing: plugin-level configuration silently downgraded `octopus-wl-tool`'s
working ktlint/detekt gates to reports; `octopus.quality.skip` set in a consumer POM did nothing, because
Maven activates profiles from system properties only; `spotbugs:check` and `pmd:check` **fork** their analysis
goal and the fork ignored the execution's configuration, so PMD analysed with its **default** ruleset; a JDK
guard on `octopus-mutation` turned an opt-in profile into an automatic one; `overwrite` did not bypass the
download plugin's own cache; SpotBugs ran on Kotlin modules, which the Gradle plugin deliberately avoids.

The fixture suite exists because of this: the rules were never the problem, the contract of executing them was.
Two of the defects were in the harness itself.

## Deliberately not included

- **`DependencyConvergence` as a gate** — fails `license-maven-plugin` on dozens of transitive Maven/Plexus
  splits and would block adoption of everything else. Still available as `mvn enforcer:enforce`.
- **PMD 7 / `maven-pmd-plugin` 3.22+** — its report goal dies with `skin cannot be null` on projects carrying
  an old `src/site/site.xml`. 3.21.2 is the last PMD-6 line and matches the Gradle pin.
- **SpotBugs `effort=Max threshold=Low`** — the Gradle plugin leaves engine defaults; Max/Low was ~2× noisier
  with nothing extra of value.
- **An owner and a date per consumer for enabling strict mode.** The *mechanism* is now here: strict mode no
  longer requires a clean repository, because `octopus.quality.maxViolations.*` lets a repository turn
  `failOnViolation` on immediately and freeze its current counts, blocking new debt while the backlog is
  worked down. Never raise a number; reaching `0` is the clean state. What remains is organisational — who
  owns each repository's transition and by when — and that belongs in tracking, not in a POM: #5.
- **Report collection in CI** — `common-java-maven-build.yml` has no `upload-artifact` step. The follow-up is
  `common-java-maven-quality-gates.yml` in octopus-base, publishing the same `quality/static` /
  `quality/tests-coverage` check names as the Gradle workflow, so `merge-gate` and `jvm-strict` work for both
  build systems.

## How a repository gets to strict mode

```xml
<octopus.quality.failOnViolation>true</octopus.quality.failOnViolation>
<octopus.quality.maxViolations.checkstyle>17</octopus.quality.maxViolations.checkstyle>
<octopus.quality.maxViolations.pmd>13</octopus.quality.maxViolations.pmd>
<octopus.quality.maxViolations.spotbugs>57</octopus.quality.maxViolations.spotbugs>
```

Set each to the repository's current count, lower it as findings are fixed, never raise it. ktlint has no such
parameter and stays all-or-nothing — acceptable because `mvn initialize ktlint:format` clears nearly all of it
in one commit. Coverage keeps its own floor.

## Known limitations

- **The ruleset fetch is a network dependency at build time.** `download-maven-plugin` defaults `failOnError`
  to `true`, a CI runner always starts cold, and a missing `configLocation` is a *configuration* error that
  `failOnViolation=false` cannot absorb. So the accurate promise is narrower than "a parent bump never
  reddens a repository": **no finding** will, but the fetch can. Documented in the README, and #6 tracks
  moving the rulesets to a resolved artifact, which removes it entirely.

- A module running surefire **after** `prepare-package` (`octopus-artifactory-npm-maven-plugin` disables
  `default-test` and runs it at `verify`) has no `jacoco.exec` when the coverage gate runs, so JaCoCo skips —
  and a skip reads like a pass in the log. Documented; such a module moves its tests back to `test`.
- A consumer pinning `build-helper-maven-plugin` 3.5.0+ reintroduces a Maven 3.9.0 requirement above the
  `[3.6.3,)` this POM enforces. The parent pins 3.4.0.

## Rollout notes

Measured against all eight Maven consumers.

author: 3alpha
body:
## Summary

Opens up the `beacon-validator` proxy nginx config. It only ever serves the other containers on the internal DAppNode Docker network, so the stock nginx defaults provide no protection — they just cap legitimate traffic.

Also hoists the shared proxy directives into the `http` block. nginx inherits them into both servers/locations, which removes the duplicated 4-line `proxy_set_header` block from each of the three locations.

## Why

Problems the old defaults could cause:

- `client_max_body_size 1m` — rejects larger request bodies.
- `large_client_header_buffers 4 8k` — `/eth/v1/beacon/states/head/validators/<many-pubkeys>` URLs overflow the default buffers.
- `proxy_read_timeout 60s` — cuts off long reads.
- `proxy_buffering on` — spools responses instead of streaming, which is wrong for the SSE endpoint `/eth/v1/events`.

## Changes

| Directive | Value | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client_max_body_size` | `0` | unlimited request bodies |
| `client_body_buffer_size` | `1m` | avoid spilling to disk |
| `client_header_buffer_size` | `32k` | long validator query paths |
| `large_client_header_buffers` | `8 64k` | multi-pubkey queries |
| `client_body_timeout` / `client_header_timeout` / `send_timeout` | `1h` | slow local clients |
| `keepalive_timeout` / `keepalive_requests` | `1h` / `100000` | long-lived validator connections |
| `proxy_connect_timeout` | `60s` | upstream warm-up tolerance |
| `proxy_send_timeout` / `proxy_read_timeout` | `1h` | long stream reads |
| `proxy_buffering` / `proxy_request_buffering` | `off` | keeps `/eth/v1/events` SSE open, streams large responses |
| `proxy_max_temp_file_size` | `0` | never spool to temp files |
| `proxy_buffer_size` / `proxy_buffers` / `proxy_busy_buffers_size` | `32k` / `8 64k` / `128k` | large response header sets |
| `proxy_ignore_client_abort` | `on` | validator timeout on publish no longer kills the upstream request |
| `proxy_http_version` + `proxy_set_header Connection` | `1.1` / `""` | upstream keepalive instead of HTTP/1.0 default |
| `proxy_socket_keepalive` | `on` | keep upstream sockets alive |
| `tcp_nodelay` / `tcp_nopush` | `on` / `off` | low latency for a JSON API |
| `reset_timedout_connection` / `lingering_time` | `on` / `30s` | free sockets promptly |
| `server_tokens` | `off` | don't advertise the nginx version |
| `worker_processes` / `worker_connections` / `multi_accept` | `auto` / `8192` / `on` | many validators fanning out |
| `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host` / `X-Forwarded-Port` | `$host` / `$server_port` | full original request info to the backend |

## Testing

- [ ] `nginx -t` against the rendered config
- [ ] Validator client reaches the beacon chain through port 3500 as before
- [ ] Beacon API reachable on port 4500
- [ ] `/eth/v1/events` stream stays open past 60s
- [ ] Multi-pubkey `validators` query with a long requester URL succeeds

> Note: not yet validated locally with `nginx -t` — no Docker daemon was running on the authoring machine. All directives are valid in `http` context for the pinned `nginx:1.27.0-alpine`.

### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR enables standard implicit type coercion for the timestamp and origin arguments of
`time_bucket`. In ANSI and legacy modes, Spark casts `DATE` and `STRING` inputs to `TIMESTAMP`.
The bucket-size argument stays strict and accepts only the supported interval types.

The PR also adds coercion tests for both modes and updates the SQL query tests and generated
golden files.


### Why are the changes needed?

`time_bucket` declares timestamp input requirements, but the expression bypasses Spark's normal
implicit casting rules. It therefore rejects `DATE` and `STRING` values that Spark accepts for
other timestamp inputs.

This change makes `time_bucket` consistent with Spark's standard timestamp coercion behavior.


### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `time_bucket` now accepts `DATE` and `STRING` values for its timestamp and origin arguments.
For example:

```sql
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '15' MINUTE, DATE '2024-01-15');
-- 2024-01-15 00:00:00

SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '15' MINUTE, '2024-01-15 10:23:00');
-- 2024-01-15 10:15:00
```


### How was this patch tested?

The patch adds ANSI and legacy type-coercion tests. It also adds SQL query coverage for `DATE`
and `STRING` timestamp and origin arguments.

```bash
build/sbt 'catalyst/testOnly *TypeCoercionSuite -- -z "time_bucket"'
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly org.apache.spark.sql.SQLQueryTestSuite -- -z "time-bucket.sql"'
```

body:
## Summary
`georangesRefreshLoop` waits `georangesBootstrapDelay` (10s) instead of the full `georangesRefreshDelay` (90s) before its very first fetch specifically when `LoadCacheRaw` finds no cached table to load at all — true of every router the first time it runs a build with this feature (#198/v0.32.20+). `knownRangesRefreshDelay` is untouched.

## Why
Confirmed live: right after updating to v0.32.21, fresh Yandex (`158.160.132.99`, `213.180.193.9`, `77.88.55.88`) and Ozon (`185.73.193.68`, `185.73.194.82`) addresses showed up in `keenetic_xray_adaptive` despite the RU-exclusion veto (#198) already being in that release. Their timeouts (~20500–21300 out of a 21600s/6h max) point to having been confirmed shortly after the restart from that same update — consistent with `ExcludedRangeLookup` having nothing loaded yet during the full 90s pre-fetch delay, a window every fresh install/update hits once. Once confirmed, an address sits redirected for the rest of its ~6h OKTTL regardless of when the table finally loads.

`knownRangesRefreshDelay` deliberately keeps its 90s: a stale/missing known-ranges table there only produces a slightly-too-narrow block-promotion guess, not a legitimate domestic service getting wrongly tunneled, so it doesn't carry the same urgency, and there's no reason to touch an already-stable, hardware-verified feature for this.

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` clean
- [x] `go test ./...` full suite green
- [x] Cross-compiled `linux/arm64` and `linux/mipsle` (`GOMIPS=softfloat`)
- [ ] Hardware: next fresh update should show a much narrower (or absent) window before Russian addresses stop being individually confirmable

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>gohugoio/hugo (hugo)</summary>

### [`v0.166.0`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/releases/tag/v0.166.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/compare/v0.165.0...v0.166.0)

This release is mostly about hardening and bug fixes, but there are some notable changes:

- [`.Render`](https://gohugo.io/methods/page/render/) now takes an optional context argument: `{{ .Render "view" $ctx }}`, mirroring the `partial` API. This makes it possible to pass e.g. a dict to a content view. See [#​15077](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15077).
- The [`return`](https://gohugo.io/functions/go-template/return/) keyword in templates has been reimplemented. It now works in any template (not just partials) and can be used anywhere, e.g. inside `if` or `range` blocks. See [#​15212](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15212).
- New [`resources.Publish`](https://gohugo.io/functions/resources/publish/) template function and [`IndexOf`](https://gohugo.io/methods/pages/indexof/) method on `Pages`.
- [`related`](https://gohugo.io/configuration/related-content/) config: new `tokenize` option for index values, and index creation is faster.
- Several [security](https://gohugo.io/configuration/security/) fixes; see the notes below.

#### Note

- tpl/transform: Bump fileCacheEntryVersion in transform.ToMath (note) [`8d88b8b`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/8d88b8b4) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​15267](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15267)
- resources/images: Bump formatVersionNumbers.PNG and fix version cache busting for images.Filter (note) [`d19e0a4`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/d19e0a4b) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​12536](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/12536) [#​12543](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/12543) [#​15266](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15266)

- hexec: Fail on symlinks that escape the Node.js permission paths [`c05c012`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/c05c012a) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep)
- config/security: Deny text/org content by default [`e6abb9c`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/e6abb9c3) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep)
- config/security: Add http.proxyFromEnvironment and document the resolved address check [`6a2a955`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/6a2a955d) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​15301](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15301) [#​15302](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15302)
- deps: Upgrade github.com/gobwas/glob v0.2.3 => v1.0.0 [`efd2456`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/efd24562) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​15273](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15273)
- hugofs: Drop symlinked mount roots [`938c820`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/938c8206) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep)
- tpl: Improve the return keyword in templates [`8405b80`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/8405b802) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​15212](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15212)
- resources/page: Don't let a title's "/" split an auto-derived slug [`39507d5`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/39507d51) [@​ipince](https://redirect.github.com/ipince) [#​4092](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/4092) [#​3577](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/3577) [#​5571](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/5571) [#​4090](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/4090)

##### Glob patterns

The glob library used for e.g. module mounts (`includeFiles`, `excludeFiles`), `cascade` targets, `segments`, `deployment` matchers and `noVendor` has been upgraded to v1.0.0. This is a complete rewrite of the matching engine that fixes a long list of correctness bugs, but it also means that some patterns may behave differently:

- Malformed patterns (e.g. an unclosed `{`, an empty `[]` class) now fail with a syntax error instead of being silently accepted.
- `**` matches any sequence of characters including separators, but it is not the `**/` "globstar" of shells: `**/x` requires the literal `/` and does not match `x`, and `a/**/b` does not match `a/b`. Use `{**/,}x` if you need both.
- `\` is the escape character, so a literal backslash must be written as `\\`.

If a pattern that used to match no longer does (or vice versa), it was most likely relying on a bug in the old engine.

##### Security

- `text/org` content is now denied by default, as Org mode's export blocks and `@@html:...@@` snippets pass raw HTML through unescaped, making it the same XSS sink as `text/html`. Sites with Org content can opt back in via `security.allowContent`.
- Remote fetches (`resources.GetRemote` etc.) now validate the resolved address at dial time and reject loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT and similar ranges. This only applies under the default `security.http.urls` allowlist; if you have customized it, you have opted into your own hosts and the check stands down. Proxies from `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` hide the destination address from this check and are now ignored unless you set `security.http.proxyFromEnvironment = true`.
- Node.js tools (PostCSS, Tailwind CSS etc.) now fail before invocation if a symlink inside the project resolves outside the allowed read/write roots. If you have a legitimate link, add its target to `security.node.permissions.allowRead`.
- Mount roots that are themselves symlinks (e.g. `themes/mytheme/assets -> /somewhere/else`) are now dropped. This closes a gap in the `themes/` confinement; absolute mount `source` values are still allowed.

##### Other

- `{{ return <value> }}` outside a partial is now an error; it was previously silently ignored.
- A page without an explicit `slug` whose title contains a `/` (e.g. `Watch/listen to this`) now gets a single URL segment (`.../watch-listen-to-this/`) instead of a nested one (`.../watch/listen-to-this/`). Taxonomy and term pages are not affected.
- Hugo is now built with Go 1.27.

##### KaTeX

When upgrading to Hugo v0.166.0, sites using `transform.ToMath` with the `output` option set to `html` or `htmlAndMathml` must update the KaTeX stylesheet referenced in their template(s) to version 0.18.4 or higher. Using older CSS versions like 0.16.21 will cause certain mathematical or chemical expressions to render incorrectly.

Example update:

```diff
- <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.21/dist/katex.min.css">
+ <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.18.4/dist/katex.min.css">
```

See these examples:

- <https://gohugo.io/functions/transform/tomath/#step-3>
- <https://gohugo.io/render-hooks/passthrough/#example>

#### Bug fixes

- tpl/strings: Fix replaceRE with zero-width assertions [`ae07063`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/ae07063f) [@​youdie006](https://redirect.github.com/youdie006)
- common/hreflect: Fix the off-by-one in the float to int overflow guards [`5130d00`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/5130d000) [@​youdie006](https://redirect.github.com/youdie006)
- resources/images: Fix filters on transparent colors and paletted images [`7785668`](https://red

body:
### What was asked

The issue reported `"pgvector_configuration": null` being saved while the UI still showed the
value as selected, which disables the toolkit's indexing option, and asked that UI and backend
state stay consistent — the field should never be persisted as null while valid options exist.

Product's follow-up: a pgvector configuration should always be set. The selector should not be
clickable when the dropdown has a single item and the field is not empty; selecting only matters
when multiple configurations are available.

### What changed

- The Pgvector Configuration field can no longer be cleared. Switching between configurations is
  unchanged, as is the `credentials` section.
- The field is disabled when the project's only configuration is the one already selected. It
  stays open for an empty field, for a configuration that no longer exists, and when a create row
  is offered.
- The locked field keeps full contrast rather than rendering greyed out, and carries the required
  marker that no toolkit schema supplies.

Note: the required marker is presentational — Save is not gated on it, so a toolkit that reaches
the form with no configuration saved can still be saved without one.

Fixes EliteaAI/elitea_issues#6635

body:
## 变更概述

全链路移除 Discord 平台：`rust/aegis` 运行时 + `go/installer` 安装器 + `README.md`。

设计文档：`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-remove-discord-design.md`
实现计划：`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-16-remove-discord.md`

### Rust（aegis）

- 删除 `src/gateways/discord/{mod,adapter}.rs`、`src/main/discord.rs`
- 删除 `Platform::Discord`、`PlatformCapabilities::DISCORD`、`PlatformSelection.discord`
- 删除 `main/runtime.rs` 的 Discord 网关块与 `runtime::run` / `AppState::new` 的对应参数（签名分别收敛为 7 参）
- 删除 `EncryptedConfig` / `SetupInput` / `DecryptedConfig` 的 `discord_token`、`discord_admin_id`，以及 `run_setup` 的两个参数
- `cargo remove serenity poise`（`poise` 早无代码引用）；`Cargo.lock` −33 个包

### Go（installer）

- 交互式选择器由 4 平台降为 3 平台；`parsePlatformChoice` / `selectDeploymentPlatforms` / `platformSetupForChoice` / `servicePlatformForSetup` / `buildSetupPayload` 签名同步
- 删除交互式 Discord 配置段与 `discord_token` / `discord_admin_id` 的解析、payload 写入
- 三语 i18n 删除 17 个废弃键（175 → 158），新增 `install.discord_removed`

## 兼容性策略（本 PR 的核心）

现有部署可能带 `--discord` 服务单元或 `config.enc` 里的 discord 密文字段，**不能静默换平台**：

1. **`--discord` 硬失败** —— `resolve_platform_selection` 在读取任何其它 flag 之前返回错误，避免落到「无 flag → 自动探测」而连上 Telegram/Matrix。
2. **`config.enc` 字段直接删除** —— 依赖 `#[serde(default)]` 与**未启用** `deny_unknown_fields`，老配置仍可加载；该承诺由回归测试 `load_and_validate_ignores_legacy_discord_fields` 锁定（该测试同时守住「未来给 `EncryptedConfig` 加 `deny_unknown_fields` 会打断老部署升级」这一回归）。
3. **安装器四面硬失败** —— keyval 键、stdin-JSON 键、既有 systemd 单元含 `--discord`、平台编号 `"3"`，一律报 `install.discord_removed`。
4. **保留编号空洞** —— `platformSetupForChoice` 的 `"3"` 作为保留报错位（`"4"`=tg+matrix、`"5"`=simplex 不动），使未修改的旧脚本**明确失败**而不是静默变成 SimpleX。
5. **恢复路径错误不再被吞** —— `installAegis` 原先 `platform, _, _ = recoveryPlatformForService(...)` 会丢弃错误，现改为 `printRed(err.Error())`。

## 验证

```
Rust  cargo fmt ✅  clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings ✅
      nextest --cargo-profile fast-test → 889 passed / 1 skipped ✅  cargo test --doc ✅
Go    gofmt -l 空 ✅  go vet ✅  go test -count=1 ./... ✅  staticcheck ✅

验收  被删符号引用 grep 空（SNI 词表除外）✅     cargo tree 无 serenity/poise ✅
      README 无 Discord ✅                      三语各 158 键，仅剩 install.discord_removed ✅
      docs/ 历史文档零改动 ✅                    工作树干净 ✅
```

测试清单变化均有据可查：Rust 仅删随代码消失的 discord 测试（`#[test]` 计数 866 → 857），Go 测试函数 46 → 47（+1 新增 `TestDiscordPlatformIsRejected`、2 个改名、零静默删除）。

审查过程：每个任务独立子代理实现 + 独立「规格合规 / 代码质量」双判（6/6 Approved，0 Critical、0 Important），终审 whole-branch 判定 Ready to merge，1 轮 fix wave + 1 次 scoped re-review（3/3 ADDRESSED）。

## 非目标

- 不改版本号 / CHANGELOG（发布节奏另行决定）
- 不改写历史文档（`docs/2026-09-16-simplex-platform.md`、`docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/2026-09-16-simplex-platform*.md` 中的 Discord 引用是当时事实）
- 不动 `src/resources/sni/*.pb`（域名词表）
- 文本模式 `firstTimeSetup` 仍可能显示未本地化的内部英文串（`invalid platform`、`platform selection cancelled`），来自既有 default 分支，非本次范围

author: firepinn
body:
`device_registry.async_get_or_create` deprecates `via_device`, logging a warning per device class per start (37 of them here) and dropping support in Home Assistant 2027.8.0.

The replacement is not a rename: `via_device` took the controller's identifiers, `via_device_id` takes its device registry id, and that can only be resolved with `hass` in hand, which entities do not have when they build their device_info. So platforms resolve it during setup via `async_get_hub` and pass a small handle instead of the bare identifiers tuple. Resolving it there also guarantees the controller device exists before anything points at it, rather than relying on `via_device` to create a placeholder.

The identifiers themselves are untouched, so no device is re-identified and no migration is needed.

`via_device_id` landed in Home Assistant 2026.8.0, so hacs.json moves up from 2026.7.0. That is not optional: on 2026.7.x the key reaches `async_get_or_create` as an unexpected keyword and raises TypeError, which entity_platform does not catch, so every entity on every platform would fail to add.

author: rkum113
body:
* Stopped resolving callers by the PII claims in their token

Identity lookups now key on the JWT subject, which user_table.uuid is overwritten with at Keycloak provisioning, so the name/email/phone claims can be dropped from the token without 401ing anyone. The legacy email/phone lookups stay as a fallback for rows whose uuid predates provisioning.

This is the deploy-first half of removing those claims: it is a no-op while the Keycloak protocol mappers still emit them, and must be live everywhere before the mappers are removed.

* Gave tenant-less admins a name in the auth response

An admin's name lives only in Keycloak — tenant_admin_user_master_table has no name column — and the auth response only looked it up in the tenant user table. Admins on no tenant, and any whose email has no tenant row, came back with a null name.

That was masked while the frontend read the name out of the token, so it surfaces as soon as the PII claims come off. The Keycloak lookup that /users/me already does is now shared and used as the fallback.

* **Improvements**
  * Improved authentication reliability by prioritizing the account identity associated with the sign-in token, with fallback support for legacy account records.

  * Admin names now display correctly in refreshed authentication responses, including for administrators without tenant assignments.
* **Tests**

author: smiggleworth
body:
## Type

Enhancement

## Linked issue

Related to #8 and #29.

## Summary

- require retained operational manifests to identify CPU, memory, filesystem, and disk capacity
- capture those fields from the hosted operational-readiness runner
- document that host identity enables comparison but does not establish a production SLA

## User/operator impact

Operators can compare retained same-profile evidence against the actual host resources that produced it instead of relying on an underspecified runner label.

## Current and expected behavior

Previously, an operational manifest could pass validation without enough host resource context to distinguish materially different machines. After this change, manifests fail closed unless CPU model, online core count, total memory, filesystem type, and evidence-volume total and available bytes are present and valid.

## Scope

This PR changes the operational evidence workflow and manifest contract. It does not define production thresholds, make an SLA claim, or complete the repeated final-candidate evidence required by #8 and #29.

## Evidence and support status

Red: `should_reject_operational_manifest_without_complete_host_resources` initially failed because the validator accepted a manifest with `memory_total_bytes` removed.

Green: the validator now rejects incomplete or invalid host resources, and the workflow captures every required field. Support remains Production Candidate pending retained repeated same-profile evidence and threshold review.

## Validation

- `cargo build --locked --bin cassie` — passed
- `cargo test --locked` — passed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings -D clippy::pedantic` — passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed after one mechanical formatting correction
- `cntryl-tools validate-tests -f tests/bench_operations.rs` — 241/241 passed

- `cntryl-tools validate-benchmarks --config .cntryl/repository.toml` — passed
- `cntryl-tools check-module-sizes --config .cntryl/repository.toml` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed

No performance benchmark workload was run because this slice changes evidence identity and validation, not runtime performance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Operational manifests fail closed without complete host resource context.
- [x] Hosted operational evidence records all required host fields.
- [x] Disk availability cannot exceed disk capacity.
- [x] Documentation distinguishes evidence context from production thresholds and SLAs.

Ready for review. Issues #8 and #29 remain open for final threshold decisions and retained repeated same-profile release-candidate evidence.

author: mubizero
body:
## Зачем

Игрок отошёл — раньше у оператора было два плохих варианта: платить за пустое место или закрыть сессию и потерять место. Теперь есть пауза: ПК запирается, время перестаёт капать, место держится за игроком.

## Что внутри

**Арифметика в одном месте.** `SessionPause` — единственный источник правды про «сколько времени реально отыграно». Её читают все три места, где считается время: чекаут (`SessionBillingService`), живая сумма и остаток на карте зала (`EfFloorMapReadService`) и автозащита по кредитному лимиту. Вычти паузу только в одном из них — и получишь ложь в деньгах; поэтому источник один.

**Фиксированная сессия не сгорает.** При снятии паузы `EndsAtUtc` уезжает вперёд ровно на простой — оплаченные часы остаются оплаченными.

**Пауза не бесконечная.** Филиал задаёт предел (`Branch.MaxSessionPauseMinutes`, по умолчанию 20 минут), после него `AutoProtectionRunner` сам закрывает сессию. Иначе брошенная пауза держала бы место занятым молча. В журнале такое закрытие подписано автоматикой (`SystemActorIds.AutoProtection`), а не оператором, открывшим смену, — это было бы враньём.

**API:** `POST /sessions/{id}/pause` и `/resume` под правом `organization.sessions.pause`, с идемпотентностью и проверкой версии как у остальных команд сессии. Уведомления по SignalR: `Paused` / `Resumed`.

**Оператор:** в контекст-меню места — одна кнопка в двух состояниях (ставить паузу на паузе нечего), на плитке — подпись «на паузе», чтобы пауза не выглядела обычной игрой.

## Проверки

- `dotnet test tests/AFK4.Platform.Api.Tests` — 2826 прошло, 46 пропущено
- `bun test` (Organization Admin) — 1277 прошло, 1 падение — известное, не от этой ветки: `supportShell.test.tsx` течёт через `mock.module` только в полном локальном прогоне, на CI зелёный
- `bun test` (i18n-гейты), `bun run lint`, `dotnet build AFK4.sln` — чисто
- Денежный тест на чекауте проверен мутацией: замена `SessionPause.BillableElapsed` на голое `now - startedAtUtc` роняет его (1500 против 2250), возврат — снова зелёный

author: jnagare-redhat
body:
## Problem Statement
The existing `get_vulnerabilities()` method loads all vulnerabilities across all pages, which causes performance issues and timeouts when a host has many CVEs spread across multiple pages (100+ CVEs).

## Solution
This PR adds a new `get_cve()` method to `NewHostEntity` that:
- Searches for a specific CVE using the vulnerability search bar
- Only loads the filtered results (typically one row for exact match)
- Handles the "no CVEs found" case gracefully
- Returns exact CVE matches without pagination overhead

## Benefits
- **Performance**: Avoids loading hundreds of CVE records across multiple pages
- **Reliability**: Prevents timeouts in tests when hosts have many vulnerabilities
- **Precision**: Uses search filtering for exact CVE lookup
- **Reusability**: Can be used in any test that needs to verify specific CVEs

## Usage Example
```python
# Old way (loads all CVEs across all pages)
vulnerabilities = session.host_new.get_vulnerabilities(hostname)
assert any('CVE-2018-10896' in vuln.get('CVE ID') for vuln in vulnerabilities)

# New way (searches for specific CVE only)
vulnerabilities = session.host_new.get_cve(hostname, 'CVE-2018-10896')
assert len(vulnerabilities) > 0
assert vulnerabilities[0].get('CVE ID') == 'CVE-2018-10896'
```

    that contract documents every other marker (`root`, `exclude`, `ignore`,
    `noindex`) while omitting this one. Across all history the string appears in
    exactly one commit's code plus an archived audit report; no layout, reference
    theme, fixture, or test ever emitted it. Dead scaffolding, so the override is
    removed rather than documented.
  - The contract never stated how `title` resolves at all, so the rule is now
    written down: normalized text of the first `h1` inside the extraction root,
    then the first `<title>`, then the page `path`.
  - The regression test is pinned to the *valued* attribute form. The removed
    branch read the attribute through `attrValue`, which returns null for a
    valueless attribute, so a bare `data-boris-search-title` was inert even
    before this change — an earlier draft of the test used the bare form and
    passed against the broken code.
- **Known Gaps**:
  - The title rule is not reachable black-box: the compiler CLI exposes no search
    flag (the producer ships through the standalone `tools/search-index` CLI), so
    the record in the contract is guarded by the unit test rather than an
    end-to-end check.

  1. `zig build test`
  2. `zig test src/search_index.zig`
  3. `zig fmt --check build.zig`

body:
## Summary

- Adds a second Western Cape Medfly pipeline (`v2`) trained on **real trap-count data** instead of the GBIF-occurrence proxy the v1 classifier uses. Ghian du Toit (industry contact) shared weekly FTD (flies/trap/day) for five regions — Warm Bokkeveld, Wolseley, Tulbagh, Elgin & Grabouw, Vyeboom — spanning 2010–2026, ~3,500 region-week records vs. the 45 GBIF points v1 had to work with.
- v2 is an **XGBoost regressor** predicting FTD directly, not a binary classifier — a stronger fit now that real ground-truth counts exist instead of a presence-only proxy. Risk thresholds (LOW/MODERATE/HIGH) are derived from the 35th/65th percentile of observed FTD, clearly labeled as data-driven rather than an entomological standard.
- The **v1 classifier is untouched** — kept as a deliberate baseline for the comparative study to follow.
- Adds `railway_app/`, a small FastAPI service (`/health`, `/pipeline/run`, `/forecast`, `/forecast/chart`) that runs geocoding → historical weather fetch → merge → train → live forecast server-side on Railway, since this pipeline needs outbound internet access to Open-Meteo that isn't available in every dev environment.

## What's not in this PR

- The source `.xlsx` from Ghian isn't committed (kept local — it's a private data share). Its parsed long-format output (`wc_trap_ftd_long.csv`) is committed, so the rest of the pipeline doesn't depend on the original file.
- Training hasn't actually run yet — this sandbox is blocked from reaching Open-Meteo by network policy, so `/pipeline/run` needs to execute on Railway (or another environment with outbound internet) before there's a trained model to evaluate.
- The comparative study vs. the California model is a follow-up once the v2 model has real trained metrics to compare.

## Test plan

- [x] All new Python files syntax-checked (`py_compile`)

author: amarcher
body:
Closes #41

Findings: [`docs/voice-agent-knowledge-base-spike.md`](docs/voice-agent-knowledge-base-spike.md). Reproduction scripts: `scripts/kb-spike/`. No app or agent config changes.

## Answers

1. **Latency:** automatic RAG retrieval takes 127–187 ms per turn, with no measurable change in time to first token. Tool mode's retrieval takes 40–60 ms, but the extra LLM round trip stretches knowledge-backed answers to ~6–7.5 s (vs ~2–3.5 s). Measured in text-only sessions; still needs a voice test on a phone.
2. **Shape:** one document per element. Each indexes as a single chunk, and the right element is the only content in the top chunk 10/12 times, vs 0/12 for one combined document.
3. **CLI:** document references and RAG settings already live in the agent config and ship via `agents push`. Document contents need a small sync script (`PATCH` with `content` keeps IDs stable and re-indexes automatically).
4. **Cost:** no separate RAG fee, only LLM input tokens. With default limits every turn retrieves the whole corpus. Tool mode adds ~$0.007 per knowledge-backed question.
5. **Element context:** **not with automatic RAG.** Its query rewriter never sees `[ELEMENT CLICK]` updates, and asking it to use them made it invent some. **Yes with `knowledge_base` tool mode plus a prompt rule:** it read the correct document 4/4 times.

**Recommendation:** tool mode, one document per element named like `117-Ts`, a prompt rule, and a sync script. Rewrite the corpus for the agent first, because it's currently a video production spec.

author: barbuz
body:
Fixes two hint-generation bugs reported from a real game (target **Gurmag Nightwatch**, guesses Chromanticore, The Gitrog Monster, Norman Osborn // Green Goblin).

Both have the same shape: a multi-faced card's card-level fields — which Scryfall stores as `//`-concatenated face data — were treated as a single value.

## 1. `c=bg` over-constrained the color filter

The hint URL contained `colors="bg"`, so it excluded the target's blue and never excluded R/W.

- `The Gitrog Monster` (B,G) has a *fully matched* colors row against the B,G,U target, because a colors row is correct whenever every guessed color is on the target.
- `gatherHints()` treated that as pinning the target's exact color set and emitted a `colorSet` hint → `c=bg`.
- A "fully matched property" rule then discarded the `-c:r`/`-c:w` negations learned from Chromanticore (WUBRG).

But a correct colors row only proves the guessed colors are a **subset** of the target's, never equality. `c=` therefore over-constrains. Colors now always emit `c:` contains hints (positive and negated), colors survive past a fully-matched colors row, and the `colorSet` kind plus its `c=` clause are removed.

## 2. Filter values of `//` (and `—`)

The URL contained clauses like `-t:"//"` and `tou=//`.

- `typeTokens()` parsed a multi-faced card's card-level `type_line` (`"A // B"`) as one line, inventing `//` and `—` tokens that then became type hints.
- The positional P/T hint logic (`i === 0 ? power : toughness`) read the `//` separator segment as a toughness value.

Type tokens are now collected face-level only, mirroring what `manaCostTokens()` already did. The `pt` hint walks segments structurally (`sep` starts a new face back at power, `slash` switches to toughness), so real stats are preserved per face while separators are ignored.

## Verification

Reproducing the reported game now produces:

```
mv!=5 c:b c:g c:u -c:r -c:w t:creature -t:enchantment -t:manticore -r:mythic \
-t:legendary -t:frog -t:horror date>2016-04-08 mv!=2 t:human -t:scientist \
-t:villain -t:goblin pow=3 tou=3 -layout:modal_dfc date<2025-09-23 f:v not:reprint
```

which returns exactly one card: `Gurmag Nightwatch`. No `//`, `—`, `c=`, or `tou=//` clause remains.

## Tests

- Updated existing expectations that had encoded the buggy behavior.
- Added a regression reproducing the exact reported game (asserts `c:b`/`c:g`/`c:u`, `-c:r`/`-c:w`, and no `c=`).
- Added a regression asserting no hint ever carries `//`/`—`/`/` as a value while per-face P/T values survive.
- `npm test` → 110 passed. `npm run build` succeeds.

Also bumps `APP_VERSION` to `0.11.7` and updates the hint notes in `AGENTS.md`.

author: dimartz-tech
body:
> Reemplaza a #38, que GitHub cerró automáticamente al eliminarse su rama base al fusionar #37. Mismo contenido, verificado sin conflictos contra `main`.

## Por qué no existía

Un abono a tarjeta mueve hasta cuatro cosas a la vez: reduce la deuda, debita la cuenta que lo paga, anota la comisión del 0.20 % como gasto, y se registra a sí mismo.

Pero el registro guardaba solo **cuatro datos**: tarjeta, fecha, importe y divisa. De qué cuenta salió el dinero, a qué tasa se convirtió y qué gasto recogió la comisión quedaban fuera.

Por eso no había reversión: no era que faltara el botón, es que **no había forma de saber qué deshacer**.

## Migración 5 — el vínculo

`pagos_tarjeta` gana `cuenta_ahorro_id`, `tasa_cambio` y `gasto_comision_id`.

**Los abonos anteriores se vinculan con una reconstrucción exacta, no con una heurística.** La comisión es el 0.20 % del importe ya convertido, así que conociendo la tasa se reconstruye el céntimo. Un emparejamiento por importe sí habría sido ambiguo — lo comprobé antes de escribirlo, y varias comisiones encajaban con más de un abono.

La migración **verifica que ninguna comisión quedó atada a dos abonos y falla si no puede garantizarlo**. Sin esa comprobación, el emparejamiento sería una operación que se da por buena porque no falló, y revertir un abono dejaría al otro apuntando a una fila borrada.

La tasa vivía dentro del texto de la descripción de la comisión — el mismo defecto que se corrigió en los gastos (**H9**). Se lee **una sola vez**, para rellenar la columna, y nunca más.

Un abono pagado sin cuenta no encuentra pareja y conserva sus columnas nulas. Es lo correcto: no hubo movimiento de cuenta que deshacer.

## El caso de uso

Aplica el inverso de cada efecto, en el mismo orden en que se aplicaron. La comisión se borra **antes** que el abono, para no dejar un gasto huérfano si algo fallara.

**Sin recorte en ninguno de los dos extremos.** Si el abono había dejado saldo a favor, deshacerlo lo devuelve exactamente a cero; si repone la deuda por encima del límite, ese es el estado verdadero. Misma resolución que cerró H5 y H10.

Lo devuelto a la cuenta **se recalcula** en vez de leerse del gasto de comisión: el cálculo es el mismo que al registrar —una sola política de redondeo para el 0.20 % en todo el sistema— y así la reversión no depende de que ese gasto siga existiendo ni de que su importe no se haya tocado a mano.

## Interfaz

Cada tarjeta despliega sus abonos registrados, con un botón para deshacer uno. Los abonos se cargan al abrir el desplegable y no al pintar la vista: son un histórico que casi nunca se mira, y traerlos para todas las tarjetas a la vez sería pagar siempre por lo que se usa de vez en cuando.

La confirmación **enumera los tres efectos**, porque un abono no es una fila. Un abono sin cuenta se rotula como tal, para no dejar esperando una devolución que no va a llegar.

## Verificación

328 pruebas en verde.

Cinco de caracterización recorren el camino entero hasta SQLite, incluido **el caso que motivó todo esto**: un abono mayor que la deuda, que con el recorte antiguo sacaba el dinero de la cuenta sin que llegara a la tarjeta.

| Mutación | Resultado |
|---|---|
| La devolución olvida la comisión | fallan 5 pruebas |

El flujo de la interfaz se verificó en el navegador con datos sintéticos: el desplegable abre y cierra, la tasa se muestra solo cuando hubo conversión, un abono sin cuenta se rotula como tal, cancelar la confirmación no llama al backend, y un fallo del backend se muestra como error.

body:
## 문제

댓글 목록 조회에서 요청값이 쿼리까지 전달되지 않아 두 가지 결함이 있었다

- 같은 시각에 작성된 댓글이 페이지 경계에 걸리면 어느 페이지에도 나오지 않음
- 다음 페이지 조건이 `created_at < after` 하나뿐이라 같은 시각 행이 사라짐
- `direction=ASC`로 요청해도 항상 최신순으로 반환
- 요청값을 받기만 하고 정렬에 반영하지 않는다

## 바꾼 것

**복합 커서**

`ORDER BY`와 커서 조건을 같은 기준으로 맞춤

ORDER BY created_at, comment_management_id
WHERE    created_at < ? OR (created_at = ? AND comment_management_id < ?)

응답의 `nextCursor`를 마지막 댓글 id로, `nextAfter`를 작성 시각으로 분리
기존에는 두 값 모두 작성 시각이라 같은 시각 댓글을 구분할 수 없었음

**정렬 방향**

요청의 `direction`으로 정렬 방향과 커서 부등호를 함께 결정함
정렬만 뒤집고 부등호를 두면 다음 페이지가 거꾸로 조회되므로 한 값에서 같이 파생

`direction` 기본값 처리를 `limit`과 동일하게 맞춤
기존에는 캐시 사용 여부를 판단할 때만 변환해 저장소에는 `null`이 전달됐었음

## 검증

실제 DB와 Redis 환경에서 회귀 테스트 추가

- 같은 시각 댓글이 페이지 경계에 걸려도 두 페이지를 합치면 누락·중복이 없음
- `ASC` 요청 시 작성 시각이 빠른 댓글부터 반환
- 응답의 `nextCursor`, `nextAfter`가 페이지 마지막 댓글 값과 일치

## Summary
- Replace the `UITableView` account list with `UICollectionView` + `UICollectionViewCompositionalLayout` (single-column, card-style, estimated-height items)
- Drive the list with `UICollectionViewDiffableDataSource<Section, Account>` and `UICollectionView.CellRegistration`
- Make `Account` `Hashable` so it can be diffed directly as the snapshot's item type
- Add a toolbar "+" button that appends a random mock account, and swipe-to-delete — both apply a new snapshot with `animatingDifferences: true` to demonstrate animated diffing
- Update `README.md` to mark Phases 1–2 complete

## Trade-off note
A plain `UITableView` + manual `reloadData()` doesn't scale once account/transaction updates start coming from async network calls (Phase 6) — batched reloads are easy to get wrong and don't animate. Diffable data source moves state ownership to snapshots: mutate the array, apply a snapshot, and insertion/removal animations come for free. Compositional layout is the modern counterpart for the layout side and sets up later phases (e.g. multi-section transaction grouping) without another rewrite.

## Test plan

- Verified `Account` conforms to `Hashable` cleanly (all stored properties are already `Hashable`)

body:
## Motivation

  hipThreads' scheduler used to size itself by multiplying a fixed vcores-per-WGP
  value by the CU count, which over-subscribed the GPU and hung on CDNA at the
  shipped default. CI worked around this by pinning `HIPTHREADS_VCORES_PER_WGP=1`
  in the test scripts.
  
  The underlying bug is now fixed upstream: the scheduler derives a safe grid
  from the device itself (occupancy-checked, clamped per architecture), so the
  library's own default is safe to run under here. The pin is no longer needed.
  
  JIRA ID : ROCM-30565
  
  Fixed in ROCm/rocm-libraries#11789.

  Removes the `HIPTHREADS_VCORES_PER_WGP` override from `test_hipthreads.py` and
  `test_hipthreads_examples.py`, and updates the comments that referenced it.

  Validated on TheRock multi-arch CI with the pin already removed, on gfx94X,
  gfx950, and gfx110X, before the underlying fix landed and merged.

body:
## Purpose

This PR updates the application runtime environment to Python 3.10, upgrades the base Docker image and MySQL service version, replaces `fuzzywuzzy` with `rapidfuzz`, and updates related dependencies for compatibility and maintenance.

## Approach

### Key Modifications

- **Runtime & Base Image Upgrades:**
  - Updated the Docker base image to `phusion/passenger-python310:3.2.0`.
  - Updated CI workflow to use Python 3.10.
  - Upgraded MySQL service from 8.0 to 8.4 in both `docker-compose.yml` and GitHub Actions.
  - Updated Passenger configuration in `vendor/docker/webapp.conf` to target `/usr/bin/python3.10`.
- **Dependency & Code Refactoring:**
  - Replaced `fuzzywuzzy` and `python-Levenshtein` with `rapidfuzz` in `rorapi/common/matching.py` and `requirements.txt`.
  - Upgraded `statsmodels` to 0.14.4, pinned `numpy` to 1.22.4, and added `setuptools` constraints.
  - Removed deprecated `yapf` installation from Dockerfile and CI.
  - Removed outdated custom NTP configuration (`vendor/docker/ntp.conf`).
- **Tests & Project Maintenance:**
  - Updated matching unit tests in `rorapi/tests/tests_unit/tests_matching_v2.py` to use `assertAlmostEqual(..., places=2)` to accommodate floating-point precision across string matching calculations.
  - Added common local development files and virtual environment directories (`.venv*/`, `.uv-*`, cache files) to `.gitignore` and `.dockerignore`.

### Important Technical Details

- Switching from `fuzzywuzzy` to `rapidfuzz` improves string-matching performance while maintaining algorithmic compatibility. Minor precision variations in floating-point score outputs are handled in unit tests via `assertAlmostEqual`.
- Upgrading to `phusion/passenger-python310:3.2.0` modernizes the underlying system packages and ensures proper support for Python 3.10.

## Types of changes

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

## Reviewer, please remember our [guidelines](https://datacite.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEC/pages/1168375809/Pull+Request+Guidelines):

- Be humble in the language and feedback you give, ask don't tell.
- Consider using positive language as opposed to neutral when offering feedback. This is to avoid the negative bias that can occur with neutral language appearing negative.
- Offer suggestions on how to improve code e.g. simplification or expanding clarity.
- Ensure you give reasons for the changes you are proposing.

AreaDay no longer talks to a licensing server or a prediction service. Everything the Skill needs at run time now runs inside the Skill itself.

Session state, completed result and TSV export are written locally and are resumable.
- **Call sites updated:** `initialize.py`, `open_workbench.py`, `generate_brief.py`, `configure_schedule.py`, `domain_registry.py` and the workbench server all use the local engine.

Installation is verified by `Installation verified` from the installer self-check instead of `license_valid`. The customer guide PDF is rebuilt.
- **Tests** for calibration, domain isolation, resolution and the workbench are rewritten for the local-only flow; 243 tests pass.

## Verification

Full end-to-end acceptance run on this branch with a fresh, isolated data directory (real OpenAlex + arXiv searches, 10 papers):

### Motivation

- The inquiries page was blocked by a serial `inquiry_bootstrap` call followed by `inquiry_list`, causing the UI to wait for expensive Apps Script/Sheets reads before showing the list. 
- Repeated navigations and scope changes triggered redundant `inquiry_list` requests and lacked a client-side snapshot, increasing request count and perceived load time.

### Description

- Removed the `inquiry_bootstrap` dependency from the list critical path so the page shows the list immediately from `inquiry_list` while `bootstrap` is loaded lazily when needed.

- Made the UI apply cached snapshots immediately and made mutations (create/reply/status/redirect) force a refresh of the list; polling now triggers a forced refresh and cache is cleared on logout/cleanup. 
- Exposed `can_admin` from the Apps Script `inquiry_list` response so the admin tab visibility does not require running `inquiry_bootstrap`, and added small test updates to validate single-flight, cache semantics and forced refresh behavior.

runtimes and extensions were left behind while ChairLift reported cleanup
complete.

## Fix

`flatpak.UninstallUnused` now runs the cleanup for both the `--user` and
`--system` scopes, combines their output, and reports an error from either
scope (via `errors.Join`) instead of masking it.

Also updated the Flatpak wrapper tests: the old single-argument case could not
express two invocations, so `TestUninstallUnusedRunsBothScopes` verifies both
scopes are invoked and `TestUninstallUnusedReportsScopeError` verifies a
failing scope is surfaced.

author: trakshan-mishra
body:
Fixes #557.

### Problem

`Older::check_older` (`src/wallet/utils.rs`) computes the height at which a relative locktime is satisfied as `create_height + n` and unwraps the sum with `expect("Overflowing addition")`. `Wallet::finalize_psbt` maps an unconfirmed previous transaction to a `create_height` of `u32::MAX`, so that addition overflows and panics for any `older(n)` with `n` greater than zero.

The `Older` satisfier is only consulted when the input's `nSequence` does not already satisfy the CSV branch, so this is reachable through ordinary use: spending an unconfirmed UTXO of a descriptor that contains an `older()` branch which is *not* the one being used, e.g. spending via `pk(A)` of `or_d(pk(A),and_v(v:pk(B),older(144)))`. Since `Wallet::sign` finalizes by default, callers reach it without opting in.

### Fix

Return `false` when the satisfaction height does not fit in a `u32`, rather than panicking. Such a height can never be reached, so the branch is simply not satisfied — the same answer the comparison would give with wider integers. This matches the behaviour the issue asks for ("the `older()` branch should simply be treated as not satisfied").

The change is in the `Satisfier` impl, so it covers both call sites: finalization in `src/wallet/mod.rs` and policy extraction in `src/descriptor/policy.rs`.

`After::check_after` performs no addition and is unaffected.

### Tests

- `test_finalize_psbt_with_unconfirmed_input_and_unused_csv_branch` (`tests/wallet.rs`) reproduces the reported panic end to end. Verified to fail on master with `panicked at src/wallet/utils.rs:117: Overflowing addition`, and to pass with this change.
- `test_check_older_unreachable_satisfaction_height_is_not_satisfied` covers the overflow directly at the unit level.
- `test_check_older_compares_against_the_satisfaction_height` covers the ordinary satisfied and unsatisfied heights, which had no unit coverage before.

### Checklist

- [x] All commits are GPG signed.
- [x] The PR description links to the issue it solves.
- [x] Ran the `just pre-push` steps locally: `cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check`, both `cargo check` variants, `clippy` with `-D warnings` on the stable and unstable surfaces, `cargo test --workspace` on both surfaces, and `cargo doc` with `-D warnings`. All pass.
- [x] Tests reproducing the bug (and now passing) have been added.
- [x] No API change, so nothing breaking.

One note: `cargo +nightly fmt` on current master also wants to reformat `src/descriptor/policy.rs`, which is unrelated to this fix (and looks like the nightly drift tracked in #535), so I left that file untouched.

author: dlohvinov
body:
**Stack 4/6** — [WS-32](https://webitel.atlassian.net/browse/WS-32). Base: #52.

## What

The offer card itself, rendered top-right per AC_06.01.01, plus the store the domain features fire into.

## Why a separate surface from the toast store

`useNotificationsStore` stays as-is for toasts. Offers differ in every dimension that matters: they live until the interaction resolves rather than timing out, stack in their own corner, and follow a fixed layout from [DES-727](https://webitel.atlassian.net/browse/DES-727). Folding them into `AppNotification` would make that type a union every consumer has to narrow.

## Why the contract is channel-neutral now

DES-727 specifies one preview for calls **and** chats, and the chat producer ([WS-19](https://webitel.atlassian.net/browse/WS-19)) is the next ticket with the same assignee. Calls fill `identifier`/`source` with a number and a queue; chats will fill them with a username and a gateway, plus `body` (last message) and `onBodyClick` (AC_06.01.04), which stay unset for calls. Shaping it call-first would guarantee a rename across the component, its tests and the producer a week later.

Nothing here imports an SDK — producers map their own domain objects onto `IncomingInteractionPreview`. That boundary is the point of the split.

## Two subtleties worth a careful look

- **`shallowRef` for the entry list is load-bearing.** The preview is carried as a ref so the card tracks the live entity; a deep `ref([])` would unwrap that nested ref on property access and silently freeze it into a snapshot. There's a regression test for exactly this.
- **`useWaitingTime` takes an absolute `waitingSince`, not a duration**, so the counter stays correct across re-renders and tab sleep with nobody pushing updates.

## Known gap: the progress bar ships hidden

The queue's *Max wait time* isn't on the wire — `QueueParameters` has no such field and agents have no REST scope on `/call_center/queues`. Asked for on [WS-16](https://webitel.atlassian.net/browse/WS-16) / [WS-35](https://webitel.atlassian.net/browse/WS-35), both in `Need info`.

The label and ticking counter work today; the bar renders only when `maxWaitSec` is present, so it lights up with no further change once the field lands. Colours follow the 0-33 / 34-66 / 67-100 thresholds.

## Localization

All nine languages. **uk and ru wording for "Unknown contact" is verbatim from the spec; the other six are drafts and want a localization review.**

## Verification

31 unit tests across the store and `useWaitingTime` (stacking, single-ring, per-offer action routing, double-accept, reactivity, colour thresholds, timer cleanup). Typecheck clean.

author: yhonda-ohishi
body:
開発ツールが作る作業用 worktree (`.claude/worktrees/<名前>/`) を、git と vitest の視界から外す。

そこには **repo のコピーがまるごと入る** (`test/` も含む)。追跡も走査もされる状態だったので、
2 つの実害が出ていた。

## ① vitest がネストした worktree のテストを二重計上していた (本体)

**この repo には vitest の設定ファイルが 1 つも無かった。** `"test": "vitest run"` は既定の include で
走るため、cwd 配下を丸ごと舐めて `.claude/worktrees/*/test/*.test.ts` まで拾っていた。

実測 (修正前):

```
実ファイル             3 本
worktree がある状態 →  Test Files 5 passed (5) / Tests 77 passed (77)   ← 水増し
隔離した状態     →    Test Files 3 passed (3) / Tests 47 passed (47)   ← 正しい
```

**数が合っているように見えて、古いコピーのテストが混ざる。** worktree が古い commit を指していれば、
**既に直したはずの版のテストが green を出す** — これが `git status` の汚れより本質的な害。

`vitest.config.ts` を新規作成し、`include: ['test/**/*.test.ts']` で**置き場を明示**した。
`exclude` に `.claude/**` を並べる形は採らない — 除外を並べると、次に別の場所へコピーが増えたときに
同じ穴が開く。

## ② `git status` が汚れていた

`.gitignore` に該当の行が無く、worktree を作るたび `?? .claude/` が出ていた。
`gh pr create` が毎回「Warning: 1 uncommitted change」を出し、**`git add -A` すると worktree 一式が
commit に入る**状態だった。

`.gitignore` に `.claude/worktrees/` を 1 行足した。**`.claude/` 全体は無視しない** —
この repo の `.claude/` には将来 skill や設定が入りうるため、`worktrees/` だけを対象にする。

## 検証 (この repo は CI が無いので手元で実行)

**ネストした worktree を実際に作った状態**で回して、水増しが起きないことを確かめた:

```
git worktree add .claude/worktrees/tmp-verify --detach HEAD
npx vitest run   →  Test Files 3 passed (3) / Tests 47 passed (47)   ← 4 以上にならない
git worktree remove .claude/worktrees/tmp-verify
```

- `npm run typecheck` green
- `git status --short` が空
- `git check-ignore` で `.claude/worktrees/…` は当たり、`.claude/` 直下の他のパスは**当たらない**
- 既存 3 テストの中身と `package.json` は無変更

Refs ippoan/rust-alc-api#644

author: maximilian-nesslauer
body:
Closes #251

`borea instance deactivate` leaves no instance active. It calls `IInstanceRepository.ClearActiveInstanceAsync`, which the App already uses.
The command deletes nothing. Without an active instance, `enable` and `disable` need `--instance`.
When no instance was active, the command says so and exits with 0.
When the active instance pointer names an instance that does not exist any more, the command clears the pointer and prints the id.
`--json` gives `deactivated`, and the `id` and `name` of the instance that was active.

author: maximilian-nesslauer
body:
Closes #176

This builds on #252 and targets its branch until that one merges.

Most players already have mods in the game's own profile in `My Games/Kitten Space Agency` (`Constants.DocumentsFolderPath`).
Borea could not bring them into an instance.

`ISharedProfileImporter` lists the mod folders of `ModLibrary.LocalModsFolderPath` in the order of the profile's `manifest.toml`, with their enabled state.
A folder that the manifest does not list comes last and disabled, as `ModLibrary.AddMods` adds it.
The import creates a new instance, copies every folder into it, and writes the manifest entries in the same order with the same enabled state.
It never moves, changes or deletes anything in the shared profile.
Then the existing release matcher compares each copy with the content index. A copy whose files match a release is recorded as that release. Every other copy is a manual install.

A matched copy gets foreign ownership, the same as after `borea instance adopt`.
Borea wrote the copy, but the files came from outside Borea and can hold more than the release, for example changed settings.
So Borea still never deletes files that it cannot prove it installed.
When the import fails or is stopped, Borea deletes the new instance. That instance only holds files that Borea wrote in this import.

- CLI: `borea instance import-profile <name>`, with `--dry-run` and `--json`.
- App: when the game directory is saved and the profile has mods, Home and Library show "N mods in your game profile" with Create instance and Dismiss. Dismiss is saved in the App preferences.
- App: Library has "Import from game profile". Closing the modal stops the import.
- App: the new instance opens. A note names the mods that stay disabled because their folder name is not a valid content id, and the mods that Borea could not compare with the index.

`IGamePathProvider.GetSharedProfileRoot()` is the one place for the profile path, so tests use a temporary folder.

Fixture output from the tests, `borea instance import-profile Main --dry-run`:

```text
Would create instance 'Main' with 2 mods from the shared profile. Nothing was changed.
enabled   LocalOnly     not in the content index
disabled  flight-tools  in the content index
```

body:
### Agent Completion Report

- **Status**: complete
- **Branch and Worktree**:
  - Branch: `feat/contract-claims-gate`
  - Worktree: `./` (primary checkout)
- **Commit and PR**:
  - Commit: `300c1245` (head; `791e1a0e` is the gate, `300c1245` the fragment rename)
  - Target PR / Branch: `main` (this PR is #997)
- **Linked Issues (auto-close convention)**:

  Refs #907

  This PR does **not** close the issue. It records the divergence as a
  `known-divergence` claim and makes it fail the moment the upstream fix lands;
  the defect itself is still open and its fix lives in Oliver.
- **Changed Files**:
  - `test/contract-claims.txt` — the claim registry (six records)
  - `test/contract-claims.checks.sh` — the named black-box checks
  - `scripts/test-contract-claims.sh` — the gate runner
  - `build.zig` — `test-contract-claims` step, wired into `test`
  - `test/README.md` — registry documentation and the three failure conditions
  - `docs/changelog.d/997-contract-claims-gate.md` — changelog fragment
- **Preserved Unrelated Files**:
  - Nothing pre-existing was dirty when this work started. The `stash@{0}` entry
    belonging to `fix/issue-close-declared-intent` and the
    `t3code/cli-reference-current` branch are untouched. Local `main` was not
    used or moved. The separate rendered-search title fix is on its own branch
    and is not included here; this branch is verified green without it.
- **Implementation Summary**:
  - A contract can state a load-bearing rule that nothing executes, and the
    implementation then diverges silently. The Cooklang adapter contract says
    the `{` closing a multiword name must touch the name, and spells out the
    exact failure if it does not — an unrelated braced word later in a sentence
    being absorbed into the name and the prose between them deleted. The pinned
    parser scans to the first `{` on the line and had never enforced it.
  - `test/contract-claims.txt` pairs a verbatim quote from a normative contract
    with a black-box check against the installed binary. Three failure
    conditions: the quote no longer appears in the contract (prose drift), an
    `enforced` claim is violated, or a recorded `known-divergence` no longer
    reproduces.
  - The third condition is the ratchet that was missing: a `known-divergence`
    passes while the bug is present, so the upstream fix fails the gate and
    forces the record to be reclassified instead of being left stale. Neither
    direction can rot quietly.
  - Ships six records: five `enforced` (legacy `parentEntry` / `parent_entry`
    rejection, `EPARENTMISSING` for an absent parent, `EUSAGE` exit 2, pure I/O
    exit 3, and the version pin reusing `scripts/test-version-pin.sh` verbatim
    via `check: script:<path>`), plus the Cooklang divergence.
  - Checks drive the installed binary and never re-implement compiler logic: a
    check that re-derived what the compiler does would pass while the compiler
    was wrong. The `parentEntry` check asserts the absence of `EPARENTMISSING`,
    which is what makes it a test of "no silent alias" rather than of "this
    corpus fails".
  - `--audit` lists contracts with no quoted tether, framed as a worklist: 52 of
    57 today. Untethered is not untested — `publication-claims.md`, `scanner.md`,
    `watch-mode.md` and others carry dedicated test steps of their own. An
    earlier draft of that output said "no executable claim", which overclaimed,
    and was corrected before landing.
- **Known Gaps**:
  - The registry holds six of the normative rules; the audit list is the
    remaining work, not a completed survey.
  - `rendered-search.md` is deliberately left untethered. Its title rule is not
    reachable black-box — the compiler CLI exposes no search flag — and tethering
    it would have required either a nested build or asserting structure and
    calling it behavior. Its own unit test still guards it.
  - The gate adds roughly a second of process spawns per run (six records, each
    one or two `boris` invocations). Acceptable now; a registry of dozens of
    records would want batching.
- **Exact Commands Run**:
  1. `zig build test`
  2. `zig build test-contract-claims`
  3. `bash scripts/test-contract-claims.sh --audit`
  4. `zig fmt --check build.zig`
  5. `git diff --check origin/main...feat/contract-claims-gate`
- **Exact Gate Results**:
  - `zig build test`: pass — exit 0 on this branch alone, with the new
    `contract-claims` step running inside it and `src/search_index.zig` still at
    its original revision
  - `zig build test-contract-claims`: pass — `5 enforced, 1 known divergence(s),
    6 record(s) total`
  - `bash scripts/test-contract-claims.sh --audit`: pass — `52 of 57 normative
    contracts have no record in this registry`
  - **Prose drift proved to bite**: changing one contract word (`exit 2` → `exit 9`
    in the `EUSAGE` row of `docs/contracts/diagnostics.md`) made the gate exit 1,
    name `cli.usage-error-exit-2`, and print the stale quote; the other two
    records in that file stayed green. Restored, `git diff` clean.
  - **Enforced divergence proved to bite**: making one check assert an exit code
    the binary does not produce made the gate exit 1 with
    `the implementation does not honor this contract claim`, naming the record,
    contract, and check. Restored.
  - `zig fmt --check build.zig`: pass
  - `git diff --check origin/main...feat/contract-claims-gate`: clean
- **Determinism Result**:
  - Deterministic. The gate reads fixed registry and contract bytes and runs
    fixed corpora in a per-run scratch tree under `.zig-cache/contract-claims`,
    which is removed on exit. No content enumeration order is relied on; the
    audit walk sorts by filename through the shell glob.
- **Generated Artifacts**:
  - `.zig-cache/contract-claims/` scratch trees only (gitignored, removed on
    exit). No `dist/`, `rag/`, or `source-rag/` output was committed.
- **Blockers and Next Card**:
  - Blockers: None
  - Next Card: Tether the highest-risk untethered contracts next — `html-output.md`,
    `validation.md`, `scanner.md` — and, separately, land the Cooklang adjacency
    guard upstream so the recorded divergence can be flipped to `enforced`.

커뮤니티 요청("TIGER 외에 KODEX·ACE·RISE·SOL·TIME·PLUS 도", "커버드콜이 타이거만 있다")에 따라 국내 ETF 분배금 원천을 미래에셋 TIGER 사이트에서 예탁결제원 SEIBro 분배금지급현황으로 바꿉니다. 지난 1년 지급이 있는 국내 ETF 가 210 → 953개(운용사 27곳), 커버드콜은 16 → 62개입니다.

## 원천

- SEIBro `ETF > 권리행사정보 > 분배금지급현황`(BIP_CNTS06030V). 로그인·세션 없이 XML 서비스 하나로 열리고 건마다 기준일·실지급일·주당분배금·배당구분·운용사가 옵니다. 30건씩 쪽을 넘기며 한 달치 카운트와 맞춥니다(열다섯 달 150여 회, 2분 반).
- '청산분배'(상장폐지 때 순자산 반환)는 뺍니다. 단축코드는 ISIN 4~9번째 글자(KRX ISU_CD 와 같음, 새 형식 0094M0 포함).
- 검증: TIGER 사이트 '전체 분배 내역'과 네 달(2025-12·2026-04·07·08)을 건마다 맞대어 지급일·금액이 전부 같았습니다. 다른 건 상장폐지된 ETF 한 건뿐(시세 목록에 없어 어차피 빠집니다).
- 예전에 "운용사 열 곳은 열린 원천이 없다"고 적었던 것은 SEIBro 를 안 찔러 본 탓이라 config 머리말을 고쳤습니다. 푸터의 출처는 이미 한국예탁결제원이라 그대로입니다.

## 화면

- `etf_dividend` 986행이라 `.limit(1000)` 대신 쪽으로 읽습니다(1,000행 캡).
- 수익률 순 바스켓에 같은 지수의 운용사별 사본이 줄을 채우지 않게 국내 ETF 는 커버드콜 바스켓 운용사당 하나, 계좌 맞춤(ISA·연금저축·IRP) 운용사당 둘. 카드 알약과 툴팁에 적었습니다. 시뮬레이션 결과 커버드콜 국내 다섯은 SOL·ACE·PLUS·KODEX·TIGER 하나씩입니다.
- IRP 안전자산은 주식 40% 이하 채권혼합까지라 이름의 '혼합50' 이상과 커버드콜·밸런스를 뺍니다. 화면의 30% 계산(isSafeAsset)과 바스켓 안전자산 셋이 같은 식이 됐습니다 — 전에는 화면 쪽이 국채 커버드콜을 안전자산으로 셌습니다.
- 문구의 TIGER 를 국내로: 더 보기 안내(ETF 986개 · 국내는 운용사를 가리지 않고 지난 1년 분배가 있는 전부), 검색 결과 없음 문장, 커버드콜 규칙 알약.
- changelog 1.15.0 한 줄. README·워크플로 주석 갱신.

## 확인

- `fetch_etf_dividends.py --dry-run` 986종목(국내 953 · 미국 33) · 시세 없어 뺀 것 22 · 실패 0.
- 새 행을 파일로 물려 로컬에서 페이지를 그려 봤습니다: HTML 1.7 → 2.0MB, 더 보기 ETF 줄에 KODEX·RISE·ACE·SOL·PLUS·WON 이 섞여 서고 바스켓은 위와 같습니다. eslint 통과, tsc 는 무관한 channel-photo 하나뿐.
- 머지 뒤 첫 정기 실행(07:00·18:00)에서 국내 ETF 가 953행으로 바뀝니다. 그 전엔 DB 가 TIGER 210행이라 화면 문구만 먼저 바뀝니다.
