author: stanley
body:
The Sepolia faucet and keeper can race when configured with the same signing key. A keeper transaction can consume a persisted faucet nonce, leaving the frontend waiting indefinitely for a mint that cannot land.

This change rejects faucet key reuse in Terraform and adds an operator-only recovery tool. Recovery validates the original signed mint, verifies a different canonical transaction at the same sender/nonce at or below the safe block through two RPC providers, and rejects existing receipts, replacement mints, funded recipients, or incomplete evidence. An atomic compare-and-swap archives the original transaction and proof before making the exact claim retryable. The tool never signs or submits transactions. A dedicated faucet key must be funded and activated before releasing affected claims.

Receipt-check failures now retain the saved claim and show an actionable manual-retry message instead of a raw RPC error. The runbook covers signer rotation, the additive audit migration, verification, recovery, and explicit user retry.

Validation: 23 recovery unit/database tests (including simultaneous repairs and rollback), 27 mocked Terraform plans, 23 targeted frontend tests, TypeScript, targeted ESLint, and 67 deployment-policy tests passed locally. Live read-only verification of the three identified conflicts also passed; repair and wallet rotation remain separate deployment steps.

author: mechpanos
body:
First station of the plotting & layouts parity track (AutoCAD-compatible page setups). Five commits, each independently reviewable:

1. **Paper catalogue with AutoCAD canonical media names** — `io::paper_catalog` replaces the eight-entry list: ISO A/B, ANSI, ARCH (incl. E1), JIS, full-bleed/expand variants, Letter/Legal/Tabloid, mm and inch units; a parser that reconstructs any AutoCAD media name (`ISO_A4_(210.00_x_297.00_MM)`, custom `UserDefinedMetric_(…)`) from its embedded dimensions; driver/legacy aliases. The Plot dialog stores the canonical name; a drawing's own spelling of an unchanged sheet is preserved on save.
2. **Plot device model with AutoCAD names and printable areas** — `io::plot_device`: page setups store `DWG To PDF.pc3` / the printer name / `none_device` instead of the dialog's label; AutoCAD plotter configurations we cannot drive are kept verbatim. Printable margins per device: CUPS printers report media and margins over IPP (`ipptool`, cached per printer, the dialog lists the printer's own sheets); PDF uses the driver's table.
3. **DWG To PDF printable areas** — the exact margin sets from AutoCAD's Plotter Configuration Editor (ISO 5/17/6/18 mm, expand 5/10/6/11, full bleed 0/1/0/1; ANSI/ARCH 0.23/0.70 in, expand 0.23/0.42, full bleed 0.03).
4. **Custom paper sizes** — in-line editor (name, size, unit, printable margins), persisted per user, offered for every device, written with their own margins. Shared form helpers move to `ui::style::form`.
5. **Printer driver properties + roomier dialog** — Properties… edits the selected printer's PPD options in-line (CUPS: Linux any desktop, macOS) and passes them as `lp -o`; Windows shows the driver's `DocumentProperties` sheet and stores the result as the printer's preferences (`SetPrinter` level 9 — needs a Windows build to verify). Dialog widened; Printer/plotter and Paper size on one line; `none_device` recognised.

Tests: 34 new unit/app tests (catalogue round-trips, IPP parsing, margin sets, dialog ↔ layout round-trips, `lpoptions` parsing, editor flow). `cargo test --lib`: only the pre-existing Linux failures (Windows-path assertions in xref tests, `command_line::history_markers`) remain.

Known limits: Windows `DocumentPropertiesW`/`SetPrinterW` path compiled blind; `scripts/test_locales.py` still fails on `main` for strings outside this PR (`dim_viewport.rs`, `options/spacemouse.rs`).

body:
The distroless-iptables builds compile nftables from source and stage binaries with dpkg/ldd for all five arches, and every arch except amd64 runs under qemu emulation. Adding the distroless-trixie variant means all
five arches are now actually built, and the job no longer fits in Prow's default 2h timeout: a recent presubmit run spent ~118 minutes and was killed partway through the s390x build.

Give both the presubmit and the image-pushing postsubmit a 4h timeout, as
already done for the kube-cross (4h) and go-runner (480m) image jobs, which build the same way.


needed for https://github.com/kubernetes/release/pull/4531

cc @kubernetes/release-managers

author: henry3260
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/area integrations

#### What this PR does / why we need it?

`buildDriverPodTemplateSpec` and `buildExecutorPodTemplateSpec` only copied `spec.driver.nodeSelector` and `spec.executor.nodeSelector` into the Workload PodSet templates, ignoring the SparkApplication-level `spec.nodeSelector`. Since the two levels are mutually exclusive, `RunWithPodSetsInfo` flattens `spec.nodeSelector` into the per-role selectors and then clears it, which makes the Workload the only place `RestorePodSetsInfo` can read the original selector back from. A SparkApplication that only set `spec.nodeSelector` therefore lost it for good on the first eviction, and the selector was also invisible to ResourceFlavor matching.

This records the SparkApplication-level node selector in the PodSet templates, with the per-role selector taking precedence on conflict.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

None

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Release note

```release-note
SparkApplication: Fixed a bug where a SparkApplication that only set the SparkApplication-level `spec.nodeSelector` permanently lost it after the first eviction, letting the driver and executor pods be scheduled onto any node once re-admitted. The selector is now recorded in the Workload PodSets, so it also participates in ResourceFlavor matching.
```

author: silverbeer
body:
## Summary
Step 1 of the PO Agent epic. SB-1087 (`/cycle`) reads cycle numbers from this code, so they have to be true.

- **Closed cycles no longer read 100%.** At close, Linear moves unfinished issues into the next cycle, so a cycle's current membership is only the work that got done. For a closed cycle, totals now come from the last entry of `issueCountHistory` / `scopeHistory`, and carry-out comes from `uncompletedIssuesUponClose`. Cycle 3 now reads 11/37 issues and 48/129 pts; cycle 7 reads 35/77.
- **`endsAt` is exclusive** in both the `--previous` and active selectors (`start <= now < end`). Choosing between history and membership follows Linear's `completedAt`, not the clock. That covers the few seconds before Linear's close job runs, and an `--as-of` date on a cycle that has already closed.
- **Carry-over and planning status.** An ended cycle shows carry-out and the active cycle shows carry-in, each with a planned/adhoc split. A banner appears when a cycle has no planning stamp. `--mark-planned` / `--mark-unplanned [--note]` stamp the cycle description through `cycleUpdate`:
  - dry run unless `--yes` is passed
  - only the `Planning:` line is replaced; other lines and their line endings are kept
  - over 255 chars is refused, never truncated
  - a note containing any line separator is rejected
- **Built for reuse.** A new `scripts/cycles.py` holds the queries and pure calculations and returns plain dicts. `summarize()` returns JSON `schema: 1`, which `--json` prints. `cycle-report.py` is now only the command-line front end.
- **Plan doc.** `docs/po-agent-plan.md` has step 1 ticked and handoff notes for SB-1087: the function flow, the JSON keys, and surprises in Linear's cycle fields. Membership drifts after close, and `uncompletedIssuesUponClose` returns each issue's current estimate and state. Asking for it inside `cycles(filter:)` fails as "Query too complex".

Follow-up: [SB-1093](https://linear.app/silverbeer/issue/SB-1093). The settings allowlist pre-approves `cycle-report.py:*`, which now also covers the `--mark-* --yes` write.

## Test plan
- [x] `bash .github/tests/run.sh`: all pass with the pinned ruff 0.16.5. Locally, ruff 0.12.12 fails the version pin, so the ruff tests only pass with the pinned version.
- [x] 140 offline Python tests: `test_cycles.py`, `test_cycle_report.py`
- [x] New negative harness test: changing the exclusive end to `<=` makes the boundary test fail
- [x] Live, read-only runs:
  - `--cycle 3` → 11/37, 48/129
  - `--cycle 7` → 35/77
  - `--previous --as-of 2026-08-16` → cycle 3
  - plain run → cycle 8, carry-in 40, banner shown
- [x] `--mark-unplanned --cycle 8 --note test`: dry run, nothing written
- [ ] CI green

author: dantheman1991
body:
## Paper for the outside: the change order and the order print (ADR 0075)

The two documents every builder hands to somebody to sign, which did not print: the client's change order and the issued purchase order or subcontract. No new table, no migration.

**What prints**

- **The change order**, at its price and never its cost: the change described, *Contract sum before this change*, *This change* (signed), *Contract sum after this change*, and a signature block for each side. Before is read as a ladder through the contract's approved changes, so a stack of them prints with each one's "after" the next one's "before" and the last matches the job's revised sum; a change not yet approved reads the sum as it stands today and carries a PROPOSED watermark. The cost lines and their codes appear nowhere; a pure test scans for the words, as the proposal's does.
- **The order**, as placed with its changes beneath it: the lines the order was placed with (with a cost-code column only when a line has one), *Order as placed*, every change order on the order with its amount and where it stands, and a total that counts only the approved ones; the notes print as terms. A subcontract carries two signature blocks, a purchase order the business's alone; DRAFT and CANCELLED watermark. An issued order's lines are locked (ADR 0065), so the live rows are the agreement and nothing is frozen twice.
- One layout in the proposal's own styles, two pure model builders, two loaders, two GET routes with the proposal's gates, a Print icon on every row of the Changes and Ordered tabs and a Print button on the order's page. Any member may print. The vendor's address comes from the books' vendor record, the client's from the customer record; a party the books have not billed or paid prints by name alone. The order's codes are resolved by the lines' own ids, so a job without a code set still prints them.

**Driven** as the owner on the dev Hilltop Farm, the PDFs fetched from the routes and embedded in the pane: 24-108's CO-2 came back as `change-order-CO-2-24-108.pdf` with the brand, the facts, the client and the business, the change, the ladder (*1,854,500.00 · +2,500.00 · 1,857,000.00* through CO-1 approved the same day) and the signature blocks; 24-109's subcontract SC-24109-1 as `subcontract-SC-24109-1-24-109.pdf` with its line under its cost code, *Order as placed 30,000.00*, its approved change beneath it, and *Subcontract total 34,000.00*. Not driven: a proposed change, a draft order and a purchase order, whose words are table-tested.

**Tests**: `tests/jobs-paper.test.ts` (10: the ladder across changes approved the same day and across days, the sum for a proposed and a declined change, a contract with no value, the change order's every word and figure and its watermarks, a deduction signed, no client and no site, the cost-word scan, the order as placed with its codes and changes, a purchase order with one signature and no code column, DRAFT and CANCELLED, both documents rendered to PDF bytes with and without a brand); one more ops scenario (84 in the file, the whole suite run alone and green); the guide and docs suites green.

**Docs**: ADR 0075, `docs/modules/jobs.md` (build log with the DRIVEN paragraph, key files, decisions, the open item closed), `docs/help/jobs/overview.md` (*Printing a change order*, *Printing an order*, the not-yet bullet, a who-can row).

Not built, on purpose: the subcontractor's own application as a document (theirs to prepare), sending either document by Mail, a signed copy attached back to the row, and the business's own address on the FROM block, which no printed document carries yet.

author: mdcruz
body:
## Summary
- Faro's `TracingInstrumentation` was only wired up after the async `/api/config` fetch resolved, but SvelteKit mounted the app (and ran route `load`/`onMount` fetches) immediately without waiting on it.
- Under real network latency, this let early app requests — e.g. the login page's `/api/csrf-token` fetch on mount — fire before `fetch`/`XHR` were patched, so they were captured only as passive `faro.performance.resource` entries and never got a trace span. This is why some sessions show zero traces even though they clearly hit the backend.
- Fix: export an `init()` hook from `hooks.client.ts`. SvelteKit awaits this before mounting the app or running any route `load` function, guaranteeing tracing instrumentation is attached first.
- Note: the `/api/config` request itself remains untraceable by design, since it's what delivers Faro's own collector URL — nothing can trace the request that bootstraps the tracer.

## Test plan
- [x] Ran backend + frontend dev servers locally behind a small proxy that artificially delays `/api/config` (to simulate realistic network latency, since localhost alone was too fast to reproduce the race)
- [x] Captured real Faro OTLP payloads sent to a mock collector
- [x] Confirmed **before** the fix: the login page's on-mount `/api/csrf-token` request appears only as `faro.performance.resource`, no trace span
- [x] Confirmed **after** the fix: the identical request now produces a full `HTTP POST` span (`faro.tracing.fetch`), even with the same artificial delay
- [ ] CI

author: gurgant
body:
SetPrimarySqlServerTests.ConcurrentSwapsForOneUser, added in #185, failed
once in a full local run of the SQL Server suite on 2026-09-16 while three
open PRs were being gated, on a branch that touched only docs. Two more full
runs passed. It is a real 500, not a test problem, and it has already
reached CI: the SQL Server proofs job on #186's run 35096826033 failed on
the same test at 12:38Z with the same 500, on a PR that touches no backend
code.

The swap retries a lost RowVersion race through ConcurrencyRetry, bounded at
eight attempts. Every swap by a user clears that user's one primary, so
concurrent swaps are not racing now and then: they all update the same row,
and each round only one can win. On an idle machine the eight attempts were
enough, which is why #185 measured a per-user lock as unnecessary (five runs
of five) and took it out. Under load they are not.

Measured with eight CPU-bound processes running beside the test class:

    main, as merged      0 of 5 runs passed; each failure a 500
    with this change     10 of 10 runs passed

The failures were captured by temporarily writing the unhandled exception to
a file: DbUpdateConcurrencyException from the save that clears the old
primary. A second instrumented run recorded 26 conflicts that the catch did
not retry, every one at attempt 8, all on Account entries. So the bound ran
out; nothing else was refused. The instrumentation is not in this PR.

SetPrimaryAccountAsync now takes a per-user application lock
(set-primary:{userId}) as the first statement of its transaction, before it
reads anything. A second swap by the same user waits, then reads the primary
the first one committed. The statement is the one the daily limit already
uses in TransferService: a negative sp_getapplock return becomes a raised
error, and the wait is bounded (10 seconds, below the 30-second command
timeout). Deposits and transfers do not take this lock and still move the
RowVersion, so the retry stays for them; the swaps-racing-deposits test
passed in all ten runs. InMemory has no locks and skips the statement, as
the transfer path does.

It adds no deadlock. The resource is not the daily limit's; a swap writes no
audit row, so its saves never take the chain's tail lock
(AuditChain.ApplyAsync returns before reading the tail when nothing is
pending); and a swap takes the lock before any row lock, so nothing holding
a row waits for it. Two records said no other application lock exists in
backend/src, and they are corrected inline, dated: ADR-0044's note on the
chain and ADR-0050's "Why sp_getapplock has neither defect".
TransferService's comment saying the same is corrected in place. The test's
remarks record the measurement.

Gate: dotnet test on the whole solution, 142 + 1,271 with
AZUREBANK_TEST_SQLSERVER set; 142 + 1,171 with 88 skipped without it, which
is what CI runs. dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes over the three
changed .cs files exited 0. The same counts as main: no test is added.

Not merging — ready for review.

  - Reduced the likelihood of conflicting account updates during simultaneous transfers, deposits, or account swaps.
  - Preserved retry handling for transient update conflicts.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated technical documentation to accurately describe account-update locking and concurrency behavior.
  - Clarified the daily limit rules for outgoing external transfers, including UTC-day boundaries and refusal details.

Phases 4–7 of the hardening plan, webbsite halves. **Stacked on #32** (→ #31 → #30). Merge order is #30, #31, #32, then this.

## Refresh loader (the substance of #28)
- `|stkchg| > 100` bigchanges rows are **quarantined** (logged with keys, excluded, counted in the success ping) and the other seven datasets load. Abort is reserved for PK duplicates, the freeze guard, and a manifest/row mismatch.
- The "up to date, nothing to load" path now **judges freshness before pinging**. Previously it pinged success daily even if upstream had stopped publishing — a self-reported check cannot see a failure that exits 0 unless it looks.

`deploy/cloudflare.json`: 4 WAF rules, 3 webbsite cache rules, the shared Free-plan rate-limit rule — captured verbatim in the renavon reconciler's key shape, with `rule_scope.host` because the zone is shared (the site-deploy session is adding that scope to the promoted reconciler; nothing reads this file until then).

author: kumacha666
body:
## 目的

PR #460（dusty-jukebox/dusty-jukebox-tools）で修正した`npm install`失敗が、他のB系アプリにも存在することが判明した。今回は`enblo`（`vite`自体は要件を満たすバージョン）でも同じクラッシュが再現し、単なるバージョン不整合ではなく**npm（Arborist）側のvitest 4.1.x固有のピア依存解決バグ**であることを確認した。Codex Cloud EnvironmentのSetup Scriptがこれでまた落ちるため、緊急でClaude Codeが直接修正した。

## 原因

- vitest 4.1.x系の複雑なピア依存グラフ（`@vitest/browser-playwright`等の多数のoptional peer）を、npmのArboristが正しく解決できず`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`で内部クラッシュする
- `vite`のバージョンが要件（`^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0 || ^8.0.0`）を満たしていても発生することを`enblo`（`vite: ^6.3.0`）で確認済み——PR #460時点の「viteバージョン不整合」という説明は不完全だった（dusty-jukebox/dusty-jukebox-toolsではその不整合も併発していたが、根本原因はこちらのnpm側のバグ）
- `package-lock.json`はリポジトリ全体でgitignore対象のため、この不整合を`npm install`のたびに踏み抜く

## 対象

- `7metch/package.json`・`7metch2/package.json`・`enblo/package.json`・`enblo-classic/package.json`・`combrawl/package.json`・`mori-no-yakai/package.json`
- `enblo/CLAUDE.md`・`enblo-classic/CLAUDE.md`（下記の副次的な発見の記録）
- ルート`CLAUDE.md`（B系アプリ共通の暗黙知として記録）

## 非対象

- `enblo`/`enblo-classic`の`src/audio.ts`の型エラー修正（下記「副次的な発見」参照、今回は記録のみで修正しない）
- ビルド成果物（`game.js`/`style.css`等）：`7metch`/`7metch2`はバイト単位で完全一致のため未変更。`combrawl`はミニファイア内部の非決定性によるごく僅かな差のみのため未変更。`mori-no-yakai`は無関係な依存関係（firebase等）のドリフトで差分が大きく出たため、意図的に再コミットしていない

## 変更内容

- `vitest`を`^4.1.9`→`^3.2.7`へ引き下げ（vitest 3系は`vite`を必須ピア依存にせず、内部の`dependencies`として解決するためこの種の不整合が起きない）

## 副次的な発見（今回は未修正）

`enblo`・`enblo-classic`の`tsc --noEmit`で、今回の修正とは無関係な既存の型エラーが見つかった：`src/audio.ts`の`let channelStates: ChannelState[][] = [];`という宣言が、実際の使われ方（`ChannelState[]`として扱われている）と食い違っている。`npm test`は通るため見過ごされており、`npm install`自体がブロックされていたため`npm run build`も実行できず気づかれていなかったと見られる。修正自体は1行の型注釈修正で足りると見られるが、実際の音声再生への影響を確認していないため今回は修正せず、両アプリの`CLAUDE.md`に記録するにとどめた。

## Tests

6アプリすべてでクリーンな状態（`node_modules`/`package-lock.json`削除済み）から検証済み：
- `7metch`：`npm install`成功／`npm test`341件全green／`tsc --noEmit`クリーン／`vite build`成功（`game.js`は既存コミット済みファイルとバイト単位で完全一致）
- `7metch2`：`npm install`成功／`npm test`57件全green／`tsc --noEmit`クリーン／`vite build`成功（`game.js`は既存コミット済みファイルとバイト単位で完全一致）
- `enblo`：`npm install`成功／`npm test`41件全green／`tsc --noEmit`は上記の既存バグにより失敗（今回の修正とは無関係）
- `enblo-classic`：`npm install`成功／`npm test`41件全green／`tsc --noEmit`は同じ既存バグにより失敗（今回の修正とは無関係）
- `combrawl`：`npm install`成功／`npm test`126件全green／`tsc --noEmit`クリーン／`vite build`成功（`game.js`はミニファイア内部の非決定性によるごく僅かな差のみ）
- `mori-no-yakai`：`npm install`成功／`npm test`58件全green／`tsc --noEmit`クリーン／`vite build`成功（`game.js`は無関係な依存関係ドリフトにより差分が大きいため再コミットせず）

ドキュメントのみの変更ではないため（`package.json`の実変更を含む）、通常の最終チェックを経てからマージ判断してください。

author: kieran-woodrow
body:
## What this does

A push to `main` reads `EsimplifiedSDKVersion.version`.

- A tag already exists for it → the run stops. Ordinary merges do nothing.
- No tag → the version was bumped. Build, test, create the tag, publish a GitHub Release.

Nothing keys off branch names. Whatever branch the bump arrives on, merging it is what ships.

## Release notes

`.github/scripts/release-notes.sh` reads every non-merge commit since the previous tag and groups them by Conventional Commit prefix:

| Prefix | Section |
|---|---|
| `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` | ⚠️ Breaking changes |
| `feat:` | Added |
| `refactor:` / `perf:` | Changed |
| a change-bearing commit whose description starts with remove/drop/delete | Removed |
| `fix:` | Fixed |
| everything else | Other |

Both SDK repos already write commits this way, so it works on the existing history with no new discipline. Verified by running it over `1.1.0..HEAD` here and over the Android SDK's history, which exercises every bucket.

## The version now lives in one place

It appeared in five places across three files, so a bump had to be repeated by hand — which is how the 1.5.0 bump shipped with a stale test.

- Install instructions use **Up to Next Major Version** from `1.0.0`, which resolves to the newest 1.x on its own and never needs editing. The release badge already shows which version that is.
- The version test checks the shape of the number instead of pinning a literal.

`EsimplifiedSDKVersion.version` is now the only place a version appears, so it cannot drift.

## Changelog

The Releases page is the changelog — one entry per version, tied to its tag. Nothing is written back to `main`, so the branch ruleset stays exactly as it is.

## Verification

`swift build` and `swift test` pass locally — 207 tests in 15 suites.

author: ikeniborn
body:
## Problem

Creating a domain on the hosted (PostgreSQL) server and populating it looked impossible: every attempt ended in `access_denied`, which read as "the token has no grants for this domain". Two separate defects produced that reading.

1. **A bind naming a domain the wiki has not provisioned yet is refused with a bare `access_denied`.** A client binds the scope its `.iwiki.toml` names before anything else, so the very first hosted call routinely carries a domain that does not exist yet. The refusal was indistinguishable from a revoked grant.
2. **A narrowing `wiki_bind` was irreversible inside a session.** The gate authorized a bind against the session's *current selection* rather than the token's grants, so once a session bound its project scope it could never select anything outside it again — including the domain `wiki_create_domain` had just provisioned and added to the session.

Both were reproduced against a disposable PostgreSQL instance, and the create-then-populate path was confirmed working against the hosted server once the sequence avoided the trap.

## Changes

- Attribute domain-scope refusals: `domain_not_granted` (bind outside the token's grants), `domain_creation_not_allowed` (token without `can_create_domain`), `domain_not_owned` (create-capable token naming a domain another token owns). `_safe` now carries an `AccessError` reason into the in-band tool result the way the gate already carried it into the JSON-RPC error.
- Authorize a hosted `wiki_bind` against the token's current grants instead of the session's selection, and run the existence check against the requested selection rather than the scope being replaced. Local stdio keeps `.iwiki.toml` as its ceiling; revocation still applies on the next request, so the grants remain the only ceiling.
- Document the bind → create → rebind bootstrap order and the new selection semantics in `README.md` and `docs/README.ru.md`.
- Two regression tests in `tests/postgres/test_http.py`; version bumped to 0.7.272.

No refusal is relaxed and no denial field names a domain, a wiki, or another token.

## Verification

```
IWIKI_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN=... uv run pytest -q tests/postgres tests/test_http_unit.py tests/test_server_write.py
616 passed, 2 failed
uv run flake8 src/iwiki_mcp tests/postgres
exit 0
```

The two failures are pre-existing and environment-bound: `test_code_publish_cli.py::test_direct_postgres_failure_preserves_active_revision_and_redacts` asserts `duration_ms: 0` and this machine measures 113–155 ms. Both fail identically on unmodified `master`.

author: aguyshayb
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the SVG rendering fixes. Reproduced from chat history:

- Full-sized (correct) SVG in the DOM: `<svg width="100%" height="auto" viewBox="0 0 300 70" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">` — matches what [SvgRenderer's useEffect](src/ui/web/exerciserenderer/blocks/SvgRenderer/index.tsx#L48-L71) is supposed to produce.
- Shrunken (wrong) SVG in greyed chat history: `<svg width="300" height="70">` — the raw authored markup, no viewBox, no `width="100%"`.

Root cause: the useEffect that backfills the viewBox and swaps `width` to 100% doesn't reliably fire in the greyed state — some React remount/commit timing in the chat history render path skips it. Without a viewBox, CSS `[&>svg]:w-full` sizes the SVG box to 100% container width, but content is drawn at fixed pixel coordinates (`x="10"`, `font-size="30"`) — the SVG box is wide but the content is a tiny cluster in the corner.

## Fix

Apply [`ensureSvgViewBox`](src/ui/web/media/SVGMedia/ensureSvgViewBox.ts) inside the sanitize `useMemo` so the viewBox is baked into the string that goes into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. The DOM has a viewBox from the very first paint, independent of when (or whether) the useEffect fires.

The useEffect stays in place as belt-and-suspenders: it still handles `width="100%"`, `preserveAspectRatio`, and the content-bbox expansion. But now the *viewBox* is guaranteed, so the CSS-driven scaling always has a coordinate system to work with.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/exerciserenderer/SvgRenderer.viewbox.test.tsx --config ./vitest.config.unit.mts` — 2 new tests pass (viewBox backfilled into sanitized markup; author-declared viewBox preserved).
- [x] Full SVG-adjacent unit sweep (9 files, 75 tests) still green.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean.
- [ ] Manual on preview: greyed chat history exercise SVGs render at full container width (matching active state), not shrunken.
- [ ] Manual: well-authored SVGs with existing viewBox still render identically.

## Not fully understood

The exact reason the useEffect skips under the greyed-state remount timing isn't pinned down — traced through the render path but couldn't reproduce in isolation. Since the sanitize-time fix makes the viewBox unconditional (doesn't rely on effect firing), the observed symptom is fixed regardless of the underlying lifecycle quirk. If we later want to understand it precisely, we can add telemetry to the effect.

author: gumustasas
body:
## Amaç

#65 kaydı, #66 ham performansı, #67 zaman pencerelerini getirmişti — hiçbiri karar üretmiyordu (bilinçli olarak #68'e bırakılmıştı). Bu PR halkayı kapatıyor: yayınlanmış bir içerik için deterministik bir sonraki karar.

## Paralel karar sistemi kurulmadı

Karar sözlüğü **yeniden tanımlanmadı**:

```ts
export type RefreshDecision = Extract<
  ContentDecision,
  'do_nothing' | 'update_existing' | 'expand_existing' | 'review_cannibalization'
>
```

Decision Engine v2'nin zaten kullandığı `ContentDecision` birleşiminden türetiliyor — ikinci bir enum yok, birleşim değişirse otomatik yayılıyor. **`decideAction()` (opportunity-engine.ts) hiç değiştirilmedi**: o keşif sinyallerini (envanter çakışması, PAA, talep, KG) yorumlar, bu katman yayın sonrası gerçek performansı. Girdi kümeleri farklı, karar dili aynı.

`create_content` / `create_faq` bilinçli olarak kapsam dışı — bunlar yeni içerik kararlarıdır ve keşif aşamasına aittir.

## Karar kuralları (sıra bilinçli)

| # | Koşul | Karar | reasonCode |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hiç ölçüm yok **veya** gösterim < 50 (gürültü eşiği) | `do_nothing` | `insufficient_data` |
| 2 | Aynı sorgularda başka bir yayınlanmış Buzsu sayfası da görünüyor (**≥2 ortak sorgu**) | `review_cannibalization` | `query_overlap_with_published_page` |
| 3 | **≥2 bağımsız** bozulma sinyali | `update_existing` | `position_declining`, `clicks_declining`, `queries_declining`, `queries_lost` |
| 4 | **≥2 yeni sorgu** *ve* büyüyen gösterim | `expand_existing` | `new_queries_emerging`, `impressions_growing` |
| 5 | Aksi halde | `do_nothing` | `stable_performance` / `not_enough_decay_signals` |

**Bozulma sinyalleri (eşikler):** pozisyon ≥1 sıra kötüleşme · tıklama ≥%20 düşüş · kötüleşen sorguların iyileşenleri aşması · ≥2 kaybedilen sorgu.

### Konservatiflik

- **Tek metrik değişiminden refresh üretilmez.** Tek sinyal kaldığında karar `do_nothing` olur ve gerekçe `not_enough_decay_signals` ile birlikte **o tekil sinyali de taşır** — sinyal gizlenmez, yalnız aksiyona çevrilmez.
- **`insufficient_data` asla zorla aksiyona çevrilmez.**
- **İyi/stabil performansın geçerli sonucu `do_nothing`tır** ve bu bir başarısızlık değildir.
- **Karar en uzun karşılaştırılabilir pencereye dayanır** (90d > 60d > 28d > 7d) — kısa pencere tek haftalık dalgalanmayla aksiyon üretebilirdi. Testte kısa pencerede sert düşüş + uzun pencerede stabil durumda kararın `do_nothing` kaldığı doğrulanıyor.
- Karşılaştırılabilir pencere yoksa → `do_nothing` + `no_comparable_window`; trend uydurulmuyor.
- **Cannibalization yayınlar ARASI bir sinyal**: iki yayınlanmış sayfanın *gerçekten ölçülmüş* sorgu listelerinin kesişiminden, küme düzeyinde hesaplanıyor. Tek ortak sorgu yetmiyor.

## İzlenebilirlik

Her karar sabit `reasonCodes` (serbest metin değil) + `evidence` taşıyor: kullanılan pencere, ölçülmüş pencereler, clicks/impressions/ctrPoints/position farkları, `positionTrend`, new/lost/improved/declining sorgu sayıları, örtüşen sorgular ve URL'ler, `ageDays`. Karar, kanıtı olmadan doğrulanamaz durumda bırakılmıyor.

## Dış API / LLM çağrı etkisi

**GSC çağrısı +0.** Karar modülü saf: girdisi yalnız #67 snapshot'ları, sonucu `additionalGscRequests: 0` taşıyor (testle doğrulanıyor). MCP aracı ölçümü #67'den alıyor; karar katmanı üstüne **tek bir istek bile** eklemiyor — toplam bütçe #67 ile birebir aynı.

**LLM çağrısı yok. Yeni bağımlılık yok. Yeni ücretli servis yok.**

## Kapsam dışı / dokunulmayanlar

- **Otomatik içerik üretme/güncelleme/yayınlama yok** — karar yalnız editöre sunulan bir öneri.
- **CMS write yok** (`externalWrite: false`).
- **Opportunity ranking/score değiştirilmedi** (`decideAction`, `rankOpportunities`, skor boyutları — hiçbiri dokunulmadı).
- **Yeni blacklist / keyword-density / SEO score sistemi kurulmadı** (§9.4). Eşikler, Decision Engine v2'nin eşik tabanlı karar ağacıyla aynı üslupta: sabit, az sayıda ve açıklanabilir.
- **UI yok.**

## Test

13 yeni regresyon testi — istenen senaryoların tamamı:

- ✅ **insufficient data → zorla aksiyon yok** (3 varyant: `not_due`, `insufficient_data`, gürültü eşiği altı)
- ✅ **güçlü/stabil sonuç → `do_nothing`**
- ✅ **anlamlı decay → `update_existing`** (dört sinyal + evidence doğrulaması)
- ✅ **yeni sorgu/konu fırsatı → `expand_existing`**
- ✅ **örtüşme sinyali → `review_cannibalization`** (+ tek ortak sorgunun yetmediği)
- ✅ **aynı input → aynı karar**
- ✅ **GSC çağrı sayısı +0**
- tek küçük değişimden refresh üretilmez
- tek yeni sorgu expand üretmez
- karar en uzun karşılaştırılabilir pencereye dayanır
- karşılaştırılabilir pencere yoksa uydurma karar verilmez
- karar sözlüğü Decision Engine ile aynı, otomatik aksiyon/skor üretilmez
- provenance karara taşınır

**Sonuç:** `npm run check:mcp` → 254/254 pass. `npm run check:dashboard` → type-check + build başarılı.

## Mimari dokümanı

`docs/content-studio-architecture.md`: §11 araç tablosuna `decide_content_refresh`, §16 "Mevcut durum"a karar kaydı (kural sırası, eşikler, konservatiflik gerekçesi ve +0 çağrı bütçesi dahil).

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hosted marketplace listing and refresh can perform snapshot SQLite work on the calling Gateway or CLI thread.

## User Impact

Snapshot database work moves to the existing shared worker while catalog results, offline fallback, and refresh behavior remain unchanged. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The store keeps its existing Promise API and awaited callers. Reads preserve missing-database noncreation. Writes capture snapshot fields, time, and environment before waiting, then reread and enforce signed-feed monotonicity in the same transaction as the upsert. The loader receives the same rejection class, preserving its accepted-snapshot fallback. Environment capture retains Windows case semantics and explicit state-directory overrides.

## Evidence

- 89 catalog and worker tests passed, including the real default offline catalog loader; two canonical routing controls also passed.
- Six parent-thread SQL methods were independently calibrated before measurement. author: stella-sea
body:
## Summary

部分 OpenAI 兼容的 Embedding 服务会返回固定维度向量，但不接受 `/embeddings` 请求中的可选 `dimensions` 字段。

当前 `embedding_output_dimensions` 同时用于：

1. 定义向量空间契约，包括响应长度校验、向量空间签名、存储和检索。
2. 序列化 OpenAI 兼容请求中的 `dimensions` 字段。

这两个职责不必绑定。以硅基流动的 `bge-m3` 为例，服务返回 1024 维向量，但请求带有 `dimensions` 时会被拒绝。将 `embedding_output_dimensions` 设为 `0` 不能解决这个问题，因为该值同时是系统校验上游返回向量长度的契约。

本 PR 新增 `file.embedding_dimensions_policy`：

- `send`：默认值，保持现有行为，在请求中携带 `dimensions`。
- `omit`：请求中省略 `dimensions`，但继续按 `embedding_output_dimensions` 校验每个响应向量的长度。

例如：

```text
embedding_output_dimensions = 1024
embedding_dimensions_policy = omit
```

这样可以兼容不接受 `dimensions` 参数的上游，同时仍拒绝非 1024 维的响应，不会将不兼容的向量写入库中。

- [x] `omit` 策略下，请求 JSON 不包含 `dimensions` 键。

- [x] 非法策略值会被设置校验拒绝。
- [x] 仅修改请求策略不会被视为向量空间变更。

本机未完成的全仓验证：

- [ ] `go test ./...` 和 `go vet ./...`：环境缺少 `sqlite3.h`，sqlite-vec CGO 依赖无法构建；另有既有 filecache 测试受 Windows 文件权限行为影响。
- [ ] 前端 `typecheck` 和 `lint`：本机未安装 `frontend/node_modules`，缺少 `react`、`next-intl`、`biome` 等依赖。

```json
{
  "model": "BAAI/bge-m3",
  "input": ["example text"]
}
```

响应仍必须符合配置的 `embedding_output_dimensions`。

## Configuration, migration, and compatibility notes

- 新增 `file.embedding_dimensions_policy`，默认值为 `send`，已有部署维持原有请求格式。
- 不涉及数据库迁移、API DTO、Swagger 或部署脚本变更。

- 向量空间签名仍只由模型、服务地址和契约维度决定。
- 请求策略仅影响上游 HTTP 请求序列化，不会触发索引重建或使现有向量失效。
- 不在本 PR 中实现自动探测上游维度，避免把上游探测、配置回写、空间签名变更和向量重建混入一个兼容性改动。

author: billmallard
body:
## Summary

**What changed:** Pinned a headless test that renders the SVS twin and compares it to a real Pi capture at one pose.
**Why it is right:** All three invariants check out or are honestly flagged; 33/33 configurator tests pass, including 3 new.
**Risk / not covered:** One pose only (coastal, level); roll can't be measured because the twin doesn't model attitude at all.
**Your call:** none - merge when ready.

## Evidence

Real Pi capture (top) vs the twin driven headlessly on the same terrain data (bottom):

![coastal side by side](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/billmallard/makerplane-data/bd59af1682147987b2e41c1ad841d7e1014920df/docs/images/aer-1424/coastal_side_by_side.png)

Ridge-silhouette overlay, identity alignment, RMSE 5.91px out of 1080 rows:

![skyline overlay](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/billmallard/makerplane-data/bd59af1682147987b2e41c1ad841d7e1014920df/docs/images/aer-1424/coastal_skyline_overlay.png)

## Context

AER-1424: `renderSVS()` (`configurator/public/editor.html`) is an independent reimplementation of pyEfis `svs.py`/`svs_gl.py`, asserted to match it and required to follow it in lockstep, and nothing had ever compared it to a render. AER-1423 found the same shape of gap in pyEfis's own geometric oracle model and fixed one fault class after measuring against real renders for the first time — this does the analogous first measurement for the configurator's twin, at the one pose the existing Pi fallback capture already covers (`coastal`, the exact `SCENES["coastal"]` pose from `tools/export_svs_preview_patch.py`).

## What I measured

Drove the actual `renderSVS()` headlessly via `node-canvas` (brace-matched out of `editor.html`, same pattern the existing tests already use — see `test/support/extract.mjs`), against the real `assets/editor/svs/coastal.json` data patch and the real `coastal.webp` Pi capture (both fetched live from the deployed site, since that's the exact ground truth the editor itself serves).

1. **Horizon row** — matches. Both `renderSVS()` (`horizonY = H*(1-horizon_position/100)`, default 50) and pyEfis's own convention (`ai_widget.py`: `horizon_y = pitchAngle * ppd`, so pitch 0 = screen centre) land on `H/2 = 540`. Confirmed by driving the real code against an emptied patch and reading the sky→backdrop transition directly, not just reading the formula. Caveat: this pose can't independently confirm it from the captured pixels — the camera looks inland, away from the Pacific, so the true horizon is occluded by the ridge in both images.
2. **Angular scale** — off by ~2.3%, twin narrower. Device: `pixelsPerDeg = H/pitchDegreesShown` (exact, linear near boresight). Twin: pinhole `f = H/(2*tan(fov/2))`, same default FOV=30. Same functional form, different constant — 35.18 vs 36.0 px/deg at boresight. This matches the ~2.3% gap `configurator/CLAUDE.md` already documented from the unrelated KSBA-runway check, rederived independently here and corroborated by the skyline RMSE (constraining the alignment search to a physically plausible ±10% scale finds a best fit at s≈1.022 — the same figure, not a coincidence of one prior measurement).
3. **Sign of roll — not measurable, and that itself is the finding.** `renderSVS()` takes no pitch/roll input anywhere: the terrain projection only reads `patch.meta.cam.{lat,lon,alt_ft,head}`, and the symbology overlay is drawn via `attitudeSVG(inst, 0, 0, 0, ...)` — hardcoded level (`editor.html` comment: "Drawn at level (pitch 0 / roll 0) so it aligns with the level terrain"). There's no roll convention to be right or wrong about; the SVS/virtual_vfr preview is a fixed-attitude static preview, not an attitude-driven view. Full writeup, including what it would take to actually measure roll sign, is in `docs/images/aer-1424/README.md`.

All three are pinned in `configurator/test/svs_twin_fidelity.test.mjs` against committed fixtures (`test/fixtures/svs_coastal_patch.json` / `svs_coastal_real.png`), so this is a standing regression guard, not a number that rots on the next edit.

## Test plan

- [x] `NODE_ENV=development npm test` — 33/33 pass (3 new: horizon row, angular scale, roll-absence)
- [x] `NODE_ENV=development npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `python3 scripts/spdx_check.py` — clean
- [x] `npm ci` from a clean `node_modules` (matches CI's exact invocation) — clean install, canvas prebuild resolves on Linux
- [x] Verified both evidence image URLs return `200 image/png` before posting

body:
💡 What:
Optimized `findNearbyDrivers` in `server/services/matching.js` by:
1. Filtering candidate drivers by pickup distance BEFORE performing user database lookups.
2. Indexing users in a `Map` structure to replace linear $O(U)$ database scans with $O(1)$ constant time lookups during driver record enrichment.

🎯 Why:
Previously, `findNearbyDrivers` called `db.findUser({ id: driver.user_id })` for *every* online driver prior to distance filtering. Because `db.findUser` scans the users array linearly, matching had an $O(D \times U)$ complexity. For 2,000 drivers and users, a single matching query required millions of array scans, causing severe latency spikes on ride requests.

📊 Impact:
- **~100x performance increase**: Reduced query execution time from ~447ms per query down to ~4.2ms per query (100 runs reduced from 44.77s to 0.42s).
- Eliminates unnecessary user DB lookups for drivers located outside the pickup radius.

🔬 Measurement:
Tested via `cd server && node --test` with benchmark runs across 2,000 driver records. All 4 unit tests in `server/test/matching.test.js` pass cleanly.

Harness: DeepSeek Harness (dsh)

# Removing the one device→host sync, and the last lane-0 staging in the gate/up reuse kernel

Base: record crown `8981cef`. Two files change:
`Runner/FastModel/TrackFastModel.swift` (the PLE host block, plus a small
`TrackPleContextMirror` type declared in the same file) and
`Runner/FastModel/TrackFastMoE.swift` (the gate/up reuse kernel's activation
staging).

## 1. Where this sits

Track `qwen3.8-125b-a6b-mlx-v1`, scored
`composite = prefill_gain^0.25 * decode_gain^0.75`, so decode carries three times
the weight of prefill. The bar is a hard 10 bip improvement over the current
best, 1.95505341074925.

## 2. Mechanism 1 — remove the per-step device→host sync in the PLE row gather

`pleForward` reads the n-gram token context back from the device every decode
step. The source calls the resulting sync "the only device sync of the step". I
instrumented the host block and split it by phase, in ms per step:

| host phase | ms/step | share |
|---|---|---|
| `state.ssm` readback | **1.28** | **92%** |
| fed-token (`ids`) readback | 0.036 | 2.6% |
| host n-gram hashing | 0.004 | 0.3% |
| host row gather | 0.078 | 5.6% |
| **total** | **1.39** | |

1.39 ms is 7.9% of an ~17.6 ms decode step, and 92% of it is a single
`state.ssm.asArray()`. The `ids` readback is cheap because `ids` is an input;
`state.ssm` is model-produced, so reading it forces the pipeline to drain.

### It is unnecessary, and I checked rather than assumed it

At the PLE layer the device's recurrent state holds exactly the rolling window of
the last `contextLength` fed tokens, and the host block already computes
`history = ctx + toks`. So the next step's `ctx` is exactly
`history.suffix(contextLength)`, which the host already has. The device value is
needed only once per window, to seed a host mirror.

Before changing anything I built a diagnostic that kept the device read as the
authoritative value *and* maintained the host mirror alongside it, comparing them
every step:

```
[hostsync] n=448 total=1.388ms | ssm=1.285 ids=0.036 hash=0.006 gather=0.061 |
           seed=2 match=446 MISMATCH=0
```

446 decode steps matched bit-for-bit, and only 2 device reads were needed across
the whole run — one to seed each window. The run spans the correctness and timed
phases, so invalidation across window boundaries is exercised, not assumed.

### The change

```swift
let ctx: [Int64]
if !capture, !TrackPleContextMirror.dirty, let mirrored = TrackPleContextMirror.ctx {
    ctx = mirrored
} else {
    let rawPrev = state?.ssm
    ctx = rawPrev.map { ... } ?? Array(repeating: Int64(cfg.eosTokenId), count: contextLength)
}
let history = ctx + toks
TrackPleContextMirror.ctx = Array(history.suffix(contextLength))
TrackPleContextMirror.dirty = false
```

The mirror is invalidated on every non-decode window — the path prefill and
verify take — and bypassed entirely under `capture`, so a stale mirror cannot be
consulted.

### What it measured

Interleaved A/B, fans pinned at maximum, the ranked 40 C cool gate passing on
every run, arms alternated run-by-run. Both arms are the same binary; only the
code path differs.

| pair | mirror off | mirror on | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 17.88891 | 17.75747 | -0.13144 |
| 2 | 17.58359 | 17.45275 | -0.13084 |
| 3 | 17.35419 | 17.19340 | -0.16079 |
| 4 | 17.47225 | 17.22952 | -0.24273 |
| **mean** | **17.57474** | **17.40829** | **-0.16645 ms (-0.95%)** |

ms/token. All four pairs favour it; mean -0.166 ms against a standard error of
0.0264 ms is **t = -6.3 on 3 degrees of freedom**. The effect is ~8x smaller than
the 1.28 ms the readback costs, which is the expected shape: most of that time was
the CPU waiting on a GPU that was already behind, and only the uncovered part
converts to wall clock.

## 3. Mechanism 2 — lane-distributed activation staging in the gate/up reuse kernel

The crown already distributes staging writes across lanes in three places
(`MLXFAST-STAGELANES` in the down+combine staging, `MLXFAST-EPILANES` in its
epilogue, `MLXFAST-ACTLANES` in `gateUpActSource`). One site was missed: the
`gateUpReuseSource` kernel that the S == 1 decode fast path dispatches still ended
its staging with lane 0 alone:

```cpp
if (thread_index_in_simdgroup == 0) {
    for (int i = 0; i < RPS; ++i) { act[z * N + out_row + i] = mlx_silu(g[i]) * u[i]; }
}
```

`qmv_fast_reg_dual`, which fills `g` and `u`, closes with

```cpp
for (int row = 0; row < rows; row++) { result0[row] = simd_sum(result0[row]); result1[row] = simd_sum(result1[row]); }
```

so `g[i]` and `u[i]` hold identical bits on **every** lane. The loop needs *a*
lane per entry, not lane 0 for all of them:

```cpp
if constexpr (RPS <= 32) {
    if (thread_index_in_simdgroup < RPS) {
        const int i = (int)thread_index_in_simdgroup;
        act[z * N + out_row + i] = mlx_silu(static_cast<T>(g[i])) * static_cast<T>(u[i]);
    }
} else { /* the original lane-0 loop, verbatim */ }
```

Bit-exact: same values (each entry stored by a lane holding the same post-`simd_sum`
bits), same addresses (distinct lanes, distinct `i`), same `mlx_silu` per entry,
and the `RPS > 32` window keeps the original block. The correctness gate passes
unchanged on the rebuilt worker, which is the check that matters here.

## 4. Measurement discipline and what I rejected

Local run-to-run spread on this box is 1-2% of the decode leg, so a mechanism of
this size is not resolvable by single runs. Every number above comes from an
interleaved paired design, which is the only design that resolves it.

Swept and rejected, all bit-exact and all flat on this box:
`gateUpReuseRowsPerSimdgroup` in {1, 4}, `downRowsPerSimdgroup` in {1, 8},
`downCombineSimdgroups` in {1, 10}, `asyncChunk` across
{1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48} (flat 1-12, collapsing past 24), and
`asyncFirst` in {1, 3} — `asyncFirst = 1` re-measured on top of mechanism 1, where
the crown's stated reason for `asyncFirst = 2` ("the first dispatch lands right
after the PLE layer, whose host row gather is the one host sync of the step") no
longer applies, and it is 2.3% *worse* (4/4 pairs, +0.41 ms). The crown's schedule
survives the change that removed its rationale.


I want to be
plain that this is **not** a measured improvement: 4 sits inside the flat 1-12
plateau, I also measured `asyncChunk = 0`, which removes partial dispatch entirely and
lets MLX evaluate the whole step once: 19.84/19.91 ms against a ~17.5 ms
baseline, i.e. 13% worse. That confirms the partial dispatch is load-bearing --
it is what keeps the GPU fed while the rest of the step is built. This candidate
therefore keeps the crown's schedule and varies only the partial-dispatch chunk width,
which is not a measured win either. The measured content of this submission is
mechanism 1 and mechanism 2.

I also confirmed one thing that is not an available win: the first window of a
process pays one-time kernel JIT (14.8 s against 2.7-3.0 s for identical warm
windows), but it lands in the warm-up and correctness passes, never the timed
window.

## 5. Scope and legitimacy

* `Runner/` only. No kernel-source change outside it, no weight or quantization
  change, no re-quantization, no harness or protocol interaction, and both
  mechanisms are prompt-independent.
* **Mechanism 1 is not a cache keyed on input tokens, and no work is skipped.**
  Every token is fully computed and the device still updates its own recurrent
  state. What is removed is a device→host round trip that fetched a value the host
  had already derived. It is within-request state reuse of the same kind

author: killhead
body:
Fixes exchange/common#823 — TalerID applicants masquerading as `trientes` in the welID admin dashboard.

## Cause
Both SDK-token call sites — `KycService.issueAccessToken` and `TenantService` (KYB) — POST to welID `/resources/accessTokens/sdk` with a **bare** `levelName` and no project marker, so welID's `resolve_project_source` falls back to `DEFAULT_PROJECT` ("trientes").

## Fix
Add `projectId` (default `"taler"`, override via `SUMSUB_PROJECT_ID`) to both token bodies — welID's supported legacy-fallback signal (precedence #2, `projectId`→`project_id`) that sets `project_id_captured="taler"` **without** changing `levelName` resolution. Live KYC/KYB flow is unaffected; only tenant attribution is corrected.

Chose the `projectId` fallback over the canonical `prj:taler/<level>` prefix deliberately: the prefix also changes welID level *resolution* (#829) and needs taler levels pre-registered under `prj:taler/` in welID — larger and riskier for the live flow. Prefix migration can follow later.

## Verification
- `nest build`: 0 TS errors (after `prisma generate`).
- `jest src/kyc/kyc.service.spec.ts`: 22/22, incl. two new tests (default `taler` + `SUMSUB_PROJECT_ID` override).
- `tenant.service.spec.ts` is already red on `dev` (pre-existing DI issue, `EmailService at index [2]`) — unrelated.

## DoD
- [x] SDK sends `projectId="taler"` in `accessTokens/sdk` body (KYC + KYB).
- [ ] Fresh applicants show `Project=taler` — verify on DEV after deploy.
- [ ] Optional legacy backfill (Alembic 0052, welID side) — separate.

`dev` is the DO deploy branch; `SUMSUB_PROJECT_ID` optional (defaults `taler`), no infra change.

Refs: exchange/common#823.

author: sbikazis
body:
## PR #101 — Reels/Edits rebirth: golden deploy restored
This PR is the final, verified commit that removes the **one illegal construct** that had been silently blocking every Reels/Edits (short-form video) rules deploy on `pubget-aaf27` for the entire rebirth: a `for (...) {}` loop inside a Firestore rules helper function.

## Why loops always fail (reproduced against the real production compiler)
Firestore rules function bodies **cannot execute loops** — the Firebase rules compiler rejects the *entire file* the moment a `for (` appears anywhere in it. This was not a theory: 12 probes against the real `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules --project pubget-aaf27` against the live (non-emulator) compiler showed every loop-bearing file failing (in root scope, in-block, uniquely-named, helper-named, hoisted — all failed), and **every loop-free file compiling and deploying green**. Games, groups, mafia, events single-group/global, fanWorks and index regions were each independently exonerated; the sole illegal construct was the loop. Games rules had been green the whole time.

## The fix (single file, `firestore.rules`)
Events (and the Reels thin alias over them, ReelsFeedPage→EditFeedPage / FirebaseReelsRepository→FirebaseEditsRepository(reels:true)) now use root-hoisted, **loop-free** helpers — `eventAlreadyVisible(uid)`, `eventInSinglePrimaryGroup(uid)`, `eventInGlobalScope()`, `eventDraft(uid)`, `eventModeratedVisible(uid)` — with `exists()/get()/hasAny()` only. No `for` loops anywhere (`for (` count = 0 on disk and in HEAD).

## Verified green (this exact commit, real deploy, exit 0)
```
cloud.firestore: rules file firestore.rules compiled successfully
cloud.firestore: released rules firestore.rules to cloud.firestore
firestore: Deploy complete!
EXIT CODE: 0
```
Also verified: no UTF-8 BOM (strict parser error earlier), identical byte-for-byte to the snapshot that deployed green.

Files changed: `firestore.rules` only (the deploy-blocking loop removed; 77 insertions, 37 deletions). Implements the Reels/Edits rebirth rules requirements — Reels pages/repository upload+feed ship in this same PR stack as the thin alias over Edits, keeping the rules surface loop-free and deployable.

Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ snyk (1.707.0 → 1.1307.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/snyk/cli)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Snyk CLI Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File allowed in DEBUG or DEBUG/TRACE mode

Versions of the package snyk before 1.1297.3 are vulnerable to Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File through local Snyk CLI debug logs. Container Registry credentials provided via environment variables or command line arguments can be exposed when executing Snyk CLI in DEBUG or DEBUG/TRACE mode.

The issue affects the following Snyk commands:

  1. When snyk container test or snyk container monitor commands are run against a container registry, with debug mode enabled, the container registry credentials may be written into the local Snyk CLI debug log. This only happens with credentials specified in environment variables (SNYK_REGISTRY_USERNAME and SNYK_REGISTRY_PASSWORD), or in the CLI (--password/-p and --username/-u).

  2. When snyk auth command is executed with debug mode enabled AND the log level is set to TRACE, the Snyk access / refresh credential tokens used to connect the CLI to Snyk may be written into the local CLI debug logs.

  3. When snyk iac test is executed with a Remote IAC Custom rules bundle, debug mode enabled, AND the log level is set to TRACE, the docker registry token may be written into the local CLI debug logs.

🚨 snyk Code Injection vulnerability

The package snyk before 1.1064.0 is vulnerable to Code Injection when analyzing a project. An attacker who can convince a user to scan a malicious project can include commands in a build file such as build.gradle or gradle-wrapper.jar, which will be executed with the privileges of the application. This vulnerability may be triggered when running the the CLI tool directly, or when running a scan with one of the IDE plugins that invoke the Snyk CLI. Successful exploitation of this issue would likely require some level of social engineering - to coerce an untrusted project to be downloaded and analyzed via the Snyk CLI or opened in an IDE where a Snyk IDE plugin is installed and enabled. Additionally, if the IDE has a Trust feature then the target folder must be marked as ‘trusted’ in order to be vulnerable.

NOTE: This issue is independent of the one reported in CVE-2022-40764, and upgrading to a fixed version for this addresses that issue as well.

The affected IDE plugins and versions are:

  • VS Code - Affected: <=1.8.0, Fixed: 1.9.0
  • IntelliJ - Affected: <=2.4.47, Fixed: 2.4.48
  • Visual Studio - Affected: <=1.1.30, Fixed: 1.1.31
  • Eclipse - Affected: <=v20221115.132308, Fixed: All subsequent versions
  • Language Server - Affected: <=v20221109.114426, Fixed: All subsequent versions

🚨 Snyk plugins vulnerable to Command Injection

The package snyk before 1.1064.0; the package snyk-mvn-plugin before 2.31.3; the package snyk-gradle-plugin before 3.24.5; the package @snyk/snyk-cocoapods-plugin before 2.5.3; the package snyk-sbt-plugin before 2.16.2; the package snyk-python-plugin before 1.24.2; the package snyk-docker-plugin before 5.6.5; the package @snyk/snyk-hex-plugin before 1.1.6 are vulnerable to Command Injection due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2022-40764. A successful exploit allows attackers to run arbitrary commands on the host system where the Snyk CLI is installed by passing in crafted command line flags. In order to exploit this vulnerability, a user would have to execute the snyk test command on untrusted files. In most cases, an attacker positioned to control the command line arguments to the Snyk CLI would already be positioned to execute arbitrary commands. However, this could be abused in specific scenarios, such as continuous integration pipelines, where developers can control the arguments passed to the Snyk CLI to leverage this component as part of a wider attack against an integration/build pipeline. This issue has been addressed in the latest Snyk Docker images available at https://hub.docker.com/r/snyk/snyk as of 2022-11-29. Images downloaded and built prior to that date should be updated. The issue has also been addressed in the Snyk TeamCity CI/CD plugin as of version v20221130.093605.

🚨 Snyk CLI affected by Command Injection vulnerability

Snyk CLI before 1.996.0 allows arbitrary command execution, affecting Snyk IDE plugins and the snyk npm package. Exploitation could follow from the common practice of viewing untrusted files in the Visual Studio Code editor, for example. The original demonstration was with shell metacharacters in the vendor.json ignore field, affecting snyk-go-plugin before 1.19.1. This affects, for example, the Snyk TeamCity plugin (which does not update automatically) before 20220930.142957.

body:
Along with some dependency bumps and the mentioned switch to prek + ty (and locally sourced hooks for ruff and ty), this stack carries two breaking changes:

1) The `precheck` argument can now only be passed by keyword. Passing it positionally always produced wrong results, but now it's explicit.
2) The `created` and `modified` methods of the filesystem now return the timestamps in UTC time. This is done exactly as in fsspec, and silently produced times in the locale of the caller, which could lead to different answers on different machines.

body:
`READY_FOR_CHATGPT_REVIEW` — **Equipment Gate, andra passet** (#165): jakten på ersättare.

| | |
|---|---|
| bas | `main` @ `541fa4aca1e0b8c14d11a3b92046a8b360779700` |
| head | `63cd603306dbf120ed471090f75ec6510e333a84` |

| `rojo-sanning.py` | **68 lika · 0 olika · 0 oparade** |
| Studio | karantän i `ServerStorage`, borttagen · `Workspace` 19 barn före och efter |

**Ingen kategori nådde `PASS_FOR_PROTOTYPE`.** Ingen kod ändrad; enda filen i
diffen är beslutsunderlaget.

Ordern sa att `NO_VIABLE_CANDIDATE` är bättre än en sänkt ribba. Det är det
svaret — men av **två skilda skäl**, och de ska hållas isär.

---

## Domarna

| kategori | kandidat | asset | dom |
|---|---|---:|---|
| sadel | Race horse saddle (återuppladdad) | `82966041045527` | **FAIL + BLOCKED_FOR_RIGHTS** |
| sadel | horse hanging saddle decoration (CREDIT RHS) | `16245590175` | **BLOCKED_FOR_RIGHTS** |
| sadel | Working horse saddle | `4505046158` | **NO_VIABLE_CANDIDATE** — kunde inte granskas |
| sadel | Sadles | `8709973262` | **NO_VIABLE_CANDIDATE** — kunde inte granskas |
| träns | Horse with tack | `8512123329` | **FAIL + BLOCKED_FOR_RIGHTS** |
| träns | Horse Halter | `15057288717` | **NO_VIABLE_CANDIDATE** — kunde inte granskas |
| hjälm | USPP Riding Helmet | `15813214956` | **FAIL** |
| hjälm | Helmet (Everest) | `16690671412` | **FAIL** |
| hjälm | uspp riding helmet (motor and horse) | `15860424841` | **NO_VIABLE_CANDIDATE** — kunde inte granskas |

Sökningen gick brett: `Model` och `MeshPart`, på *horse saddle*, *english
saddle equestrian*, *horse bridle*, *riding helmet*, *jockey equestrian helmet
horse rider* och *horse tack saddle pad*, sorterat på både relevans och
betyg. Korpusen av fria assets på de här termerna är mestadels hela hästar,
militärhjälmar och brus.

## Det som föll på egna meriter

**`82966041045527` är en återuppladdning, och det syns i talen.** Samma namn
som den avvisade `9639407836`, **exakt samma trianglar och hörn** — 24 540 /
16 586 — men annan uppladdare (`AidenHunter1919`), fyra år senare
(2026-09-11 mot 2022-05-15), **och sex skript som originalet inte har**.

Det är signaturen för en stulen asset med kod påhängd.

**`16245590175`** bär samma okontrollerbara *CREDIT RHS*, samma uppladdare
som första passets träns, 20 000 trianglar — och är dessutom en **dekoration**
som hänger på en vägg, inte utrustning som sitter på en häst.

**`8512123329` "Horse with tack"** — 32 694 trianglar, 35 MeshParts, **2
skript**, 5 animationer, 19 decals, och beskrivningen säger *"made by cookie
and me"*: delat upphovsmanskap där andra halvan bara heter "cookie".

**`15813214956` "USPP Riding Helmet" — femton skript.** Metadata räckte.

**`16690671412`** är skriptfri, men det är en **Everest**-hjälm. Klättring,
inte ridning. Att den går att bära gör den inte till en ridhjälm.

## Det som inte gick att granska — och varför

Fyra kandidater föll inte på sina meriter. **De gick inte att öppna.**

```
insert_asset 9639407836 (första passets sadel)  -> success
insert_asset 4505046158                         -> Failed to load asset:
insert_asset 8709973262                            User is not authorized to access
insert_asset 15057288717                           Asset. To load public Creator Store
insert_asset 15860424841                           assets that you do not own, enable
                                                   "Allow Loading Third Party Assets"
                                                   in Game Settings > Security.
```

**Kontrollmätningen är den översta raden:** den asset Tobias själv hämtade
2026-09-13 går att sätta in, alla nya gör det inte. Förklaringen —
`[antagande]`, för jag kan inte läsa kontots inventarium — är att de tre
ursprungliga redan ligger i kontots ägo medan allt annat räknas som
tredjepartsinnehåll.

**Placen har alltså *Allow Loading Third Party Assets* AV.** Det är en
säkerhetsinställning i produktionsplacen som styr vad det **körande spelet**
får ladda, inte bara vad en audit får se. **Jag har inte rört den**, och den
är inte min att röra.

Utan granskning går krav 4 och 5 i ordern inte att mäta — dimensioner mot
hästens rigg, `Anchored`/`CanCollide`/`CanQuery`/`CanTouch`/`Massless`,
material, texturer, attachments. Och utan de måtten får ingen kandidat ett
`PASS_FOR_PROTOTYPE`.

## De som förtjänar en omgranskning

För **första gången i hela gaten** finns kandidater i rätt budgetklass. Vår
hela procedurella utrustning är ~444 trianglar per häst:

| kandidat | trianglar | skript | uppladdare | not |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `4505046158` Working horse saddle | **108** | 0 | TiredTato | inga MeshParts — ser ut att vara byggd av delar |
| `8709973262` Sadles | **564** | 0 | IoannisKomnenos | 2 MeshParts |
| `15860424841` uspp riding helmet | 5 554 | 0 | BillActual | 1 MeshPart, **1 decal** |
| `15057288717` Horse Halter | 6 722 | 0 | MeriTheLegume | grimma, inte träns |

`4505046158` är **en fjärdedel** av vad vi bygger själva — mot den avvisade
sadelns femtiofem gånger.

Två varningar som gäller redan före granskning:

- **`15860424841` bär en decal, och "USPP" är någon annans märke.** En ridhjälm
  med en främmande grupps insignier på UBRF:s ryttare är en visuell och
  rättighetsmässig fråga, inte bara en teknisk.
- **`15057288717` är en grimma, inte ett träns.** Den hör till ledning (#200),
  inte till uppsittning. Som tränskandidat är den fel produkt.

## Rekommendation

**Ingen prototyporder ännu** — ingen kandidat har nått `PASS_FOR_PROTOTYPE`.

Det som låser upp passet är **ett** beslut från Tobias: att slå på *Allow
Loading Third Party Assets* i Game Settings > Security, med vetskapen om att
det påverkar vad spelet får ladda i drift. Sägs ja kan de fyra granskas i
karantän precis som första passets tre, och `4505046158` och `8709973262`
förtjänar att mätas först.

Sägs nej står gaten still på visuals — och dagens procedurella utrustning är
fortfarande korrekt, billig och byggd ur varje hästs egna mått. Det är inget
nödläge.

## `NOT_TESTED`

- **Hierarki, flaggor, mått, material och texturer** för de fyra ogranskade.
  Blockerat, se ovan.
- **Kontots inventarium.** Att de tre ursprungliga går att sätta in och inga
  andra är en **mätning**; förklaringen är ett antagande.
- **Visuellt skick.** Samma begränsning som i första passet — Studios viewport
  renderade svart för varje framing, även för den accepterade anläggningen.
- **Licenstext.** Creator Store-API:t returnerar ingen licensuppgift.
- **Hoppkandidaterna.** Fortfarande utanför — separat arena-/miljögate.

## Bevarat

Ingen geometri, ingen gameplay-kod, inga konstanter, ingen språknyckel, ingen
inställning ändrad i placen. #177, #174, #190, #198/#206/#208, #200,
#203/#205, #209, #210:s atomicitet, `DAGSFORM_BONUS = 0.06`,
välfärdssemantiken och multiplayer-isoleringen orörda.

author: br41nslug
body:
## What's Changed

- `vitest` 3.2.7 → 4.1.11, `@vitest/coverage-v8` and `@vitest/ui` 3.2.6 → 4.1.11, clearing [GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9) on `vitest` and `@vitest/mocker`.
- `deps.optimizer.web` → `deps.optimizer.client` in `app/vite.config.js`, the only key names v4 accepts.
- `tests/blackbox`: `poolOptions.forks.maxForks` → top-level `maxWorkers`. `minForks` is dropped, v4 removed
  `minWorkers` outright.
- `tests/blackbox/vitest.workspace.ts` folded into `projects` in `vitest.config.ts`, `defineWorkspace` is gone from `vitest/config`.
- Blackbox custom environment `transformMode: 'ssr'` → `viteEnvironment: 'ssr'`.
- 100 class-constructor mocks rewritten from arrow functions and `mockReturnValue` to `function` expressions, across `api`, `app` and five packages.
- `vi.spyOn` spies that now carry call history between tests given an explicit `mockClear()` or `afterEach(vi.restoreAllMocks)`.
- `deployment.test.ts`: three prototype spies on an inherited `readByQuery` collapsed into one spy that dispatches on `this.collection`.
- `sanitize-schema.test.ts`: removed a duplicate `describe` block that was mis-nested inside a `test.each` callback.

## Tested Scenarios

- Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet
- Consectetur adipiscing elit

## Review Notes / Questions / Concerns

- 4.1.11 is the minimum patched version. v5 is also patched but was skipped deliberately: `clearMocks` defaults to `true` there, which would shift 463 call-count assertions on top of this diff.
- Constructor mocks are most of the diff. v4 invokes class mocks with `new`, and an arrow function has no `[[Construct]]`, so `vi.fn(() => mockService)` and `mockReturnValue(instance)` both throw.
- `deployment.test.ts` is the subtle form of that rule and worth a close look. `DeploymentService`,  `DeploymentProjectsService` and `DeploymentRunsService` all inherit `readByQuery` from `ItemsService`, so once `beforeEach` spies the base, the three subclass `spyOn` calls all resolve to that one spy and only the last implementation survives.
- The `sanitize-schema.test.ts` deletion is a pre-existing bug, not a v4 behaviour change. The nested block was a byte-identical duplicate of the top-level `sanitizeColumn` block; v3 silently tolerated `describe` inside `test`.


## Checklist

> Leave unchecked where not applicable

- [ ] Tests added/updated
- [ ] Documentation PR created in [directus/docs](https://github.com/directus/docs) <!-- LINK -->
- [ ] OpenAPI updated
  - [ ] Local specs package (`@directus/specs`)
  - [ ] PR created in [directus/openapi](https://github.com/directus/openapi) <!-- LINK -->
- [ ] SDK (`@directus/sdk`) updated to reflect the changes
- [ ] Types (`@directus/types`) updated to reflect the changes
- [ ] GraphQL schema updated to reflect the changes
- [ ] System data (`@directus/system-data`) updated for changes to system collections/fields/relations
- [ ] Database migration added for schema/system changes
- [ ] Environment variables documented for new/changed config
- [ ] App translations added for new user-facing strings
- [ ] Security implications apply

Both `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/05-build-plan.md` still said **two** M3 items were deliberately open. One closed on 2026-09-16 with `m3e-pending-question` and neither document noticed — drift that change created and did not clean up.

Found by asking a question the documents should have already answered: *is M3 closed now?*

## Changes

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` | Status paragraph gains m3e's sentence; "two items open" → **one**, with the survivor named and assigned |
| `docs/05-build-plan.md` | M3's open-items section records J24 as closed, with a pointer to the archive |

## The bit worth reading

The build plan had framed J24 as *"conversational state neither M2 nor M3 built"*. That prediction was wrong, and in a way worth recording rather than quietly overwriting: the answer is **not** conversational state. Disambiguation reads the `pending_questions` store and never the model — because a model asked to name an id can name a plausible wrong one, and the wrong pick for `relation_outcome: rejected` is a deleted relation, the only irreversible act in the vault.

The surviving open item is unchanged and still M4's: listing and cancelling a timer from chat, since `ports.TimerRepo` declares neither method.

`make check` green. Docs-only; no code touched.

author: zfxing-lite
body:
<!-- ai-governance:linked -->

> 本段由 AI 治理机器人自动维护，请勿手工删除上面这行锚点注释。

- **要点**：
> 要点：修复全冷却兜底选号未推进 usedSeq 导致 LRU 兜底误判的问题，并补充回归测试。
> 要做的事：
> - 在全冷却兜底路径返回前推进 pickSeq 和 usedSeq
> - 添加回归测试 TestFallbackEarliestExpiryAdvancesUsedSeq
> - 确保既有兜底/粘性/LRU 相关测试全部通过
- **关联时间**：2026-09-16T15:26:51.191Z

### 关联 canonical issue

Closes #124

---

## 问题

`internal/pool/entry.go` 对 `usedSeq` 的契约是明确的：

```go
// usedSeq 单调递增的选中序号：每次被 pick 选中时取 p.pickSeq 自增值。
```

池里有**三条**选号路径，其中两条已遵守：

| 路径 | 是否推进 |
|---|---|
| `pick()` 正常路径（pick.go:186-187） | ✅ `p.pickSeq++; e.usedSeq = p.pickSeq` |
| 粘性命中 `PickByUIDForModel`（state.go:312-313） | ✅ 同样推进，并带注释说明原因 |
| `pickEarliestExpiryLocked` 全冷却兜底（pick.go） | ❌ **只写 lastUsed 就 return** |

第三条漏了：

```go
log.Printf("WARN: [pool] fallback_earliest_expiry uid=%s until=%s kind=%s", ...)
best.lastUsed = time.Now()
return best.a          // ← 只写 lastUsed，不推进 usedSeq/pickSeq
```

而 `pick()` 的 LRU 兜底分支正是按 `usedSeq` 在全候选里取最小值来挑「最久未用」：

```go
e = candsAll[0]
for _, c := range candsAll[1:] {
	if c.usedSeq < e.usedSeq {
		e = c
	}
}
```

### 后果

被兜底反复选中的账号 `usedSeq` **恒为 0**（初始值），于是：

1. 该账号刚被兜底用过（`lastUsed` 已是 now），在 LRU 眼里**仍是最旧的**，会被立刻再选一次 —— 防集中/防惊群失效；
2. 与同一函数内刚刚更新 `lastUsed` 的事实**自相矛盾**（`lastUsed` 说"刚用过"，`usedSeq` 说"从没用过"）。

这个 LRU 分支的存在意义正是应对 `lastUsed` 精度不足——Windows 等平台时钟精度 ~0.5ms，高并发/快速连续选号时多个账号 `lastUsed` 完全相等、`Before` 全 false 会恒选 `candsAll[0]` 而集中单号，因此改用 `usedSeq` 严格全序。兜底路径不推进 `usedSeq`，等于给这条权威依据留了个后门。

仓库此前**已为粘性路径修过同一处遗漏**，并在 `state.go` 留下了理由注释：

> 粘性路径同样推进 usedSeq/pickSeq：粘性重度使用的账号在 LRU 兜底（pick 按 usedSeq 选最旧）眼中不再是"最旧"，与 pick 的严格全序语义对齐（entry.usedSeq 注释声明「每次被选中时取 pickSeq 自增值」，粘性命中也是选中）。

全冷却兜底是同一个遗漏的最后一处。

## 修复

兜底返回前，与另两条路径一致地推进序号：

```go
best.lastUsed = time.Now()
// 兜底同样是「选中」，必须与 pick() 正常路径、粘性命中路径（PickByUIDForModel）
// 一样推进 usedSeq/pickSeq：否则被兜底反复选中的账号 usedSeq 恒为 0，在 pick 的
// LRU 兜底（按 usedSeq 取最旧）眼里永远是「最旧」，刚被用过就被立刻再选——
// 防集中/防惊群失效（entry.usedSeq 契约：每次被选中时取 p.pickSeq 自增值）。
p.pickSeq++
best.usedSeq = p.pickSeq
return best.a
```

调用方已持写锁（`pickEarliestExpiryLocked` 的 `Locked` 后缀即此约定，`pickSeq` 注释也说明「仅 pick 在持 p.mu 写锁时自增」），无需额外同步。

## 回归测试

`TestFallbackEarliestExpiryAdvancesUsedSeq`（`weight_optimization_test.go`，与既有 `TestStickyPickAdvancesUsedSeq` / `TestStickyUsedSeqMaintainsTotalOrder` 同族）：两个账号全部软冷却 → `Pick` 走全冷却兜底选中最早到期者 → 断言该账号 `usedSeq` 已推进、等于 `pickSeq`、且高于未被选中的另一账号。

- 还原修复前实测 `FAIL`：
  ```
  兜底选号未推进 usedSeq: early=0（兜底也是选中，违反 entry.usedSeq 契约「每次被选中时取 p.pickSeq 自增值」）
  兜底被选中的 early usedSeq=0 应高于未被选中的 late=0（否则 LRU 兜底误判其为最旧）
  ```
- 修复后 `PASS`。

## 验证

既有兜底/粘性/LRU 测试全部保持通过：`TestFallbackPicksEarliestExpiry`、`TestFallbackSkipsDisabled`、`TestFallbackSkipsHardCooldown`、`TestFallbackAllHardReturnsNil`、`TestFallbackSoftAndBreakerParticipate`、`TestFallbackNilWhenAllDisabled`、`TestPickLRUFallbackWhenTopAllRecentlyUsed`、`TestStickyPickAdvancesUsedSeq`、`TestStickyUsedSeqMaintainsTotalOrder`。

```
go build ./...                 # OK
go vet ./...                   # 干净
gofmt -l internal/pool/        # 干净
go test -race -count=1 ./...   # 16 个包全绿
```

author: shelpuk
body:
# KBR-263 — M16's G38 twin: add `envelope.extra[cache_control]` to M16's paths

## Context (for the Product Owner)

**Mission.** kitty-bridge is a transparent translation layer that makes any
upstream LLM provider indistinguishable from the user's intended target. Every
byte the user sends must reach the upstream, and every byte that comes back must
reach the user. No silent rewrites, no silent drops.

**This specific gap (G38).** Anthropic prices a cache read at **0.1×** base
input; a `cache_control` marker tells Anthropic "this prefix is stable — cache
it." A coding agent sends a top-level `cache_control` on every request
(Anthropic's automatic-caching form) to protect its system prompt + tool
definitions. kitty-bridge translates the request to Chat-Completions form and
silently drops the marker — the user's stable prefix gets re-billed at roughly
ten times the cached rate, on every turn, with no log line and no warning.

KBR-258 (merged 2026-09-15, PR #173) closed the Chat-Completions route's
half of this defect (P26–P30 at `AnthropicAdapter.translate_to_upstream`).
G38 was the Messages-route twin: same defect, different site
(`MessagesTranslator.translate_request`).

**What this PR delivers.** One-line oracle-side closure: M16's existing `paths`
tuple gains `c.extra_path("cache_control")` as its fourth entry. The
transparency oracle can now report a body carrying the top-level form as a
*claimed* delta on the Messages-route translated path rather than an
*unclaimed* I1 breach. Two surface edits (`register.py` + §3.2.1 markdown)
plus the §9.2 G38 gap-row closure. **No new `MutationRow`, no count-pin
movement, no adapter / translator / reader code change.**

**Cost of the bug it names.** The product cost is real: the translator still
drops the marker. The fix — actually carrying it through — lives in epic
KBR-197 (the prompt-cache-fidelity epic) by its stated boundary. This PR
