author: gregorgullwi
body:
## Summary

Out-of-line destructors on class templates were routed through constructor-only attachment, while constructors declared by nested member class templates were discarded during parsing. This left no authoritative declaration node for identity-based attachment and caused valid definitions, including out-of-line = default definitions, to fail during instantiation.

This change preserves nested member-class constructors as constructor declarations, resolves destructors through the same source-member identity boundary without treating them as constructors, and replays nested constructor bodies and initializer expressions with the combined enclosing-class and member-class template environment. Missing pattern-owner metadata no longer triggers a name-based recovery path; substitution simply omits the current-instantiation rewrite when there is no canonical pattern owner.

The new regression exercises observable out-of-line destructor behavior, a nested member-class constructor using both template heads in its initializer, and the corresponding out-of-line defaulted destructor and constructor forms. The previously documented limitation is removed from KNOWN_ISSUES.md.

### What changed
- Rebuild current-season RB recent-production and efficiency inputs from verified regular-season TalentX game events so every active RB is compared on the same season window.
- Count verified RB regular-season games before the generic usage fallback, preventing one game from becoming a fake nine-game sample.

- Add a regression test reproducing the Kenneth Walker vs. Jahmyr Gibbs failure shape.

### Why
The live artifact showed Kenneth Walker III at ~$223 while Jahmyr Gibbs was ~$129, Bijan Robinson ~$112, and James Cook III ~$103. Walker's stored `recentProduction` was his 2025 full-season line while the others used 2026 Week 1, his one current game was treated as a nine-game sample from generic usage, and sparse award points produced an artificial achievement gap. This fixes those systemic cohort inconsistencies without player-specific price overrides.

Scope is intentionally limited to issue #3 only:
- move provider network calls outside the task's DB transaction
- claim queued messages before send to prevent concurrent duplicate workers
- persist permanent failures durably as FAILED
- reset transient failures to QUEUED before Celery retry
- keep existing SENT/DELIVERED/READ idempotency and Hosted AI isolation
- include dedicated regression tests for transaction boundaries and failure lifecycle

This PR excludes unrelated staging documentation and other staging-only changes. The same code has already passed staging CI and an isolated staging deployment.

author: czeslavo
body:
**Description of your changes:**

Runs every controller of the operator binary on one controller-runtime manager and cache, without changing what any of them does. This is the plumbing for moving the ScyllaDBDatacenter controller onto a read-your-writes client, so that it decides from a cache that has observed its own writes.

- **`pkg/controllermanager`** owns the manager: the operator's scheme, the existing resync period as the cache sync period, a read-your-writes client, a one-minute default reconciliation timeout for the controllers that will be registered through controller-runtime, controller-runtime's package logger routed to klog, and neither metrics nor health probes served. Leader election stays in `pkg/leaderelection` around the manager, so the lease and the standby behavior are unchanged. The controller wiring moved here from `pkg/cmd/operator/operator.go`; the multi-datacenter part sits in its own file. The manager also decides whether the ScyllaDBMonitoring controller runs, from the presence of the Prometheus Operator CRDs.
- **The `InformerFor` bridge** hands the legacy controllers their client-go informers and listers from the manager's cache, so a controller on controller-runtime and one that is not share the same informer for a kind: one informer per kind in the process.
- **`pkg/ctrlclient`** adapts a controller-runtime client to the function-shaped interfaces `resourceapply` and `controllerhelpers` take (apply, prune and claim controls, object control), provides client-backed Pod and Secret listers, and converts metav1 options field by field, since controller-runtime's option structs overwrite `Raw`.
- **`kubecrypto.CertificateManager`** takes an `ObjectControl` per kind, with the typed-client construction kept for its current callers.
- **controller-runtime v0.25.1**, which fixes the resource version parse error of a subresource create through the read-your-writes client that we hit in the PoC.

**Which issue is resolved by this Pull Request:**
Resolves https://scylladb.atlassian.net/browse/OPERATOR-417

author: kirill-markin
body:
When the workspace of a running chat turn stops being accessible to the user, the web app now logs a non-error `workspace_unavailable` event instead of several `action: "error"` lines, so `WebErrorEventsAlarm` no longer fires for it.

## Incident

On 2026-09-16 the post-deploy live smoke cleanup deleted its workspace while a chat run was active (request `bb55de84-7ba3-4822-b034-990e2426c9f8`). `/expense-tracker/web` got three `User … is not a member of workspace …` error lines: two from the run heartbeat (`stage: "stream"`) and one from the run's terminal path (`stage: "agent"`). The smoke flake that triggered it is fixed in #325.

## Change

- `logger.ts`: new `ChatWorkspaceUnavailableEvent` with `action: "workspace_unavailable"` in the `LogEvent` union.
- `chat/logging.ts`: `createChatErrorLogEvent` returns that event for a `WorkspaceAccessError`, so the runtime, fresh-session, and existing-session call sites inherit it. Every other error keeps the `error` shape.
- `runtime.ts`: a heartbeat touch that fails with `WorkspaceAccessError` clears the heartbeat interval without logging; the run's next workspace-scoped write logs the single event.
- `tools.ts`: a tool call that hits the same error logs `workspace_unavailable`. What the model sees is unchanged.
- Tests cover the classification, the tool log, and a runtime replay of the incident: heartbeat stops after the failure and exactly one `workspace_unavailable` line is logged.

## Not changed

- The alarm metric filter in `infra/aws/lib/monitoring.ts`.
- API routes, which already answer this error with a 409 and no error log.
- `apps/sql-api` and what the chat user sees when the workspace disappears.

author: 92khsang
body:
## Summary

Claude Code loads path-scoped rules when it reads a file. Codex has no read tool, so this PR finds the files a Codex tool call reads or changes: `apply_patch` headers, path fields of tools such as `view_image`, and a best-effort reading of `Bash` commands. The hook runtime (a later PR) feeds these paths to rule discovery; nothing is wired into `c2c-rulesync hook` yet.

## Changes

* `src/c2c_rulesync/touched.py`: `touched_paths(tool_name, tool_input, cwd, home)` returns normalized absolute paths. It tolerates a non-object `tool_input`, which Codex sends when a tool's arguments are not valid JSON.
* `src/c2c_rulesync/patch.py`: `*** Add File:`, `*** Update File:`, `*** Delete File:` and `*** Move to:` headers between `*** Begin Patch` and `*** End Patch`, trimmed as Codex's parser trims them (only on the right inside an `*** Update File:` section), with lines split at line feeds only. Unified diff markers and header-like lines outside a patch are ignored.
* `src/c2c_rulesync/shell.py`: a POSIX lexer (quotes, `$'...'`, escapes, line continuations, comments, here-documents, `$(...)` found with the lexer itself, backquotes, `<(...)`, subshells, `(( ))`, `[[ ]]` and all separators including newline and `&`) and a reader of:
  * operands of `cat`, `nl`, `head`, `tail`, `less`, `more`, `bat`, `tee`, `diff`, and of `sed`, `awk`, `grep`, `rg`, `jq` and `perl -e` after their script, pattern or filter, with option clusters such as `grep -nC 3`;
  * `git diff|show|log` paths after `--` or existing files without it, `git show REV:PATH`, and `git blame`'s file, with `-C`, `-c` and other global options;
  * redirection targets other than `/dev/*` and descriptor duplication;
  * `apply_patch` here-documents and arguments, and `-c` scripts or here-documents of `bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh`;
  * wrappers (`env`, `sudo`, `timeout`, `nice`, `nohup`, `time`, `command`, `builtin`, `exec`, `stdbuf`), also called by path, and assignments;
  * `cd` tracking, a `pushd`/`popd` stack, substitutions resolved in their command's directory, unknown directories after `cd -`, `cd $X` and bare `cd`, and `~` expansion.
  Words the shell would expand (variables, command output, unquoted globs and brace expansions), existing directories and `find` are left out. Work is bounded at 20,000 commands and 16 nesting levels.
* `tests/test_touched.py`: 161 tests, including every `touched.rs` case of codex-path-rules that still applies and the defects the port fixes (newline and `&` separators, here-document bodies, subshells, `bash -lc` with following commands, empty arguments, comments, redirections, prefix commands, git global options, `~`, unknown `cd` targets, `Move to`, trimmed headers).
* `docs/behavior.md`: new "Which tool calls load rules" section.

## Verification

* [x] `uv run pytest`: 324 passed. `uv run ruff check`, `uv run ruff format --check` and `uv run mypy` pass.
* [x] A review checked the lexer against bash (`bash -n` and word splitting with `printf`) and the patch reader against the Codex rust-v0.154.0 sources; its findings are fixed with regression tests (`test_review_cases` and the tests after it).
* [x] 150,000 random commands from shell fragments, NUL and lone surrogates: no exception, at most 0.2 ms each. Adversarial sizes stay bounded: `"cd a; " * 200000` 0.73 s, `"cat a\n" * 300000` 0.96 s, a 3 MB here-document inside `$(...)` 0.07 s, 5,000 nested `$(` under 0.01 s.

## Related issues

None.

author: fw-bot
body:
When a record disappears from a theme's data files, updating that theme deletes its per-website copies. The context built for `copy_ids` in `_process_end_unlink_record` used the literal `'MODULE_UNINSTALL_FLAG'` instead of the constant, and passed it as a positional dict, which replaces the whole context rather than extending it.

`ir.ui.view.unlink` therefore did not cascade to the inheriting views and the `inherit_id` foreign key refused the deletion, aborting the theme update.

Reported by: https://github.com/odoo/odoo/issues/286171

Forward-Port-Of: odoo/odoo#288548

## 何が違っていたか

deploy 対象 4 つのうち、**conclair だけ `README.md` が日本語**で、英語版が存在しませんでした。

| repo | README.md | 日本語版 |
|---|---|---|
| cognilens | 英語 | `README_ja.md` |
| lexora | 英語 | `README.ja.md` |
| prismind | 英語 | `README.ja.md` |
| **conclair** | **日本語** | **無し** |

## 直した内容

- 日本語の本文は **`README.ja.md` へそのまま移動**。このファイルへの変更は言語切替リンクの 2 行だけです（元の `README.md` との diff で確認できます）
- `README.md` は同じ文書の英語版。**節の順序・コマンド・表をすべて対応**させています（コードフェンス外の見出しが en/ja とも 24 個で一致）
- 切替リンクは lexora と同じ形（`**[日本語版はこちら](README.ja.md)**` / `**[English version](README.md)**`）

`README_ja.md`（cognilens 式）ではなく **`.ja.md`** を採ったのは、3 つ中 2 つが既にそうであることと、`pyproject.toml` の `readme = "README.md"` が英語版を指すようになり、外から来た読み手が最初に当たる想定と合うためです。

## 付随して直したもの

`docs/usage-cheatsheet.md` が `README.md` を 2 箇所参照していて、うち 1 つは**日本語の節名**（`"API クイックリファレンス"`）を指していました。移動後は dangling になるので両方 `README.ja.md` に向け直しています。cheatsheet 自体が日本語なので、そちらが自然な参照先です。

## 触っていないもの

- **cognilens の `README_ja.md`（アンダースコア）**も少数派ですが、今回の依頼は conclair なので変えていません。揃えるなら別途
- `pyproject.toml` の `readme = "README.md"` は変更不要（英語版を指したままで正しい）

## What
- **Gift cards fund sticker + sales tax.** `funding_target` = approved sticker total × (1 + cost-stack tax %), recomputed with the lines, the cards and the stack. Every consumer reads it; the till-overrun warning is gone — that number IS the target now. Header: *Approved $390.00 · To fund $422.18 incl. 8.25% tax*.
- **The buyer's list stays open until they close it.** No "send": every add is a question (card to Telegram). **Close the request** = list complete → the desk may fund. No card can be recorded until the list is closed and every line is decided. **Re-open to add more** until the receipt is in: issued cards stay, new lines raise the target, the desk records a top-up. Decisions on a funded request are pending-only (frozen approvals). Telegram gets `buying_request_closed` / `buying_request_reopened` on the same webhook (Make routes on `event`), and every payload carries `env: dev|prod`.
- A pending pair is the buyer's to withdraw (×) while the list is open; "Pull it back" is gone.
- Lines ordered by shoe (first asked about) then size, small → large.
- Financial audit panel says it was recorded (it saved and looked like it did nothing).
- Queue + request show "Buyer still adding" / "List closed".

Docs: `docs/context/buy-cart.md`, SOP articles. E2E: 6 new tests in `buy-cart.spec.js` (73/73 green), milestones spec updated. Tested end to end against the live Make scenario from the dev instance (BC-4255: photo card, buttons, closed/reopened notes, tap recorded on dev).

body:
#### 87e263d95e83a83776966c8c790fcc03d7823619 
[JSC] WASM debugger tests: fix a prologue-attach flake and a silent JSC exit
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=324357
rdar://187592091

Reviewed by NOBODY (OOPS!).

Two independent test-infrastructure fixes.

MultiInstanceUnreachableStepTestCase flaked under -p. An attach can land in a wasm
prologue, one of the two safepoints JSC services interrupts at, and a prologue stop
is reported at the function's first body instruction because setPrologueStopData
builds the address from callee->bytecode(). A test that breakpoints that address
therefore has LLDB believing the process is already stopped on the site: the next
resume runs z0/step/Z0, lifting the patch exactly when the program arrives, so the
arrival is never reported. That only loses a test when something stops the debugger
before execution comes back round, which is why 26 other tests breakpoint a first
instruction and still pass. Here the step lands on `unreachable`, so the resume
traps and the first `c` reports the trap instead of breakpoint 2.

multi-instance-unreachable.js therefore carries two leading nops: the first keeps
`unreachable` itself off the first instruction, which is the permanent form of the
same collision, and the second does the same for this test's breakpoint. The four
tests on that fixture move up a byte. The bare si gains a pattern for where the step
landed, which makes the dis that followed it redundant.

DEBUGGER_READY is printed by the JS fixture, so it says nothing about whether the
debug server bound its port. JSC exits when it cannot bind and reports that only
under --verbose-wasm-debugger, so the session waited out its full 60 s and then
blamed the missing banner rather than the exit. The wait now polls the process and
raises as soon as it is gone, quoting the exit code -- 60 s becomes 0.1 s. A bind
that fails without taking the process down is still caught after the wait as before.

body:
## Waarom

Op het rapport stond "Is dit werkelijk een buitenstof?" op 123/124 beantwoord, met koppelingen als `vochtgedrag_buiten → country_of_manufacture` en `gebruiksdoel → martindale`. Twee problemen: één kenmerk volstond om een vraag te beantwoorden, en de koppelvoorstellen waren slecht.

## Wat er verandert

**Alle kenmerken nodig** (scanversie 6.0.0)
- Een vraag is pas beantwoord als elk kenmerk waar hij op leunt er staat. Binnen één kenmerk volstaat nog één van zijn kolommen.
- `modus: een` in een lijst wordt niet meer gevolgd; de lezer zegt dat erbij.
- Generatieprompt en plugin-naslag: noem alleen de kenmerken die het antwoord werkelijk dragen.

**Koppelvoorstellen**
- Elk blok van 100 kenmerken ziet alle kolommen. Eerst kregen latere blokken alleen wat nog vrij was, en moesten ze kiezen uit de restjes.
- Het model wijst per koppeling één waarde uit de kolom aan als bewijs. `readProposals` (`src/semantic/prompt.ts`) houdt alleen wat een echt getoonde waarde aanwijst.
- `claude-opus-5` (effort medium, structured output) in plaats van Haiku 4.5; vier blokken tegelijk. Categorieën, facetten en markt blijven op Haiku.
- De opdrachten staan in een eigen module, zodat `scripts/mapping-eval.ts` precies meet wat live draait.

## Gemeten

De Groot + woontextielbank, 98 open kenmerken:

| Model | Voorstellen | Fout of twijfel |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | 31 | `weefdichtheid → martindale`, `voorraad_m → roll_length`, hele waardenrij als bewijs |
| Sonnet 5 | 38 | `meubeltype → categories`, `toplaag → coated` |
| Opus 5 | 31–33 | `merk → supplier`, `meubeltype_advies → categories`; vond `machine_washable` en `sustainable` |

Ongeveer $0,20 en 80 s per blok van 100 kenmerken.

## Niet in deze PR

- Koppelingen die al bewaard zijn, blijven staan; die haalt de merchant zelf weg.
- Het browsermodel (zonder sleutel) is ongewijzigd.

## Controle

`npm test` (284), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`. De route is lokaal getest: vochtgedrag bleef ongekoppeld, lichtechtheid ging naar `lightfatness`.

author: msdianprince-7
body:
Fixes #42277

## Summary

When a published app is called by an end user (service API / web app), the LLM node never gets `#context_files#`, even though the same workflow works in Studio preview. There's no error, the attachments are just dropped.

The issue author's analysis was right: the first guard in `DifyRetrieverAttachmentLoader.load()` is the one returning `[]`, because `granted_retriever_segment_ids` is empty by the time the LLM node reads it. The reason the grant disappears is in how the graph engine runs nodes, not in the retrieval code.

`grant_retriever_segment_access()` records the grant by calling `ContextVar.set()` with a new copy of the `FileAccessScope`. But graphon's worker enters the run's `execution_context` around every node, and `ExecutionContext` / `FlaskExecutionContext.enter()` restores the contextvars snapshot that was taken when the run started (`for var, val in context_vars.items(): var.set(val)`). So once the knowledge retrieval node finishes, the next node starts from the original scope with no grants. It happens on the same worker thread too, so it isn't a thread issue.

Accounts don't hit this because `is_retriever_segment_access_granted()` only checks the set when `user_from == END_USER`, which is why Studio preview works.

## Changes

- `FileAccessScope` now keeps its granted upload file IDs and retriever segment IDs in a small lock-protected container that the scope object references. `grant_*` add to that container instead of replacing the scope in the context var, so every copy of the context for the run sees the same grants.
- `granted_upload_file_ids` and `granted_retriever_segment_ids` are still there as read-only `frozenset` properties, so callers like `DatabaseFileAccessController` don't change.
- Grants are still per scope. Each request binds a new `FileAccessScope`, so nothing is shared between runs or users, and the loader's second check (the segment has to be in the LLM node's selected context) is unchanged.

The upload-file grants had the same problem. It didn't cause a visible bug because the attachment loader grants the upload files again inside the LLM node, but they now carry over between nodes as well.

## Tests

- `test_file_access_grants_survive_execution_context_restore_between_nodes` captures the context the same way the workflow entry does, grants inside one "node", then checks the grant from a later "node" on the same worker thread and on a different one. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.
- `test_file_access_grants_do_not_leak_between_scopes` checks that a grant made under one scope isn't visible under a new scope for the same user.
- Existing file access, retrieval, node runtime and app generator tests still pass.

### Defect found and fixed by the live runs

The headless branch's post-send poll read the captured `agent_settled` `ctx`; the extension-initiated nested run replaces the session, so a retry chain's second poll threw pi's stale-session `assertActive` error — an uncaught **Extension error** on every multi-attempt run. `main` under the same harness produces none. author: baziyer
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

Factory controls shared a revision with run activity. Deployment mistook normal settlement for an operator change, and same-value/stale-identical control replay could erase an operator's explicit stop intent.

Use the existing factory revision only for explicit controls. Every accepted dispatch/capacity command requires exact revision authority and advances it, including a same-value stop. Admission and settlement preserve their timestamp authority and publish their existing task/run invalidations; event Head still refreshes browser activity and counts. Remove their redundant factory invalidations.

Deployment reads controls and active count in one snapshot, drains against its unchanged owned pause revision, and restores only that revision. A pre-install timeout restores the owned pause; operator changes or uncertain installation do not. Delete settlement arithmetic and the intermediate CAS retry loop entirely. No commands are replayed.

The initial upgrade from older activity-revision/replay semantics needs the documented controlled operator pause/drain/prepared install/live identity check. Automatic restoration applies only after the updated daemon and CLI are verified. The shared CLI exposes definite stale revision refusal for diagnosis; it does not trigger retries.

Production delta: +46/-42, net +4. Removed two ambiguous control no-op/replay branches, obsolete change boolean, two activity revision increments and redundant factory invalidations, settlement accounting and restoration retry. No schema, protocol field, dependency, service, ownership token or persistent state added.

## Validation

- 20 Python checks PASS, including actual subprocess settlement, initially enabled/disabled origins, drain timeout, explicit operator changes, installation refusal and uncertain/refused command non-replay.
- Shared kernel two-actor tests prove explicit operator stops before and during deployment pause invalidate stale restoration. Old source fails these authority assertions.
- Full kernel short suite PASS51.171s. Actual browser admission/settlement snapshots and STATE_WATCH regression PASS0.412s: active counts0→1→0, advancing event Head, unchanged control revision. Original activity-revision production overlay fails that regression deterministically.
- The first protected run exposed four obsolete daemon API Head/revision expectations. Updated those assertions to current explicit control and activity semantics; the full DaemonDispatches/capacity/browser activity family PASS1.213s. No production change in that correction.
- The configured controller performs App review at this exact head; protected combined-tree full macOS CI is required. No deployment claimed here.

Refs #726

author: ayaangazali
body:
Closes #2003.

Type: Feature

## What is wrong today

Nothing survives a `max_loops="auto"` run except the final output. An agent that works out a good multi-step sequence for a recurring job re-derives it from scratch on the next run, at full planning cost, every time.

The loading half of this already exists: `SkillsManager` discovers `SKILL.md` files under `skills_dir`, keeps name and description in memory (Tier 1), folds the matching ones into the system prompt per task, and pulls a full body on demand (Tier 2). What was missing is anything that writes one.

## What this change does

`SkillsManager.save_skill(name, description, steps)` writes `skills_dir/<slug>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter and a numbered step list, and the autonomous loop calls it once a run finishes, recording the subtasks that reached `completed` in execution order. The file is read back by the existing loader with no new plumbing.

The artifact is a plan fragment, not code. It can be diffed, edited by hand, committed or deleted, and it cannot do anything the agent could not already do with the tools it has: it only shortens the path. That is the property the issue asks for, and it is why this does not need the sandboxing and trust decisions that tool synthesis (#2002) does.

```markdown
---
name: publish_release_notes
description: Collect merged PRs since the last tag and write release notes.
---

# Steps

1. read the git log since the previous tag
2. group changes by type
3. write notes to RELEASES.md
```

**Promotion is explicit approval, not one success.** The issue asks for repetition or approval before a sequence becomes a skill; this takes approval, as `Agent(skill_accretion=True)`. It is off by default, and with it off the loop writes nothing, so no existing agent changes behaviour. Frequency-based promotion needs run history that is not stored yet, so it is not attempted here.

Failed and skipped subtasks are left out: a skill is what worked, not what was tried.

## Not in this change

Parameterisation. A recorded sequence is the concrete steps the run took, so a path or a filename in a step is recorded literally. Extracting the variables is the real work the issue names, and it wants its own design (which parameters, inferred how, substituted when the skill is used). Recording the sequence is the half that is useful on its own, and it is what a later parameterisation pass would build on.

## Verification

Offline, no network:

- `tests/agents/test_skills_manager.py`: a saved skill round-trips through `load_metadata`, a description containing YAML punctuation (`Answer: is 3:1 fine?`) survives the frontmatter, and nothing is written with no steps or no skills directory.
- `tests/agents/test_autonomous_loop.py`: an opted-in run leaves a skill carrying both completed steps in order, a default run leaves the directory empty, and a subtask that ended `failed` is excluded.

All six fail on `master`. `tests/agents`: 331 passed, with the same 3 failures that are already on `master` (`test_agent_marketplace_handler` error-identity pair and `test_llm_manager` delegation) and unrelated to this diff.

author: wingedguardian
body:
#2079 and #2085 each shipped with an accepted finding I deferred rather than looping their review rounds. This closes all three. They are one shape: **a check standing in for something it did not actually verify.**

| | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| unit-path allowlist | read only `argv[0]` | every path-looking token |
| installer enablement | `is-enabled` **exit code** | requires the literal `enabled` state |
| subcommand bypass | `[ -d "$HOME/tmp" ]` | the slot path's own validated resolution |

## The part worth reading

**Widening the first one moved the narrowness rather than removing it.** Going from a positional check to a classifier put the same flaw inside the predicate, where it failed silently in *both* directions. Measured against a table built from systemd's grammar — not from the diff — **12 of 12 wrong**:

- Dropping a token that matched no start-character is **fail-open**, and systemd allows `@ + ! !! :` beyond the `-` I stripped. `ExecStart=+%h/genesis/x.sh` produced *no tokens at all*.
- `.split()` leaves quotes attached, so `/bin/bash -c '%h/genesis/x.sh'` was invisible — and that `-c '...'` shape **already ships** in `config/genesis-guardian-watchman.service`.
- The `$`/`%` catch-alls flagged `ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID` — *the* documented reload idiom — and advised replacing it with `__REPO_DIR__`. That advice ends with the token allowlisted or the test weakened.

Fixed by unquoting with `shlex`, stripping the full prefix set from `argv[0]` only, and requiring a separator before judging a root. **25/25 correct** after; 0 offenders across all 23 shipped sources, unchanged.

The cells are now parametrized from the **format's grammar**. That distinction is the lesson: *"all 23 shipped sources still pass"* only measures the corpus the author already handled, which is exactly why the first version looked right.

## The other two

**`is-enabled` exit 0 ≠ durable.** It also succeeds for `enabled-runtime`, which lives under `/run` and is gone after a reboot. Verified live: real units read `enabled`; two real `static` units exit 0 and are now correctly rejected.

**The bypass accepted any directory that existed.** Existing ≠ ours, writable, or private — a root-owned `sudo` leftover would have been handed to `claude install`/`update`. The slot path already did this properly, so that loop moved into one `_cc_resolve_tmpdir` both call rather than becoming a third copy; the defect being fixed *is* drift between copies. It also no longer fails silently, which made the scenario the block exists for the one that failed undiagnosably.

## Also removed: a comment that was false

`cc-slot.sh` claimed the bashrc wrapper carries a twin of the temp loop needing hand-sync. It does not and never did — that block has no temp handling, and the loop exists nowhere else in the repo. It sat four lines under new text explaining that a second copy *was* the defect.

Two smaller things the audit caught in my own tests: a drift guard whose `count() >= 3` could not trip (one of the four mentions is prose), and a comment describing a rejection branch the test never reaches.

## Verification

- **Verify-RED on each fix**, restores hash-verified: reverting the state check, the `-d` check, and the old `argv[0]` helper each fails the right test for the right reason.
- **Live e2e** against the real script and real `claude`: ephemeral subcommand → 7 servers, zero tmux calls; `gateway` → keeps its slot; bare session → still pins `TMPDIR=~/.genesis/cc-tmp`, so the extraction preserved the door's behaviour.
- **200 tests pass**; ruff clean; `bash -n` clean on both scripts.

**Not claimed:** that `_path_tokens` is complete. It is an allowlist over a grammar I enumerated, not a systemd parser — a construct outside that grammar has no cell and would pass in silence. Stated so the next reader knows what the table covers.

E2E: the live run above is the end-to-end proof; `mcp list` through the door and a bare session both exercise the restructured resolution against the real binary. Post-merge, a bypassed `claude update` on a box with an unusable `~/tmp` should now print the temp-dir warning rather than proceeding silently.

author: luish18
body:
Adds a harness that takes a group of ONNX models, sweeps the parameters a designer controls when generating RTL, and reports which of them actually matter — with a Pareto front over cycles, modelled area and modelled energy.

This answers the two design-space questions the project already wrote down and had no machinery for: `docs/hetero-mesh-plan.md:196` ("2x8 for iteration, 8x8 for the headline number?") and `docs/relatorio-desenvolvimento.md:555-560`, which records the 2x8 choice as a simulation-time compromise with no evidence about the alternative.

```bash
python pipeline/sweep/run.py --models ops/mnist ops/kws --grid ofat -o results/sweep/s1
python pipeline/sweep/report.py results/sweep/s1/sweep.jsonl
```

## What it does

| Knob (MNIST, 4 images) | Cycles/image | vs base |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 582,712 | — |
| Spatz lanes 2 | 616,728 | +5.8% |
| Spatz lanes 8 | 558,399 | −4.2% |
| Ara lanes 2 / 8 | 582,712 | **0.0%** |

The Ara row is the one that says the harness is trustworthy: it is *correct* that Ara's lane count does nothing on a scalar `cva6` host, and the sweep reports exactly zero rather than noise. About 24 s a cell including calibration, so the full screening grid is minutes.

## Why it is shaped this way

**One design file, not `--config-opt`.** The same numbers have to reach the GVSoC boards, the C header generator, the linker scripts and Deeploy's offload budget. They all import `hetero.system`, and the environment is inherited across the subprocesses `run_hetero.py` spawns; gapy's CLI overrides reach only the boards.

**Almost nothing needs a rebuild.** This checkout runs GVSoC's legacy runner (`USE_GVRUN` unset, `platform_tree` absent from every emitted config), so every parameter already resolves through JSON. Only VLEN and the ISA string are compiled in. TCDM size, which looked like the expensive axis, needs no rebuild at all.

**The mapper is recalibrated per design point.** `RATES` measures one specific SoC, so a 16-lane Spatz would otherwise keep being handed work at a 4-lane Spatz's prices — the sweep would measure the mapper's staleness rather than the hardware. `mesh_calib.c` re-measures the table in one build and one run.

## Reviewer notes

**A latent bug fixed in passing.** `HOST_HARTID` was a hardcoded 16, commented as "above every cluster hartid". It was not — Spatz occupies 9–17, so the host shared core 7's id. Harmless today (only trace attribution keys on it) but it made the core-count axis impossible. Now derived, with a collision assertion. **This is the only change to the generated header: `HES_HOST_HARTID` 16 → 18.**

**Area coefficients are placeholders, and the code refuses to pretend otherwise.** There is no characterized area figure anywhere in the tree, so `area.py` computes a structural model in "au", never mm², and `report.py` will not print a ranking without the ±30% robustness pass beside it. Sourcing them from the Ara/Spatz/Snitch/CVA6 papers is the main outstanding work; it changes the weights, not the structure.

**Energy is dynamic only.** The cache instrumentation is verified to ten significant figures against `accesses × pJ + refills × refill pJ`, anchored on Siracusa's characterized 16 KiB SRAM bank. Leakage reports zero — the source is registered and started exactly as `memory.cpp` does it, but nothing accumulates, most likely because the power engine wants a supply state set on the block, which no board here calls. Main-memory energy is a flagged estimate, deliberately *not* derived from the SRAM √size rule. The Siracusa anchor's technology node is not recorded upstream, so energy and area cannot yet be combined into one figure of merit.

**Two traps worth knowing about, both documented in the code.** The `#include "hes_system.h"` in `runtime/mesh/*.h` is quoted, so GCC resolves it next to the including file before any `-I` — a cell that shared the directory would build its own linker script against another cell's addresses with no error, just wrong numbers. And GVSoC hashes `sources + cflags + libs` in order, so the VLEN flag must be replaced in place, never appended.

## Verification

- Baseline replication is exact: **572,820 cycles/image**, matching the committed result to the cycle, with the recalibrated mapper loaded and the same node placement. (`make mnist IMAGES=16` regenerates `mnist_data.h` and gives 572,849 — that is the data layout changing, not the model. Use the committed header.)
- `make mesh-probe` and `make mesh-test` pass; `gen_system_header.py --check` is green.
- A design asking for 5 Snitch cores, 17 Spatz cores and a 256 KiB TCDM boots and probes clean (`failures=0`) with no GVSoC rebuild.
- Calibration independently reproduces the committed table's structure (Conv 0.586 vs 0.59, 0.652 vs 0.65) and picks the identical placement.
- Defaults are unchanged throughout: with no design file and no new flags, every path is the one it was.

author: joy-void-joy
body:
## The defect

`dev preserve capture` walks the tree through `tracked_python_sources` in `packages/lup/src/lup/devtools/dev/boundaries.py`, which ran `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`. Without `--deduplicate`, git prints an unmerged path once per index stage, so a module still conflicted in the index — `packages/lup/src/lup/policy/kernel/lex.py` after `git restore --ours` without `git add` — reached the capture three times:

- mid-merge: `195 operation(s), 13202 export(s) across 587 module(s)`, three identical `lup.policy.kernel.lex` entries
- once staged: `195 operation(s), 13128 export(s) across 585 module(s)`, one entry (13202 − 13128 = 74 = two extra copies of its 37 names)

## The fix

The listing passes `--deduplicate`, git's own reduction of stage duplicates ("suppress duplicates that may come from having multiple stages during a merge"), and reads through the repository's `git.lines` reader instead of `str(...).splitlines()`. The docstring says why the flag is there. Every caller of the walk — the boundary scan, application placement, library placement, and the capture — inherits it.

## The test

`test_a_module_mid_merge_is_one_surface_however_many_stages_it_holds` in `packages/lup/tests/unit/test_preservation.py` builds a repository under `tmp_path` with `src/pkg/mod.py`, commits both sides of a merge editing one line, runs `git merge` and leaves it unresolved with the working copy restored from ours and unstaged, confirms the index holds three unmerged rows, runs the live `preservation.capture` against it, and asserts the module list is `["pkg.mod"]` with `declares == ["VALUE"]`. Against the previous walk it fails with `['pkg.mod', 'pkg.mod', 'pkg.mod'] == ['pkg.mod']`.

## Gate

`22/22 checks passed in 110s` (`dev check`, worktree `fix-preserve-capture-stages`). The checked-in `preservation-capture.json` is unchanged: no row asked for a recapture.

## Same listing shape elsewhere, not touched here

Five other `git ls-files` listings read the cached index without `--deduplicate` and would list an unmerged path once per stage the same way; each is a one-flag change outside what this PR touches, so they are named here for a follow-up rather than folded in:

- `packages/lup/src/lup/devtools/dev/antipatterns.py:200` (`scanned_files`)
- `packages/lup/src/lup/devtools/dev/model_config.py:214` (`python_files`)
- `packages/lup/src/lup/devtools/dev/comments.py:68` (`scan_tracked`)
- `packages/lup/src/lup/devtools/dev/cites.py:65` (`sweep_cites`)
- `packages/lup/src/lup/devtools/dev/documented.py:108`

author: joy-void-joy
body:
## The defect

The merge skill's Mode B documents the conflict workflow without `uv run`, because `uv` parses `pyproject.toml` before it runs anything and a conflicted manifest would take the toolchain down:

```
.venv/bin/lup-devtools git conflict status --json
lup-devtools git conflict status --json
.venv/bin/lup-devtools git conflict audit <files> --json
.venv/bin/lup-devtools git conflict complete
```

During a real merge the policy refused every one of them, and its diagnostic quoted the refused spelling as the admitted one:

```
deny  lup-devtools git conflict status --json
      reach this toolchain through `uv run lup-devtools`, which guarantees the environment
      it runs in — only the conflict workflow, whose commands must start while the manifest
      does not parse, is documented without it — `lup-devtools git conflict status --json`
```

## Why

`55d863c31` moved the conflict sub-app to `git conflict` (the wired CLI, `docs/commands.md`, the skill and the conflicted-manifest notice all follow it), and three surfaces stayed on `dev conflict`:

- the policy carve-out in `src/lup_template/harness/content/shell_vocabulary.py`, declared under the `dev` subcommand — so `lup-devtools dev conflict …` allowed and the documented `git conflict …` denied;
- the console script's import-safe dispatch in `packages/lup/src/lup/devtools/entrypoint.py`, which built the library-only repair tree for `dev conflict` and sent the documented `git conflict` through the full project application — the path a conflicted module takes down;
- the shell fixture rows and two conflict tests, which judged and drove `dev conflict`.

The `.venv/bin/` and `./.venv/bin/` path forms, a `cd <worktree> &&` prefix, and a `2>&1 | head` suffix were never the problem: the classifier already resolves the launcher to its name and composes those shapes. Only the subcommand was wrong.

## What changes

- `fix(devtools)`: the import-safe dispatch and the tree it builds answer `git conflict`; the tests that drove `dev conflict` drive the documented words (`test_conflict_workflow_does_not_import_the_project_application`, `test_uv_cannot_start_once_the_manifest_is_what_conflicts`).
- `fix(policy)`: the carve-out moves to the `git` subcommand; the fixture suite gains one row per spelling a session types — bare, by path (both `.venv/bin/` and `./.venv/bin/`), behind `cd /some/worktree &&`, ahead of `2>&1 | head -60`, and through `uv run --directory` — plus denies for `dev conflict`, `git pr push`, `dev check` and `harness generate all` reached without `uv`.
- `chore(harness)`: both dispatchers' `policy_data.py` regenerated (`shell:lup-devtools.dev.conflict` → `shell:lup-devtools.git.conflict`, `shell:lup-devtools.dev` → `shell:lup-devtools.git`), ownership present.

The skill text is unchanged: it already documents the right spelling.

## Verdicts after

| spelling | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `lup-devtools git conflict status --json` | deny | allow |
| `cd /some/worktree && lup-devtools git conflict status --json` | deny | allow |
| `lup-devtools git conflict status --json 2>&1 \| head -60` | deny | allow |
| `.venv/bin/lup-devtools git conflict status --json` | deny | allow |
| `./.venv/bin/lup-devtools git conflict audit a.py b.py --json` | deny | allow |
| `cd /some/worktree && .venv/bin/lup-devtools git conflict status --json 2>&1 \| head -60` | deny | allow |
| `uv run --directory /some/worktree lup-devtools git conflict complete` | allow | allow |
| `lup-devtools dev conflict status --json` | allow | deny |
| `.venv/bin/lup-devtools git pr push` | deny | deny |
| `lup-devtools dev check` | deny | deny |

## Gate

`22/22 checks passed in 110s — pytest (lup) 110s, pytest 109s, pyright 87s, bun test 3s, ruff check 0s, ruff format 0s`

- **`sup_e_almox` virou aditivo** (`admin/almoxarife OU qualquer área concedida`): é um **superset** do gate atual, então as ~41 RPCs que já gateavam por ele **destravam automaticamente** para quem for concedido, **sem editar cada uma** e sem ninguém perder acesso.
- **Seed:** os almoxarifes atuais entraram nas 5 áreas — mantêm exatamente a visibilidade que já tinham, agora **removível** pela engrenagem.

## Frontend
- `supAreaAcesso(key)` (= `is_admin || ME.sup_areas[key]`) gateia os blocos **Almoxarifado** (`supBlocks*`) e a **Conferência**; `supCatArea(cat)` mapeia área; `supAreaGate/supAreaGateRender` é a tela da engrenagem.
- Quem não tem acesso vê o card como bloqueado (`via engrenagem`).

## ⚠️ Nota de escopo (backend coarse)
A **visibilidade** é fina por categoria (frontend). Já a **autorização** de backend é grossa: quem tiver **qualquer** área concedida passa em `sup_e_almox` em todas as telas de almoxarife (a UI, porém, só mostra a categoria concedida). Foi a escolha segura pra não reescrever 41 gates de uma vez. Se quiser **trava dura por área também no backend**, faço numa 2ª rodada.

## Deploy / cache
`sw.js` → `coleta-v144`.

## Doc
`docs/MODULOS.md §5` e `CLAUDE.md §8` atualizados.

## Verificação
`node --check` OK; página sem erros de console. Backend validado com rollback E2E: admin recebe todas as áreas; conceder uma área a um usuário `campo` liga o `sup_e_almox` dele e o `ME.sup_areas` correspondente; a engrenagem trava só o admin. body:
Las tres recomendaciones del recorrido por las 19 pantallas.

## 1 · Cuatro palabras para el mismo botón

Todas apuntaban a `/contacto`:

| Etiqueta | Veces |
|---|---|
| Pedir una demostración | 9 |
| Escríbanos | 4 |
| Pedir una cotización | 1 |
| Pedir un tema | 1 |

Lo peor en `/precios`, que es donde se decide: el botón principal decía **«Pedir una cotización»** y la barra fija de esa misma página decía **«Escríbanos»**. Dos palabras para el mismo botón en la misma pantalla — y «cotización» promete algo distinto de «demostración».

Queda una regla: **primario «Pedir una demostración», secundario «Escríbanos»**, que es otra intención (preguntar, no agendar). «Pedir un tema» sobrevive porque es secundario y sí es otra acción: sugerir de qué escribir una guía.

## 2 · 18 de 19 páginas sin una sola imagen

Solo el home tenía. Son ~60.000 px de texto corrido — exactamente lo que nuestro propio benchmark le señaló a la competencia.

- **`/funciones`** recibe el tablero y el historial de inspecciones. La segunda había quedado **sin uso** al recortar el home: ya existía y estaba probada.
- **`/para/taller-general`** recibe el tablero. **Solo esa.** La página de tipos dice que el tablero cambia según el taller, y los datos de demostración son de mecánica general; poner la misma captura en centro de servicio y en eléctricos diría algo que la página misma desmiente. Esas dos quedan sin captura hasta que exista una suya.

`/funciones` pesa 160.252 B contra un techo de 204.800.

## 3 · El antetítulo del home

Decía en categoría («GESTIÓN DEL TALLER FORMAL, DE PUNTA A PUNTA») lo que el h1 ya dice en promesa. Fuera.

## De paso

El titular «Su trabajo y su herramienta, **lado a lado**» describía en las tres verticales una disposición que en teléfono no existe — misma familia que la frase «a la izquierda / a la derecha» corregida en el commit anterior.

## Verificación

`verificar.sh` y `sin-desborde.mjs` pasan en las 19 rutas; axe y Lighthouse los corre CI. Las tres capturas cargan (`naturalWidth > 0`) tras desplazarse.

author: richardtathata
body:
Three gaps on the AE line, found while building the private exporter against it. Each looks like an omission on its own; together they meant the slice **enforced a declared remit and could say nothing about having done so**.

## 1. The gateway wrote nothing

`ae_preflight` refused, logged, bumped a counter and returned. No record for a refusal, none for a permit — so a node enforcing a remit produced no evidence at all, and any exporter downstream had an empty stream to ship.

Every evaluated dispatch is now sealed into the node's tamper-evident audit chain as an `AeEvidence` document (`mycelium.ae/evidence/1`) in the record's `detail`.

**Both outcomes, deliberately.** Recording only refusals leaves the interesting half invisible: an evidence stream that omits its permits cannot support any statement about what an agent was *allowed* to do.

**Why a document and not just the audit fields.** An `AuditRecord` carries a three-valued outcome. An authorisation decision carries a verdict, a policy revision, the constraints actually checked, whether the action then ran, and the reviewed activity it maps to. Rounding those into `Success | Denied | Error` collapses *prohibited* into *not established* — the precise distinction this slice exists to protect. The document travels beside the summary; a reader takes the document.

**A decision that cannot be recorded refuses the dispatch** — `PreflightRefusal::NotRecorded` (`-32032`), permit included. Enforcement without attribution is not governance, it is an unlogged gate, so the failure is visible rather than silent. A build without `compliance` has no chain to write to, and `with_action_evaluator` now warns at attach time rather than leaving an operator to infer it from an empty stream.

## 2. `/a2a` was unguarded

The evaluator ran on `tools/call` only, while `/a2a` is the other edge foreign agents act through and the plan names both as the wedge. A remit enforced at one door could be walked around by choosing the other — and the evidence would have gone on saying `coverage.complete: false`, truthfully and uselessly.

Both A2A paths (`tasks/send` and the `tasks/sendSubscribe` stream) now run the same preflight under enforcement point `gateway:a2a`. The preflight takes a `TaskCtx` rather than an `HttpCtx` so the two routes share one implementation instead of growing a second copy that drifts.

## 3. The stale-policy check could never fire

`expected_policy_revision` was hardcoded `None`, with a comment saying it awaited a deployment report — so the seam had no second opinion and a gateway running a superseded policy was undetectable, which is the one condition the check exists for. `GossipAgent::set_deployed_policy_revision` supplies the revision an operator reported as deployed. Unset it still does not fire; that is now a reported fact rather than a structural impossibility.

## Also

CI's compliance job builds `a2a` alongside it. Neither standard gate built the pair, so a test needing both — like the A2A evidence test here — would silently never have run. Widening an existing gate can only catch more.

## Five-part statement

- **Guarantee:** with an evaluator attached, no gateway-originated call reaches a provider through the MCP or A2A routes without its decision being sealed into this node's audit chain first, and the sealed document reports the verdict the evaluator returned, verbatim.
- **Assumptions:** the auth layer is the only source of the actor (item 7); the node has a `tls` identity and a `compliance` build, without which there is no chain and the seam says so.
- **Enforcing component:** `ae_preflight`, with `ae_record`.
- **Failure behaviour:** a decision that cannot be recorded refuses the dispatch, including a permit; `Deny` and `Indeterminate` refuse as before; a panicking evaluator is contained only in an unwinding build.
- **Detecting tests:** `every_gateway_decision_is_sealed_into_the_audit_chain`, `a_reported_deployment_makes_a_stale_policy_detectable`, `the_a2a_edge_refuses_and_records_under_its_own_enforcement_point`.
- **Strength:** `SelfImposedPrevention` for the routes this gateway fronts — never `HardPrevention`, which only a resource fence earns. A gateway decision remains a route-level preflight, **not** enforcement at the effect; what changed is that it now leaves a trace.

## Compatibility

Additive. `PreflightRefusal` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, the new types and methods are new surface, and a node with no evaluator attached behaves exactly as before. No wire change.

## Gates

`make check` clean. Tests: 506 (`compliance,a2a`) · 447 (`tls,metrics,a2a,llm`) · 343 (`--no-default-features --features gateway`) · 179 (`mycelium-core`).

## Still open on this line

The remaining gateway dispatch paths beyond MCP and A2A, and the node-local evidence journal with its `append -> LocalSync` receipt and three failure tests (saturation, persistence failure, lost acknowledgement). Today's sealing is a direct audit-chain write — honest, but it gives the enforcement point no durability receipt to act on beyond success or failure. Recorded in `docs/design/action-envelope-ae0.md` §11.

body: Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬 --- This PR scaffolds the `LumeWeb/php-portal-sdk` repository: it adds the project metadata, development tooling, vendored OpenAPI specs, and the generator configuration/script used to produce the PHP clients. **What was added** - **Vendored OpenAPI specifications** – `specs/account.yaml` (Portal account/auth API) and `specs/admin/quota.yaml` (Portal admin/quota API). - **OpenAPI Generator configuration** – `config/openapi-generator-account.yaml` and `config/openapi-generator-admin.yaml`, setting the generated namespaces (`LumeWeb\Portal\Generated\Account` / `Admin`), package names, and output layout. Generated code is intended to be committed under `generated/account` and `generated/admin` and marked as auto-managed / do-not-edit. - **Generation script** – `scripts/generate.php` runs `openapitools/openapi-generator-cli` via Docker, targets one or both specs, validates inputs, cleans up generator artifacts (duplicate `composer.json`, `README.md`, etc.), and reports failures. - **Project scaffolding** – `.gitignore` for `vendor/`, PHPUnit cache, and `composer.phar`; `phpunit.xml.dist` for PHPUnit 10 with strict test settings. - **README** – Documents the SDK's intended scope (account operations: login, API-key login, OTP, ping, registration; admin quota), the layered architecture (handwritten `src/` wrapper vs. generated clients), error-handling model, usage examples, and generation/test commands. **Review finding (high)** - `scripts/generate.php:95` reads the subprocess output sequentially (`stream_get_contents` on stdout first, then stderr). If the Docker generator writes enough to stderr to fill the pipe buffer while stdout is still being drained, the process can deadlock. The pipes should be drained concurrently (e.g., non-blocking reads or `stream_select`) to avoid the hang.

author: nathanpond
body:
Round 4 on M4c. Three fixed and closed; #493 is instrumented and stays open because I could not prove a cause.

## The blocker: my own hardening had weakened the gate

#490 reported an unparseable `skipped=` as `-1` and let `main` **sum** it, so one bad file cancelled one real skip. Against the true pre-fix commit, same input:

```
8925215:  ::error::1 test(s) were skipped in the backend shards...   rc=1
5b46f33:  All 20 discovered test cases ran.                          rc=0
```

Unreadable files are their own list now, fatal before any arithmetic. A *missing* `skipped=` line counts as unreadable too — the "old artifact" excuse does not survive the fact that these files are written fresh in the same run with `retention-days: 1`. Restoring the sentinel kills both new tests; the clean case stays green.

**`make test-slim` had no skip check at all**, so CLAUDE.md's "runs every test GitHub runs" was false in the direction it warns about. Both projects now run under a trx logger through `tier_gate.py`. The promise needed the check, not another caveat.

Five guard-quality items went to **#497** at `sev:low` rather than into this commit — round 2's only strict regression came from hardening a guard, and this commit was fixing that regression.

## The app really runs under a Dapr sidecar now

Two measurements changed the design mid-story, and neither was foreseeable from the issue:

- **The app was talking to the wrong sidecar.** `appsettings.Development.json` hard-codes `Dapr:HttpEndpoint` to `127.0.0.1:3500`, where the **`autonate-web-dapr` container** answers — `curl` returns its metadata under app-id `autonate-web`. The first version started a sidecar the app never used and the probe answered from the container's. The fixture now overrides the endpoints to this run's private ports.
- **The app-id cannot be per-run.** `pubsub.yaml` is `scopes: [autonate-web, flowable]`, so any other id loads no pub/sub and the firehose stays empty — measured, the Bus Watcher assertion failed. It uses `autonate-web`, as `make app-dapr` does.

**The seam is the tier, not the fixture.** Slim runs the same 202 untraited specs through the same fixture on a runner with no Dapr CLI, so `AUTONATE_E2E_DAPR` is set by `make test-full-local` and by nothing else. Verified both ways: **slim 202/202** without it, the Dapr spec 3/3 with it, a dead endpoint makes the app refuse to boot with Program.cs's own message, and a missing CLI fails loudly naming the variable.

## The delete path was worse than the bug it sat next to

Fire and forget: no await, no catch, **no banner at all**, and `onChange` already dirty with a live item missing — so "Save order" would post a list omitting it. Now awaited, reported, and rolled back. `toggleVisible` got the test it never had, the refusal test's race is closed by waiting on the banner (which also asserts the complement that was missing), and both rollbacks are field-scoped so a drag landing mid-flight is not silently reverted.

## #493 — instrumented, not fixed

Both my filed diagnosis and my replacement hypothesis were wrong, and I measured the second rather than shipping it. The pooled-session theory would have explained `schemas=0` exactly; a probe reported **0 sessions before the clear and 0 after**. What shipped is precondition assertions, so the next occurrence names the broken precondition instead of blaming the sweep. The issue stays open.

## Evidence

```
== tier integrity: skips ==
ok   n8-full-backend.log  0 skipped (1 summary line(s))
ok   n8-full-e2e.log  0 skipped (1 summary line(s))
== tier integrity: discovered counts ==
ok   RequiresService=Flowable  204 (pinned)
ok   full-local (E2E)  407 (pinned)

  backend : Passed:  2713
  E2E     : Passed:   405
```

Five failures, all known and filed: three are **#481** (`Exception while reading from stream`, minute-long timeouts, 7/7 green in isolation) and two are **#369** (deterministic, scheduled to M4d). Slim E2E **202/202** green.

Closes #492
Closes #495
Closes #487

author: jdatcmd
body:
**`pgcolumnar.compression` does not only choose a codec. It also decides which
lightweight encodings your data gets, and we documented the opposite.**

`columnar_encoding.c` returns "FSST helps" unconditionally when the codec is
`none`, before it looks at the corpus or at the margin:

```c
if (compressionType == COLUMNAR_COMPRESSION_NONE)
    return true;
```

The reasoning is right — with no codec the encoded length already *is* the stored
length, so the per-vector test is measuring the right thing. The consequence is
that `none` is a **different cascade**, not the same cascade minus a step.

## Two published claims are refuted by measurement

`docs/administration.md` described `none` as *"Lowest write cost, largest size"*.
Measured on 200,000 rows per shape, backend instruction counts, `zstd` against
`none`:

    high-entropy hex text     0.92     zstd CHEAPER to write
    repetitive text           0.99     zstd CHEAPER to write

**Neither shape made `none` the cheaper one.** Repetition spreads were 0.08% and
0.19%, so the 0.67% on repetitive text is small and outside the noise. On the hex
shape `zstd` also produced a table **1.4 percent larger**, because dropping FSST
cost more than the codec saved.

**What the pages deliberately do NOT say.** They do not claim zstd is cheaper in
general. These are instruction counts on one box with `fsync` off, and an
instruction count cannot see an I/O saving at all — the same limit
@OffgridwithJD established on #890. The wording is "not reliably the cheapest",
with both numbers shown.

`docs/best-practices.md` said each chunk *"takes the encoding that makes it
smallest"*. Wrong twice: the target is the smallest **stored** result, so it
depends on the codec; and a FSST win below `fsst_min_gain_percent` is given up on
purpose.

## Arms in both harnesses, every one a differential

"FSST is kept under `none`" on its own is satisfied by any corpus FSST always wins
on — green and empty. So each arm loads the same corpus at the same margin **with**
a codec, where FSST is dropped, and the only variable is the setting under test.
One arm exists only to assert the corpus is marginal rather than one-sided.

`fsst_margin.sh` gains three checks. `test_compression_reaches_the_cascade.py` is
independent: its own corpus, its own descriptor parse, neither file naming the
other.

## Removal proof, on both harnesses

Deleting the early return and rebuilding moves the `.so` `c8e5c790dbac` →
`6455728725e5`:

    fsst_margin.sh   14 passed + 2 failed + 0 unrunnable + 0 skipped = 16
    pytest            8 pass + 2 fail + 0 unrun = 10

Only the codec arms redden. **Every content invariant stays green on both sides**,
which is the right answer — the mutant still writes correct rows, so this is a
decision changing rather than corruption.

## Five majors, this tree

Own `make clean`, own build and own `.so` each:

    PG15 16 PASS   PG16 16 PASS   PG17 16 PASS   PG18 16 PASS   PG19 16 PASS

`cluster_tests` re-derived by collection 406 → 410. `guard_tests` re-derived in
the same run and did **not** move (342) — checked rather than assumed. No ledger
change: `fsst_margin` has 0 rows in main's ledger.

## Two tools caught me

`plain_language_check.py` failed my first draft on six over-long sentences and two
prose double-hyphens, in prose written to explain a measurement. Rewritten to its
rules rather than argued with. And `test_docs_cover_the_corpus.py` caught the new
pytest file having no numbered `TESTS.md` section, which is #1024's arm doing
exactly its job.

Closes #1076. Addresses the documentation half of #1074; its remaining half is the
measurement, which stays on the issue.

author: byeongsu-hong
body:
Fixes #1977.

## The bug

`write_node_toml` built the file by hand: `storage_dir` inside literal single quotes, every other string inside double quotes, neither escaped. A path is filesystem bytes, so this corrupts valid paths:

- `/srv/eddy's-chain` → `storage_dir = '/srv/eddy's-chain'` → the rewritten node.toml no longer parses.
- a literal backslash-n in a Unix path → `"...\note"` → reads back as a newline, i.e. a different path.

`merged_plumbing` faithfully preserves whatever an existing file carries, so this fires on any rewrite — `init` re-run, `join`, enabling the sandbox — and `write_node_toml` overwrote the workspace's live config and returned `Ok`.

## The fix

- `keystr` encodes every string value through `toml::Value::String` (the `toml` crate was already a dependency of this crate, and is what reads the file back).
- Before the file reaches the disk, the rendered text is parsed back into `NodeToml` and every value compared against the `Plumbing` it came from; a mismatch is an error from the verb, not a corrupted workspace.

## Verification

`awkward_paths_survive_every_rewrite` pins a path carrying an apostrophe, a double quote, a backslash and non-ASCII through write → read → `merged_plumbing` → rewrite → read. It fails at `dev` with the exact issue symptom (`TOML parse error at line 17`) and passes here.

- `cargo test -p workspace-config` — 95 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p workspace-config --tests --no-deps` — clean
- `rustfmt --check` on the one touched file — clean

No workspace on this box was touched; the test runs in a scratch directory.

body:
![get_recording_status before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cagataycali/robots/media-pc2-087-recording-status/pc2087_status.png)

**What.** A 37-frame save was reported as `[idle] Not recording (last episode: 0 steps)` — byte-identical to the answer a sim that has never recorded gives. It read the trajectory mirror `stop_recording` clears when it releases the recorder, so the count was structurally zero after *every* successful save, and no reply carried a json block at all.

**Why it matters twice.** Two docs send a reader here for exactly that number: `docs/simulation/overview.md` advertises "Episode, frame count, output dir" for this method, and `docs/troubleshooting.md` says to "check `get_recording_status()` frame count" when an MP4 is empty — so the zero was the false confirmation of the "stopped before any frames" diagnosis the operator came to rule out. Both rows are now met, so **neither doc changes**.

**The remedy is runnable — measured, not asserted.** The printed call carries `root=` because a bare id is not always enough:

| the call | outcome |
|---|---|
| `replay_episode(repo_id='lab/so101_ep', root='/tmp/x')` — what status prints | ok, 37/37 frames applied |
| `replay_episode(repo_id='lab/so101_ep')` — bare id, same session | ok, adopts the root (#3786) |
| `replay_episode(repo_id='lab/so101_ep')` — bare id, **after a later session recorded** | error: `No dataset ... at the local default ...` |

A later session that saves nothing still moves the id/root stash #3786's adoption reads, so only the printed form stays runnable. That same later session neither claims a save nor erases the real one.

**Scope.** #3786 already owns replay's root adoption and the Hub-miss sentence; this is the one half it left — the reader that reports what was saved. `stop_recording` stashes the id, root, frame count and episode count as **one** mapping (a reader must never pair one save's id with another's counts); an open session names the dataset it is writing into through the `_active_dataset_repo_id`/`_active_dataset_root` seams that already prefer the live recorder; and all three branches return a json block of one shape so a poller reads a mapping instead of parsing three sentences.

**Gate.** 9 new cells, **9/9 fail on `main`**. **7/7 mutants caught**, including the plausible shortcut of stashing inside `_release_dataset_recorder` (which would record the empty-capture *refusal* as a save). 294 passed across the recording/replay/status scope; `tests/simulation` 16,113 passed; `ruff` clean; `mypy` error set byte-identical to `main` (28 in 12 files). LOC delta **+250/-5** (production +54: the stash, the two branches and the shared json payload).

body: Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬 --- ## Summary This pull request introduces the foundational generated client for a new **Account API** SDK in PHP (namespaced under `LumeWeb\Portal\Generated\Account`). The generated code is based on the Account API OpenAPI document (`v0.3.1-0.20260911165854-4c8f9a587763`) and produced by OpenAPI Generator 7.26.0-SNAPSHOT. ## What was added ### Client core infrastructure The PR adds the base components needed by the generated SDK to function: - **`Configuration`** – manages API keys, access tokens, host, authentication settings, and debug options. - **`ApiException`** – exception type carrying HTTP response headers/body for error handling. - **`ObjectSerializer`** – handles serialization/deserialization of requests and responses, query parameter formatting, dates, file handling, and model hydration. - **`HeaderSelector`** – negotiates `Accept`/`Content-Type` headers. - **`FormDataProcessor`** – prepares multipart/form-data payloads, including nested models and file uploads. - **Generator metadata** (`.openapi-generator/`) – version and file manifest plus ignore rules to protect generated files from being overwritten. ### Initial model classes A comprehensive set of DTO/model classes covering the Account API domain, including: - **Account management** – account info, permissions, profile updates, email/password changes, email verification. - **Authentication** – login, registration, OTP (enable/disable/validate/verify), password reset, SSO consent, token responses. - **API keys** – create/list responses and key models. - **Key identities** – challenge, verify, connect-verify, and listing models. - **OAuth** – client registration, approval, redirect, token request, and client response models. - **Billing/Pricing** – balance, change plan, checkout session/UI, subscription status, public pricing plans, gateway public info. - **Quota/Status** – quota history/status, usage points, status/pong responses (model files for these are manifest-but-not-shown; core model list is extensive). - **Management/Operations** – capabilities, management request/result, operation filters, access models/policies. ## Known issue The review found that the `.openapi-generator/FILES` manifest lists API invoker classes (`BillingApi`, `DefaultApi`, `MCPOAuthApi`, `QuotaApi`, `StatusApi`) that are **not committed** in this PR. As a result, the generated SDK currently contains only the core client helper classes and data models — it does not yet include the endpoint-calling methods and cannot perform actual API requests until those invoker classes are added.

author: scottsolowild
body:
Mirrors the notes copy of `stripe_sync.py` byte for byte, and documents the fourth command on the plugin's own surfaces.

## Added

`credit <client>` reads every succeeded payment tagged to that client under the crediting offer and says which are still inside the window and which a link already spent.

`new --credit-client <slug>` subtracts them, mints the link at the net, and stamps the payment ids it spent onto the new link as `credit_from`. That stamp is the ledger, and it is what stops one payment coming off two offers.

A credited create also prints three lines for the offer page: the full price, the credit with the date it was paid, and what is owed today. A payment link charges one number and `PostPaymentLinks` takes no `discounts` parameter, only `allow_promotion_codes`, a code the buyer types in. So Stripe's page can only ever show the net, and the arithmetic has to live on the offer page. That is the better home anyway, since it is where the buyer decides and the words are the seller's rather than Stripe's "Discount" label.

`--unfiled` and `--tag` cover a link that sold to whoever clicked, whose payment lands with no client slug on it.

`new --redirect URL` sets the link's `after_completion`, so a buyer can land on a booking calendar after paying.

`STRIPE_CREDIT_OFFER` and `STRIPE_CREDIT_WINDOW_DAYS` join the config table.

## Changed

A Stripe error now exits with the message Stripe sent instead of a traceback. A restricted key missing a permission says which permission and where to add it, since reading payments needs `payment_intent_read`.

## Contract

Per the CHANGELOG's contract (skill behavior, documented CLI flags, metadata keys), this is a minor bump: it adds capability and breaks nothing. `credit_from`, `credit_amount`, `gross` and `client` join the metadata a link can carry. Version moves 0.4.0 to 0.5.0 in `plugin.json` and the CHANGELOG.

Mirror of [scottsolowild/notes#449](https://github.com/scottsolowild/notes/pull/449), where the tests for this live (`scripts/tests/test_stripe_credit.py`, 24 passing).

author: cdkellyy
body:
Promotes `staging` (`c4a3b961`) to production. Every deploy behind it succeeded
(runs #520, #521, and c4a3b961's own), staging is settled, and no PRs remain
open against it.

Four changes, each already deployed to staging and exercised there.

## Segments can be built once, in several accounts (#466)

Sharing a group's segment down (#461) already covers accounts with a group in
common. This is what that cannot reach: accounts with no common parent, and the
case where an account needs a version it can change rather than a read-only copy
of the group's. "Also create in…" writes a separate segment per account, and the
whole batch is refused before anything is written if the filter is invalid in
any chosen account or the name is taken there — so it never lands in some
accounts and not others.

It also fixes an audience check in the ad-gen offer email that had gone quietly
wrong twice: `audience.accountKey === config.accountKey` never matched a
platform-wide segment, and since #461 shipped it stopped matching a group's
segment shared down to a rooftop either. Both landed the draft **untargeted**
behind a warning saying the audience belonged to another account when it
belonged to none. It now asks `lib/segments/visibility.ts`, the definition the
list page, read scope and write gate already share.

## One OEM offer email per sweep (#464)

Offer notification mail is sent per sweep rather than per rooftop.

## Changelog entries import from the PR that wrote them (#465)

The importer listened on `main` only, so it read the promotion PR's body — the
one description that never carries a feature's changelog block — and silently
dropped every block authors wrote. #461 and #462 both had good blocks and
produced nothing. It now imports each PR on its own merge.

**Per that change's own rule, this promotion deliberately carries no
`## Changelog` block:** the entries it contains were filed when their feature
PRs merged to staging, and restating them here would double-file each one under
a second sourceKey.

## A Reporting leakage guard (#452)

An end-to-end test proving a client session cannot see Oz margin in Reporting.
Test-only. Its branch was 34 commits behind staging, so it was updated and both
checks re-ran against current staging before merging rather than trusting a
two-day-old green.

## Deploy safety

- **No schema change** (`prisma/` untouched between main and staging), so the
  deploy's `prisma db push` is a no-op.
- **No new or modified `deploy:prepare` scripts** and no `package.json` change —
  nothing added to the 15-minute SSH budget.
- The only workflow touched is `changelog.yml` (adding the `staging` trigger).
  `typecheck.yml` is untouched, so the required `verify` check still reports.

body:
Fixes a startup bug in the new cabin ambience.

The previous implementation marked ambience as started before the browser had actually accepted `play()`. If the first mobile autoplay attempt was rejected, every later gesture skipped playback forever.

This change:

author: kyivcommit
body:
Until now the Application section of the settings window announced nothing when
something was refused. A person using a screen reader pressed "Record", the
system declined, a paragraph appeared explaining why — and they heard silence,
because focus stayed on the button and `aria-describedby` is only read when
focus arrives, not when the description changes underneath it.

This makes those refusals audible. It changes nothing a sighted user sees: no
visible sentence is reworded, no control moves.

## What is in here

**Two permanent live regions**, `polite` for a state that simply stands and
`assertive` for a refusal answering a press. Both sit outside `{#if prefs}`, so
they exist in the DOM before the first message (ARIA22) and before the first
`appPrefs()` read can even reject — a rejected first read leaves no groups at
all, and a region inside one would not exist for the very refusal it is for.
Each sentence is its own child node, with `aria-atomic` left at `false`, so an
engine announces the node that arrived rather than the whole region again.

The first attempt was a single region holding one joined string. It was wrong
and the mutants said so: one text node means every change rewrites all of it,
so a second refusal makes a reader replay the first one, assertively.

**Answer stamps** in `locale-choice.ts`. A refusal that repeats verbatim writes
an identical string, an identical string moves nothing in the DOM, and a live
region announces nothing: pressing "Retry reading" on a failure that fails the
same way again was measured at 0 DOM changes. The obvious fix — clear the
message before asking again — is wrong here: that button lives inside the
`{#if}` its own message gates, so clearing deletes the control under the finger
that just pressed it. The stamps move on every answer and key the announced
node instead. Three of the ten paths into a refusal state were silent this way,
not the two we set out to fix.

**Visible text is asserted against visible text.** Once a hidden copy carries
the same words, an assertion reading the whole body is satisfied by the copy,
and the visible element can be deleted without failing anything — which is
exactly what happened to two existing tests here. They now read a query that
strips live regions first.

## Proof

28 new tests, and they pin the mechanism rather than the text: an earlier
revision passed 78 of 78 while `aria-live` and `sr-only` could both be removed
without a single failure. Every mutant named above was run, killed, reverted —
including 20 separate runs, one per site, for the attribute that links a
visible paragraph to its region.

Gate, run synchronously: `ui` 900/900, `svelte-check` 407 files / 0 errors /
0 warnings, `scripts/lint.sh` and `cargo fmt --check` clean.

## What is deliberately not here

The rest of the cycle is stopped and booked as debt: deduplicating a backend
sentence that appears twice under Wayland, the works-but-could-not-save
criterion that today compares only the combination, the neutral heading while a
corrective read is still in flight, the four other settings screens, and a
markup guard.

Two product decisions are open, and both are only audible to a screen-reader
user: whether a re-read refused after a press should interrupt or wait for a
pause (the code and the design disagree, in both directions), and whether the
"you can still open search from the tray" line should be announced — today it
is the one sentence of that block left out, so the announcement names the
dead end without the way out.

**No live check has been run.** jsdom announces nothing, so "a person will hear
this" remains a hypothesis until it is heard on WebKitGTK, WebView2 and
WKWebView with Orca, Narrator and VoiceOver.
