author: gregoryharper84-ship-it
body:
Repairs the P0/P1 items from the V17 Scout pipeline diagnosis, after verifying the relayed evidence against CI logs and the live Supabase schema. Plumbing and observability only — no probability behavior changes, no gate relaxed, `can_execute` stays `false` everywhere.

## Evidence

Verified against run [35108242250](https://github.com/gregoryharper84-ship-it/WOW-Dashboard/actions/runs/35108242250) (nightly, success) and [35108859326](https://github.com/gregoryharper84-ship-it/WOW-Dashboard/actions/runs/35108859326) (brain-persist, failure):

```
DISCOVERY_COMPLETE_WITH_SOURCE_BLOCKERS                    confirmed
AUTO_ADVANCE_COMPLETE_WITH_BLOCKERS                        confirmed
DOWNSTREAM_GOVERNED_BLOCKERS_PRESENT                       confirmed
WOW_SCOUT_DATABASE_URL                                     empty
scout_brain_edge_sync.py:43  HTTP 546 WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT
```

Live `wow_scout` schema at the time of diagnosis:

```
research_runs       30 rows   last 2026-09-15 18:43Z
candidates         221
observations      1370
final_boards         0 rows   never materialized
```

## 1. Board refresh reported success while doing nothing

`Materialize current boards` was skipped by an `if:` guard on the empty credential, and the reporting step exited 0, so the job concluded success. `final_boards` was empty across 136 runs. The scheduled path also ran independently of whether the paired persist had landed anything.

- absent `WOW_SCOUT_DATABASE_URL` now exits 1 with the reason in the step summary
- scheduled and dispatch runs assert the latest completed `wow-v17-scout-brain-persist` run on `main` concluded success, and fail closed with that run's URL when it did not
- materialization is unconditional once the gates pass
- the `workflow_run` path keeps its existing job-level conclusion gate, which was already correct

## 2. Brain persist exceeded the Edge Function worker limit

The whole handoff was posted in one request (that run's artifact was 1.8 MB zipped) and the worker was killed, losing the run.

- `scout_brain_edge_sync` uploads `BEGIN` / `APPEND*` / `FINALIZE`, batching candidates under both a count and a serialized-size bound, so no worker parses the whole slate at once
- the Edge Function accepts those phases, re-validates governance on **every** phase, and accumulates run tallies server-side rather than trusting caller-supplied counts
- a request with no `persist_phase` keeps the original single-request behavior for small slates and un-updated callers
- the client reconciles uploaded rows against the finalize receipt and raises rather than writing a receipt for a run that did not fully persist
- the Edge Function source is vendored into the repo; it previously existed only as a deployed artifact with no diffable history

## 3. Persist reported success on a lost discovery artifact

Found while verifying the deploy, and the reason persistence had been silently dead for a day. Every sync step is guarded on the artifact lookup's `present == 'true'`, so an empty lookup skipped all of them and the job still concluded success — runs 237–241 all green, nothing written.

- an absent artifact now exits 1, naming the source run and its event
- a `pull_request` source run still exits 0, because discovery is skipped there by design and there is genuinely nothing to persist
- the pre-existing `test_persistence_requires_recoverable_artifact_before_sync` pinned the old fail-open summary string; it now asserts the job actually fails, so the guarantee is stronger than before rather than relaxed to match the change

## 4. Prop-source degradation was invisible

When the vendor rejects the event-scoped market-inventory endpoint, the proxy substitutes `{h2h, spreads, totals}` and answers **200**. Prop markets then vanish with no source blocker, making an entitlement failure indistinguishable from a genuinely prop-free slate. Two runs on 2026-09-14 carry `ODDS_API_FEATURED_ODDS_FALLBACK_ERROR`, so the path is live.

- the proxy reports the degradation in the response **body**, not only in a header the acquisition client discards
- the 401/403 marker is time-bounded instead of a process-global boolean that disabled prop inventory for the lifetime of the process with no re-probe
- Scout records a `MARKET_INVENTORY_DEGRADED` source blocker, so a degraded run terminates as `DISCOVERY_COMPLETE_WITH_SOURCE_BLOCKERS` rather than clean-and-empty

## Deployment state

The Edge Function **is deployed** — `wow-v17-scout-brain-persist` version 3 on project `iczfhsmjrrafhvcpmqhr`, `verify_jwt: false` preserved (it performs its own GitHub OIDC verification). It accepts both the phased and the original single-request shapes, so it is compatible with `main` before and after this merge.

Deployment was not verifiable by read-back from the deploying session. What the phased path has **not** yet been observed doing in production:

- OIDC minting across a multi-batch upload
- the phased SQL against real data (`accumulate`'s jsonb tally merge, `closeRun`'s sport-count recompute)
- whether the 25-candidate / 256 KiB batch bound actually clears the worker limit

The existing tests mock the transport, so they establish batching, reconciliation and governance refusal — not those production properties. The preserved discovery artifact for run 35108242250 (1,640,256 bytes, expires 2026-12-15) is the intended stress test, and `persist-resume` picks it up on its own `*/15` schedule.

## Tests

25 new regression tests, wired into the nightly workflow's gating verify job. The board-refresh and persist tests were confirmed non-vacuous by running them against the pre-fix workflows.

## Still open after this merge

- **`WOW_SCOUT_DATABASE_URL`.** Still unset, so board refresh now fails loudly rather than silently. Intended behavior, but the job goes red on its next cron until the secret is set or materialization moves behind a governed path.
- **P4 blocker classification.** The per-row `DOWNSTREAM_GOVERNED_BLOCKERS_PRESENT` reason codes live in `auto-advance-receipt.json`, reachable only once persistence works.

author: griffinwork40
body:
## Summary

Implements `GoblinPortal --wait <file>` so the app binary can be used as `$EDITOR` / `$VISUAL` for git commit messages, crontab, and any POSIX tool that honours the editor convention.

Closes #57.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `CLIArguments.swift` _(new)_ | Parses `--wait <path>` from `CommandLine.arguments`. Single parse at module load; `CLIArguments.shared.waitFile` is the only access point. Fails soft — a missing or incomplete flag leaves `waitFile` nil and falls through to a normal launch. |
| `AppDelegate+WaitMode.swift` _(new)_ | `openWaitFile(_:)` — the extension method called by `applicationDidFinishLaunching` in `--wait` mode. Delegates to `SpaceWindowController.presentForWaitMode(opening:)`. |
| `AppDelegate.swift` | One line: `restoreSpaces()` → branch on `CLIArguments.shared.waitFile`. Net zero line change (replacement). |
| `FileViewerPane+Document.swift` | `documentWillClose()` terminates the app when the closed file matches the `--wait` path. Only fires for the specific requested file, not for any other file opened in the session. |
| `SpaceWindowController.swift` | `presentForWaitMode(opening:)` — a new present-family method that registers the controller in `open` (the single writer invariant) but skips `openFirstDocument()` (no terminal) and `persistOpenRoots()` (transient session). |

## Behaviour

```bash
# As $EDITOR for git
export EDITOR="/path/to/GoblinPortal.app/Contents/MacOS/GoblinPortal --wait"
git commit

# Or directly:
/path/to/GoblinPortal.app/Contents/MacOS/GoblinPortal --wait /tmp/test.txt
```

- The app opens a single window showing the requested file.
- No terminal document, no restored Spaces from the previous session.
- Closing the file tab (⌘W or the × button) exits the process with code 0.
- The calling process unblocks immediately.
- Normal launches (no `--wait`) are completely unchanged.

## Verification

```
swift build                    # Build complete
./Scripts/check-file-size.sh   # OK: all 137 source files within the 350-line ceiling
```

**Manual test:** `swift run GoblinPortal --wait /path/to/some/file.txt` in a shell. The file opens in a fresh single-document window. Closing the tab exits the process.

## Known limitations (v1)

- **Fresh-launch only.** If `GoblinPortal.app` is already running when `GoblinPortal --wait <file>` is invoked, macOS activates the running instance and the `--wait` args are ignored by the already-running process. Use the existing `goblin-portal` CLI binary (`GoblinPortalCLI`) for the already-running-app case — it handles that via distributed notifications + Unix socket. A future v2 could detect a running instance and fall back to CLI IPC.
- **No `$PATH` symlink in this PR.** The binary is at `GoblinPortal.app/Contents/MacOS/GoblinPortal`. Setting `$EDITOR` requires the full path. The `make-app-bundle.sh` script can create a wrapper symlink; that is a follow-up change.

author: alballaa
body:
## Why this was unusable without it

`lib/public-quote.js` builds a customer's price from a saved printer preset and refuses outright without one. Presets are `store.printers`, written only by the other app's calculator — so slice 6 could serve the upload and never answer. The shop's own book has an empty `printers` list and nothing in this app could change that.

## What this adds

- **Settings → Online** carries the whole block: the switch, the preset, a material from the shelf or a flat spool cost, margin, minimum, waste, and the per-visitor hourly ceiling. In Khayt's own `lan.iq_*` words.
- It **says** when there is no preset yet, rather than leaving the form silently unanswerable.
- It **makes** one: a name and the seven figures a part is costed at, which is exactly what "Save preset" writes over there. A name already in use **replaces** that preset and keeps its id, as the other app does, so anything pointing at it still does.

## The bug found on the way

The shared settings save merges the LAN block by naming the fields it knows, and `intakeQuote` was not among them — so **every one of these settings would have been discarded silently on save.** It is merged whole now, over what was stored, so a field a newer build wrote survives an older pane saving.

Waste is a fraction in the book and a percentage on screen, in both directions; storing what is shown would multiply every shop's allowance by a hundred.

## Proof

`LanServerTests`: the block survives a save including a field the pane never showed and without losing the PIN; the percentage/fraction round trip both ways; a preset carries all seven figures and a row with no id is not a preset. Two more on the shared rule in `test/settings-edit-lan.test.js`. Swift 15 + 222 + 1355, Node 4670, lint clean.

author: max-imalgutaussehend
body:
## Summary
- Login still redirect-looped after moodle_appstore#4's IPv6 `HTTP_HOST` parsing fix — verified that fix works by hitting the `moodle` container directly with the correct `Host` header (200 OK), but through nginx it still looped.
- Root cause: nginx's `$host` variable strips the port from the `Host` header, but `$CFG->wwwroot` is `https://[...]:8443` WITH the port. Moodle's `initialise_fullme()` compares `parse_url($CFG->wwwroot)`'s host against `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']` and redirects on any mismatch — a portless `Host` header can never match a `wwwroot` that has one, regardless of how correctly the IPv6 brackets themselves parse.
- Fix: `proxy_set_header Host $http_host;` instead of `$host` — passes the client's original `Host` header through unmodified, port included. This is nginx's own documented pattern for exactly this case.

## Test plan
- [x] Verified the underlying theory by hitting the container directly with `-H 'Host: [ipv6]:8443'` (200 OK) vs. through nginx with the old `$host` config (redirect loop)
- [ ] After merge: confirm `https://[2001:7c0:1b20:c913:1::15a]:8443/login/index.php` serves the real login page through nginx

author: stingingt
body:
## Root causes reproduced

The old quarantine/settlement paths compared fresh game ticks against the original command's tick even after that tick origin had reset. Ordinary traversal across floors was also rejected by the combined life/plane guard. Separately, repeated planner refusals could move a blocker deadline forward, and an explicitly exhausted navigator attempt retained its exploratory objective.

## Changes

- Measure a fresh, continuous 30-second present-context window when there is evidence of an ended epoch/life/floor/tick origin. New client sessions and elapsed time alone are not evidence. Account identity, current owner, complete observations, safety, inactivity, increasing current ticks and maximum observation gaps remain enforced.
- Quarantine only the exact eligible historical bank command, preserving its original receipt and permanent ID ban. Current complete bank/inventory accounting does not retroactively establish the old transaction outcome.
- Retire captured ordinary traversal as administratively interrupted across an ended context without inventing success, rewards, death counts or loss values. Unknown choices/rewards and unobserved interactions remain excluded.
- Apply the same measured recovery to both Astra journals in parallel and preserve exact lease/command attribution.
- Defer explicitly exhausted navigation approaches, preserve valid partial routes, and prevent identical blocker reports from continually extending their deadline.
- Surface the next bounded discovery eligibility time instead of disguising a legitimate discovery budget cooldown as missing capability. Ordinary productive alternatives remain eligible.
- Export bounded recovery summaries, not full archived receipts.

No character-specific goals, target coordinates or scripted escape instructions were added.

## Test harness corrections

- Restore the captured process exit code explicitly after the intentional startup-failure test. This reproduces/fixes the all-tests-pass-but-exit-2 result; assertions and real failure checks remain active.
- Isolate the shared-world test in a temporary working directory and use native paths. It no longer deletes a player's shared-world history and runs on Linux as well as Windows.

## Validation

Run 35126725720 passed the new exact recovery/exhaustion regressions, shared agency suite, unchanged controller integration, scoped type checks, and the repository-local Bun suite. Permanent PR CI adds Windows/Linux recovery tests.

Four unchanged suites require the separate upstream game assets and were not validated in the clean runner: src/economy/market.test.ts, src/economy/metalworking.test.ts, src/goals/planner.test.ts, src/goals/outcomes.test.ts. Run full bun test in the configured local game checkout before restarting agents. Live-game effectiveness remains unverified.

Temporary patch/apply workflow files have been removed from the final diff.

author: jmackenzie11
body:
Answers the question directly: **the open count was already including recurring commitments.** What it wasn't doing was ever letting one count as *progress*.

## The bug

`priority_progress` counts one unit per **commitment row**. An ongoing commitment is one row for the whole cycle — 0140: *"the commitments row itself never leaves `open` status while the cycle is active, one row, many occurrences"* — so a recurring commitment kept faithfully every week for a quarter counted as exactly **one open commitment** and contributed **nothing** to `kept_count`.

A priority whose only commitment is recurring therefore sat at 0% forever, however reliably the team did the work. Three Benson Seafood priorities are in that state today.

Same shape as the bug 0163 fixed: a progress view counting something that doesn't match how the data behaves.

## The rule was already written down

0140 recorded it for Follow-Through: *"non-ongoing resolved commitments contribute one entry each, ongoing rows contribute one entry per occurrence."* This view never got it. Applied here, on your call: **a kept week is progress, one unit per occurrence.**

A unit is now every live commitment row bucketed by its status, **plus** every occurrence bucketed by its own. It can't double-count: resolving an ongoing commitment writes an occurrence and leaves the parent open; resolving a one-off updates the parent and writes no occurrence. A resolution lands in exactly one of the two.

The parent is counted uniformly rather than skipped when `is_ongoing`, because stopping a cycle sets `is_ongoing = false` and leaves `status` alone — the row becomes an ordinary commitment with real history behind it, and both halves are real weeks.

**Not changed:** what counts as progress. `kept_on_time` and `kept_late` both do, per 0163 — progress means the work got done, deliberately *not* Follow-Through's rule, which is on-time only and measures discipline. This changes the unit, not the numerator.

## Measured, not asserted

The view replaced inside a transaction on the dev clone and rolled back, every non-archived priority compared before and after:

```
  Blast Gm social, job boards        0% -> 50%   denom 2 -> 4
  Build Reference Lists/Checklists  50% -> 63%   denom 6 -> 8
  Refer a friend program             0% -> 50%   denom 1 -> 2

  3 of 137 priorities changed, 134 identical.
```

3 is also exactly the number of priorities that have resolved weeks behind a recurring commitment — so it moves what it should and nothing else. A recurring commitment with no weeks resolved yet still reads 0%, which is right: nothing has been kept.

## One thing I did not change

`company_follow_through` (0174) also counts rows and ignores occurrences, so the same "iterate both tables" rule from 0140 is missing there too. Different surface, different question, and it deserves its own look rather than riding along here.

## Gates

Typecheck, lint, unit, help coverage — green locally; CI is the gate. The new test pins the rule against the **latest** view definition rather than by name, because the failure mode is a future `CREATE OR REPLACE` written from the older body — which is how 0163's statuses went stale. Shown red with the migration removed.

Column names, order and types unchanged, so `CREATE OR REPLACE` is legal and `annual_goal_progress` / `sfa_progress` need no change.

## Deploy

`npm run migrate:instances` before the code deploy. View-only, no table or column changes.

author: dpmills
body:
A run took the sum of its gates because they shared one job, and the Lean gate
rebuilt from scratch every time because nothing cached it.

Each gate becomes a job. `check` — the context the "CI" ruleset requires —
now only collects their results, so splitting, renaming, or adding a gate needs
no ruleset edit. Shared Rust setup moves to a local composite action rather
than being copied into four jobs; its rust-cache saves only from main, because
rust-cache keys on the job id and a saving branch would store one entry per
gate and start evicting at the repo cache limit.

Two caches cover the Lean model. `elan-init` records the toolchain pin and
fetches nothing, so elan downloaded ~150MB inside the gate itself; that is now
keyed on the pin. `formal/.lake` is keyed on every input the build has, with
a restore-keys prefix holding the toolchain fixed so editing one theorem reuses
the other modules through lake's own per-module traces.

The `Clean rustpython-parser cache` step goes: `rustpython` left Cargo.lock
with the custom parser, so it cleaned a package that no longer exists.

author: tmac1973
body:
Follow-up to #11, which fixed the verdict rule but left the figures too low at the optimistic end. Reported from the panel: the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoints read **2.3 GB and 15.5 GB per card** — implausible for a 124B model however much is offloaded.

Two causes, both taking a *bound* for an *estimate*.

## The residual overestimates the embedding table

`checkpoint − structural` is every tensor the structural formula does not model — the PLE table **plus** the MTP draft weights and the vision tower, and those two stay on the GPU. The two checkpoints measured on compute agree closely on the size of that gap:

| checkpoint | residual | table measured | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPTQ | 43.6 | 38.8 | 0.890 |
| MXFP4 | 52.2 | 47.7 | 0.913 |

So the table is **0.90 of the residual, ±5%** — banded tightly because those two agree to about a point. Previously the whole residual was taken as offloadable and then widened *upward* to 1.2×, which pushed host-resident higher still and device weights lower.

## The expert ceiling is not the amount offloaded

`--expert-offload-mem 46` was measured moving **18.72 GiB** — 30% of that checkpoint's idle expert weight. Using the ceiling as the optimistic bound assumed the maximum permitted offload and the largest plausible table *simultaneously*, which nothing observed does. That is what produced 2.3 GB per card.

The ceiling still caps the optimistic end; it no longer sets it.

That 30% is **fitted to a single measurement**, so it carries a ±50% band and is flagged in `plan/todo.md` as the weakest number in the estimator. The PLE share is corroborated twice and banded tightly. The asymmetry is deliberate: the confidence in each number matches the evidence for it.

## Result

Predicted at TP=4 on four 31.86 GiB cards, against what the engine itself reported:

| checkpoint | predicted per rank | engine reported |
|---|---|---|
| GPTQ | **18.5–19.6 GB** | 19.07 |
| MXFP4 | **11.0–17.4 GB** | 14.15 |

Both label "fits TP=4". The 27B block-FP8 is untouched (no offload): 7.9 GB at TP=4, recommends TP=2.

## Tests

They now pin **narrowness as well as containment**. The previous version passed while reporting 15.5–20.3 — containing the measured 19.07 while claiming a floor below anything a 124B checkpoint can physically occupy. That was the failure mode caught by eye rather than by the suite, and it now fails the suite.

MXFP4 gains a test of its own, asserting that the ceiling is not read as the amount, that the on-card cache is counted on the card, and that its TP=2 **straddles** the budget and must therefore withhold a verdict rather than claim one in either direction — the case the two-verdict split exists for.

Golden fragments unchanged.

## Known-weak, recorded in `plan/todo.md`

- The expert share rests on one data point. A second offload configuration — different ceiling, different model — would corroborate it or expose it as coincidence.
- **The better fix is not done:** counting MTP draft weights and vision-tower parameters structurally would make the residual *be* the table, and the 0.90 correction could go away entirely. Worth doing before more calibration constants get bolted on.
- `--expert-cache-gb` is assumed GPU-resident. That fits the flag names but is unconfirmed against vLLM's source; if it is host-side, 5.5 GB per card is on the wrong side of the ledger.

author: qoeop
body:
`docs/architecture/product-edge.md` says "a production Market Data binding
resolver remains unavailable". This adds it, and the R&D seam that consumes it.

## What was actually missing

The Composer's public operation carries only a canonical Research request
locator. Neither the Design nor the reread Research custody names a PIT request,
but `lock_strategy_input_declarations_v1(p_pit, p_design)` needs one as input.
So there was no admitted way for R&D to learn which PIT cut a Design binds
against, and the only implementation of `SourceResearchComposerBindingOwnerV2`
sidestepped the question by hardcoding a 32-byte selection identity.

The reads were never the missing part — `market_data_rd_api` already exposes
seven locked readers to the R&D transaction. Nothing assembled them.

## The resolver

Market Data owns the answer because it owns the declarations.
`lock_pit_request_for_strategy_design_v1` returns a Design's declaration rows
under `FOR SHARE`; `resolve_pit_request_for_strategy_design_v1` requires them to
agree on one PIT request and one decision cut.

**Ambiguity is refused, not resolved.** A Design whose declarations span two
cuts has no single admitted coordinate, and choosing one would invent an Owner
decision no stored fact supports. The decision cut is decoded from the stored
request with the same codec the custody reread uses, so a Design cannot present
a PIT request from one cut and a decision cut from another.

## The R&D seam

`PostgresSourceResearchComposerBindingOwnerV2` runs entirely on the caller's
open R&D transaction through the locked facade, so no caller can offer a Market
fact or a binding receipt. On the run path R&D states the Design's complete role
set and the Owner's stored roles may only agree with it. The recovery path has
no Design, so there the Owner's own roles are the claim and the engine still
compares the result against stored custody.

## Cleanup carried here

Two names had stopped describing their jobs. The engine's
`run_with_acceptance_control` is the production run path with an optional
control, so it is now `run_with_optional_control`; the sealed wrapper keeps the
old name because it really does only serve acceptance. The two places where
acceptance control leaked into the production body are now a pair of cfg sibling
helpers, matching how `composer_commit_query_v2` already handles the same split.

## What this does not do

`POST /v2/develop-composer/runs` still returns 503. Wiring it needs
`source_research_composer_postgres_v2` to become a production module, and that
is **not** a matter of removing `#[cfg]`: de-sealing it makes production paths
demand acceptance fixtures (`a2_fixed_binding_requests`,
`sealed_source_research_composer_design_v2`,
`commit_prepared_run_in_transaction_with_fault_for_test`). Production logic and
acceptance scaffolding are genuinely interleaved there, and separating them is
real surgery rather than a flag change. That is its own piece of work.

## Verification

`vibe-data` 585 and `vibe-strategy-factory` 523 unit tests pass; both crates
compile from clean under default and sealed features. The resolver's
real-database assertions extend the existing durable custody test, which needs
the full canonical Owner topology, so they are verified on Linux CI rather than
locally.

author: guillaumedespaux
body:
DEUX CHOSES DANS CE COMMIT, et la première est un manque de ce que j'ai livré hier.

1. LES REMISES N'APPARAISSAIENT NI DANS LA FEUILLE DE ROUTE NI DANS LE SUIVI QUALIOPI. J'avais branché la quatrième nature d'étape sur l'ÉDITEUR de parcours, pas sur le RÉSOLVEUR qui calcule l'état d'un dossier (`lib/parcours.js`). Une remise cochée dans un parcours n'existait donc que sur la fiche du stagiaire : invisible du bandeau « Ce qui manque », et sans effet sur le pourcentage. C'est corrigé aux trois points d'appel.

2. « SANS OBJET », migration 161. Une remise cochée s'applique à tous les stagiaires de la formation, or certaines ne concernent qu'une partie d'entre eux — un diplôme que plusieurs ont déjà. L'étape restait « à faire » pour des gens qui n'attendaient rien, et leur dossier paraissait incomplet à vie.

POURQUOI PAS `applies_when`, QUI EXISTE DÉJÀ. Cette colonne porte une RÈGLE évaluée sur les données de la fiche — « seulement si le financement est X ». Elle répond parfaitement quand la distinction se lit dans une donnée. L'utilisateur a décrit l'autre cas : « ça dépend des personnes », un jugement qu'aucune règle n'anticipe. Les deux coexistent sans se remplacer.

UN DRAPEAU, PAS UN STATUT DE PLUS : « sans objet » est orthogonal à l'état de la remise. On écarte le plus souvent AVANT tout dépôt, et rétablir doit rendre l'étape telle qu'elle était, fichiers et accusé intacts. En faire une valeur de `statut` aurait écrasé l'état précédent.

CE QUE ÇA CHANGE AU COMPTAGE, et il n'y avait que deux issues fausses. La compter comme FAITE gonflerait le score de conformité sur une étape que personne n'a faite — un contrôle y lirait un document remis qui ne l'a jamais été. La compter comme DUE empêcherait le dossier d'atteindre cent pour cent, ce qui est le défaut qu'on corrige. Elle sort donc des DEUX côtés de la fraction : d'où un QUATRIÈME état de retour, `skip`, que les appelants écartent AVANT d'incrémenter leur total.

UN DÉFAUT INTRODUIT PUIS CORRIGÉ EN L'ÉCRIVANT, gelé par un test : demander `sans_objet` sans cascade faisait échouer la requête entière, et le rattrapage rendait une liste vide. Toutes les remises auraient disparu chez qui a joué la 160 mais pas la 161 — une fonctionnalité qui marchait, effacée par l'ajout d'une option.

Une assertion existante épinglait la forme exacte de l'appel au résolveur, ce qui condamnait tout ajout d'argument : elle vérifie maintenant que `pieces` est TRANSMIS, et que `remises` l'est aussi.

Build complet du front vérifié. Trois tests, tous vérifiés rouges.

author: thepotentianetwork-rgb
body:
A call list is read at a glance, so hiding the one thing being scanned for behind a toggle was the wrong trade — it fixed the height by making every lead cost a tap.

## Where it goes instead

A pipeline lead has nothing in **Value**, **Open Work** or **Latest Note** — three empty columns to the right of every one of them. The detail goes there, across all three, laid out horizontally:

```
Teel Premium Auto Detailing   (805) 504-7933   —   LEAD   WHY  Site has no mobile viewport, 18 Google reviews.   OPEN →
41/100 · NO MOBILE                                                SITE https://teelmobiledetailing.com/
OXNARD, CA                                                        SPEED 41/100 mobile · no mobile viewport
NEW LEAD                                                          ADDRESS 601 N Del Norte Blvd, Oxnard, CA
                                                                  TRADE Mobile Detailing · Auto detailers
                                                                  GOOGLE Open their listing →
```

No toggle, no full-width row underneath, and none of it in the narrow Client column where it was wrapping three times to begin with.

Rows carry 6 cells for a lead (one spanning 3) and 8 for a client, so the table still lines up.

## Two other things

- **The reason moves to the front of the block.** It is what someone is looking for, and it was last — four fields to read past before reaching the point.
- **A real note on a lead is kept**, shown under the detail rather than displaced by it.

On a phone the table is already a stack of blocks, so the cell keeps its own **Why** label there and drops the column minimum, which would otherwise just push the page sideways.

## Testing

Front-end only; `node --test worker/*.test.mjs` still passes 125. The page was loaded against a stub DOM with a real pipeline lead and a real client in the list — 6 cells and 8 cells respectively, nothing thrown, logout still bound.

author: mattbodle
body:
## What

Data plan kit blocking is applied on some of the paths that carry user data to a kit and not on others.

`blockUserAttributes` / `blockUserIdentities` (via `dataPlanOptions`, or `blok.ua` / `blok.id` in a server data plan) are honoured for:

- event payloads (`KitBlocker.createBlockedEvent`),
- `setUserAttribute` / `removeUserAttribute` forwarding (`handleForwarderUserAttributes`),
- the user object passed to `onUserIdentified` and the `on*Complete` callbacks (`filteredMparticleUser`).

They are not honoured for:

- the user attributes and user identities passed as the fifth and sixth arguments of `forwarder.init()`,
- `forwarder.setUserIdentity()`.

The identity side of that is visible in one function. After an identity call completes, `setForwarderCallbacks` first forwards identities through `setForwarderUserIdentities`, which passes on every identity that survives the per-kit `userIdentityFilters`, and then invokes the completion callbacks, which pass a blocker-filtered user. A kit that implements both `setUserIdentity` and `onUserIdentified` is handed two different identity sets by those two steps.

## Observable behaviour

With `blockUserIdentities` enabled and a `user_identities` data point that plans `customerid` and `email` with `additionalProperties: false`, a kit still receives `google` and `yahoo`:

- as `init()`'s sixth argument — at SDK start, when a kit is initialized later by conditional forwarding, and when a kit is initialized by a user change;
- through `setUserIdentity()` after every identify, login, logout and modify.

The same applies to a user attribute that is not named in a restrictive `user_attributes` data point: it reaches `init()`'s fifth argument, even though the identical attribute is correctly withheld from the same kit's `setUserAttribute()`.

## Change

- `initForwarders` builds the user attributes it passes to a kit with `filteredMparticleUser`, which already applies the kit blocker and then the per-kit `userAttributeFilters`. A kit is now initialized with exactly the attributes the identity callbacks receive.
- `initForwarders` and `setForwarderUserIdentities` both remove blocked identities before the per-kit `userIdentityFilters` run, so the plan level decision is applied once, ahead of the kit level filters.
- `KitBlocker.isIdentityBlocked` no longer throws when `blockUserIdentities` is enabled and the plan carries no `user_identities` data point. It returns `false` in that case, which is what `isAttributeKeyBlocked` already does for user attributes, and what `transformUserAttributes` and `transformUserIdentities` already do for events.

Nothing changes when no data plan is configured, or when the data point sets `additionalProperties: true`: the kit blocker is either absent or reports nothing as blocked, and every attribute and identity is passed through as before. The SDK's own stored user profile is untouched — only what is handed to a kit is filtered. The conditional forwarding rule in `isEnabledForUserAttributes` deliberately still reads the unfiltered attributes, because it decides whether a kit is enabled rather than what it is given.

## Tests

`test/src/tests-kit-blocking.ts` gains nine tests in a new `integration tests - kit initialization and setUserIdentity` block:

- the `init()` arguments at SDK start, at a conditional forwarding initialization, and at an initialization triggered by a user change;
- `setUserIdentity()` after identify, login, logout and modify;
- a configuration with no data plan, asserting that everything is still delivered;
- `isIdentityBlocked` against an empty data point list.

Every assertion that a blocked value is absent is paired, in the same test, with an assertion that a planned value is present, so none of these tests can pass because nothing reached the kit at all. Eight of the nine fail against the unchanged source; the ninth is the no data plan case, which must pass both before and after.

The mock kit in `test/src/config/utils.js` now records copies of its `init` arguments and every `setUserIdentity` call. `setUserIdentity` overwrote `userIdentities` on each call, so only the last call was observable and "never called for this identity type" could not be distinguished from "called and then overwritten"; and the user attributes object handed to `init` is mutated in place by a later `setUserAttribute`, so a copy is needed for an assertion about the `init` arguments to mean anything.

---

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Unit tests

`test/jest/forwarders.spec.ts` and `test/jest/kitBlocking.spec.ts` add nine unit tests alongside the karma integration tests: the identity and attribute sets handed to `forwarder.init()`, the identities passed to `forwarder.setUserIdentity()`, the web-view bridge path, and `KitBlocker.isIdentityBlocked` with `blockUserIdentities` enabled and no `user_identities` data point. They exercise a real `KitBlocker` built from a data plan and the real `Helpers` implementation, and the recording kit stores copies of its `init` arguments so an assertion about them is not invalidated by a later in-place mutation.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved data-plan enforcement for user attributes and identities during initialization, forwarding, login, logout, identification, and profile updates.
  - Prevented errors when identity rules are absent or when unplanned identities are encountered.
  - Ensured blocked identities are consistently excluded before forwarding.

- **Behavior Updates**
  - Users without a data plan continue to have supported attributes and identities passed through.
  - User data handling remains consistent across identity-related actions.
  - Kit initialization is skipped in webview bridge mode.

author: maboa
body:
Captions that come from the caption editor, Whisper JSON import, and three faults that could cost you work.

- **#634 — exports carry the captions you curated.** Sidecar .vtt/.srt were regenerated from the transcript and burn-in re-chunked it again by different rules, so edited cues reached neither output and the two disagreed with each other. Both come from the caption track now. Cue text is never rewritten; only the times move onto the edited timeline. Burn-in draws the cues' own words, line breaks and out times, using word timings solely to light the read-along.
- **#633 — struck words no longer reach generated captions.** `caption.js` takes every timed span and knows nothing of strikes. Generation now hands it a copy with the struck spans removed. The same change removes a second, discarded generation pass that ran at every settle and re-showed captions on mp3 and m4a projects.
- **#628 — a failed transcription can no longer overwrite the open project.** The error card was painted into the editable transcript and captured as its content: pressing Save wrote the card, with zero words, over the project's saved state. Cards are marked as messages now, and no state write captures one.
- **#627 — transcribing from a URL no longer buffers the whole file.** Sniffing read the entire body, then handed the same bytes to the decoder; a 5.85 GB video killed the tab, and the message blamed the worker. Sniffing reads 64 KB, the audio track is read on its own through mediabunny, and the whole-file fallback is capped with an honest refusal past it.
- **#631 — Import Whisper JSON**, in the five dialects it comes in: the CLI and faster-whisper, the OpenAI API, whisper.cpp, WhisperX with its speakers, and transformers.js. Segment-only files have their words spread by syllable weight; unplaced words are interpolated rather than dropped.
- **#629 — audio projects keep their picture in Safari.** WebKit leaves poster display mode when playback starts even for audio, so the player went bare mid-play. The same picture is painted behind the player, where WebKit keeps drawing it.

Fixes #627
Fixes #628
Fixes #629
Fixes #631
Fixes #633
Fixes #634

author: nabil-hfz
body:
Step 2 of the graded-export deletion fix (#507 was step 1).

#507 stopped active data loss by making both colour validators **skip** when a grade was
active. That was the right call under time pressure, but it blinded the only end-to-end
colour check exactly when colour is being changed. This restores it on the direct
(screen-only) export path by grading the reference the way the writer graded the file.

## Measured, across the whole slider range

Every grade collapses onto the identity floor, not merely under the budget:

| | BEFORE | AFTER | identity floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| light, SLIDER MAX (all five) | 0.2784 | **0.0032** | 0.0018 |
| light, exposure −1.00 | 0.4789 | **0.0015** | 0.0018 |
| light, exposure −0.25 *(the one that shipped broken)* | 0.1791 | **0.0008** | 0.0018 |
| dark, SLIDER MAX | 0.4071 | **0.0252** | 0.0119 |

Worst residual anywhere: **0.0252 against a 0.18 budget.** The dark fixture's ~2×
ratio over its own floor is the grade's derivative passing through the pre-existing
sampling error, and it is bounded.

## Three load-bearing details, each measured rather than reasoned about

- **`VideoColorPipeline.makeCIContext()`, not a default CIContext.** The grade filters are
  working-space operations; Core Image's default working space is LINEAR, makeCIContext
  declares gamma-encoded sRGB. They disagree by up to **54 code values (0.21)** — wider
  than the 0.18 budget. Grading in the wrong space would have kept deleting correct
  exports, just with different arithmetic.
- **The input colour space is declared, not inherited.** `normalizeForColorAnalysis`
  returns its input unchanged when `CGImage.copy(colorSpace:)` fails; grading a
  GenericRGB-tagged frame drags pure blue to (7,38,197) where the retagged one gives
  (0,0,197).
- **On failure it returns nil and the caller SKIPS.** It must never fall back to the
  ungraded frame — that is the exact comparison that deleted exports.

**Sampling resolution deliberately untouched.** An earlier version of this plan forced
full-resolution reference sampling when a grade was active. That is backwards: the final
file is *always* sampled with `videoComposition: nil`, so it is always 64-capped, and the
writer graded it at full resolution before that. Both sides are already
grade-then-downsample in that order. Forcing the reference full-size would have created a
new asymmetry.

## Scope: the two camera paths still skip, on purpose

Both say why at the call site.

- **Inline-camera reference** — not a sampled composition frame but a re-composite, where
  the writer grades only the screen sub-image and deliberately leaves the bubble and
  background ungraded to match the live preview.
- **`validateFinalStyledCameraExport`** — crops to the bubble, and the two sides are
  cropped from images at very different resolutions (`.integral` rounding is ~9% of an
  ~11px crop window), which a grade multiplies by its own gain.

Neither has a fixture that renders it with a grade, and `_testValidateFinalStyledCameraExport`
cannot even accept one yet. **Un-skipping a validator that calls `removeFileIfExists` with
nothing measured behind it is how the original defect shipped.** Both are specified in
`TODOS.md` with the traps named, including an explicit "do not try full-resolution
sampling, here is why it is backwards".

## Tests

`ColorGradeValidatorMarginTests` stops being a printout and becomes the regression guard.
It asserts three things, and the third is what keeps it honest:

1. no grade in the sweep gets its export deleted;
2. the residual stays **near the identity floor** (< 0.05), not merely inside the 0.18
   budget — a "just under budget" check would wave through the linear-working-space bug;
3. the fixture is **still hot** (the ungraded delta still exceeds the threshold), so the
   file cannot go green by quietly ceasing to exercise the defect.

It also no longer writes to a fixed `/tmp` path that three concurrent methods would race on.

`testAColourGradedExportIsNotDeletedByTheReferenceValidator` inverts from "we refused to
look" to "we looked and it matched", bounded at 0.02 rather than the 0.14 budget so a
half-applied grade cannot pass.

**Full `LetterboxExporterTests`: 92 passed — unchanged from before this commit.**

author: janwelker
body:
Follows #728 (merged).

## Why

The vendored upstream dashboard counted findings, but you couldn't act on anything it showed, and it wasn't even counting right:

| Problem | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| Every per-namespace panel shows one series, `kubescape` | The exporter sets a `namespace` label. Prometheus renames it to `exported_namespace` because it clashes with the target's own label, and the chart's ServiceMonitor has no `honorLabels` option |
| Headline numbers are inflated | Only `kubescape_vulnerabilities_total_*` is charted. The `relevant_*` series (packages actually loaded at runtime) already exist: 67 critical loaded vs 261 in whole images |
| Nothing below namespace level | `prometheusExporter.enableWorkloadMetrics` is off by default |
| Controls panels are all zero | Scans never completed. Fixed in #728 |

## What

- `prometheusExporter.enableWorkloadMetrics: true`. The render shows `ENABLE_WORKLOAD_METRICS=true`. Adds about 60 containers × 15 series plus workloads × 5 control series.
- The new dashboard. It keeps uid `kubescape-vuln-overview`, so the docs and ArgoCD links still work.
  - **Top row:** critical and high CVEs, loaded vs whole image, plus critical and high control failures.
  - **Image CVEs:** a per-container table sorted by critical CVEs in loaded packages, with whole-image counts beside them, and per-namespace trends.
  - **Configuration controls:** a per-workload table and per-namespace trends.
  - **Details:** the `kubectl`/`jq` commands to go from a row to the CVE IDs and fix versions.
  - A `datasource` variable and a multi-select `namespace` variable on every panel.
- Docs: rewrote the dashboard section (including the known limits of the counts) and fixed "Reading results without Grafana". Listing those objects with `kubectl get` returns names only, and `configurationscansummaries` has one object per namespace, not per framework. Updated the dashboard table in `monitoring.md`.

body:
Passo 1 do novo `docs/discovery/54_P2_COMPUTE_RUN.md`. Não há mudança de comportamento.

## O documento 54
- Mede as dez fases do `cmd_run` (1074 linhas) e a natureza de cada uma (pura, I/O ou efeito).
- Fixa as portas com os nomes do ADR-0040: `ImageStore`, `StorageProvider`, `NetworkProvider`, `WorkloadRuntime` e `ContainerRecords`. Diz onde vivem até os contextos-alvo existirem.
- Define a ordem em quatro PRs, até o CRI deixar de lançar o binário, com os riscos: re-exec, fork do supervisor, e a classe de defeito "aplicado só depois do retorno do supervisor".

## O código
- `delonix_compute::run::build_record(&RunOpts, ResolvedRun) -> Result<Container>` é pura e decide o que o registo diz:
  - comando e `--entrypoint`;
  - limites da casa e hierarquia do kubelet;
  - env pela ordem imagem → `--env-file` → `-e` → CDI;
  - workdir, mounts, labels, hostname e `--user`;
  - recursos, userns (recusa de `--no-userns` em rootless), extra hosts, group-add, DNS, caminhos mascarados e só-leitura, knows, shaping e log driver.
- O `cmd_run` resolve antes o que precisa de store, ficheiros ou host (nome livre e duplicado, config da imagem, `--env-file`, `--user`, volumes e CDI, defaults do nó) e chama o construtor.
- Depois do construtor continuam no binário: seccomp, AppArmor, segredos, caminho do log e os efeitos.
- O `kube_default_limits` muda com o construtor, e os seus testes também.
- Os comentários da secção "fs & limits" foram reescritos em inglês; a linha de base do `lang_ratchet` desce no mesmo commit (3435 → 3426).

## Medido
- `delonix-compute`: 13 testes, 8 novos sobre o construtor (limites, env, entrypoint, workdir, userns, caminhos, add-host/group-add). `delonix-runtime-bin`: 834 + 4.
- fmt, clippy `-D warnings` no workspace, lang_ratchet (actualizado) e arch_fitness: verdes.
- **Bateria `scripts/e2e.sh` completa** (raiz isolada): **PASS=748 FAIL=4 SKIP=5**. As 4 falhas estão fora do que este PR toca:
  - `cluster kubeconfig sem nome resolve ao único em cache`: com uma raiz **vazia**, o comando lista `delonix-dev` e `dev`, clusters reais deste host. Lê estado fora do `DELONIX_ROOT`, com qualquer binário. É um defeito anterior e fica registado à parte.
  - três verificações do estado `Paused`/`Stopped` no `vm ls`, em código de VM que o diff não toca (só `cmd/container.rs::cmd_run`, o Compute, o documento 54 e a linha de base de língua).

author: pgaberra
body:
Updates the comment on `pr-checks.yml`'s trigger. It said GitHub Pro was needed to require this check before merge, so skipping a run on push to master left nothing to catch two PRs merged close together. Both stopped being true on 2026-09-15, when the repo went public:
- the `protect-master` ruleset now requires this check on a branch that is up to date with master;
- Actions minutes are free for public repositories.

The same comment is updated in web, bff, db-service, espn-service and yahoo-service. fantasy-projection-service keeps it, because it is private again and the old text is true there.

**Why did it happen?** The comment recorded the constraints of a private repo on GitHub Free, and nothing tied it to the repo's visibility.

**What could be removed instead?** The "only net" and minute-cost reasoning. The decision itself stands: no second full build on push to master, since the ruleset guarantees the squashed commit was tested up to date.

**Is this the best solution, or just the proposed one?** Deleting the comment was considered, but "why no push trigger" is the question the next reader will ask.

No code changes; only a comment in the workflow file.

body:
Planning a cook took the recipe's own serving count and never asked. The count
was settable nowhere and shown nowhere, which left `entry.serves` as a field
that could only mirror the recipe or go stale — and left no way to say "the
same stew, but for two on Tuesday".

## What changed

The portions step the batch flow already had now covers both kinds of entry:

| | Opens at | Shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A cook** | the recipe's own count | "Stew serves 4 as written. The shopping list scales to whatever you set here." |
| **A batch day** | 2, or what's left | "Saturday's batch makes 6, with 4 already planned from it" + what's left after this |

A cook opens at the recipe's count, so the common answer is already filled in
and the step costs one tap.

## Every route now asks the same questions

All four ways into a slot go through `planInto`:

- the Plan screen
- *Cook it fresh* on the batch question
- Inspire me's *Put it on today*
- **Add to plan** on a recipe — this one wrote the entry itself, so it asked
  neither about portions nor about the batch. Planning a dish from its own
  page was the one route that silently skipped both.

The plan screen now shows a cook's count as well (`Serves 4`), which nothing
did before.

planned for 8  -> 16 sausages, 800 ml stock

author: ggalgoczi
body:
The kernel is latency bound: most of its L2 traffic is memory spill of state kept live across the optixTrace continuation
call. Shrinking the live set across the trace is therefore the main way to speed up the GPU, and the largest reconstructible block in it is the 64 B curandStatePhilox4_32_10.

Philox is counter based, so the full state is a function of (seed, photon index, linear draw position): keep only the 4-byte position across the trace and reconstruct the state at point of use with init + skipahead.

The random stream is exactly preserved, the rebuilt state lands on the same draw position (u32 wrap safe delta, and no curand_normal state exists in the propagation code) so hit output is bit identical, verified on the DUNE-scale LAr module benchmark (125M photons, RTX 4090, seed-fixed md5 gate). Kernel wall time improves by ~4% on that benchmark. Guarded by RNG_PHILOX, the XORWOW configuration does not use this.

## Descrição

Adiciona o `DSOTPField`, campo de código de uso único (OTP) do design system,
renderizado como caixas separadas por dígito com um caret piscante marcando a
posição ativa. Refatora a antiga implementação em arquivo único para uma pasta
`DSOTPField/` com responsabilidades separadas.


## O que mudou

- **`DSOTPField`** — caixas decorativas por dígito sobre um `TextField` oculto e
  acessível; aceita só dígitos, faz clamp em `length` e dispara `onComplete` uma
  única vez por código completo.
- **`DSOTPFieldBlinkingCaret`** — caret piscante que marca a caixa ativa; respeita

- **`DSFont.digito`** — nova fonte para os dígitos do código (nomenclatura em
  português, alinhada ao restante do `DSFont`).

## Acessibilidade

- As caixas são decoração (`accessibilityHidden`); o controle real é o `TextField`
  oculto, que já se comporta como campo de texto para o VoiceOver e levanta o teclado.
- O valor é lido dígito a dígito ("1 2 3 4 5 6"), não como um número grande.
- Compatível com Dynamic Type (`@ScaledMetric`) e Reduce Motion.

## Testes

- `DSOTPFieldInputTests` — 9 testes cobrindo sanitização (strip de não-dígitos,
  clamp, vazio, só-letras) e o disparo único do `onComplete` (completa uma vez,

author: kinfe123
body: > Top of the stack: #1097 → #1106 → #1108 → this. Base is `fix/workos-callback-state-binding`; retarget down the stack as each merges. This is the follow-up #1108 called out as a known limit. ## Problem `@farm.js/auth0` and `@farm.js/workos` each carried their own copy of the HMAC sign/verify pair used for cookie payloads. The copies were byte-identical — I introduced the second one in #1108 by copying auth0's. That code decides whether an attacker-reachable cookie is trustworthy: base64url encoding, HMAC comparison, the length guard that stops `timingSafeEqual` from throwing, and the JSON parse that must not leak a partial value. Duplicated security code drifts. A fix or hardening applied to one copy silently leaves the other behind, and nothing in the build or tests would flag the divergence. No behavior is wrong today. This removes the conditions for a future bug rather than fixing a current one. ## Change `signCookieValue` and `unsignCookieValue` move into `@farm.js/integration-utils`, which AGENTS.md designates as the home for provider-neutral integration helpers. They live in `cookies.ts` next to `createRequestCookie`/`getCookieValue`, since that is what they exist to serve. Both packages import them and their local copies are deleted. The shared implementation is the same code both packages already ran, so this is a move, not a rewrite: - auth0: session payloads and the OAuth state cookie - workos: the OAuth state cookie added in #1108 `unsignCookieValue` additionally accepts `null` (not just `undefined`), which removes the `?? undefined` workaround #1108 needed at the `getCookieValue` call site. Now-unused `createHmac` and `timingSafeEqual` imports were dropped from both packages. auth0 keeps `createHash`/`randomBytes` for PKCE, workos keeps `randomBytes` for state. The doc comment states plainly that this provides integrity and not confidentiality — the payload is encoded, not encrypted, and is readable by anyone holding the cookie — so nobody later signs a secret expecting it to be hidden. ## Safety and compatibility - No behavior change. Same algorithm, same encoding, same failure modes, so cookies issued before this change still verify. - Public API is additive: two new exports from `@farm.js/integration-utils`. Nothing is removed; the deleted functions were module-private. - No new dependency. `node:crypto` moves from the two packages into the shared one. - No effect on renderers, runtimes, or deployment targets. ## Verification macOS, Node v23.11.0, pnpm 8.12.1. ```bash pnpm --filter @farm.js/core exec vitest run src/__tests__/integration-cookie-signing.test.ts pnpm --filter @farm.js/integration-utils type-check pnpm --filter @farm.js/auth0 type-check pnpm --filter @farm.js/workos type-check pnpm --filter @farm.js/auth0 build pnpm --filter @farm.js/workos build pnpm exec oxlint packages/farm-auth0/src/index.ts packages/farm-workos/src/index.ts packages/farm-integration-utils/src/cookies.ts ``` The refactor's real test is that the callers are unchanged in behavior. All suites that exercise these paths pass: **61 tests across 6 files**, covering the workos callback state binding, auth0 and workos sign-out, supabase auth routes, integration instance injection, and server-action security. The pre-existing `auth0-secret-resolution` and `workos-cookie-password-resolution` suites also pass (18 tests with the workos callback suite). 6 new tests cover the helper directly, including the cases that matter for a security primitive and were previously untested in either package: - round-trips a payload - rejects a payload edited in transit (swapped body, original signature) - rejects a value signed with a different secret - rejects missing, empty, and unsigned values - rejects a signature of the wrong length **without throwing** — guards the `timingSafeEqual` length precondition - rejects a correctly signed payload that is not valid JSON I also confirmed the built output actually resolves to the shared helper rather than an inlined leftover: `unsignCookieValue` appears in both `packages/farm-auth0/dist/index.js` and `packages/farm-workos/dist/index.js`. ## Documentation and release None. No user-facing API or behavior changes; the new exports are for integration authors and are documented by their doc comments. --- ## Summary by cubic Moves the duplicated HMAC cookie signing helpers out of `@farm.js/auth0` and `@farm.js/workos` into `@farm.js/integration-utils` so the security-sensitive code stops existing in two copies. Behavior is unchanged — the shared implementation is the same code both packages already ran — so cookies issued before this change still verify and no migration is needed. **Refactors** - Both packages now import `signCookieValue` and `unsignCookieValue` from `@farm.js/integration-utils`; their local copies and unused `node:crypto` imports are deleted. - `unsignCookieValue` also accepts `null`, removing the `?? undefined` workaround in the WorkOS callback handler. - The changes are additive: two new exports, no removed public API, no new dependencies. - A doc comment now states the signing provides integrity, not confidentiality. - Adds 6 tests covering the shared helper directly, including the `timingSafeEqual` length guard and rejection of tampered values. Written for commit d1a2528912b089590fff03dc111b47e95b3995b3. Summary will update on new commits.

author: by5160887-oss
body:
## Why

Bug report: a base delayed-baggage question gets the generic checklist, and every specific follow-up (governing law, responsibility, the 21-day rule, delay vs loss vs missing contents, claim deadlines, whether a PIR is a financial claim) repeats nearly the same checklist.

Root cause (audited, not guessed): the live page has no AI at all. `answer()` in `1-index.html` is a stateless keyword-substring matcher over 6 canned entries; the baggage topic has exactly one entry, so any follow-up containing "כבודה"/"מזוודה"/"לא הגיעה" returns that same checklist verbatim, and anything else returns the generic fallback. No conversation history is ever read.

Owner decision: fix via the **free path** — Cloudflare Workers + Google Gemini free tier, no cards, no paid plan — with a possible later upgrade to a paid Claude path.

## What this PR does

**AI backend — `worker.js` + `wrangler.toml` (new)**
- A Cloudflare Worker (free tier, no card) calling the Gemini `generateContent` API. Model defaults to `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` (free-tier model code confirmed in the Google AI docs; override via the `GEMINI_MODEL` var).
- The Hebrew system instruction makes two behaviors structural: (1) answer only the LATEST question — history is context, never a template to repeat; (2) changing legal/policy facts (conventions, deadlines, compensation) get the general rule + the official source to verify against, with invented amounts/deadlines explicitly forbidden.
- Secret-key safety: `GEMINI_API_KEY` lives only as a Worker secret and is sent as an `x-goog-api-key` header — never in the browser, never in the URL.
- Input normalization: role alternation (assistant→model), 12-message / 2000-char caps. Errors map to clean codes; a 429 (free daily quota exhausted) returns `rate_limited` and the client falls back to the built-in KB — the chat degrades instead of breaking.

**Client — `1-index.html` (edited)**
- Posts the running conversation history to `/api/chat` and renders the reply. On ANY failure (no backend, no key, timeout, quota) it falls back to the existing keyword KB, so the page behaves exactly as today wherever the backend is not deployed. Merging alone cannot change the live experience.

**Installable app (PWA) — `manifest.webmanifest`, `sw.js`, `icons/` (new)**
- Standalone display, Hebrew/RTL metadata, maskable icons (generated in-branch: 192, 512, maskable 512). Installs from Chrome (Android) and Safari (iPhone) with no app store and no publication cost.
- The service worker caches ONLY the static app shell (HTML, manifest, icons). `/api/` requests bypass the cache structurally — no question, answer, or secret is ever stored. Offline, the shell still opens and answers from the built-in KB.

**Tests — `tests/chat.test.mjs`, `tests/pwa.test.mjs` (new), zero dependencies**
- The core regression test replays the exact reported scenario — base baggage question → checklist → materially different 21-day-rule follow-up — and asserts the follow-up gets its own answer: the model's specific reply is returned (not the checklist), the newest question is the final upstream content with history as context, the system instruction carries newest-question-priority and source-verification rules, and the key travels as a header (never in the URL).
- Also covers: 503 without a key (drives client fallback), 400/405 handling, history capping/alternation/length caps, 429→`rate_limited`, model override, manifest installability, icon existence, and the service worker's `/api/` bypass preceding all cache reads/writes.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 12/12 pass locally (Node v22).
- Every pushed file byte-verified against the tested local copies (icons verified by git blob hash after a GitHub-upload naming quirk was corrected).
- Mobile experience visually verified (screenshots available in the task report).

## Activation (owner steps, none done here)

1. Merge this PR (on approval).
2. Create a free Cloudflare account and a free Google AI Studio API key — neither takes a card.
3. In the repo: `npx wrangler login`, `npx wrangler secret put GEMINI_API_KEY`, `npx wrangler deploy`.
4. The Worker then serves both the static chat and `/api/chat` on one free host.

Known limits: Gemini free tier ≈500 requests/day for Flash-Lite (beyond that the chat falls back to the KB); free-tier prompts may be used by Google to improve its products — no client personal data through the chat. The duplicate `2-index.html` is intentionally untouched.

author: monogamie
rubensaucedo
body:
## Problem

The engineering package exposed 19 overlapping roles. Implementation and review responsibilities were mixed, UI QA did not cover API/CLI acceptance, and the applied-AI role assigned code-level testing to QA. Long prompts and undifferentiated judgment profiles made direct use unnecessarily expensive to maintain.

The operator approved the 13-agent cleanup for standalone use with core plus engineering, with ongoing direct-use feedback instead of a prerequisite pilot. Wiring between agents is explicitly deferred.

## Change

- Introduce focused investigation, architecture, software/platform builder, and independent code/quality/security/reliability/privacy reviewer identities.
- Retain technical writing and the PR, release, and incident workflows; preserve human-only production, publishing, merge, and risk-acceptance boundaries.
- Keep the five existing engineering skills task-local. Direct requests do not require a sibling-agent call or automatic workspace initialization.
- Keep changed-behavior tests, AI evaluations, and pipeline validation with implementers. Broaden independent QA to browser, API, CLI, system, and requested locale checks.
- Move the unchanged pre-sales solutions-architect source to kai-revenue without duplicating it.
- Update registration, assessment safeguards, structural tests, generated catalog, host inventory, and lockstep 10.0.0 metadata. All 13 engineering agents are at most 160 lines.
- Merge the creative foundation from current main (#213), preserving its three agents, six skills and four source-contract tests. The combined repository inventory is 50 agents and 46 skills. CI runs both engineering guards alongside the creative guards.

The direct-use roster and retirement mapping are documented in `docs/reference/packages/kai-engineering.md`.

## Deliberately not done

- No compatibility aliases, cross-agent routing migration, stored-item owner migration, or blanket rewrite of historical references.
- No live-host behavioral certification, performance benchmark, publication, or release.
- No unrelated creative evaluation/spec files are included.

Upstream #213 is now integrated by merge commit `28a3e44`, without rewriting branch history. Prepared metadata remains 10.0.0, and both the 9.0.0 creative and 10.0.0 engineering changelog entries are retained.

## Review fixes

Independent review found that investigation and code review delegated their required coordination-record writes to the grantor. These roles now record their own granted evidence and revision-bound verdicts, with edit authority limited to assessment output and coordination records, never product remediation. Scoped re-review accepted the correction.

Separate review of the seven risk-review and delivery/incident definitions found no significant issues. Late fixes also updated the assessor registry, removed the redundant onboarding ownership override, and changed the synthetic dispatch fixture to an active identity.

The conflict-resolution review found two stale inventory/version stamps in the README and interaction guide; both now describe 50 agents, 46 skills and prepared 10.0.0 metadata.

## Verification

Passing on this branch:

- `node test/engineering-agents-self-test.mjs`
- `node test/engineering-foundation-self-test.mjs`
- `node test/creative-foundation-self-test.mjs`
- `node test/creative-core-contract-self-test.mjs`
- `node test/creative-agent-contract-self-test.mjs`
- `node test/creative-skill-contract-self-test.mjs`
- `npm run pack-preview:check`
- `npm run docs:check`
- `npm run host-contract`
- `npm run check-syntax`
- `npm run release-guard -- --base origin/main --head HEAD`
- `git diff --cached --check` before commit

**Failing:** after integrating main, `npm test` passes all six engineering/creative guards, then stops at **284 global source-validator errors**: 234 references to retired engineering identities and 50 other policy/reference errors. No error is reported against an engineering or creative agent source file. Later commands in that test chain do not run. The original pre-refactor baseline also had a pack-preview self-test TypeError.

**GitHub CI:** [validate run 35145682424](https://github.com/RubenSaucedo/kai/actions/runs/35145682424) on `28a3e44` fails the required `contract` job at plugin validation with 283 errors. `runtime-dependencies` is skipped because its prerequisite failed. Conflicts are resolved, but merge remains blocked.

These are structural/source checks, not proof of host behavior, lower latency, or completed fleet integration. No validator or branch-protection gate was disabled.

## Rollout / reversibility

**Ready for review, not yet merge-ready.** The upstream conflicts are resolved. The required `contract` status still needs to pass before merge; no protection is bypassed. Publishing this PR for review does not merge, tag, release, or deploy the plugin.

Retired identities have no aliases. Consumers can evaluate direct invocation from this source, but coordinated use needs the separately deferred owner/routing migration.

author: g3a
body:
## Qué cambia y por qué

La plantilla de `EXPERIMENTS.md` mandaba **copiar** la lista de escalamiento de `github-plan-build`
«para que las dos digan lo mismo». La corrida del 2026-09-15 la siguió al pie de la letra: copió el
escalamiento y **borró** «cambios que tocan autenticación, secretos o datos de personas» por no
estar ahí.

Al comparar las dos listas aparece algo que el issue no dice: **no divergieron por descuido,
contestan preguntas distintas.** El escalamiento mezcla dos clases de fila:

| Fila del escalamiento | Clase |
|---|---|
| Escrituras en producción, despliegues, acciones irreversibles | **límite del permiso** |
| Comunicaciones reales a destinatarios reales | **límite del permiso** |
| Trabajar alrededor de una credencial o permiso que falta | **límite del permiso** — hoy **faltaba** en la plantilla |
| Una falla de CI ambigua | gate del ciclo |
| Un loop que no converge tras 3 intentos | gate del ciclo |
| Una decisión de producto sin fuente de verdad | gate del ciclo |

**La instrucción «copia la lista» era la causa, no el síntoma.** Mientras existiera, cualquier
corrida futura volvía a borrar filas.

Ahora la sección 2 viene escrita en la plantilla, con la procedencia declarada: las filas de límite
del escalamiento **más una propia** que ese listado no tiene. Se suma la fila de la credencial que
faltaba, y se nombran los tres gates que deliberadamente quedan fuera, con su porqué.

## Qué se decidió sin que se note en el diff

**Autenticación y secretos se quedan, pero marcados por lo que son.** `github-plan-build` sí los
cubre — con un **gate obligatorio**, no con una parada: `build-loop-execute.md:88` exige
`/security-review` cuando el diff toca auth, secretos, parseo de entradas o E/S externa, con
`Never proceed on red`. Eso los deja **revisados, no permitidos**, y la plantilla invita al equipo a
ratificarlo en la sección 1 en vez de resolverlo por él.

**La decisión de producto lleva su propio porqué.** Un genérico «son gates del ciclo» suena a
evasiva justo en esa fila, porque tiene filo de permiso. La razón real es otra: es **reversible**
—lo que falla es el plan, no producción— y su disparador vive dentro del ciclo
(`that Step A did not close`).

**No re-añadí la fila de auth al `/EXPERIMENTS.md` de la raíz.** Quitarla fue una decisión del
equipo en aquella corrida; volver a ponerla sería decidir por él la postura de riesgo, que es
exactamente lo que ese archivo existe para evitar. Queda como pendiente, con el dato que falta para
decidirla, y con un aviso de que la diferencia con la plantilla es deliberada.

**Se cita `github-plan-build/SKILL.md` por nombre de archivo**, no «la lista de escalamiento» a
secas: hay una segunda copia íntegra en `references/build-loop-execute.md:269-278`, y una cita sin
archivo mandaría al lector a cualquiera de las dos.

**Sin sensor, a propósito.** Un check que exigiera igualdad haría cumplir el invariante equivocado,
porque las listas **no deben** ser idénticas.

**Un bug preexistente que el issue destapa de rebote:** el hint de C2 enlazaba «la lista de
escalamiento» a `04-ciclo-por-feature.html#S3`, y **S3 es «Aprueba el plan»**. Repuntarlo a `#VL2`
habría sido peor: VL2 nombra justo las dos filas de CI que este cambio declara *no copiadas*. Se
quitó el enlace y se cita la sección en prosa.

**Lo que `/code-review` encontró, y era justo.** Cinco hallazgos. El que importa: **mi propio texto
se contradecía** — decía «toma **solo** las filas que son límites del permiso» y tres líneas después
traía una cuarta que el mismo texto admite que no sale del escalamiento. Esa es exactamente la
contradicción interna que produjo el bug original: una corrida que lee «solo las filas del
escalamiento» y ve una que no está ahí, la resuelve borrándola. Corregido a «ni copia ni
subconjunto estricto». Los otros cuatro, de severidad baja, también corregidos.

**Una afirmación del plan que no se cumplió.** Dije que este cambio reduciría `SKILL.md` unos
110 B. El resultado real es **−2 B**: no crece, y eso es todo lo que se puede afirmar. La deuda del
archivo sigue en #143.

| Comando | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `node playbook-sdlc-ia/verificar-cobertura.mjs` | verde — 71 cajas, contadores cuadrados |

**Gates que degradan a verde:** `make ci` de `base-conocimiento` no aplica (no se toca Java), y los
hooks de lefthook están acotados con `root: "base-conocimiento/"`, así que este diff no los dispara.

**Lo que no queda probado:** que una corrida real de la skill produzca la sección 2 correcta. Como
en #140, verificarlo aquí no serviría —la raíz ya tiene su `EXPERIMENTS.md` y el modo aumentar no

author: martialcayre-sketch
body:
## Ce que cette PR livre

`D-213` a laissé **quatre gestes au praticien**. Un seul avait sa surface de relecture — les trois lignes du catalogue de conduites, écrites le matin. Les trois autres l'ont désormais.

**Cette PR ne change aucun code.** Elle produit la surface AVANT la demande d'attestation, ce que `D-195` §2 exige et que `signature-clinique-jamais-posee-par-loutil` rappelle : l'outil écrit les lignes, il ne les signe pas.

Pour les écrire, il a fallu lire — **108 claims** des quatorze sources d'assiette en production, et l'état réel des protocoles. **Deux des trois surfaces déplacent la question qu'on croyait poser.**

## L'écart de plan mesure un terme qui sature

`mesurerProtocole` compte les actions dont le plan idéal diffère du plan minimal. Or `ProtocolMiniBuilder.tsx:277` **refuse d'enregistrer** un brouillon dont l'un des trois plans est vide : le plan idéal est donc toujours rempli, et les deux textes ne coïncident que si le praticien recopie le même mot à mot.

**`actionsAvecEcartDePlan` vaut donc, en pratique, le nombre d'actions engagées** — exactement ce que `nombreActionsFermes` compte et ce que les trois lignes du barème lisent. Une table signée sur ce terme redirait le barème sous un autre nom.

Ce qui discrimine est le **complément** : les actions **sans** repli. C'est ce que `D-213` §4 visait dans son propre texte (« précisément sur les protocoles sans repli »), et cela se dérive des mesures existantes sans donnée nouvelle. Ajouter ce cinquième terme est une décision — **posée dans la surface, pas prise ici**.

## Dix des douze assiettes n'ont pas d'indication fondée

Les douze fiches (`WN-SRC-0296` → `WN-SRC-0307`) sont des `Support patient`, `prescriptive: false`, vigilance faible — et **aucune n'est au registre des interventions**, dont le critère est justement « porte une conduite ». Leurs 81 claims sont tous `VALIDE`, `active`, compartiment `ACTIF` : **le blocage n'est pas la validité**.

Il est que ces claims décrivent le **contenu** de l'assiette, pas le moment de la proposer. Deux seulement portent une indication :

- **épargne digestive** — `WN-CL-0297-004`, et son déclencheur existe déjà en champ énuméré (`intolerances_alimentaires`, écrit pour être lu par un moteur déterministe) ;
- **détoxication** — `WN-CL-0287-007/-008/-009`, trois portes distinctes. Mais elles viennent du **protocole** `WN-SRC-0287`, qui n'est pas dans les douze.

L'assiette protéinée est refusée sur un motif que le dépôt avait **déjà écrit** : aucune borne d'âge n'a de provenance, et `dateNaissance` reste un fait administratif jamais lu par une gate (`DC-19`).

## Aucune famille d'équivalence n'est proposable, et ce n'est pas de la prudence

Aucun claim ne fonde une substitution. Ce que le corpus porte — **association** (`WN-CL-0302-003`), **inclusion** (`WN-CL-0301-002`), **parenté de modèle** (quatre assiettes rattachées au même modèle) — en est l'inverse logique : si A doit s'associer à B, A ne remplace pas B.

Et la raison est arithmétique : une famille suppose deux assiettes servables sur une **même** indication. Il y en a deux, leurs indications sont **disjointes**.

**Le fait structurel à connaître avant toute déclaration** : `decidePlateSubstitution` ne teste que l'égalité d'appartenance à `substitutionFamily`. Une famille est donc une **clique complète** — symétrique et transitive. Déclarer trois assiettes, c'est attester **six** substitutions. Une intention asymétrique (un repli plus simple) serait **élargie en silence** : la classe exacte de défaut que `D-208` a fermée sur le catalogue de conduites.

Ne rien déclarer n'est pas un trou : `substitutionFamily: null`, une source sans famille lève, et le chemin par défaut est `status: 'none'` avec `reason: 'no_validated_alternative'` — une **absence déclarée**.

## Ce que la production a dit

| Mesuré le 2026-09-16 | Valeur |
| --- | ---: |
| `protocol_drafts` | 1 (une observation alimentaire, sans actions) |
| Actions de protocole | **0** |
| Références d'assiette enregistrées | **0** |
| `protocol_checkins` / `protocol_diffusion_approvals` | 0 / 0 |
| Claims des 12 fiches, tous `VALIDE`/`active`/`ACTIF` | 81 |

Deux conséquences : les bornes de la table de repli **ne peuvent pas être calibrées sur l'observé**, et le changement de `catalogVersion` qu'exige l'extension du catalogue est **gratuit aujourd'hui** — la première assiette prescrite ferme cette fenêtre.

## Portée

Documentaire. Aucun code, aucune migration, aucun drapeau, aucune ligne signée. Aucun contenu clinique du corpus n'entre au dépôt : les documents **désignent** leurs claims, ils ne les recopient pas — G6 reste fermée.

## Validation

**T2 vert** — voir le commentaire de validation.

body:
Production currently advertises deployment-preview URLs whose two-label hostname cannot be covered by the installed `*.gregale.dev` certificate. Pending custom-domain rows can also reserve a hostname forever after their verification deadline, and one missing reserved slug still leaves a platform hostname allocatable.

This grouped hostname-safety change:

- emits deployment previews as `deploy-{N}-{slug}.gregale.dev`, validates the certificate contract in tests, adds an exact-URL public release smoke, and converges Caddy/Cloudflare examples away from the retired `*.apps.gregale.dev` wildcard;
- makes expired unverified custom-domain claims atomically reclaimable, prevents stale DNS proofs from verifying replacement claims, keeps retries within the original seven-day window, and limits challenge creation to 10 attempts per minute per client IP;
- enforces the complete reserved app-slug set at API, project admission, and PostgreSQL allocation boundaries, while allowing a hypothetical legacy collision to be renamed away;
- repairs expired pending-domain rows during migration. A production audit found no active reserved-slug collision.

- `go test ./pkg/gateway ./pkg/api ./pkg/reconcile ./pkg/state ./cmd/apid ./cmd/gregale ./pkg/dashboard`
- `go test ./migrations -run TestHostnameReservationSafetyMigration -v` (compiled; local PostgreSQL unavailable, so integration body skipped)
