body:
### Motivation

- Ensure laboratory records are not discarded solely because `canonical_analyte` is missing and allow downstream evaluation of BTRIS provenance-derived labs. 
- Provide a stable analytical identifier for each lab so episode selection, wide pivoting and family-based derivations can operate deterministically when canonical mappings are absent.

### Description

- Use `lab_id` as the analytical grouping key by setting `ANALYTE_KEY = KEY + ["lab_id"]` and pivoting wide features on `lab_id` instead of `canonical_analyte`.
- Introduce `_slug()` and `_add_lab_id()` to build a deterministic fallback `lab_id` that is `canonical_analyte` if present else `order_name_original + __ + cluster_name_original` (slugged); call `labs = _add_lab_id(labs)` early in `main`.
- Remove the mapping requirement from the inclusion filter so `eligible = valid_result & matched & ~ambiguous`, but keep `_mapping_valid()` available for QC purposes and compute `mapped` where still needed for harmonization/QC.
- Group episode selection, unit harmonization and family-based derivations by `lab_id`; preserve original metadata fields (`canonical_analyte`, `order_name_original`, `cluster_name_original`, `lab_family`, `analytic_role`) in the analyte-level artifact.
- Exclude rows that lack a resolvable `lab_id` from analytical grouping (they are not silently invented) by selecting only `usable` records with `lab_id.notna()` for analyte-level selection, and add a QC artifact `01_labs_lab_id_inventory.csv` summarizing `lab_id` provenance and counts.
- Add regression tests to `tests/test_serological_profile_schema.py` for `_add_lab_id()` behavior and for `build_wide()` using fallback `lab_id` (tests updated alongside implementation).

### Testing

- Successfully checked Python syntax with `python -m py_compile src/block_A/01_serological_profile.py tests/test_serological_profile_schema.py` and found no syntax errors.

author: pgaberra
body:
Updates the comment on `pr-checks.yml`'s trigger. It said GitHub Pro was needed to require this check before merge, so skipping a run on push to master left nothing to catch two PRs merged close together. Both stopped being true on 2026-09-15, when the repo went public:
- the `protect-master` ruleset now requires this check on a branch that is up to date with master;
- Actions minutes are free for public repositories.

The same comment is updated in web, bff, db-service, espn-service and yahoo-service. fantasy-projection-service keeps it, because it is private again and the old text is true there.

**Why did it happen?** The comment recorded the constraints of a private repo on GitHub Free, and nothing tied it to the repo's visibility.

**What could be removed instead?** The "only net" and minute-cost reasoning. The decision itself stands: no second full build on push to master, since the ruleset guarantees the squashed commit was tested up to date.

**Is this the best solution, or just the proposed one?** Deleting the comment was considered, but "why no push trigger" is the question the next reader will ask.

No code changes; only a comment in the workflow file.

author: huntharo
body:
Closes two window-hardening gaps in the main process, found while comparing navigation guards across PwrSnap / PwrAgnt / PwrGit.

## Gap 1 — window-open handlers opened URLs without validating them

`external-links.ts` defines `isSafeExternalUrl` and `openExternalUrl`, and its own comment calls the latter *"One safe, awaited boundary for every renderer- and menu-originated link."* The bus verb `shell:openExternal` goes through it. Four `setWindowOpenHandler` call sites did not — they called `void shell.openExternal(url)` on the raw URL and returned `{ action: "deny" }`.

So a renderer-driven window-open reached `shell.openExternal` with no protocol check and no credential check, while the same URL arriving over the bus was validated. `file:///etc/passwd`, `javascript:` and `https://user:token@host/` all went straight out to the OS.

All three link-opening call sites now route through `openExternalUrl`, and the refusal is logged instead of dropped silently.

`isSafeExternalUrl` is unchanged. It is deliberately permissive — any http/https host, rejecting only embedded credentials and non-web schemes — which is correct for a git client that opens arbitrary remote, PR and CI URLs. The gap was that it was not consulted, not that it was too loose.

## Gap 2 — `will-navigate` was guarded on only one window

Only the agent-access consent window blocked in-place navigation. The main window, Settings, Logs and the bundled-document viewers had none, so nothing stopped the app frame being navigated away from its own renderer.

## One helper, applied by every window factory

Both gaps close in `apps/desktop/src/main/window-security.ts`, following PwrAgnt's `applyWindowSecurityHardening`. Its header there states the reason it is shared rather than per-window — *"so the second window can never silently inherit weaker defaults than the first"* — which is exactly the shape of gap 2 here.

| Window | `windowOpen` | `navigation` |
|---|---|---|
| Main, Settings, Logs | validated `openExternalUrl` | `file://` + dev-server origin |
| License / Third-Party Notices | `deny` | `file://` + dev-server origin |
| Agent-access consent | `deny` | `deny` |

The document viewers and the consent prompt already denied outbound links and open nothing now either; the consent prompt keeps its stricter unconditional navigation block rather than gaining the `file://` allowance it did not have before.

The navigation predicate allows `file://` and, when `ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL` is set, that origin — PwrGit's windows load either `loadURL(rendererUrl)` or `loadFile(...)`, and several append a hash (`#settings`, `#logs`, `#document-*`). A hash change keeps the same protocol and origin, so it passes. (Electron does not raise `will-navigate` for an in-page hash change at all, but the predicate does not depend on that, and the tests cover it either way.)

## Tests

New `window-security.test.ts` (11 cases), using the `shell` mocking idiom from `shell-handlers.test.ts` and driving the real `external-links` module, so the assertion that a raw URL never reaches `shell.openExternal` is end-to-end rather than against a double:

- a non-http scheme, a `javascript:` URL and a credential-bearing URL are each denied, logged, and **not** passed to `shell.openExternal`
- an ordinary https URL is passed through
- a `windowOpen: "deny"` window opens nothing at all
- `will-navigate` to a remote origin is prevented and logged
- the app's own `file://` entry and the dev-server origin are allowed, hash routes included

author: adron
body:
Closes out the verify-then-build in #56. **Do not merge before #98** — this branch has `fix/xcode27-document-ambiguity` merged into it so the App-target gate could run; that commit vanishes from the diff once #98 lands on `dev`.

## What the verify pass found

The pane exists, but "some of the six may already be present" turned out to understate the problem in one direction and overstate it in the other. Three actions had UI that **could not work**, and three had no UI at all.

| Action | UI before? | Worked against live? |
|---|---|---|
| Set as main workstation | yes | **no** — `PATCH {"isMainWorkstation":true}` → 400 |
| Rename a machine | yes | **no** — `PATCH {"name":…}` → 400 |
| Remove a machine | yes | yes, but discarded `promotedDeviceId` and never refetched |
| View settings (shared + per-machine, last-updated, size) | **no** | — |
| Copy a machine's settings to shared | **no** | **no** — `PUT` without `baseVersion` → 400 |
| Delete shared settings | **no** | Kit builder existed; no Domain method, no UI |

All six Kit *route builders* were already present, which is why this read as further along than it was. The routes were right; the bodies and the decoders were not. Nothing caught it because **nothing in production consumed the settings half** — `deregisterDevice` was the only method wired to a view, so the broken paths were never exercised.

## Probe results (2026-09-16, test account, verbatim)

First-run state, exactly as #56 describes — preserved, not "fixed":

```
GET  /api/user/app-settings/interlinedlist-macos          -> 404 {"error":"Not found","code":"not_found"}
GET  /api/user/app-settings/interlinedlist-macos/devices  -> 200 {"devices":[]}
GET  .../bootstrap?deviceId=probe-recon-device            -> 404 {"source":"none"}
```

Then I stored real settings — the main verification value in the issue — and re-probed. Five DTO guesses were wrong:

**1. Writes require `baseVersion`; the whole family is compare-and-set.**
```
PUT /api/user/app-settings/interlinedlist-macos  {"settings":{…}}
-> 400 {"error":"baseVersion must be an integer >= 0","code":"bad_request"}

PUT ... {"settings":{"theme":"dark","sidebarWidth":280},"baseVersion":0}
-> 200 {"appKey":"interlinedlist-macos","scope":"account","deviceId":null,
        "version":1,"updatedAt":"2026-09-16T19:39:07.135Z","schemaVersion":1,
        "settings":{"theme":"dark","sidebarWidth":280}}

PUT ... {"settings":{"theme":"light"},"baseVersion":0}   # stale
-> 409 {"error":"version_conflict","code":"version_conflict","current":{…version 1…}}
```
Note the document is returned **bare**, `scope` is `"account"` (the OpenAPI *example* says `"user"` — live wins), and the write **replaces**: `sidebarWidth` was gone after a PUT carrying only `theme`. That is the direct evidence behind the destructive copy-to-shared confirmation.

**2. Devices use `deviceName` / `isDefault`, not `name` / `isMainWorkstation`.**
```
GET .../devices -> 200 {"devices":[
  {"deviceId":"probe-mac-alpha","deviceName":"Probe Alpha","platform":"macos",
   "isDefault":true,"lastSeenAt":"2026-09-16T19:38:42.214Z",
   "appVersion":null,"osVersion":null,"hasDeviceSettings":true}]}
```
The shipped decoder looked for `name`/`deviceLabel` and `isMainWorkstation`/`isMain`. **None exist** — so every row would have displayed its raw UUID and the Main badge would never have appeared, silently, because the fields were optional. `hasDeviceSettings` is new and list-only.

**3. `PATCH` names its own contract when you get it wrong.**
```
PATCH .../devices/probe-mac-beta  {"name":"…"}               -> 400
PATCH .../devices/probe-mac-beta  {"isMainWorkstation":true} -> 400
{"error":"at least one of deviceName or isDefault is required","code":"bad_request"}

PATCH .../devices/probe-mac-beta  {"isDefault":true}         -> 200
```
Promoting beta demoted alpha on the next list — promote/demote confirmed server-side.

**4. `POST`/`PATCH` wrap the device.** `-> 200 {"device":{…}}`, not bare, so register and rename both threw a decoding error on success. (POST answers 200, not the spec's 201.)

**5. `bootstrap` is one document plus a `source` tag**, not the `shared`+`device` pair the DTO modelled — so it decoded to empty on every launch. The full precedence chain, each branch driven live:
```
source "self"           -> this device's own document
source "default-device" -> the MAIN WORKSTATION's document, + defaultDeviceId/defaultDeviceName
source "account"        -> the ACCOUNT document
source "none"           -> 404, nothing stored anywhere
```

**Remove semantics — better than the issue assumed.** The server *names* the successor, so there is nothing to guess:
```
DELETE .../devices/probe-mac-beta   (beta was main, alpha remained)
-> 200 {"deleted":true,"promotedDeviceId":"probe-mac-alpha"}
DELETE .../devices/probe-mac-alpha  (last device)
-> 200 {"deleted":true,"promotedDeviceId":null}
```
Also confirmed: removing a machine **deletes its per-device settings** (re-registered the same id, its settings read back 404) and **leaves shared settings untouched**. `DELETE` on shared is idempotent — `{"deleted":true}` then `{"deleted":false}`, never a 404.

**One trap found while checking whether to auto-register this Mac:** `POST …/devices` is an **upsert keyed on `deviceId`** — re-posting an existing id does not duplicate the row, it overwrites `deviceName`. Registering unconditionally on pane load would have reset the machine's name to its hostname every visit, silently undoing any rename. Registration is therefore guarded on absence.

**Test account left clean** — `{"devices":[]}` and 404 on shared, the exact state I found it in. Everything written (`probe-mac-alpha`, `probe-mac-beta`, `probe-idem`, and the account document) was deleted.

## What was built

- **Kit** — DTOs rewritten against captured payloads; `baseVersion` is a non-optional initialiser parameter, since no valid write exists without one. Speculative key aliases removed: they never matched anything, and keeping them would hide the next mismatch as well as they hid these. New `AppDeviceEnvelope`, `DeleteDeviceResponse`, `DeleteAppSettingsResponse`, `AppSettingsSource`.
- **Domain** — `AppSettingsDocument` carries `version` so callers can legally write; `copyDeviceSettingsToShared` reads the destination's version (not the source's — independent counters); 409 → `AppSettingsError.versionConflict`; a 404 from the device-settings *write* → `.deviceNotRegistered`, because there it means the device is missing, not the document.
- **App** — the three missing actions, plus consequence-stating confirmations. Badge suppressed as "unknown" only when the server named no successor *and* the reconcile read failed. Tab relabelled **Applications** to match `/help/app-settings`.
- **Test support** — `StubAPIClient` now records request **bodies**. A wrong body is as breaking as a wrong path and far quieter: this surface shipped for weeks sending `{"name":…}` while every path-and-method assertion passed.

Not gated — this section is free, per the issue.

## Deliberately NOT built

- **The 409's `current` document.** `APIClient` reduces every non-2xx body to a message string, so surfacing `current` means teaching it typed error payloads — a change to every endpoint's error path, far outside this pane. Re-reading costs one request and the blob is opaque, so there is nothing to merge field-by-field. Conflicts surface as "reload and try again".
- **Migrating the Sync Agent's `UserDefaults` state.** #56 scopes this in "*if* the pane's read/write half is solid — otherwise split it out." It was not solid; it was non-functional. Now that it works this is worth its own issue, on top of a foundation that has been exercised against the live API.

## Gate (actual output)

```
xcodebuild build  -> ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **
xcodebuild test   -> Executed 984 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected) in 17.444 seconds
                     ** TEST SUCCEEDED **
swift test InterlinedKit --skip ContractTests

author: jheller1212
body:
## Measured first

- The archive allows cross-origin browser requests (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`).
- 16 concurrent comment requests: 17 req/s, zero load-shedding.
- A windowed sweep of all comments in a subreddit returned **exactly** the per-post comment sets on the 40 largest threads (0 mismatches); ~8× fewer requests.
- Late comments: 0 arrive more than 30 days after a post window closes.

## What

- **Browser → archive directly** (`web/archive.js`): no 26 s function limit, no cold starts; 12-slot semaphore, timeouts, capped-backoff retry, contiguous shards under exclusive bounds; automatic fallback to the server path if the archive stops answering the browser.
- **Comment sweep + top-up** for whole-community / time-frame scopes: one sweep per chunk (window + 30-day settle margin, 4 shards) grouped by post; posts below 95% of Reddit's count walked individually, 8 in parallel, persisted every 25. Keyword / newest-N scopes walk per post.
- **`web/mappers.js`** — single definition of post/comment normalisation for browser and function.
- **Reuse**: complete, settled posts from earlier finished runs of the same community (overlapping window) are reused.
- **Bounded memory**: comment trees leave RAM once persisted; exports read IndexedDB.
- **Honest completeness**: "threads not fully fetched" vs "archive holds <95% of Reddit's count (nothing more to fetch)" — separate tiles and report lists. (7% of old posts in the test community are in the second group: comments removed before archiving, verified directly against the archive.)
- Estimates use comment counts; CSP updated.

## Verified (headless Chrome, draft)

- One year of r/MyBoyfriendIsAI with comments: **89 s** (was ~24 min), 3,115 posts / 40,470 comments, 3 chunks.
- 30-day window: 66 s, 149 / 1,213 — matches an independent count made an hour earlier (148 / 1,211).
- Same window again: **2 s**, 117 posts reused.
- Stop → reload → resume → complete still works; auto-download and run report intact; zero JS errors.
- Reviewer's five findings fixed (settle-bound off-by-one, incremental top-up persistence with failure-tolerant concurrency, zero-count posts in the sweep, window-scoped reuse, memory).

author: premal
body:
## Summary

Clay-parity features across the grid, signals, and outbound:

**AI column authoring**
- `POST /tables/:id/metaprompt` — describe a column in plain English and get back a full column draft (name, kind, output type, `config` with `{{Column}}` bindings, optional `runCondition`). The prompt is fed the live provider catalog so it emits real provider/action ids; the column editor applies the draft for review before save.
- `POST /tables/:id/run-condition` — translates a plain-English condition ("only when B2B is checked") into a formula expression, sanity-checked by evaluating it against a sample row before returning. Available from a "Generate run condition" modal in the column editor.

**Waterfall validation** — `waterfall.validate` runs a verify-category action on each accepted result; an explicit invalid/undeliverable/bounced verdict (or `valid: false`) falls through to the next provider instead of accepting a bad email. Validation credits are folded into `creditsUsed`. Mock provider gains a deterministic `verifyEmail` action.

**Per-column cost caps** — `maxCost` on enrichment/waterfall/agent/http configs; when the estimated credit cost exceeds the cap the cell is marked `skipped` with a reason and published over SSE. Editable in the column editor.

**Table-scoped signals** — a signal definition can point at `sourceTableId` instead of the whole workspace: the poller resolves domain/email columns (configured names or fuzzy aliases), dedupes targets, links each `SignalEvent` back to matching Contact/Company records, records an `Alert`, and POSTs a summary to an optional `alertChannelId` webhook. Schedules extended to weekly/monthly; `sourceTableId`/`alertChannelId` are validated against the workspace. Signals UI gets watch-table, frequency, and alert-channel pickers; new `GET /usage/channels` lists alert channels.

**AI sequence generation** — `POST /sequences/generate` takes a name, campaign brief, and step count; an LLM writes the cold-email steps (`{{contact.*}}`/`{{company.*}}` placeholders, delayHours spacing), with one corrective retry on invalid JSON, then persists the Sequence + steps. Sequences page gets a "Generate with AI" flow.

**Provider SDK** — new `completeChat()` export for plain chat completions on any configured LLM vendor (openai/anthropic/gemini/perplexity/openrouter/cometapi, with legacy `llm` fallback) so api features work regardless of which AI integration the workspace has.

**Schemas/tests** — shared zod schemas for metaprompt results, signal config, and generated sequences. Coverage: stubbed-LLM happy paths for all three generation endpoints (incl. the invalid-JSON retry), waterfall validation verdicts, `exceedsMaxCost` boundaries, signal column aliasing/dedupe (`signal-targets.ts`, extracted from `pollSignal`), metaprompt auth/validation, mock verifyEmail, and signal scope validation.

**Bazel** — every `src/**/*.test.ts` is now declared in exactly one test target: api integration tests run as per-file `itest_*` targets (own ephemeral Postgres+Redis each), pure api tests and all worker tests as per-file `unit_*` via `dbgen.sh`; `//apps/api:itest` remains as a `test_suite`. `bazel-affected.sh` now maps a changed test file to precisely its target instead of falling back to the full suite.

#### Test plan
- [x] `bazel test //...` — 52/52 pass locally (lint, typecheck, per-file unit/itest targets, builds)
- [x] `pnpm exec prettier --check .` clean
- [x] Deployed to gtmai-api / gtmai-worker / gtmai-web — all healthy; demo login + `/tables` verified on fly

body:
## Summary `neat-core` is now a **git dependency pinned to a NEAT-AI-core release tag** instead of an unpinned sibling path dependency, and the pin is refreshed automatically on every pull request. Closes #153. - `backpropagation/Cargo.toml` pins `neat-core = { git = "https://github.com/stSoftwareAU/NEAT-AI-core", tag = "v0.22.2" }` (core's newest release) and `Cargo.lock` records the resolved commit. - `scripts/family-pins.sh` is copied byte-for-byte from NEAT-AI-core `Develop` (core #681). `.github/workflows/family-sync.yml` now syncs **both** canonical helpers (`runlib.sh`, `family-pins.sh`), runs `family-pins.sh`, and commits the refreshed helpers together with a moved tag and `Cargo.lock`. Both those paths are build-affecting, so `version-increment.yml` bumps the patch behind the move — the pin never moves at an unchanged version. - Nothing checks NEAT-AI-core out beside the repository any more: the `setup-rust-workspace` composite installs the toolchain alone, and the content-drift gate reads core `Develop` over https. - `scripts/check-runlib-canonical.sh` is generalised to `scripts/check-canonical-copies.sh`, covering both copied helpers. - The `neat-core.expected-version` breaking-bump gate is **retired** (gate, test twin and baseline file). It acknowledged breaking bumps of an unpinned dependency on paper and went red on every PR whenever core released a new pre-1.0 minor (#156); with the pin, a core release this crate cannot consume fails the build and tests of the PR that moves the pin. - `scripts/lockfile_integrity.py` verifies a git package by its immutable `?tag=…#<40-hex>` pin instead of a registry record; `deny.toml` allows the one NEAT-AI-core git source. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["PR opened / updated"] --> B["family-sync job"] B --> C["sync runlib.sh + family-pins.sh
from core Develop"] C --> D["family-pins.sh:
newest v* tag on NEAT-AI-core"] D -- "pin already current" --> E["no commit"] D -- "pin behind" --> F["rewrite tag + cargo update
commit Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock"] D -- "remote unlistable" --> G["job fails"] F --> H["version-increment.yml
bumps the patch"] H --> I["ci.yml builds against the new release"] ``` ## Evidence Backend/CLI change — no web interface to screenshot. Verified by running the real commands: **The workspace builds with no sibling checkout.** A fresh clone in `/tmp/nosibling/NEAT-AI-Backpropagation`, with no `NEAT-AI-core` beside it: ```text $ ls /tmp/nosibling/ # only the repo — no sibling NEAT-AI-Backpropagation $ cargo test --workspace --all-features -- --test-threads=2 test result: ok. 15 passed; 0 failed … (13 suites, 0 failures) ``` **A stale pin is moved, and the move is idempotent** (same isolated clone): ```text $ sed -i 's|tag = "v0.19.0"|…|' backpropagation/Cargo.toml # rewind the pin $ ./scripts/family-pins.sh [family-pins] neat-core v0.19.0 → v0.22.2 (backpropagation/Cargo.toml) [family-pins] 1 pin(s) moved; Cargo.lock updated exit=0 $ ./scripts/family-pins.sh # second run exit=0 # no output, no diff ``` **The patch bump follows the moved pin** — the same script `version-increment.yml` runs: ```text $ ./scripts/bump-backpropagation-version.sh --base-ref origin/Develop OK build-affecting changes vs origin/Develop: Cargo.lock backpropagation/Cargo.toml backpropagation/src/gradient_check.rs OK bumped neat_ai_backpropagation 0.1.38 -> 0.1.39 ``` **Gates green.** `./quality.sh` → `All quality checks passed!` (shellcheck, actionlint, codespell, markdownlint, `cargo deny check`, lockfile integrity — `58 packages verified`, with `neat-core 0.22.2: git package pinned at v0.22.2 9b26d47c`, `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo doc`). ## Acceptance Criteria - **met** — The workspace builds with no `NEAT-AI-core` checkout beside the repo — evidence: `backpropagation/Cargo.toml:29`, `Cargo.lock:195-197` (`source = "git+…?tag=v0.22.2#9b26d47c…"`), the deleted checkout/symlink steps in `.github/actions/setup-rust-workspace/action.yml`, and the isolated-clone test run above — reviewer: met - **met** — A PR whose pin is behind core's latest release receives a CI commit moving the tag and `Cargo.lock`, followed by the patch bump — evidence: `.github/workflows/family-sync.yml:64-150` (sync, run, stage `backpropagation/Cargo.toml` + `Cargo.lock`), the rules asserting both in `scripts/check-family-sync-workflow.sh:104-131` (`scripts/test-check-family-sync-workflow.sh::rejects a workflow that never runs family-pins.sh`, `::rejects a commit that does not stage Cargo.lock`), and the pin-move / bump transcripts above — reviewer: met — reason: the reviewer flagged that a `GITHUB_TOKEN` fallback push would not fire `pull_request: synchronize` and so would not trigger the bump; that App-token → `ACTIONS_PUSH` → `GITHUB_TOKEN` ladder is the pre-existing pattern copied from `version-increment.yml:100` and is unchanged here - **met** — Tests and quality checks pass — evidence: `./quality.sh` end to end (above), `cargo test --workspace --all-features` 13 suites green, `scripts/test-check-canonical-copies.sh` 11/11, `scripts/test-check-family-sync-workflow.sh` 20/20, `scripts/test-check-lockfile-integrity.sh` 16/16 — reviewer: met - **unrequested** — `scripts/runlib.sh` refreshed from core `Develop` (core #699, +188 lines) — reviewer: unrequested — reason: the drift gate now reads `Develop` live, and core had moved, so the committed copy was stale; this is the mechanical re-copy the family-sync job would itself have pushed, and without it CI is red on its first run - **unrequested** — the git-package rules in `scripts/lockfile_integrity.py` (immutable tag + commit, tag/version agreement, no checksum) — reviewer: unrequested — reason: the minimum was to stop classifying a `git+` source as a registry package, which would have left a git dependency *unverified*; the rules keep the gate's "never pass an unverified lockfile" contract, with five cases covering them - **unrequested** — `scripts/check-canonical-copies.sh` fetches core `Develop` over https with a loud sibling fallback, rather than only reading a sibling — reviewer: unrequested — reason: a sibling is only as current as its last fetch, so a local run and CI disagreed about what "canonical" means; the fallback is announced and "neither available" exits 2, never 0 - **unrequested** — `backpropagation/src/gradient_check.rs` reads `neatCoreBaseline` from the manifest pin, and `GRADIENT_CHECK_SCHEMA` goes `2` → `3` — reviewer: unrequested — reason: the crate `include_str!`d the deleted baseline file, so it no longer compiled; the field keeps its shape but changes meaning, which the schema bump is what tells a consumer - **unrequested** — comment/description-only edits to `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml`, `renovate.json`, `scripts/auto-format.sh` and `scripts/check-renovate-config.sh` — reviewer: unrequested — reason: each described the retired path dependency or sibling checkout; a code change owes its docs change ## Standards Review - **violation** — the auto-format commit message and change-detection comment still described the path dependency and a sibling checkout — evidence: `scripts/auto-format.sh:18`, `scripts/auto-format.sh:74` — reason: fixed here - **violation** — the Renovate gate's rule text and messages still called `neat-core` a path dependency synced by Auto Format, contradicting the `renovate.json` this diff rewrote — evidence: `scripts/check-renovate-config.sh:10`, `:220`, `:224`, `scripts/test-check-renovate-config.sh:170` — reason: fixed here - **violation** — the CodeQL call-site comment still asserted a sibling checkout exists —

author: mirogers-jha
body:
Closes #242.

## The problem

`gsd_validate_milestone` refuses a `pass` verdict while a required subjective UAT criterion is unanswered, but the error was a bare UUID:

```
Error validating milestone: Milestone validation pass requires accepted
subjective UAT criterion 3dee6b2e-870c-4a77-a427-70e4ceaa4294
```

Two separate defects made that blocker look unresolvable from inside the unit that hits it. In the reporting project it cost eight consecutive `validate-milestone` sessions and produced five duplicate criterion rows across three keys for one underlying question — recovered only by reading `workflow_acceptance_criteria` out of a DB backup by hand.

## Root causes

**1. The facts were fetched and thrown away.** `currentRequiredSubjectiveProofs` projected only `criterion_id`. `criterion_key` and `description` are columns on the very row it reads.

**2. The allow-list omitted the fix.** `gsd_prepare_milestone_subjective_uat`, `gsd_answer_milestone_subjective_uat`, `gsd_prepare_milestone_subjective_uat_retirement`, and `gsd_retire_milestone_subjective_uat` appeared in *no* unit's `allowedGsdTools`. Since `SCOPED_GSD_LIFECYCLE_TOOLS` is the union of every unit's allow-list, the enforcer never saw them either — which is exactly why they were callable everywhere yet advertised nowhere, next to a reminder warning that "near-miss variants are rejected".

## What changed

`milestone-validation-domain-operation.ts` now also selects `criterion_key`, `description`, and the criterion's open question text, and renders:

```
Error validating milestone: Milestone validation pass requires an accepted subjective UAT criterion.

  criterion_id:  3dee6b2e-870c-4a77-a427-70e4ceaa4294
  criterion_key: developer-owns-domain-types-in-repo
  criterion:     This service owns its domain types in-repo.
  question:      Does this service own its domain types in-repo?

  To settle it, call one of:
    gsd_prepare_milestone_subjective_uat            (ask, then answer with gsd_answer_milestone_subjective_uat)
    gsd_prepare_milestone_subjective_uat_retirement (retire a stale row, then gsd_retire_milestone_subjective_uat)

  Reuse criterion_key 'developer-owns-domain-types-in-repo' to rephrase — a new key opens a second required gate.
```

The `question:` line is omitted when no open question survives (a rejected answer closes the question but leaves the criterion required and unaccepted); the message falls back to the criterion description. Both branches have tests.

`unit-registry.ts` adds the four tools to `validate-milestone` and `complete-milestone`.

## Reviewer notes

- **Adding these tools to an allow-list is an enforcement change, not just an advertising one.** They now enter `SCOPED_GSD_LIFECYCLE_TOOLS`, so every *other* unit hard-blocks them where previously they were silently permitted. `complete-milestone` is included deliberately: closeout readiness applies the same `required = 1` current-head filter, so it can hit the same blocker, and granting only `validate-milestone` would have newly trapped it.
- **The issue's third point — duplicate criterion rows — needed no work.** d9ceafb0 already added `unansweredRequiredSubjectiveCriterion`, which rejects a prepare that would open a second required chain and names the key to reuse.
- **No prompt prose was added.** The derived Tool Surface line and tail reminder now list the four tools, and the error itself names them, so `validate-milestone.md` prose would only cost tokens on every validation run.
- One existing assertion moved from `/requires accepted subjective UAT criterion/i` to `/requires an accepted .../i` to track the reworded first line.

## Verification

- `pnpm run typecheck:extensions` — exit 0
- `pnpm run test:unit` — 14450 passed, 0 failed, 28 skipped
- `pnpm run test:changed:src` — 48/48

body:
### 🚨 Severity: MEDIUM
### 💡 Vulnerability
1. Direct unhandled `JSON.parse()` on `storage` event `newValue` could throw `SyntaxError` and break cross-tab real-time sync if corrupted/invalid data was written to `localStorage`.
2. `getStoredFeedbacks()` assumed `JSON.parse()` always returned an array, which could cause runtime `.map()` or `.filter()` crashes if `localStorage` was populated with non-array JSON objects.
3. `updateFeedbackStatus()` accepted arbitrary string statuses without input validation.

### 🔧 Fix
1. Wrapped `JSON.parse` in a `try...catch` block in `subscribeToRealtime` and verified payload type with `Array.isArray()`.
2. Added `Array.isArray()` check in `getStoredFeedbacks()` with a fallback to `INITIAL_FEEDBACKS`.
3. Restricted `newStatus` in `updateFeedbackStatus()` to an allowlist of valid statuses (`ACKNOWLEDGED`, `ALERT_TRIGGERED`, `RESOLVED`).

### ✅ Verification
Ran `npm run lint` and `npm run build` successfully.

## Why
gluetun-rotator restarted gluetun on a blind 6h sleep, independent of the indexer guard. A guard rotation for an IP ban could be followed minutes later by a second tunnel cycle, and the guard could rotate right before the rotator did anyway.

## What
- Both actors record each rotation in `logs/vpn-rotation/last-rotation` (one epoch-seconds line, atomic tmp+rename).
- The rotator (now `scripts/gluetun-rotator.sh`, mounted read-only, runs as `PUID:PGID`) restarts gluetun once `GLUETUN_ROTATE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` have passed since the latest rotation by either actor; polls every `GLUETUN_ROTATE_CHECK_SECONDS` (default 300).
- The guard holds its rotation when the rotator rotated within the window or is due within it.
- Zero intervals (any spelling) refused by both; unwritable shared directory reported loudly at startup; in-memory fallback prevents a restart-every-poll loop.
- New `tests/gluetun-rotator.bats`, extra guard bats/pytest cases, mutation corpus entries for both scripts (all killed), and a test pinning the default intervals across script, module, compose and `.env.example`.

## Deploy note
Create `logs/vpn-rotation` as the deploy user **before** recreating `gluetun-rotator` (docker would create it root-owned). Recreate only via `docker-compose.utilities.yml`.

## Verification
- bats: executed=793 skipped=18 failed=27 (same pre-existing macOS-only set as baseline); pytest 758 passed; shellcheck clean.
- Adversarial review: round 1 REJECT (zero interval, untested inline loop) → fixed; round 2 PASS after remaining nits addressed.

author: gowads047-dot
body:
gtag.js loaded on every page for every visitor, with Consent Mode
holding analytics_storage at "denied" until the banner was accepted.
That kept the cookie off, but the 191 KB script — the largest resource
on the site, more than all the page's own JavaScript — still downloaded,
parsed and ran on every first visit: about a quarter of a second of
main-thread time on a desktop, four times that on a throttled phone,
competing with hydration on a homepage whose largest paint was already
waiting on the main thread (Lighthouse: gtag 250 ms of the 800 ms
bootup, 42% of it unused).

Now nothing from Google is fetched until somebody has said yes: a
returning visitor who accepted gets it at start-up (AnalyticsLoader), a
new visitor at the moment they press Accept All (or turn analytics on in
the cookie settings). The consent-mode default and the stored-consent
update still run first from the root layout, so gtag sees the right
state the instant it arrives; track() still no-ops without it.

What this gives up: Google's "advanced" consent mode, where the tag runs
before consent and sends cookieless pings that GA models traffic from.
With no advertising and a handful of accepted sessions a day there was
nothing to model — but it does mean GA now counts only visitors who
accept, where before it also received cookieless pings from the rest.

Verified on next start: a new visitor loads no gtag script; pressing
Accept All appends it and the config call lands in dataLayer; a
returning visitor with "all" stored has it at start-up with the consent
update ahead of it; "essential" loads nothing.

tsc, lint, 1299 tests.

author: lalmei
body:
Stacked on #214.

## Why

`Test on Linux` in `tests.yml` already ran `make test`, `make build` and
`make package` on `ubuntu-latest`, and `docs.yml` already ran `make docs-build`
there too. The self-hosted job in `ci.yml` ran all four again, on a machine that
has to be switched on — and nothing in it wanted a Mac. The references are
managed DLLs, and CI was already fetching the `linux-x64` client archive even for
that job.

## What moved, rather than vanished

| The macOS job did | Now |
| --- | --- |
| `make test` / `make build` / `make package` | already in `Test on Linux` |
| `make docs-build` | already in `Build docs` (`docs.yml`) |
| Upload `dist/*.zip` as a workflow artifact | the `test` job, so a PR still has a zip to download |
| Attach the zip to the release draft on push to `main` | a `release-package` job in `tests.yml` |

## What got better on the way

- **The release asset now waits for green.** The old arrangement had `ci.yml` and
  `tests.yml` racing from the same push, so a package could be attached to the
  draft while the Linux tests were still running — or had already failed. The new
  job is `needs: [test, benchmark]`.
- **Least privilege.** `contents: write` is declared on that one job instead of
  over a whole workflow, so the tests and the benchmark run with read-only
  tokens.
- **A run on `main` is no longer cancelled by the next push.**
  `cancel-in-progress` is now `pull_request`-only: cancelling a superseded PR run
  is good, cancelling a run that is part way through attaching a release asset is
  not.
- The owner/`run-local-ci` gate is gone with the runner it was protecting — that
  gate existed to keep fork PRs off the self-hosted machine, and it also meant a
  contributor's PR ran no build at all unless you labelled it.

## Checked before removing

- No branch protection and the repository's `main` ruleset is **disabled**, so no
  required check disappears with `ci.yml`.
- The `local-ci` environment has **no protection rules** — it was nominal, and
  nothing in the job used environment secrets beyond `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- The repository is public, so GitHub-hosted runners cost nothing.
- `make docs-build` passes locally, and `docs/dev/index.md` — which documented
  the release flow and warned that the runner had to be online — is updated to
  match.

## Left for you

The `run-local-ci` label and the `local-ci` environment now do nothing, and the
`astraterra-local` runner can be deregistered. I have not touched any of the
three: they are repository settings, not code.

author: earthlingdavey
body:
## What

`packaging/hotserve.service` gains a restart policy:

```
Restart=on-failure
RestartPreventExitStatus=1
RestartSec=1s
TimeoutStartSec=240s
```

A crashed hotserve comes back on its own and reattaches to the running apps; a start it refuses stays down.

## Why

The unit has never carried `Restart=`. A SIGKILL, an OOM kill or a panic in any goroutine took every site on the box down until a human ran `systemctl start hotserve` — while the apps, as units under the hotserve user's own manager, were still serving. It was the one incident on the 3am comparison board where hotserve's paved road is "down until someone types a command".

## Why this shape

Every hotserve exit is Caddy's (`cmd/hotserve/main.go` is `caddycmd.Main()`; nothing in liveswap/penaltybox calls `os.Exit`):

| cause | what systemd sees |
|---|---|
| startup refused (rejected config, host that cannot sandbox, no user manager) | `exit-code` **1** — Caddy's `ExitCodeFailedStartup`, which Caddy's own comment says never to restart on |
| running, self-initiated non-zero exit | impossible: `cmdRun` blocks on `select {}` |
| Go panic in any goroutine (no `recover()` anywhere); SIGQUIT | `exit-code` **2** |
| SIGTERM (`systemctl stop`/`restart`) | 0, or 3 if the stop fails; a stop job never triggers `Restart=` |
| SIGKILL, OOM kill | `signal` / `oom-kill` |

So `on-failure` restarts crashes and `RestartPreventExitStatus=1` never retries a refusal — including the case where an upgraded binary refuses the old config. Not `on-abnormal` (it excludes unclean exit codes, so a panic would stay down). No `WatchdogSec=` (Caddy never sends `WATCHDOG=1`). The start limit stays at systemd's default: a crash on every start ends in `start-limit-hit`; a slower loop retries for as long as it takes, like the app watchdog. `TimeoutStartSec=240s` sits above the start's bounded probe path with margin: `Type=notify` counts until `READY=1`, which comes after the manager connection's two dials (`NewConnection` opens two sockets, each 10 s to connect and a fresh 10 s to authenticate), the two manager probes `App.Start` makes (10 s each, `probeManager` and again inside `measureSandbox`) and up to two sandbox-probe attempts, each hung attempt then stopped with its 5 s grace and liveswap's 30 s stop slack — 40 + 20 + 130 = 190 s, before Caddy's own start. systemd's 90 s default would cut the in-process retry off on exactly the host it exists for, and its `timeout` restart would start the sequence over instead of reaching the exit-1 verdict. The install smoke test asserts `TimeoutStartUSec=4min` so the sizing cannot drift silently, and its client-side wrappers around a start sit above the unit's budget.

The sandbox probe's one retry on timeout stays. Its stated reason was "the unit does not restart"; it is now "the unit never retries an exit 1", the same fact for that path.

## Tests

Every assertion reads the unit's own record (`Result`, `ExecMainCode/Status`, `NRestarts`), never a `systemctl` exit status: Caddy sends `READY=1` in `Load`'s defer whether or not the config loaded (caddy.go, v2.11.4), so `systemctl start` can return 0 for a start that then exits 1.

- **e2e systemd suite** (real unit + real postinstall): hotserve is killed three ways — SIGKILL, SIGQUIT (exit 2, a panic's code), a `memory.max` write into its live cgroup (OOM) — and each row asserts exactly one automatic restart with the same app pid reattached. Then a config hotserve refuses (`liveswap_webhook` with no apps, the READY-then-exit-1 shape) is swapped in: the unit stays `failed` with `NRestarts` unchanged after longer than `RestartSec`, the app keeps running, and the restored config reattaches.
- **install smoke test** (the built .deb, both arches): asserts `Restart`, `RestartPreventExitStatus` and `RestartUSec` on the loaded unit, keeps the `NRestarts==0` tripwire, and adds a SIGKILL-comes-back stage before the upgrade stage.

Local: `make lint test`, `make e2e`, `make package && make install-test` all green (Debian 13, systemd 257; `Result=oom-kill` was reported cleanly, no race with `signal`).

## Docs

Present-tense fixes wherever the old "no `Restart=`" fact was stated or relied on: the unit's own comments, `liveswap/sandbox.go`, `liveswap/DESIGN-sandbox.md`, `DESIGN-threat-model.md` (app-unit lifecycle line; the probe-interference paragraph), `liveswap/DESIGN-liveswap.md` inventory, `liveswap/README.md`, `docs/upgrading.md`, and a new "If hotserve dies" bullet in `docs/after-first-deploy.md` — which also says that a restart loads whatever is in `/etc/hotserve/Caddyfile`, so an un-reloaded edit goes live then.

## Not in this PR

- `OOMScoreAdjust=` for the proxy (today the kernel rates it as killable as any app).
- `OnFailure=` alerting.
- Reaches installs with the next release; the `.deb` carries the unit.

author: strelov1
body:
## Summary
- Fixes a reported "tabs wobble/shake on scroll" bug in the account tab strip (`Profile / Contacts / Location / …`, and every other section that uses `TabStrip`).
- Root cause, confirmed via live debugging against a running local stack (frame-by-frame video analysis, then automated position/mutation/hover probes with Playwright): `TabStrip` sits in normal document flow, not sticky. A page scroll therefore carries the tab row past a pointer that never moved, and each tab/gap boundary crossing the stationary cursor fires a genuine browser `:hover` enter/leave. `transition-colors` turned every one of those into a visible fade — over a continuous scroll gesture that reads as the row shimmering.
- Verified two things were *not* the cause before landing on this one: the strip's own bounding-box position tracks `scrollY` with zero deviation (proven across ~300 sampled frames, two scroll patterns), and nothing in its subtree mutates (`MutationObserver`, zero hits) during an ordinary scroll — so this isn't a layout bug, it's specifically the hover-transition path.
- Fix: suppress the CSS transition (not the hover state itself — hovering still darkens the tab text once the page is still) while a page scroll is in flight, restoring it ~150ms after scrolling settles.
- This is a partial fix per the reporter: it measurably reduces the effect but a second, rarer trigger of the same visual symptom may still exist and hasn't been isolated yet.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm check` (svelte-check) — 0 errors
- [x] `pnpm lint` (oxlint + eslint) — no new warnings
- [x] `pnpm test` (vitest) — 157/157 passing, including a new regression test asserting the transition is `transition-none` during a `window` scroll event and reverts to `transition-colors` after the debounce
- [x] Manually verified against a locally running stack (`docker compose` + `vite dev`) that `getComputedStyle(tab).transitionDuration` goes `0.15s` (idle) → `0s` (mid-scroll) → `0.15s` (after scroll settles)

author: kristofferremback
body: ## Problem PR 2 (#2227) lets the backend open a tool step on start and finish the same row in place. The SDKs couldn't use that yet: `StepFrame` had no `phase` or `durationMs`, every remote runtime was forced to post a "Forwarded to …" thinking step, and each runtime carried its own copy of the `pi_tool_trace` serializer. ## Solution - `bot-runtime-client` `StepFrame` gains `phase?: "started"` and `durationMs?`, sent over both WS and the HTTP fallback. Phased frames bring their own `clientStepId`. - `remote-session`: - Sealed turns drop `started` frames and seal only the finish, with its duration. Encrypted scratchpads keep one row per call and no spinner, which the plan defers. - `RuntimeDescriptor.forwardedNote` is optional. Without it, no thinking step is recorded. - A new exported `toolTraceContent({ headline, sections })` serializes `pi_tool_trace` under the 9,500-char budget. It uses the trimming algorithm from claude-code-remote/pi-remote (re-pick the largest section up to 24 times, then fall back to a Details section) and caps the headline at 500 chars. pi-remote and claude-code-remote keep their private copies for now. No npm publish here; that follows the normal release. ## Test plan - [x] `remote-session` bun test: 315 pass - a sealed start+finish seals one step with `durationMs` - a plaintext turn forwards both frames - no forwardedNote means no thinking step - three 5k sections plus a 12k headline still fit - [x] `bot-runtime-client` transport: 24 pass (phase/durationMs reach WS payload and HTTP body) - [x] tsc clean for bot-runtime-client, remote-session, hermes-remote, claude-code-remote. Prettier clean. - [x] Adversarial verify: 1 finding (truncation could exceed the limit), accepted and fixed. --- 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? author: postmill-ai
body:
> Stacked on #91 (its commit is cherry-picked here because prod runs this branch; merge #91 first and this PR's diff shrinks to its own commit).

## Why
Sentry `POSTMILL-APP-P`: a user's Google AI Studio key hit a 429 quota error in Media Studio. The user saw a toast with the literal string `{"statusCode":500,"message":"Internal server error"}` and a truncated JSON blob in the render queue — i.e. *Postmill* broke. Mapping the plumbing showed this is systemic, not Google-specific:

- **36 media adapters** threw plain `Error("<X> failed: " + body)` — the upstream status was discarded at the throw site (three redaction tiers, 8 local copies of `isTransientStatus`, 4 SDK-backed adapters leaking `APICallError`).
- **LLM facade**: nothing classified the AI SDK's `APICallError`. It carries `{statusCode, message}`, which Nest's `BaseExceptionFilter` duck-types as an HTTP error and **replays as our status** — a provider **401 logged the user out**, a provider 429 showed Postmill's "too many requests" toast.
- Route catch-alls collapsed everything into "X is temporarily unavailable" 500s; Sentry filed all of it as unhandled Postmill errors.

## What
- **Kernel** `ProviderUpstreamError` (`kernel/src/upstream-error.ts`): `{domain, providerId, providerName, operation}`, `kind` ∈ auth | quota | rate_limit | invalid_request | timeout | unavailable | unknown, `upstreamStatus`, `retryable`, a message that names the provider, and deliberately **no `statusCode`** property. Classifier (status + body hints), JSON message extraction, redaction, `APICallError` detection by symbol marker.
- **Media**: one pattern across all 36 adapters + `media-helpers` (`mediaUpstreamError` / `mediaUpstreamFailure` / `mediaUpstreamFromPoll` / `mediaUpstreamFromUnknown`); local `isTransientStatus` copies removed.
- **LLM facade**: conversion at `_withFallback`, both `*WithModel`, and the `languageModel()` proxy; an open circuit breaker is a retryable `unavailable` error instead of a bare `Error`.
- **HTTP**: `ProviderExceptionFilter` → **502** `{ error:'ProviderUpstreamError', provider, providerName, domain, operation, kind, upstreamStatus, retryable, message, settingsUrl }` (502 because the frontend's global handlers own 401/402/406/429). One backend warning per occurrence; Sentry gets **only** `unavailable`/`timeout`/`unknown` as *warnings* tagged provider+kind. `rethrowProviderError` in the ai-user (10 routes) and posts-generator catch-alls.
- **Frontend**: `components/ai/provider-error.ts` (`readApiError`, headline/advice/toast text); `AiErrorDisplay` provider branch (*"Google AI Studio returned an error — this comes from your Google AI Studio account, not Postmill."* + advice + settings link); studio hook/shell/render-queue, daily brief (generate + regenerate), comment composer, generator, narrate modal, separate-post all read the envelope.
- Specs +40ish across kernel / adapters / facade / filter / controllers / studio / frontend; docs (`agents/providers/{media,ai}.md`, ops guide "Provider errors vs. Postmill errors"), CHANGELOG.

## Verified live (deployed to prod before opening)
Test org, bogus keys, restored afterwards (creds row diffed against backup):
- Media Studio → Google with a bad key: `POST /media/studio/google/generate` → **502** `{provider:"google", kind:"auth", upstreamStatus:400, message:"Google AI Studio rejected the API key (HTTP 400): API key not valid…"}`; toast reads *"Google AI Studio rejected the API key (HTTP 400): API key not valid. Please pass a valid API key. — The API key was rejected. Check the key in Settings."*; render-queue row shows the same; no raw JSON; **still logged in**.
- Dashboard brief / `/ai/hashtags` with a bad OpenRouter key: **502** `{provider:"openrouter", kind:"auth", upstreamStatus:401}`; the brief toast names OpenRouter (screenshot below); **still logged in** — this path used to replay the 401 and log the user out.
- Real key: brief 201, hashtags 201. Sentry: no new *error* issues from any of it.
- Suites: providers 3281, nestjs-libraries 6332, backend 1071, frontend 1856 — all pass; frontend `tsc` clean; lint warnings unchanged vs baseline (7 pre-existing).

Brief toast as rendered: `OpenRouter rejected the API key (HTTP 401): User not found. — The API key was rejected. Check the key in Settings.`

author: almothafar
body:
Two small things: a note telling visitors how to view the Pages demo, and a link from the demo's own package name back to this repository.

## The viewing tip is narrower than "use a phone"

The premise was that the demo needs mobile emulation to work at all. Measuring it says otherwise — in an ordinary desktop browser with a mouse, hide-on-scroll moves the header (`translateY` reaches `-56`), and the stretch header still expands from 56px to 220px on scroll-to-top. Nothing is broken.

What you actually miss is **iOS mode**. Ionic resolves its mode from the user agent, and `HidenavStretchheaderComponent` styles its host per mode — `:host.ios` gets a hairline border, `:host.md` gets a Material drop shadow. Measured across three profiles against the built demo:

| Profile | Ionic `mode` | host class | `border-bottom` | `box-shadow` | width |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop Chrome | `md` | `md` | `0px none` | present | 1280px |
| Pixel 5 (Android UA) | `md` | `md` | `0px none` | present | 393px |
| iPhone 13 (iOS UA) | `ios` | `ios` | `1px solid` | `none` | 390px |

So an Android profile only fixes the viewport, not the mode — you need an **iPhone** profile to see the `ios` rendering at all. The README note says exactly that rather than the vaguer "open it on mobile".

## The demo link

`@almothafar/ionic-hidenav v8.0.0` on the demo index now links to this repository, opening in a new tab with `rel="noopener"`. It is underlined in the Ionic primary colour so it reads as a link against the muted note text rather than disappearing into it. An e2e test pins the `href`.

## Verification

Lint clean, 10 unit tests pass, 11 e2e tests pass (the 10 on `master` plus the new link test), demo builds.

One note in the interest of accuracy: on the first e2e run, `header moves up when scrolling down` failed once and passed on an immediate re-run, on a page this change does not touch. It looks like timing under load — that test waits a fixed 600ms after a 250ms animated scroll. CI is configured with `retries: 1` and has been consistently green, so I have left it alone rather than widen this PR, but it is worth knowing the fixed wait is the weak point if it ever recurs.

author: araratpoghosyan
body:
A pod's detail could say what it is but not what it belongs to: the services that route to it, the config maps and secrets it mounts or reads, the claim behind its data, the account it runs as, the policies that apply to it.

Every link carries its reason — "mounted as volume", "envFrom in web", "selects these pods", "runs as" — because a relation nobody can explain is a guess, and a guess about somebody's cluster is worse than a gap. Nothing here is inferred from names that look alike: the references come from the pod's own spec, and the services and policies from selectors that actually cover its labels. The same config map reached through two containers is two relations, each with its own reason, rather than one that hides where it came from.

Pods first, since a pod is where every relation is concrete. A workload's relations are its template's, which is the same reader over a pod spec, and can follow once the shape has proven itself on the busiest screen.

author: lbockenstedt
body:
## Problem
In the LM WebUI **mTLS readiness card** (System → Hub Status), **AppBuilder shows as OFFLINE** — even though its WebSocket link to the hub is up and it holds the hub-CA mTLS client cert.

## Root cause
The hub's `mtls_readiness()` probes every connected primary spoke (AppBuilder included) with `SPOKE_GET_MTLS_STATUS` and marks any spoke that doesn't reply `{"status":"SUCCESS","mtls":{...}}` within 4s as `offline`.

Every *real* spoke inherits that handler from lm's shared `core/src/messaging/control_plane.py`. **ab is deliberately self-contained** (`hub_agent.py` does not import that control_plane), so the probe fell through to `logger.debug("Unhandled Hub message type…")` with **no reply** → the hub's `request_response` timed out → `online = isinstance(None, dict)` → **false "offline"**.

ab genuinely participates in mTLS (it stores the hub-CA client cert via `SPOKE_SET_MTLS_CLIENT_CERT`) — it just never reported its status back.

## Fix
Add a read-only `_handle_get_mtls_status` responder to `hub_agent.py` that mirrors the canonical control_plane reply shape (`enabled`, `ca_present`, `client_cert_present`, `client_key_present`, resolved `*_path` fields), reporting ab's own `/etc/ab/hub-client-*.pem` cert/key + optional `LM_HUB_CA_CERT`. Top-level `correlation_id` echoes the inbound `message_id` so the hub's `request_response` matches the reply (same pattern as the existing `get_version` reply).

Backward-compatible, additive wire change. ab still keeps its SAN-pinned dedicated cert and continues to ignore the wildcard `SPOKE_SET_MTLS_MATERIALS` fan-out.

## Tests
- New `test_hub_agent_mtls_status.py` (AST-extract convention) — asserts one signed `COMMAND_RESULT`, correct `correlation_id`, `status=SUCCESS`, an `mtls` dict with the readiness keys, and truthful present/absent cert reporting. All cases pass.
- Existing `test_hub_agent_help_ask_requirements.py` still passes.

body:
## Summary

PR #73 added `CustomerSuccessHandoffReconciler`/`PrismaCustomerSuccessHandoffRepository`, fully unit-tested against a fake repository, but deliberately left it unwired to any live schedule — at the time there was no control-api route that could create a `Deal` or move it to `CLOSED_WON`, so there was nothing for the reconciler to actually find. PR #74 added those routes. The reconciler itself needs no logic changes; this wires it into the orchestrator-worker process on a recurring interval.

- `apps/orchestrator-worker/src/customer-success-handoff-worker.ts` (new) — `BullMqCustomerSuccessHandoffWorker`, mirroring `database-reconciliation-worker.ts`'s `BullMqDatabaseReconciliationWorker` structure exactly: one BullMQ `Queue` + `Worker` pair, `queue.upsertJobScheduler(...)` for the repeatable tick, identical retry/backoff/cleanup options (`attempts: 3`, exponential backoff from 5s, `removeOnComplete`/`removeOnFail`), `onError`/`onFailed` hooks, `close()`. Since `CustomerSuccessHandoffReconciler.reconcile()` takes no arguments (unlike `DatabaseReconciler`, which needs a `scope`), the job carries no payload, so — unlike the Database version — no `@atoms/contracts` changes were needed; the queue name and scheduler ID are just local constants in the new file.
- `apps/orchestrator-worker/src/main.ts` — new env var `CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_HANDOFF_RECONCILIATION_INTERVAL_MS` (same shape/bounds/default as `DATABASE_RECONCILIATION_INTERVAL_MS`, 5 minutes), construction of the repository/reconciler/worker, `start()`, `onError`/`onFailed` logging, and a `close()` call in `shutdown()`.

Unlike `BullMqDatabaseReconciliationWorker`, which only runs when Phase 3 (`SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`) is configured, this reconciler has no external-provider dependency — it only needs the Postgres connection the whole worker process already requires. So it's wired **unconditionally**, alongside the always-on `worker`/`attachmentWorker`, not inside the `phase3Enabled` block.

## Deliberately out of scope / known limitation

- **No unit test for the new wrapper class itself** — `BullMqDatabaseReconciliationWorker` has none either; its only exercise in this codebase is a slow, opt-in, real-Redis integration test (`database-reconciliation.integration.test.ts`). Constructing a BullMQ `Queue`/`Worker` eagerly attempts an ioredis connection, so a fast fake-Redis unit test isn't a pattern this codebase has established, and I didn't want to invent a new one for this thin, mechanical wrapper. The reconciler's actual logic is already fully covered by PR #73's 6 unit tests against a fake repository — this PR only adds the scheduling shell around it.
- Live end-to-end behavior (a real Redis-scheduled tick actually calling `reconcile()` against real Postgres) is therefore unverified locally, exactly like `BullMqDatabaseReconciliationWorker` already is — this matches the codebase's existing accepted verification boundary for this class of component.
- No `packages/contracts`, `packages/db`, or route changes — purely wiring an already-tested reconciler into the existing worker process.

## Verification

Local environment note: `turbo` is unusable in this sandbox, worked around via `pnpm config set script-shell` pointing at `bash.exe`; all commands below use `pnpm -r`/`pnpm --filter` in place of `turbo`. CI uses `turbo` and is authoritative.

- `pnpm --filter @atoms/orchestrator-worker build` — new file compiles, `main.ts` wiring type-checks.
- `pnpm --filter @atoms/orchestrator-worker test` — 50 pass / 3 skipped (pre-existing), unchanged from before this change — including PR #73's 6 reconciler tests, confirming zero behavior change to the reconciler itself.
- `pnpm -r run build` — 14/14 workspaces, 0 errors.
- `pnpm -r run test` — 0 failures across all workspaces.
- `pnpm -r run typecheck` — 14/14 workspaces, 0 errors.
- `pnpm db:validate` — schema valid (no schema changes in this PR).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @atoms/orchestrator-worker test` — 0 regressions
- [x] `pnpm -r run build/test/typecheck` — 0 new failures

author: natosys
body:
## Summary

A damage control casualty operated on at R2E returned to that theatre for the definitive repair unconditionally, so the model had no way to represent the casualty flown out with the abbreviated operation still the only one they have had. That disposition is the one a forward surgical establishment reaches when it saturates, and its absence makes a sweep over forward surgical capacity self-limiting. This PR adds `r2eheavy.second_surgery.saturation_queue_threshold`: the number of casualties waiting to be operated on at or above which a casualty awaiting their definitive repair is released to strategic evacuation instead, carrying that repair and the intensive care following it to the national support base. The decision reads the queue and draws nothing, and the threshold ships at `0`, which disables the release, so the published model is unchanged.

A released casualty waits for their flight in an intensive care bed on the critical airlift route, whatever their triage priority: one whose definitive repair is outstanding is not a casualty a holding bed is for, so the release moves work rearward at the cost of forward intensive care rather than at no forward cost at all.

Closes #365

## Documented Manual Test Plan

### Setup

Seed 42, 30 days, `default` scenario, single replication. Two configurations are compared: the shipped `r2eheavy.second_surgery.saturation_queue_threshold = 0`, and the same field set to `1`, which puts the release in force. A third configuration, with the `second_surgery` block removed from `env_data.json` altogether, stands in for the model as it was before the field existed.

### Steps

1. `Rscript scripts/check_definitive_repair_release.R` — runs all three configurations and makes the twenty-three assertions below.
2. `Rscript scripts/check_baseline_reproduction.R` — runs seed 42 for 30 days into a temporary directory and compares the tracked evidence set byte for byte.
3. `Rscript scripts/run_all_checks.R --fast --jobs auto`.
4. `Rscript scripts/check_lint.R` and `Rscript scripts/check_roxygen.R`.
5. `Rscript scripts/check_env_data_summary.R`, `Rscript scripts/check_markdown.R`, `Rscript scripts/check_references.R`, `Rscript scripts/check_structure_tables.R`.

### Expected outputs

Step 1 passes twenty-three assertions across four groups.

*The shipped configuration and its validation.* The threshold ships at `0` and the accessor reads it as disabled. A threshold of `-1`, `"many"`, `c(1, 2)` or `NA` is rejected with a message naming `saturation_queue_threshold`.

*Disabled, the model is the one published.* A threshold of zero and no field at all produce the same campaign, compared as the arrival monitor in canonical row order. No casualty carries `definitive_repair_outstanding`, while 55 still reach the second operation, so that assertion is not empty for want of casualties.

*In force, who is released and how they leave.* At a threshold of 1 the release fires, 17 casualties at seed 42. Every one is on the damage control pathway, was operated on at Role 2E, has no `r2e_surgery_2_start`, has no `post_definitive_min`, carries `r2e_evac == 1` and no `return_echelon == 3`, and waits on the critical airlift route (`ame_route == 1`) holding an intensive care bed (`ame_icu_hold == 1`) rather than a holding bed.

*What the trigger counts.* `r2e_theatre_queue()` names and sums both halves of the queue, agrees with an independent recount taken directly from the same resources on a live environment, and the establishment fields more surgical sections (3) than theatre beds (2), which is what would make a section-only count unable to see the backlog.

Step 2 reports `logs/logs.txt` and all seven `data/arrivals_*.txt` diagnostics and `data/mass_casualty_events.csv` identical.

### Regression checks

The seed-42 evidence set reproduces **byte for byte**: `scripts/check_baseline_reproduction.R` passes on every tracked file. No value in `CLAUDE.md`'s Key Parameters table or in `docs/Single_Run_Analysis.md` moves, because the release consumes no random draw and the shipped threshold of zero makes its branch unreachable. The two seed-42 rows this change could have touched, the second-operation count (55) and the post-definitive care split, are unchanged; the check asserts the second-operation count directly.

`Rscript scripts/run_all_checks.R --fast --jobs auto`: **41 of 41 checks passed**. The lint ratchet holds at 1,164 findings and the roxygen ratchet at 171, both equal to their tracked baselines rather than refreshed.

The slow suite was not dispatched. The change cannot affect the died-of-wounds calibration at the shipped configuration, the branch it adds being unreachable there.

### Known limitations

The test plan measures the release at one seed and one threshold. It establishes that the mechanism fires, and on whom, but says nothing about the population effect of enabling it: doing so changes which activities consume random draws, so an arm with the release in force and one without are different realisations rather than a controlled comparison. No replicated measurement of the lever is published here, and no figure in any of the four documents is measured with it enabled.

The trigger is an informed estimate. No open-access source reports the surgical load at which a theatre begins to evacuate between the two operations, or the share of casualties it does so for, so the threshold is exposed as a planning lever rather than calibrated.

**The threshold cannot ship at a value that fires until #368 lands, and this is an ordering rather than a caution.** A released casualty's outstanding operation currently leaves the model at the moment of boarding: the Role 4 census reports only the bed types that echelon is given, and an operating theatre is not among them. Enabling the release today would take surgical work off the deployed hospital's figures and deliver it nowhere, understating total demand rather than redistributing it. Further Development L33 records the ordering, and #368 has been updated to carry the non-zero default as one of its implementation tasks, along with the requirement that a Role 4 operating theatre requirement be assigned rather than seized, with no queue, capacity or contention, and that a released casualty's repair be carried rearward on the duration R2E already draws so surgical time is conserved end to end.

## Documents updated

- [x] `README.md` (system reference: structure, trajectories, resources, assumptions, Further Development)

The R2E trajectory section gains a paragraph on the release, what the trigger counts and where a released casualty waits; the R2E Mermaid diagram gains the saturation branch and the two staging conditions; Further Development L33 is rewritten around what the shipped configuration still leaves out and the ordering against #368; and Remondelli et al. (2026) is added as `[59]` with the entries that followed it renumbered. Neither analysis document changes: no seed-42 finding moves and no replicated experiment was re-run.

author: vibesyemmy
body:
Closes `bug-orientation-name`. @Henry's decision in #173 — option 3 of the four on the card: add `rotate`, keep `orientation`'s meaning, deprecate it, refuse a disagreeing pair, and note the contradiction only where the word actually lies.

## The defect

`orientation` names the preset's **stored** form, so `'landscape'` means "the rotated one" — and on every monitor and laptop, stored landscape-natural, it produces a **portrait** screen. `1080p-24 --orientation landscape` is 1080×1920.

It is documented in three places, so **nobody is misled by a silence — they are misled by a word**, and only on half the preset table. obsrv-e7 measured two different viewports on 2026-09-14 without noticing and nearly filed it as a parity defect.

## What this does

- **`rotate: boolean`** on all six MCP tools that take `orientation`, and **`--rotate`** on the CLI.
- **`orientation` keeps its meaning**, marked deprecated. Redefining it was the other candidate and was rejected: it would have silently changed what every existing caller receives, with no error and a plausible-looking answer.
- **A disagreeing pair is refused, not resolved.** There is no reading of `{ orientation: 'landscape', rotate: false }` that is not a guess about which half the caller meant.
- **`rotated: boolean`** in the reply, and a sentence in `warnings` **only where the word contradicted the screen it produced** — a phone asked for `landscape` gets landscape and no sentence; a monitor gets portrait and is told so.

One shared pair of pure functions (`resolveRotate`, `orientationWordNote`) serves both surfaces, so they cannot drift on what a disagreeing pair means.

## Two things worth reading

**`obsrv_drive` briefly advertised `rotate` and ignored it.** It does not go through the CLI arg builders. I found it by **listing the published input schemas** rather than counting call sites — the source count kept giving me 5 against 6 with no way to tell which tool was missing. A flag that is offered and does nothing is worse than one that is not offered.

**The c2 check (#162) earned its keep on its first real change, in both directions.** It **passed** while `rotated` was in the reply but undeclared in the output schema — which is the `colorPainted` defect exactly: `additionalProperties: false` means a validating client rejects every snap with `-32602`. Declaring it turned the check red:

    obsrv_drive: APPEARED  rotated
    obsrv_snap:  APPEARED  rotated

Snapshot refreshed, register entry written. The green that worried me was the useful signal.

## Verification

- **1281 unit tests pass**, including 19 new ones: the pure pair, CLI parsing, the refusal in both directions, and the note's per-spec behaviour under `--matrix` (the word inverts on the monitor and not the phone, in one run).
- **`npm run typecheck`** — the real four-config one, not `tsc -p tsconfig.json`, which checks nothing (#175).

## For the reader

The thing I would attack: `rotated` is declared on `obsrv_snap` and `obsrv_drive` but the other four tools that now accept `rotate` do not report it back. That is consistent with what they reported before — they never carried `orientation` in their output either — but "you can ask, and only two will tell you what happened" is a defensible line rather than an obvious one.

author: derobins
body:
Extend the sanitizer axis with a `tsan` value, taking each compiler through an uninstrumented leg, an ASan/LSan/UBSan leg, and a TSan leg. TSan needs a leg of its own because cmake/ErnicSanitizers.cmake treats ERNIC_USE_THREAD_SANITIZER together with ERNIC_USE_SANITIZERS as a hard error. Six legs total.

Build the TSan legs at -Og rather than the Debug default of -O0. At -O0 the compiler does not reorder or cache enough to expose the races a production build will hit, which makes an -O0 TSan leg weaker than it looks: on the recv_thread_running race that motivated this work, gcc reports one race at -O0 and two at -Og. -Og and -O1 detect identically on both compilers, so -Og wins as the level meant to pair with -g.

Wrap the test invocations in `setarch $(uname -m) -R` on those legs. TSan maps a large fixed shadow region at startup and aborts with "unexpected memory mapping" when the loader has already randomised something into it; against the 32 bits of mmap entropy Ubuntu 24.04 ships, that takes out 13 of 14 tests before main(). The alternative fix, `sysctl -w vm.mmap_rnd_bits=28`, needs privileges the runner may not grant and touches a non-namespaced sysctl, so it has to be arranged out-of-band on the host -- see the note in rocm-systems' hipfile-sanitizers.yml. `setarch -R` needs nothing.

TSAN_OPTIONS sets only halt_on_error. TSan already fails a run that reports a race, since exitcode defaults to 66, so this narrows the failure to the first race rather than making the leg fail at all.

All six legs build warning-free under -DERNIC_WERROR=ON and pass 14/14 ctest plus 6/6 loopback, with no ThreadSanitizer diagnostics on either TSan leg.

Two limits worth knowing. `setarch -R` calls personality(2) with ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE, which a sufficiently hardened runner could refuse; it would fail loudly at the first test rather than silently degrade, and the sysctl is the fallback. And the registered tests are mostly single-threaded, so these legs guard less than their presence suggests -- tcp-mr-bounds-unit is the only one exercising real concurrency.

author: karanshukla
body:
Closes #7.

After "Stop session" the container service keeps running as root and holds its memory, and a session start D-Bus-activates it even with the unit disabled at boot. The menu now has **Stop container service**, enabled only once the session is stopped and `id.waydro.Container` still has an owner.

## How it stops it

`StopUnit("waydroid-container.service", "replace")` on `org.freedesktop.systemd1` over the system bus, the option the issue preferred. No new dependency, no `pkexec` process.

The catch is the message flag. `Connection::call_method` sends empty flags, so polkit refuses on the spot with "Interactive authentication required" and no agent ever prompts. This goes through `Proxy::call_with_flags` with `AllowInteractiveAuth` instead. `org.freedesktop.systemd1.manage-units` is `auth_admin_keep`, so the prompt asks for an admin password and caches it for a few minutes. The tray itself stays unprivileged, and a refused stop gets the usual failure notification.

## Menu state

`container_up` is tracked in the main loop next to `session_up`, off the `NameOwnerChanged` subscription the tray already had. The service coming or going changes the menu even when the tray state doesn't, so it joins the redraw check.

## Tests

Three new ones in the harness, against a mock systemd manager on the private system bus:

| Test | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `stop_container_service_is_offered_once_the_session_is_down` | Disabled with no service, disabled while a session runs, enabled after a stop leaves the service up |
| `stop_container_service_stops_the_unit_through_systemd` | Sends `("waydroid-container.service", "replace")`, and that `AllowInteractiveAuth` actually reached systemd |
| `refused_container_service_stop_is_notified` | A refused stop notifies and leaves the tray running |

22 harness tests pass, clippy clean on `--all-targets`.

## On the device

Waydroid 1.6.3, Plasma 6.7.5 Wayland, container service active with no session, which is the state the issue describes.

- Menu gating read straight off the running tray over dbusmenu: `Stop container service` enabled, `Stop session` and `Freeze` disabled.
- The polkit prompt and the actual unit stop are being verified on the laptop now. Result goes in a comment below.

body:
> This is a review-only topic for the `codex` release controller. Do not merge it directly.

## What this fixes

Ref discovery can succeed anonymously even when the subsequent smart HTTP RPC requires authentication. If that RPC exceeds the 1 KiB compression threshold, `remote-curl` sends a gzip-compressed body.

After the server responds with `401 Unauthorized`, the retry reuses that compressed body but rebuilds the headers without `Content-Encoding: gzip`. The server then interprets the compressed bytes as an uncompressed Git request and can reject it before parsing the command.

## Change

Restore `Content-Encoding: gzip` whenever `post_rpc()` reuses a compressed body during an authentication retry.

The regression test uses protocol v2, allows anonymous discovery, requires authentication for the RPC, pushes the request over the compression threshold, and verifies that both POST attempts advertise gzip encoding.

## Testing

- `t5551-http-fetch-smart.sh` (58/58)
- `t5559-http-fetch-smart-http2.sh` (58/58)

author: notaflightrisk
body:
If you check for `ErrEmptyInput` to skip windows with no data, you end up skipping the flat ones as well, beacuse a series where every value is the same gets that error too:

    stats.Skewness(stats.Float64Data{5, 5, 5, 5})
    // NaN, Input must not be empty.

A sensor that didnt move all day isn't missing data. This returns `ErrZero` for it instead, which `SampleSkewness` passes straight through as well.

The `ErrZero` message isn't a perfect fit for a constant series either, to be fair. But `Kurtosis` already returns it from the exact same check, and so do `ZScore`, `Rescale`, `CoefficientOfVariation` and `WeightedMean` when whatever they divide by comes out as zero.

The read-only `github release start-support` command verifies the compiled repository, exact main policy, annotated App tag, and published source archive. It requires a stable main successor outside the old line and prints an absent-ref push plus a proposed enumerated policy inventory. Qualification and finalization receive an explicit main base; support publication stays gated for the subsequent provenance and dispatch changes.

Updated maintainer procedures, agent guidance, and workflow arguments. Expanded checkout tests cover successful distinct roots, independently rooted nested checkouts, and symlink aliases. Validation: full `cargo xtask ci`, focused regressions, actionlint, Markdown and whitespace checks. Pinned release-plz 0.3.160 successfully prepared the version/changelog in a temporary support fixture, followed by a signed transaction and successful nonpublishing `release check`.
