author: pythonlearner1025
body:
## What part this touches

Two small things, one in the editor and one in the CLI package.

The editor's left panel holds two tabs, Objects and Resources. The Resources tab draws three
sections: Materials, Textures and Geometries. Each section has a header row you click to open or
close it. The header sticks to the top of the panel while you scroll the list under it. Its styles
live in `packages/editor/src/renderer.scss` at `.resources-section-header`. The markup lives in
`packages/editor/src/components/BPResourcesTreeComponent.tsx`.

The second thing is the `kite3d` package build. `packages/kite3d/package.json` builds `dist/cli.js`
with `tsc`. That file is the `kite3d` command. A project that lists the package as a path
dependency gets a symlink at `node_modules/.bin/kite3d` pointing straight at it.

## The bug

Two separate faults.

**One, the headers read as selected.** In the dark theme the three headers drew a light grey band
across the panel. Nothing was selected. The owner's words: "the colors are inverted - selected
should show light gray, not de-selected."

The rule was `background: var(--pt-app-background-color)`. That variable is `rgb(47, 52, 60)` in
the dark theme. The panel behind it is `rgb(28, 33, 38)`, which the editor defines itself as
`--main-app-background` and paints on `.editorSplitContainer`. So the header was two shades lighter
than the panel it sat on.

The hover rule was dead too. It named `--pt-minimal-button-background-color-hover`. No stylesheet
defines that name. Blueprint's variable is `--minimal-button-background-color-hover`, with no `pt`.
An undefined custom property makes the whole `background` shorthand invalid, so hover fell back to
transparent. I measured it in the browser: hover computed to `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`. The screenshot
`before-left-panel-hover.png` shows the result. The hovered header went dark and the two headers
next to it stayed light grey.

**Two, the CLI loses its execute bit.** `tsc` writes `dist/cli.js` with mode 644. `npm install`
does set the bit, once, on the file the bin link resolves to. The failure comes after that. A
rebuild of this repo deletes `dist` and writes a fresh 644 file. The bin link in the linked project
still points at it. The next command fails:

```
sh: /private/tmp/.../linkcheck/node_modules/.bin/kite3d: Permission denied
exit 126
```

That is the loop the terminator project hits: install once, rebuild the editor, run
`npx kite3d dev`, get permission denied, run `chmod +x`, repeat.

## The fix

- `.resources-section-header` draws on `var(--main-app-background)`, the variable the left panel
  already draws on, so the two can never drift apart.
- `.resources-section-header:hover` draws on `var(--pt-app-background-color)`, which is opaque and
  one step lighter than the panel. A translucent hover would let scrolled rows show through the
  sticky header.
- Two short comments say why each colour is what it is.
- `packages/kite3d/package.json` build script appends
  `node -e "require('fs').chmodSync('dist/cli.js', 0o755)"` after `tsc`.
- One test, `packages/kite3d/test/cli-bin.test.ts`, asserts `dist/cli.js` has the execute bit.

Nothing else changed. No TypeScript, no new file in `scripts/`, no lockfile change.

## The risk trade

The header no longer stands out from the rows. That is the point of the change, but it costs some
separation on a long list. The caret, the uppercase bold title and the count badge still mark a
header, and the hover lift marks it as clickable. The screenshots show it reads fine.

I changed the hover colour, which the brief asked me to keep. I kept the hover, not the broken
variable. The old rule painted nothing. Left alone, the header would have had no hover feedback at
all once the base matched the panel. The colour I chose blends to within 3 per channel of what a
Blueprint tree row shows on hover, and it is opaque, so the sticky header keeps hiding the rows
under it.

The rejected alternative for the hover was the real Blueprint variable,
`--minimal-button-background-color-hover`. It is `hsla(216, 13%, 61%, .15)`, 15 percent opaque.
On a sticky header that would let scrolled rows bleed through while the pointer is on it.

For the CLI, the rejected alternative was a script file under `scripts/`. A one-line `node -e` in
the build script needs no new file and runs on every platform. `fs.chmodSync` does not throw on
Windows, it just cannot set an execute bit there, which matches how Windows runs the `.cmd`
shim instead.

## Tests

All runs are headless Google Chrome 153.0.8010.48, viewport 1512 by 982, device pixel ratio 2, a
fresh profile each run. Nothing took focus. The server ran with `CI=1` and `--no-open`. I never ran
`kite3d install`.

```
cd /Users/minjunes/games/terminator-next && CI=1 node \
  /Users/minjunes/kite3d-worktrees/resources-header/packages/kite3d/dist/cli.js dev --port 4472 --no-open
```

I confirmed both times that the served editor was my build. I fetched each bundle from the server
and matched its sha256 against `packages/editor/dist/assets`. All three matched in both runs:
`served-is-my-build-before.txt` (`index-BrtAewVw.css`) and `served-is-my-build-after.txt`
(`index-nlFnOqG8.css`). The measure script also reads the served rule back. Before it returned
`background: var(--pt-app-background-color)`, after it returned `background: var(--main-app-background)`.

### The colours I read, dark theme, all three sections collapsed

| what | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| header background | `rgb(47, 52, 60)` | `rgb(28, 33, 38)` |
| panel background | `rgb(28, 33, 38)` | `rgb(28, 33, 38)` |
| header on hover | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` | `rgb(47, 52, 60)` |
| selected row | `rgb(45, 114, 210)` | `rgb(45, 114, 210)` |

All three headers read the same value in both runs.

One correction to the report. A selected resource row is Blueprint blue, `rgb(45, 114, 210)`, not
light grey. The grey the owner saw was the header's own background. A hovered row blends to about
`rgb(45, 51, 57)`, which is close to the old header colour, so the headers looked permanently
hovered or selected. Selection is unchanged by this PR.

### Screenshots I looked at

- `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-minjunes-blitz/278f5f97-7e16-4722-b1bc-c061014966db/scratchpad/evidence/resources-header/shots/before-left-panel-collapsed.png`
- `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-minjunes-blitz/278f5f97-7e16-4722-b1bc-c061014966db/scratchpad/evidence/resources-header/shots/after-left-panel-collapsed.png`
- `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-minjunes-blitz/278f5f97-7e16-4722-b1bc-c061014966db/scratchpad/evidence/resources-header/shots/before-left-panel-hover.png`
- `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-minjunes-blitz/278f5f97-7e16-4722-b1bc-c061014966db/scratchpad/evidence/resources-header/shots/after-left-panel-hover.png`
- `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-minjunes-blitz/278f5f97-7e16-4722-b1bc-c061014966db/scratchpad/evidence/resources-header/shots/after-left-panel-selected.png`
- `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-minjunes-blitz/278f5f97-7e16-4722-b1bc-c061014966db/scratchpad/evidence/resources-header/shots/after-left-panel-scrolled.png`
- `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-minjunes-blitz/278f5f97-7e16-4722-b1bc-c061014966db/scratchpad/evidence/resources-header/edge-shots/after-light-bpx-default.png`

Before: the three headers are one light grey band. After: they sit on the panel colour and only
the caret, the title and the count differ. Hovering one header lifts only that header. With
Materials open and the first material clicked, the row is blue and the header is not.

### The sticky header

I scrolled the open Materials list to `scrollTop` 220 of 4044. `document.elementFromPoint` on the
middle of the header returned the header, its opacity was 1, and its background was
`rgb(28, 33, 38)`. No row shows through. See `after-left-panel-scrolled.png`.

### The edges

`edges.mjs` walked six combinations: dark and light, times the `bpx-default`, `bpx-flat` and
`bpx-carbon` Blueprint styler themes the settings men

author: vincenzopalazzo
body:
## Problem

bLIP 42 contact secrets are a shared 32-byte value derived from both parties' offers. LDK already returns a derivation `Nonce` from `OffersMessageFlow::create_async_receive_offer_builder` (and from `create_compact_offer_builder` in #90), but there is no helper to turn that nonce plus the peer's offer into the contact secret.

Without this, wallets reimplement ECDH + the tagged hash `blip42_contact_secret` themselves, and it is easy to hash the wrong ECDH encoding (`SharedSecret::new` SHA-256s the x-coordinate and misses the spec vectors).

## Relation to bLIP 42

This is step 2 of the stack toward [bLIP 42 (Bolt 12 Contacts)](https://github.com/lightning/blips/blob/master/blip-0042.md), after compact offers ([#90](https://github.com/vincenzopalazzo/rust-lightning/pull/90)). It is based on current upstream `main` and does **not** depend on #90: async-receive already returns a `Nonce`. Compact-offer is the intended long-lived caller once it lands.

The rest of the stack (invoice-request TLVs, `pay_for_offer` wiring, BIP 353 names) stays on [#89](https://github.com/vincenzopalazzo/rust-lightning/pull/89).

## What this PR does

- `ContactSecret` / `ContactSecrets`: store the primary secret and any additional remote secrets, with constant-time `matches`.
- `compute_contact_secret(our_offer_signing_key, their_offer)`: ECDH of our offer key against their `offer_node_id` (`offer_issuer_id` if set, otherwise the last hop of the first blinded path), then tagged SHA-256 `blip42_contact_secret`.
- `OffersMessageFlow::compute_contact_secret` / `ChannelManager::compute_contact_secret`: re-derive our offer signing key from a persisted `Nonce`.

Explicitly out of scope: no invoice-request TLV fields, no `PAYER_OFFER_MAX_BYTES`, no BIP 353 names/signatures, no `pay_for_offer` contact params.

## Test plan

- [x] `computes_contact_secret_test_vectors`: bLIP 42 Alice/Bob vectors (path-only and issuer-id-precedence).
- [x] `matches_primary_and_additional_secrets` / `offer_node_id_prefers_issuer_id`.
- [x] `computes_contact_secret_from_offers_and_nonce`: two ChannelManagers derive the same secret from async-receive offers + nonce; a swapped nonce returns `InvalidMetadata`.

Rebased onto current upstream `main`. Fork review PR in the same style as #90; not aimed at lightningdevkit GitHub.

author: rafaelcg
body:
## Summary

`main` was broken for iOS for two days this week (a missing
`Localizable.xcstrings` entry) with nobody noticing, and every TestFlight
build has been cut by hand from `docs/TESTFLIGHT.md`. Adds
`.github/workflows/ios.yml`, no changes to app code.

- **build-and-test** (PRs and pushes to `main` touching `ios/**`): regenerates
  the Xcode project with `xcodegen generate`, then `build-for-testing` +
  `test-without-building` against an iOS Simulator destination,
  `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`. `ios/Scripts/check-localization.py` runs as a
  build-phase postCompileScript on the `pqp` target, so this build fails the
  same way `main` failed this week if a literal never reaches the string
  catalogue. SPM packages are cached, keyed on `ios/project.yml` (no
  committed `Package.resolved` to key on, the `.xcodeproj` itself is
  gitignored). Skips `pqpUITests` (needs a running local server + seeded
  Postgres, see `TestSeed.swift`) and `AttachmentUploadTests` (the one file
  in `pqpTests` that actually dials out to a real server with S3 storage;
  confirmed by grepping every `Tests/*.swift` for `.connect()`).
- **testflight** (`ios-v*` tag push, or `workflow_dispatch`; only after
  build-and-test passes): archives with the manual signing already in
  `ios/project.yml`'s Release config, exports (the committed
  `ios/ExportOptions.plist`, unchanged), and uploads via
  `xcodebuild -exportArchive` with `destination: upload` and the same App
  Store Connect API key trio Electron notarization already uses (`altool` is
  deprecated; `notarytool` does not apply to an iOS IPA at all). The `.ipa`
  is attached as a workflow artifact either way. Skips the credentialed
  steps cleanly, with a job-summary note naming what's missing, until four
  new secrets are set (see `docs/TESTFLIGHT.md` "CI builds"). Also carries
  the same "verify the tag is reachable from main" backstop PR 679 put on
  `android-release.yml`, since a tag isn't a reviewed commit the way a merge
  to `main` is.

Build numbers: `100000 + github.run_number`, written into both Info.plists
at archive time without touching the committed value, so a CI upload can
never collide with a hand-cut one (repo is at 32 today). Reasoning and the
one-time setup steps are in `docs/TESTFLIGHT.md`.

## What Rafael has to do

Four new secrets beyond the existing `APPLE_API_KEY_P8` /
`APPLE_API_KEY_ID` / `APPLE_API_ISSUER` trio, all documented step by step in
`docs/TESTFLIGHT.md` "CI builds" → "One-time setup":

1. Export the Apple Distribution certificate as a `.p12` from Keychain
   Access → `IOS_DIST_CERT_P12_B64`, `IOS_DIST_CERT_PASSWORD`.
2. Download **both** App Store provisioning profiles from the developer
   portal (`pqp appstore` for the app, `pqp broadcast appstore` for the
   ReplayKit extension — a profile is scoped to one bundle id, so the
   archive step needs both to sign both targets) →
   `IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_B64`, `IOS_BROADCAST_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_B64`.

Until all four are set, `testflight` still builds and tests but skips
archive/export/upload with a clear job-summary note.

Optional: a GitHub Environment named `ios-testflight` with a required
reviewer, same defense PR 679 put on Android's `play-production`.

Per-release flow: `git tag ios-v1.1 && git push origin ios-v1.1`, then watch
the "iOS" workflow. Promote to the public Beta group in App Store Connect by
hand as before (Beta App Review + group-add) — CI does not do that part.

## Verification

- `actionlint .github/workflows/ios.yml` — clean.
- Ran the same simulator build + test commands locally by hand (Xcode 27 on
  this machine): `xcodebuild build-for-testing` then
  `xcodebuild test-without-building` with
  `-skip-testing:pqpUITests -skip-testing:pqpTests/AttachmentUploadTests`
  and `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`. **563 of 566 tests pass** (the 3 skipped
  are `AttachmentUploadTests`, which need a running local server); build
  succeeded in ~37s, tests in ~27s including simulator boot, on this
  machine. Confirmed `AttachmentUploadTests` is the only `Tests/*.swift`
  file that actually calls `.connect()` / dials a real server.
- Did not upload anything to App Store Connect. Did not merge.

## Not touched

App/product code, `ios/project.yml`, `ios/ExportOptions.plist`, the two
committed `Info.plist` files (build number is set only at archive time in
CI, never committed), and every other workflow file.

body:
Delivers the tiling cluster and revises the auto-tiling inference to a true dwindle.

## Auto-tiling — dwindle
A bare `laura open <path>` splits the **newest** pane, alternating orientation by tree depth (a dwindle). Deterministic and topology-only — no geometry, no magic constant. Replaces the earlier area+aspect heuristic, which non-deterministically targeted the roomiest pane and leaned on a `width >= height * 2` fudge. Explicit split flags and raw `{"type":"open","path":"x"}` still bypass inference.

## Also in this branch
- Collapse gate: a split that would push any pane below the renderable minimum is refused with an `error` instead of committing (#57).
- `open --panel <id>`: swap a pane's file in place — same id, rect, focus, no new split (#36).

## Wording
"cascade" replaced with "split off the newest" across docs/skills — cascade implies overlapping windows, the opposite of tiling.

Deferred: content-aware relayout (wide file → wider vertical share) — a separate later feature, marked with a `ponytail:` note in `infer_split`.

Closes #37

author: rodneydean
body:
### Shield Security Hardening: Enforce Owner/Admin Authorization on Workspace Invite Link Endpoints

**What:**
Enforced workspace role checks (`['owner', 'admin'].includes(member.role)`) in `InviteLinksController` (`apps/api/src/workspaces/invite-links.controller.ts`) for `getInviteLinks` (`GET /workspaces/:slug/invite-links`) and `createInviteLink` (`POST /workspaces/:slug/invite-links`).

**Threat:**
Previously, `InviteLinksController` endpoints only validated workspace membership presence (`workspace.members.length === 0`), allowing any standard workspace member (`role: member`) to retrieve all workspace invite links or generate new invite links. This bypassed owner/admin invitation policy controls and enabled non-admin users to harvest or generate invite links for private or restricted workspaces (Privilege Escalation / BOLA / IDOR).

**Impact:**
Prevents unauthorized members from creating or retrieving workspace invite links, ensuring least-privilege administrative access control over workspace invitations.

**Verification:**

author: kimu1109
body:
## Summary
Reorganize the widget directory structure to clarify the distinction between generic reusable widgets and those specific to particular applications or system components. This improves code organization and maintainability as the project grows.

## Changes

### Directory Reorganization
- **`widgets/apps/`** (new): Move app-specific widgets
  - `MarkdownView.hpp/cpp` — Markdown document viewer (Markdownブラウザ専用)
  - `FileExplorer.hpp/cpp` — SD file browser (ファイル選択/保存ダイアログ用)
  - `AnalogClock.hpp/cpp` — Analog clock face (ClocksScene専用)
  - `DurationPicker.hpp/cpp` — Time duration picker (ClocksScene専用)

- **`widgets/systems/`** (new): Move OS shell components
  - `AppGrid.hpp/cpp` — Application launcher tiles (ランチャ用)

### Include Path Updates
Updated all references throughout the codebase to reflect new locations:
- Scene files: `HomeScene.hpp`, `MarkdownScene.hpp`, `ClocksScene.hpp`
- Dialog files: `FileSaveDialog.hpp`, `FileSelectDialog.hpp`
- Test files: `app_test.cpp`, `markdown_test.cpp`, `mem_probe.cpp`
- Build scripts: `run.sh`, `run_mem.sh`

## Implementation Details

- **No functional changes** — this is purely a structural reorganization
- All `#include` paths use absolute paths from `src/` root, so moving files requires only updating the include statements (no changes to file contents needed)
- PlatformIO and PC builds both recursively discover `src/**/*.cpp`, so build configuration files remain unchanged
- Host test scripts (`script/host_test/*.sh`) explicitly list source files, so those were updated to reflect new paths
- Follows the convention established in `CLAUDE.md`: widgets in `widgets/` are generic reusable components; specialized widgets go in `widgets/apps/` or `widgets/systems/`

## Rationale

This organization clarifies intent:
- **Generic widgets** (`Button`, `Label`, `Checkbox`, etc.) remain in `widgets/`
- **App-specific widgets** (used by only one application) move to `widgets/apps/`
- **System shell components** (OS infrastructure, not app-specific) move to `widgets/systems/`

This makes it easier for future developers to understand which widgets are safe to reuse across applications and which are tightly coupled to specific features.

author: zachlandes
body:
## Intent

The publication gate compares a native recording to a fresh replay only at its boundaries - a combat start, a floor arrival, a turn start - so a recorder defect shows up, if at all, as a digest that differs several screens after the decision that caused it. The card-reward Skip defect lived that way for weeks. This adds `./scripts/arbiter parity`: replay a recording and hold it to the `.journal.jsonl` the recorder wrote beside it at every decision - the same verb at the same place, the sampled state either side, and the complete digest of each reading - naming the first decision and field where the replay left the journal, or "hidden state differs" when every sampled field agrees and only the digest does not. It is the first of the two numbers the recorder's release bar is computed from; the second, coverage, follows.

The oracle is one class, `TraceParity.Compare` in `Sts2PilotTrainer.Replay`, game-free, and both the CLI and the headless recorder tests go through it - so the natural-run tests now check digests too, which the old `AssertSameTrace` never did. To make that comparison possible, `ReplayStep` carries `before_digest` and `after_digest`, `Arbiter.Run` fills them, and `RunJournalEntry.AsStep` is the one conversion from a journal line to a step. `RecordingCorpus.Enumerate` is the one reader of a corpus directory; a player's store is a copy the person names with `--corpus`, never a path the CLI derives, and each replay of a corpus runs in a fresh process for the reason `SelfProcess` gives.

Two digests are deliberately not held, each for a reason the recorder's own resume already carries (`RunCapture.MatchesTheRestoredLootScreen`): the reading a fight-ending decision settled into, because the retail client rolls the rewards on its own clock after the engine has settled; and the opening reading, which no decision is held to and whose hidden state the retail client's first room changes before the first decision - in eleven of the twelve store journals on hand that carry both digests. The opening difference is reported beside the verdict, never counted against it. Everything else is held exactly.

What holds nothing, and what fails: a recording with no journal, one whose journal is in a schema this build does not read (`UnreadableJournalSchemaException`, raised for the schema refusal alone), and one with `continuity = broken` are counted in the denominator and hold nothing, so the printed figure can never read as whole - both committed native recordings are of the first kind, their store journals being schema v1, so `parity --corpus manifests` reads 0 of 2 today. A malformed journal in a supported schema, a journal of another run, a replay the engine refused, an integrity other than `complete`, and a corpus directory holding no recording at all each fail the run; the last one refuses in words rather than passing over nothing.

Known limits: a journal older than schema v6 cannot be compared, so the store's parity figure is 1 of 13 today until new recordings are made; the discarded-branch trace in `RunCapture.ToManifest` still builds its steps by hand, without digests, because giving it digests would change what the recorder writes. The store run found a recorder timing defect - a `SkipRewards` read after the map move had begun - that this change reports and does not fix.

Verified by the full local session (`./scripts/build.sh && ./scripts/fetch-baselib-parity.sh && ./scripts/test-session.sh`, every project green with the game prepared), the game-gated `ParityTests` over `manifests/` and over synthesised journals, and `parity --corpus` over a copy of the author's own recordings. `manifests/navegreed-OJ-6QXhNgdg.recorded-fights.json` is regenerated for the two added fields only, because its own test holds it byte for byte to a fresh replay. The godot stub's `Font.GetStringSize` gains Godot's defaults so `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` stops failing on a pre-existing four-argument call.

Written with an AI coding assistant; the author reviewed and is accountable for every line.

## What Changed

- New `./scripts/arbiter parity <manifest> [--journal <path>] [--out <dir>]` and `parity --corpus <dir> [--corpus <dir> ...]`: replays each recording in a fresh process and holds it to its `.journal.jsonl` through the new game-free oracle `TraceParity.Compare` in `Sts2PilotTrainer.Replay`, comparing sampled fields via `ReplayTrace.SameSample` and the complete digest where both sides carry one. It prints per recording the run id, journal and replayed decision counts, and `PARITY` or the first divergence as a decision, verb and field (or `hidden state differs` when only the digest differs), writes `parity.json` under `--out` (default `build/evidence`), and exits 0 only when every journalled recording is at parity and every integrity is `complete`. A missing journal, an unreadable journal schema (`UnreadableJournalSchemaException`) or `broken` continuity holds nothing and is counted in the denominator; a malformed journal, a journal of another run, a refused replay or an empty corpus fails as `REFUSED`. Two digests are excused by rule: the settled reading of a fight-ending decision (`ReplayStep.EndsAFight`) and the opening reading, reported beside the verdict.
- `ReplayStep` gains optional `before_digest`/`after_digest`, which `Arbiter.Run` now fills; `RunJournalEntry.AsStep` and `RunJournal.Trace` are the one journal-to-trace conversion and `RunCapture` builds its steps through it; `RecordingCorpus.Enumerate` is the one reader of a corpus directory. `HeadlessGameplayCaptureTests.AssertSameTrace` now calls `TraceParity.Compare`, so the headless natural-run tests also check digests. `manifests/navegreed-OJ-6QXhNgdg.recorded-fights.json` is regenerated for the two added fields only.
- Tests: `TraceParityTests` and `RecordingCorpusTests` (pure), and game-gated `ParityTests` running the built CLI over `manifests/` (0 of 2 with a journal this build reads, exit 0) plus synthesised corrupted-field and wrong-run-id journals; `scripts/expected-hosted-skips.txt` regenerated. The godot stub's seven-parameter `Font.GetStringSize` gains defaults so `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` stops reporting CS1503 on the mod's four-argument call. AGENTS.md, README.md and docs/in-game-host.md document the standard.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is additive (a new CLI command, a game-free oracle, two digest fields on the replay step) with the shared oracle held by both the CLI tests and the headless recorder test; the remaining findings are two unaddressed round-5 output omissions and one small duplication, none affecting the verdict or exit code.

## Testing

The baseline suite had already passed; I ran the 12 game-gated ParityTests, the 19 pure TraceParity/RecordingCorpus tests and the 6 headless capture tests that now share the oracle (all pass, none skipped), then drove `./scripts/arbiter parity` by hand through every behaviour the intent names - committed corpus (0 of 2, both named no-journal, AT PARITY, exit 0), a synthesised journal at parity, a corrupted before field, a digest-only divergence reported as hidden state, a journal of another run refused, an empty corpus refused, and a mixed multi-directory corpus exiting 1 with per-recording counts - and captured the transcripts and parity.json artifacts. No failures; the only engine error in the output is a pre-existing headless stub gap unrelated to this change. No UI surface changed, so no visual evidence applies.

<details>
<summary>Evidence: parity CLI transcripts: at parity, before-field divergence, hidden-state divergence, wrong run id, empty corpus, mixed corpus</summary>

```text
\### 1. Journal the replay reproduces (synthesised from the recorder's own RunCapture over a fresh replay's trace)
$ ./scripts/arbiter parity build/test-scratch/parity-evidence/a/native-9F8CY60C5BK7-20260906-005737.replay.json --out build/test-scratch/parity-evidence/a/out
manifest  : native-9F8CY60C5BK7-20260906-00573

author: giswqs
body:
Fixes #2438
Fixes #2439

## Root cause

Both issues have the same cause. Values typed into the attribute table in edit mode are drafts held in the table's component state; they only reach `layer.geojson` when the table's own **Save** button is clicked. The table keeps showing the drafted value, so the edit looks done. **Layer actions > Save edits to ArcGIS service / source file / PostGIS table** reads the layer from the store, so it wrote the pre-edit features and still reported success:

- ArcGIS: `planArcGISEdits` found no difference from the baseline, no `applyEdits` request was sent, and the status read "Saved to ArcGIS: 0 inserted, 0 updated, 0 deleted."
- Local GeoJSON: the sidecar rewrote the file with the original values and reported "Saved N feature(s) to the source file."

## Fix

- New `lib/attribute-draft-commit.ts`: a small per-layer registry. While the attribute table holds drafts it registers a committer (its existing `saveDrafts`, which now returns whether it committed).
- A shared `commitTableDrafts` helper in `LayerPanel.tsx` commits pending drafts and re-reads the layer from the store. `handleSaveEditsToSource` uses it before building the write.
- **Also Layer actions > Export:** `handleExportLayer` had the same root cause (an export silently contained the pre-edit values), so it uses the same helper. This is a deliberate behavior change: an export now applies the table's pending drafts, and if they cannot be applied it stops with an error instead of exporting stale values.
- Drafts that cannot be applied (invalid JSON values, attribute form violations, or an update capability revoked mid-edit) stop the action with a new `layers.pendingTableDraftsBlocked` error ("The attribute table has unsaved edits that cannot be applied. Fix or cancel them, then try again.") instead of a misleading success. The string is translated in every locale.
- Unit tests in `tests/attribute-draft-commit.test.ts`.

## Verification

- Reproduced in the web app against the public editable `sampleserver6.arcgisonline.com/.../Wildfire/FeatureServer/0` service: edit a `description` cell, skip the table Save, run Save edits to ArcGIS service. Before the fix: "0 updated", no `applyEdits` request, service unchanged. After the fix: "0 inserted, 1 updated, 0 deleted", the table leaves edit mode, and querying the service returns the new value. Checked in both light and dark themes (the test feature's original value was restored afterwards).
- Export: with a drafted `description` (table Save not clicked), Layer actions > Export > GeoJSON produces a file containing the drafted value.
- The GeoJSON file path (#2439) goes through the same handler and the same commit step before `resolveLayerGeojson`; the sidecar `/vector/write` endpoint is unchanged. It was not driven end to end in the desktop build here.
- `npm run build`, `npm run test:frontend` (8582 passed, 0 failed), and pre-commit on the changed files all pass.

author: molinajonyy-hub
body:
BETA-GATE-1 · Lote C, **Opción 1 (sin migración)** decidida por el owner. Sólo toca la Edge Function `afip-wsaa`. Detalle completo en `docs/beta-gate-1/lote-c-wsaa-refresh.md`.

> **No mergear ni desplegar sin aprobación.** No se llamó a ARCA real: todos los conteos salen de un harness que reemplaza LoginCms.

## Causa raíz

Medido en código y en producción (sólo lectura):

1. **Ventana de 30 min.** Pedía LoginCms con el TA todavía vigente para ARCA → `coe.alreadyAuthenticated` → `estado_conexion='error'` (visible en la tarjeta ARCA) y `afip-cae` 502. En prod hubo 1 LoginCms a los 696 min del anterior, dentro de esa ventana.
2. **`force_refresh` abierto a usuarios.** Cualquier usuario con `settings_sensitive` podía forzar LoginCms desde el navegador, sin límite. Ningún caller productivo lo usa (verificado sobre el código desplegado de `afip-cae` y `afip-fe-query`).
3. **Sin control de concurrencia.** Dos pedidos concurrentes hacían dos LoginCms, y el perdedor marcaba error.
4. **Vencimiento inventado.** Si WSAA no devolvía `expirationTime`, se guardaba ahora + 12 h.

El TA no es legible por `anon`/`authenticated`, y los usuarios sólo reciben flags, nunca token ni sign.

## Comportamiento anterior

```
auth → arca_config → reuse sólo si !force_refresh && restante > 30 min
     → firma → LoginCms (sin dedupe) → persiste (vencimiento ?? ahora+12h)
     → cualquier excepción: estado_conexion='error'
```

## Comportamiento nuevo

- **Margen exacto:** `WSAA_REFRESH_SAFETY_WINDOW_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000`, definido una sola vez en `afip-wsaa/ticketPolicy.ts`. Con **más de 10:00** restantes hay reuse; con **10:00 o menos** (la frontera exacta incluida), TA vencido o ausente hay refresh. Helper puro con reloj inyectable.
- **Autoridad de `force_refresh`:** sólo un caller `internal` (credencial de servidor exacta). Un usuario del navegador, aun owner con `settings_sensitive` en su propio negocio, recibe **403 `FORCE_REFRESH_FORBIDDEN`** antes de leer `arca_config`, tocar WSAA o escribir estado. Un pedido de otro negocio sigue recibiendo `FORBIDDEN` antes. Semántica: *intenta* renovar aunque el TA sea reutilizable, sin prometer un TA nuevo.
- **`coe.alreadyAuthenticated`**, identificado sólo por un faultcode SOAP único e inequívoco: relee `arca_config` y revalida el TA. Si está vigente lo reutiliza, **sin** marcar error ni hacer fallar la emisión. Si no hay TA vigente, falla con `WSAA_TICKET_ALREADY_ISSUED`.
- **TA emitido:** tiene que traer un `expirationTime` que pase las validaciones de Phase 2A (ISO con offset, fecha real, futuro y ≤ 12h10m). Si no, **no se persiste** y no se inventa vencimiento.
- **Observabilidad:** una línea JSON por pedido con `business_id`, `decision` (`reuse`/`refresh`/`force_refresh`), `reason`, `result`, clase de falla, `code` y `remaining_min`. Nunca token, sign, clave, certificado ni TRA; un test lo verifica.
- **Contrato de respuesta:** el mismo. `error_code` es un campo aditivo en las fallas.

## Matriz de casos y conteo LoginCms

El harness cuenta cada LoginCms que llegaría a WSAA, no respuestas HTTP 200. El camino es el real: `authorizeArcaCaller` → `withWsaaAuthorization` → `ticketService`.

| Caso | Escenario | LoginCms | Persiste | Marca error | Resultado |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | TA con 11 min | **0** | 0 | 0 | reuse |
| B | TA con 9 min | **1** | 1 | 0 | TA nuevo |
| C | vencido / ausente | **1** | 1 | 0 | TA nuevo |
| D | force internal, TA con 11 h | **1** | 1 | 0 | TA nuevo |
| E | force de usuario con `settings_sensitive` | **0** | 0 | 0 | 403, **0 lecturas de config** |
| F | cross-tenant (con y sin force) | **0** | 0 | 0 | 403 `FORBIDDEN`, 0 lecturas |
| G | 2 normales concurrentes, mismo worker | **1** | 1 | 0 | mismo TA para ambos |
| H | 2 force concurrentes, mismo worker | **1** | 1 | 0 | un intento compartido |
| I | fault definitivo sin TA vigente | **1** | 0 | 1 | falla, sin TA falso |
| I2 | fault definitivo con TA vigente | **1** | 0 | 1 | sirve el TA vigente |
| J | 502 HTML / red / fault desconocido | **1** | 0 | 1 | sin éxito ni vencimiento inventado |
| J2 | 503 con TA vigente | **1** | 0 | **0** | sirve el TA vigente |
| K | recién renovado → siguiente normal | **0** extra | — | 0 | reuse |
| L | exactamente 10:00 / 10:00.001 | **1** / **0** | — | 0 | frontera fijada |
| M | alreadyAuthenticated + TA vigente | **1**, siguiente normal **0** | 0 | **0** | recupera |
| M2 | carrera entre 2 workers | **2** (aceptado) | 1 | **0** | el segundo recupera el TA del primero |
| N | alreadyAuthenticated sin TA vigente | **1** | 0 | 1 | falla, sin recuperación inventada |
| O | 200 con vencimiento vacío, sin offset, pasado, >12h10m o fecha imposible | **1** | **0** | 1 (0 con TA vigente) | no persiste |

Además: precondición 422 con 0 LoginCms, clasificación estricta, logs sin secretos y paridad con los validadores de Phase 2A.

**Controles negativos: 8/8 mutaciones detectadas por comportamiento**, con los archivos restaurados y verificados por sha256:

| Mutación | Tests que fallan |
|---|---|
| ventana de 30 min | A, decisión |
| frontera `<` | L |
| sin dedupe | G, H |
| force abierto a usuarios | E, fuente |
| alreadyAuthenticated sin recuperación | M, M2 |
| cualquier fault = alreadyAuthenticated | I, I2, J |
| vencimiento inventado | O |
| falla ambigua marca error | J2, M, M2, O |

## Concurrencia

- **Mismo worker:** exactamente 1 LoginCms por negocio.
- **Entre workers:** hasta 2, aceptado explícitamente. El segundo recupera por `alreadyAuthenticated`, sin falso error, sin perder el TA y sin hacer fallar la emisión.
- **Sin lock en DB ni migración.** Deuda registrada: **WSAA distributed refresh lease**. Se reabre ante LoginCms concurrentes entre workers, `alreadyAuthenticated` recurrentes por concurrencia o un aumento de volumen que haga probable la carrera.

## Errores ambiguos

Timeout, red, 5xx, fault desconocido o TA sin vencimiento exacto: nunca se inventa éxito, TA ni vencimiento, y nunca se pisan token/sign.
- **Con un TA todavía válido:** se sirve ése y `estado_conexion` **no** cambia; un fallo transitorio no rompe un estado usable.
- **Sin TA válido:** falla y marca error.
- **Falla definitiva** (certificado o autorización rechazados): marca error aunque se sirva el TA vigente, porque va a cortar la emisión cuando venza.
- **Backoff por worker** después de una renovación fallida con TA vigente: no se repite LoginCms hasta que ese TA venza. `force_refresh` lo ignora.

## Archivos modificados

- `supabase/functions/afip-wsaa/ticketPolicy.ts` (nuevo, puro)
- `supabase/functions/afip-wsaa/ticketService.ts` (nuevo, dependencias inyectadas)
- `supabase/functions/afip-wsaa/authorizationBoundary.ts`: `force_refresh` sólo internal
- `supabase/functions/afip-wsaa/index.ts`: el `run` delega en `ticketService`. Las funciones WSAA fijadas por el guard W1 quedan idénticas y se mantiene la resolución Vault-only de la clave.
- `tests/deno/afipWsaaTicketRefresh.test.ts` (nuevo, 27 tests, corre en CI con `npm run test:deno`)
- `docs/beta-gate-1/lote-c-wsaa-refresh.md`

No toca CAE, `afip-fe-query`, el asistente de configuración, certificados, Vault, frontend, CORS ni datos de Clic.

## Migraciones

**Ninguna.**

## Edge Functions a desplegar

**Sólo `afip-wsaa`** (hoy v18, idéntica a `main`).

## Head SHA

`23b834898214fdbe3511b7c84289e4fa15e5be75`, descendiente de `origin/main` `c828e8e`.

## CI

Todo verde en `23b8348` (run 35162843649):

| Check | Resultado |
|---|---|
| TypeScript + Lint + Build | pass (2m02s). `test:deno`: **262 passed, 0 failed**, con los **27** de `afipWsaaTicketRefresh.test.ts`; guards `arca-phase2a` y `no-real-data` OK |
| E2E Smoke Tests (m7-local) | pass (9m35s) |
| SEC-08E R3 Security Matrix | pass |
| SEC-08F Security Matrix | pass |
| Vercel / Preview Comments | pass |

Validación local:
- `deno test` completo: 262/262 (235 + 27 nuevos);
- guards `afip-s2-wsaa-vault`, `arca-phase0`, `arca-phase2a` (W1 verbatim), `arca-phase2b`, `edge-cors-contract` (cada uno con su self-test), `

author: 82deutschmark
body:
**Do not merge yet** — opened for review. The fix inside has not been executed against the 27B (needs a GPU; a424's was in use by another job all session).

## What was wrong

The 16-Sep LoRA step measurement on `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (a424 / GB10) reached `loss.backward()` with no error, reported a plausible falling loss, and delivered a gradient to **64 of 208 adapters**. The other 144 were not slow — `lora_B` sat at its zero init with an exactly-zero gradient, and since `dL/dA ∝ B` their `lora_A` could never start moving either. A training round would have looked healthy and trained a quarter of the intended adapter.

## Root cause

That checkpoint's `quantization_config` fake-quantizes **input activations** on precisely the seven projections the adapter targets — `self_attn.{q,k,v,o}_proj`, `linear_attn.{in_proj_qkv,in_proj_z,out_proj}` — plus `lm_head`. compressed-tensors implements activation quantization by replacing the module's `forward`, and the quantize call it inserts (`fake_quantize`) is decorated `@torch.no_grad()`. **The input is detached, so gradient cannot cross any targeted module.**

peft conceals it: its added `lora_B(lora_A(x))` branch keeps the output's `requires_grad` alive, and because `lora_B` is zero-initialised that branch propagates exactly zero backwards. The 64 survivors are `o_proj` and `out_proj` in every layer — the only targets whose output lands on the residual stream, so upstream gradient reaches them without traversing a quantized module.

Loading with `dequantize=True` does not help: it decompresses the **weights** and leaves the patched forward in place. This is also the same bug as the earlier `lm_head` "forward runs under no_grad" finding — `lm_head` is in the same quant group and simply had no LoRA branch to disguise it.

## How it was established

CPU only, on a424 (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`, `nice -n 19`), in the existing training venv so library versions are not a confound. A tiny randomly-initialised `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` built from the real config with only the size fields shrunk (every architectural flag kept: `full_attention_interval`, `attn_output_gate`, `head_dim`, the gated-delta head ratio, kernel width), same 7-name LoRA target list.

- Does **not** reproduce under any of: `eager` vs `sdpa` (resolved implementation printed, not assumed), `use_cache` on/off, gradient checkpointing on/off with `use_reentrant=False`, fp32 vs bf16. All 26 adapters get gradient in every one.
- Reproduces **exactly, module for module**, the moment the base layers' inputs are detached — only `o_proj`/`out_proj` survive.
- Confirmed by reading `compressed_tensors/quantization/lifecycle/forward.py` and `transformers/quantizers/quantizer_compressed_tensors.py`, and the checkpoint's own `config_groups`.

Full write-up with sweep tables and an explicit list of what was **not** verified: `docs/trace-findings/2026-09-17-lora-gradient-rootcause.md`.

## What this PR adds

`tools/assert_lora_gradients.py`:
- `disable_compressed_tensors_fake_quant(model)` — the repair, one pass over `model.modules()`, call after `from_pretrained` and before `get_peft_model`.
- `preflight(model, forward_and_loss)` / `check_lora_gradients(model)` — gate a training round on **every** `lora_B` receiving a nonzero gradient. Counts `grad is None` and `grad == 0` separately; checks `lora_B` only, because `lora_A` is identically zero on the first backward by construction and proves nothing.
- `--self-test` — CPU-only, seconds, no checkpoint needed: green on a healthy tiny model, red on this exact defect, and asserts the survivors are exactly `o_proj`/`out_proj`. Verified passing on a424 CPU.

No trainer exists in this repo to change — the training scripts live on the DGX boxes — so this ships as a standalone importable rather than a config edit.

## Preferred fix, for the record

Train from the plain BF16 checkpoint (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`), which carries no `quantization_config` and needs no code at all. The helper is for when the NVFP4 checkpoint has to be used.

author: sd2k
body:
## Summary

Inlining the Tempo tools in #1149 dropped one capability the proxy layer exposed: Tempo's `docs-traceql` tool. `v2` registers 6 Tempo tools where `main` exposed 7, so an agent writing TraceQL has no reference to consult.

The existing code comment said doc tools were deferred because the content is embedded in the Tempo binary, pending "a shared tools library." This takes a route that needs no new library and ships no copy of the docs: the content *is* reachable over HTTP, just only via Tempo's MCP endpoint (`/api/mcp`), which we can hit through the same Grafana datasource proxy the REST tools already use.

Tempo rejects a `tools/call` that carries no session, so each call opens a throwaway one — `initialize`, read the session id off the response header, then call — and keeps nothing between calls. That deliberately avoids reintroducing the per-session tool store, discovery and reaper machinery that #1149 removed. `tools/call` works immediately after `initialize` with no `notifications/initialized`, so it is two round-trips.

`docs-config` stays unexposed: it describes how to configure a Tempo deployment, which these tools cannot act on.

## Benchmark evidence

[o11y-bench](https://github.com/grafana/o11y-bench), all 13 `tempo_query` tasks, claude-haiku-4-5, **n=6 per task (78 trials per arm)**, identical pinned synthetic data, zero exceptions and zero tool errors in every arm.

| arm | mean | vs main |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (proxied Tempo tools) | 0.937 | — |
| `v2` (inlined, no docs tool) | 0.903 | −0.034 |
| **`v2` + this PR** | **0.946** | **+0.009** |

**`v2` alone is statistically indistinguishable from `main`** (−0.034, 1.2 SE) — there is no large regression from inlining. This PR's effect is also small in absolute terms (+0.043 over `v2`, 1.5 SE), but the per-task direction is consistent: it is better on 8 of 13 tasks, worse on 1, tied on 4 (**sign test p=0.039**), and it puts `v2` back at parity with `main` (+0.009, 0.4 SE).

The gains land where the mechanism predicts — tasks that need structural operators and error-chain reasoning:

| task | main | v2 | v2+PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| traceql-error-chain-orders | 1.000 | 0.847 | **1.000** |
| trace-error-analysis | 0.958 | 0.792 | **1.000** |
| find-slow-traces | 0.950 | 0.858 | **0.967** |

So the case for merging is: it restores a capability `main` had, with a small but directionally consistent measured benefit.

### Caveats, and two things I got wrong first

Getting to these numbers required fixing **three o11y-bench harness bugs** and **one defective task**, none of which are in this repo:

1. Its grounding check matched Tempo tool names by `tempo_` prefix via `startswith`, scoring every `v2` native-named tool 0 and manufacturing a fake −0.45 regression.
2. mcp-grafana ≥1.x rejects the agent's compose-alias Host with 403, failing 100% of trials until `--allowed-hosts` is passed. This is why o11y-bench is still pinned to v0.11.6.
3. `regrade` hardcoded loopback, and its readiness probe could never accept a 404 (`urlopen` raises `HTTPError`, making its success branch dead code).
4. `traceql-cache-refresh-hotspot` referred to "that earlier incident window" with no window in the prompt, which pushed the model to ask a clarifying question and make zero tool calls, scoring ~0.1. **All three binaries were affected** (main bailed 2/6, v2 5/6) — it was not a `v2` regression. With the statement made self-contained, bails went to **0/78 in all three arms** and the task rose from 0.21–0.38 to 0.86–0.90.

I earlier reported that this PR closed a large gap. It does not — that reading came from n=3 runs, where `find-slow-traces` swung 0.417 → 0.983 on unchanged `v2` code. n=3 is too noisy to read per-task deltas from on LLM-judged rubrics; all figures above are n=6.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test -tags unit ./tools/` — full tools suite green
- [x] New unit tests: happy path asserts two round-trips against `/api/mcp` with the session id reused on the second; invalid topic rejected before any request to Tempo; missing session header surfaced; `tempoMCPToolText` table covers plain JSON, SSE-framed, `data:`-prefixed, tool-reported error, JSON-RPC error, empty content, malformed body
- [x] Verified end-to-end against real Tempo 2.10.3 via the datasource proxy: tool appears in `tools/list`, all four topics return markdown (2.3–5.2 KB), invalid topic rejected
- [x] o11y-bench, 13 tasks x n=6 x 3 arms (numbers above)

## Open question

Named `get_tempo_traceql_docs` to match this branch's native style (`search_tempo_traces`, `get_tempo_trace`) rather than the proxy's old `tempo_docs-traceql`. Happy to rename for continuity with the proxied name if preferred.

author: blanklabel
body:
Reported from play as *levelling up on the field and then gaining another level after the first fight*. It is a **real double-grant**, not a card arriving late.

`PlayerRun`'s per-hero vectors (`hero_levels` / `hero_xp`) are grown **lazily**, seeded from `run_level` — and `run_level` is `max(hero_levels)`, so it climbs the moment *any* hero advances.

A Mote is drunk by ONE hero, which grows the vectors to just that slot. The first fight that grows them the rest of the way then created **every remaining hero at the party's best level, having fought nothing**.

`PlayerRun::start_level` holds the level the dive began at, and that is what a hero who has earned nothing is worth. The two answers only ever agreed until the first level-up, which is precisely why one of them had to be written down rather than derived.

## Testing

`a_hero_the_party_grows_into_starts_where_the_dive_started` reproduces the exact sequence (mote → one slot → first fight grows the rest) and asserts both halves: the heroes grown into are level 1, and the drinker keeps what it earned.

jposluns
body:
Closes baseline completeness gaps in `authentication.md` — the auth baseline 183 guides cross-link. A cross-family audit (codex + claude-opus-4-8) confirmed the normative core correct (RFC 9700, OIDC hygiene, the hashing set, federated-login-is-not-authorization, MFA-at-grant) and both families independently flagged the same missing controls, which are now added:

- **Session fixation:** regenerate the session ID (invalidating the old one) on login and privilege change; reject an unissued ID; enforce idle + absolute timeouts server-side; server-side logout invalidation.
- **CSRF:** cookie sessions must carry an anti-CSRF token or strict `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-Site` check; `SameSite` alone is not sufficient; no state change via GET.
- **Password quality (new rule 17):** length ≥15 single-factor / ≥8 with MFA (NIST 800-63B-4), passphrases, no rotation/composition, and known-breach screening (Pwned Passwords range API).
- **Account recovery (new rule 18):** random single-use short-lived account-bound reset tokens, pre-verified channel, non-enumerating, reauth for recovery-address/MFA change, invalidate sessions+tokens on completion, never silently drop MFA.
- **Distributed stuffing + enumeration** (rule 9); **HTTPS across the whole session** not just the credential POST, or an equivalent authenticated transport like SSH (rule 3); **PKCE `S256`** with fresh transaction-bound `state`/`nonce` (rule 12).

**Corrections (source-verified):** the hash preference now follows OWASP's branches (argon2id; scrypt if unavailable; bcrypt legacy; PBKDF2 for FIPS); bcrypt's 72-byte limit noted with the shucking-safe pre-hash guidance (keyed HMAC + pepper, not a bare digest) and the Python `bcrypt` 5.0.0 reject-vs-truncate boundary; the `htpasswd` example fixed to `-B -C 12` (bare `-B` defaults to cost 5, below OWASP's 10 — verified at the Apache docs). Quick checks broadened to probe every non-public path + transport with protocol-appropriate rejection (incl. gRPC `UNAUTHENTICATED`, WebSocket first-message auth) and to require a real secret scanner. Sources extended (NIST 800-63B-4, Apache htpasswd, pyca/bcrypt).

Gate suite green; three QA rounds converged (NIST-15 and bcrypt-5.0.0 boundary verified at source).

author: simonf-codes
body:
Refactor, no behaviour change. `/play` plays exactly as it did.

## Why

[ADR 0005](docs/adr/0005-human-like-bots.md) puts Maia v1 behind `/play` for the ratings under Stockfish's 1320 floor. Maia does not speak UCI — it returns a probability distribution over legal moves, has no search that could be given longer, and changes strength by loading a different network rather than by setting an option. `apps/web/lib/engine/` was written around *"any worker speaking UCI"*, so that assumption has to move before Maia can land.

Special-casing Maia inside the Stockfish transport would also make Maia-2 expensive to adopt, which is the revisit trigger the ADR is holding open.

## What changed

The seam is now a **move provider**:

```ts
interface MoveProvider {
  readonly id: string;
  init(): Promise<void>;
  newGame(level: BotLevel): Promise<void>;
  chooseMove(fen: string): Promise<string | null>;
  dispose(): void;
}
```

| File | Knows about |
| --- | --- |
| `use-engine.ts` | `MoveProvider` and React. Not which engine it has. |
| `default-provider.ts` | Which provider `/play` gets. The one place that decides. |
| `stockfish-provider.ts` | That a rung is a `UCI_Elo` and a move is a search. |
| `stockfish-engine.ts` | The UCI conversation — unchanged. |
| `worker-transport.ts` | A Web Worker carrying lines of text — unchanged. |

Two design points worth review:

- **`newGame` takes the whole `BotLevel`, not a number.** `BotLevel.elo` is a `UCI_Elo`, a Stockfish scale that means nothing to a network trained on Lichess games. Passing the rung lets each provider read the part it understands and keeps both mappings out of the shared type.
- **`chooseMove` has no time budget.** `BOT_MOVE_TIME_MS` is a Stockfish knob; one forward pass cannot think longer. It is applied in `stockfish-provider.ts`.

The brief's sketch included an `AbortSignal`. It is left out: nothing cancels a move today, and a parameter the only implementation ignores would be a lie in the type. Easy to add when something honours it.

`docs/architecture.md` §10 is rewritten and §10.1 describes the seam.

## Verification

- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit` (422 tests, 26 files), `npm run build` — all green.
- **`stockfish-engine.test.ts` is untouched** and passes. It is the regression net for the UCI state machine.
- **`stockfish-provider.test.ts`** pins the traffic byte for byte: `ucinewgame` → `setoption name UCI_LimitStrength value true` → `setoption name UCI_Elo value <rung>` → `isready`, and `position fen …` → `go movetime 300`.
- **`use-engine.test.ts`** is the proof the seam holds — it drives the hook with a `ScriptedProvider` that has no protocol, no search and no engine behind it, and asserts the hook hands it the whole rung. Adding Maia is a new file, not a change to the hook.
- **Ran the real thing.** `/play` needs auth and a database that is currently down, so `PlayBoard` was mounted on a throwaway route (deleted before committing, not in this diff) against a dev server, with the real 7 MB `stockfish.wasm` in a real Worker:
  - engine reached `ready`; picker showed the same six rungs with the same Elo labels; default rung Club · 1700 as before;
  - played as Black — bot opened `1. e3`, replied `2. e4` to `1… e5`; move list, status line and take-back behaved as before;
  - `?engineLog=1` console showed `depth 15` reached in `time 300` at ~1.39M nps, then `bestmove e2e3` while the search's own PV head was `e2e4` — that divergence is `UCI_Elo 1700` capping the engine, so the strength options are still being applied through the provider;
  - switching the rung to Beginner · 1320 reset the game and re-configured the engine.

## Not fixed here, deliberately

`recommendBotLevel` in `packages/chess/src/recommend.ts` still takes a Chess.com rating and compares it against `UCI_Elo` rungs. ADR 0005 records this as a category error, and a third scale arrives with Maia. It is a behaviour change, so mixing it into a no-behaviour-change refactor would make both harder to review. Noted in §10.1.

## New dependencies

`jsdom` and `@testing-library/react`, devDependencies of `apps/web`, solely so `use-engine.test.ts` can render the hook. The repo had no component/hook test harness before; `use-engine.test.ts` uses a `// @vitest-environment jsdom` pragma so the rest of the unit suite stays on the node environment.

author: brianduff
body:
## Summary

`bossctl review start --pr <n>` honors `review_batch_fanout`: enabled requests reuse automatic review classification and atomic batch admission, creating Claude, Codex, and Grok leaves followed by the existing quorum-driven supervisor. Disabled requests retain the legacy single-reviewer path. Capacity and metadata failures return errors without a single-reviewer fallback, and `--repo` substring disambiguation is preserved.

**Activation: manual batch behavior ships inert wherever the existing default-off `review_batch_fanout` flag is disabled. An operator with feature-flag administration access can enable it. Schema migrations run on upgrade regardless of the flag.**

Batch identity includes a generation, with existing batches migrated to generation one. Explicit re-review after a completed or failed batch creates the next generation without changing prior batches, members, or executions. Active batches are reused. Automatic starts always reuse an existing batch at the head and never advance generations. Explicit starts bypass automatic redundancy skips while retaining the four-unit capacity reservation. The design document reflects these semantics.

Batch completion can precede reviewer teardown. An explicit retry waits until all prior member executions are terminal before admitting another generation; otherwise it returns an error naming the unsettled execution and asking the caller to retry once teardown settles. This prevents overlapping generations from conflicting with the coordinator's batch-scoped double-spawn guard.

Each batch persists its explicit-admission provenance, defaulting existing rows to non-explicit. The immediate creation result carries the same provenance as the persisted batch. Verdict application's same-head duplicate suppression exempts explicit batches, allowing findings from a deliberate same-head re-review to materialize remediation. Replaying an already-applied proposal remains idempotent.

`PrReviewTriggered` carries `batch_id`, `batch_generation`, `batch_execution_ids`, and `already_active` alongside the legacy `execution` field. CLI output distinguishes a newly admitted batch from reuse that starts nothing, lists all reviewer execution IDs, and retains the single-reviewer output when the flag is off. Capacity errors and reservation arithmetic share `PRE_MERGE_BATCH_RESERVATION_UNITS`.

## Merge integration

Merged current main while preserving existing PR commits. The module-declaration conflict retains both upstream `review_guide` and this PR's `review_start`; boxed request dispatch remains intact.

## Validation

- `bazel build //tools/boss/...` passed (209 targets).
- `bazel test //tools/boss/engine/... //tools/boss/protocol/... //tools/boss/bossctl/...` passed (64 test targets).
- `checkleft run` passed (21 checks, no findings), as did the push gate.
- Regression coverage checks admission/reuse/legacy event fields, all three CLI output forms, rejection of completed and failed batches with one unsettled execution, equality of returned and persisted explicit batches, generation advancement, and same-head verdict application.
- Validation caught two defects in this revision's test fixtures: a missing required repository field at compile time, and a shared database connection held across a handler call that deadlocked the rejection test. Both were caused by this revision and fixed by supplying the repository URL and limiting the connection guard to a setup block before invoking the handler; the lexical scope also satisfies Clippy's lock-across-await check.

## Open Questions

None.

author: eschizoid
body:
Closes #335.

`BatchPipelineWrapper.flushLocked` held the per-topic `ReentrantLock` across the whole flush. Holding it across `sink.apply` is contractual and stays — `BatchSink` promises implementers that flushes never overlap, so the sink need not be thread-safe. The per-record outcome dispatch carries no such promise and was holding it too: `onBatchFailure` reaches a synchronous DLQ produce that waits for a broker ack, and `failAll` performs one per record, serially, so every other worker enqueueing to that topic waited out the entire dispatch and `close()` contended on the same lock.

## The change

`flushLocked` now calls the sink under the lock and returns the dispatch to its caller, which runs it after releasing. `enqueue`, `tick` and `close` all do that, and `close` still drains every outcome before returning. `bufferedCount` comes down only after the dispatch runs, so the in-flight gauge keeps counting records the wrapper still owns; an `Error` out of the sink decrements on the way through, since those records have already left the buffer.

## Measured, per the standing rule for lock work

The win bar was written down before anything was measured: a large, unambiguous reduction in how long a competing `enqueue` blocks, no regression in the suite, and if the bar was not cleared, close #335 with the measurement and no code change.

| arm | competing `enqueue` blocked |
| --- | ---: |
| dispatch inside the lock | **221 ms** |
| dispatch outside the lock | **0 ms** |

Dispatch budget in both arms is 20 records x 10 ms = 200 ms. Reverting the production change makes the test report 166 ms and fail, so it discriminates the change rather than passing alongside it.

The 10 ms stand-in makes this a lower bound. In production the per-record wait is bounded by `max.block.ms` plus `delivery.timeout.ms`, which add; at the 120s default and a 500-record batch the hold is on the order of hours, which is exactly when a consumer can least afford to stall.

Full method and numbers in `benchmarks/results/2026-09-16-batch-flush-lock-scope.md`.

## What is deliberately not here

A JMH throughput benchmark was written first and dropped. Two harness defects had to be fixed before its numbers meant anything — `MockProducer.send` is `synchronized`, so parking inside an overriding `synchronized` method serialized every DLQ send on the producer's own monitor and made both arms identical for a reason unrelated to the change; and a `Thread.onSpinWait` loop pinned a carrier thread away from the virtual threads doing the work. Even with both fixed the gating cell returned `483 ± 185 ops/s`, a 38% relative error against a 25% bar. Error bars wider than the effect are not evidence of absence, and shipping the benchmark would have invited someone to measure with an instrument that cannot resolve what it is pointed at. The reasoning is recorded in the results file so the next person does not rebuild it.

## Risk

The one real semantic change is that dispatches may now overlap each other. The offset ordering and invariant property tests cover whether anything downstream depends on them not doing so; they pass.

## Test run

429 tests in `:lib:kpipe-consumer`, green. Four integration tests fail locally with `DockerClientProviderStrategy` errors — no Docker on this machine — and fail identically on `main`, so they are environmental and CI covers them.

## Docs

`AGENTS.md` §18 described the old behaviour and would have been false the moment this landed, so it is rewritten in the same PR.

author: git-dann
body:
Goes back over the Requests / Charts / Delivery / Support work: accessibility, DESIGN.md, naming, popup height — and the **class** of bug that caused the outage rather than the one instance of it.

## 1. The mechanism, not the value

#630 fixed the bad `orderBy`. It did not restore the compiler check that extracting a Prisma args object into a named const silently disables.

⚠️ **`as const` does not restore it.** Verified both ways rather than assumed:

```ts
const A = { id: true, bogusA: true } as const;                          // 0 diagnostics
const B = { id: true, bogusB: true } as const satisfies Prisma.XSelect; // TS2353 ✅
```

`as const satisfies T` is the form, and **both halves are load-bearing** — `satisfies` re-enables the excess-property check, `as const` preserves the literal `true` types Prisma's payload inference needs. (With `satisfies` alone, `true` widens to `boolean` and every result degrades to `{ [x: string]: any }`. A first pass did exactly that; ~20 downstream type errors is how it was caught.)

Applied to **all 19 extracted args objects across 17 files**. Reintroducing the exact outage bug is now a compile error naming all three models:

```
wiki-insights.ts(110,19): Type '{ createdAt: "asc"; }' has no properties in common
  with type 'WikiInsightSeriesPointOrderByWithRelationInput'.   (+ VennItem, + Node)
wiki.ts(872,3): TS2353 'bogusRelationDoesNotExist' does not exist in 'ClientWikiInclude'
```

Both proved by deliberate sabotage, both reverted. `prisma-args-satisfies.test.ts` keeps it that way and carries its own *"did the sweep actually find anything"* assertion — a broken matcher would otherwise report "0 unguarded" and pass forever. It caught one the hand pass missed (`CHILD_ORDER`).

**Known gaps, so a green run is not over-read:** `$queryRaw` names columns in SQL strings (~13 sites, invisible to all of this); shapes built inline in a helper's return are not matched; `where`/`data` excluded deliberately.

## 2. `audit:clipping` was crying wolf

A full wiki sweep produced ~60 findings of which **roughly half were false**. A detector that noisy trains you to skim.

| Reported | Why it was wrong |
|---|---|
| Content inside a closed `<details>` | The exclusion was only consulted on ancestors that *themselves* clip; `<details>` is `overflow: visible`, so the walk sailed past it. 12/12 Charts findings. |
| A **sticky** element below the fold | Treated as `fixed`. Sticky is in normal flow and scrolls into view. |
| Text whose value is on a **titled wrapper** | Only `el.title` was read; hovering a child shows its wrapper's tooltip. |
| An inline child of an **ellipsed** box | The ellipsis doing its job — already judged by the TRUNCATED rule on the box itself. |

All four are now in `--self-test` (seven lookalikes, up from three), each proved to discriminate by reverting the fix.

## 3. What it found once trustworthy

None of these were caught by `tsc`, `lint`, `audit:ui` or 3,461 unit tests. All needed the page *rendered at a real viewport*.

- **The hero shattered the client's own name mid-word** — `Nort / hwin / d / Studi / o.` at 768–1023px, on the front door of their wiki. The team stack beside it is `shrink-0` and the row went horizontal at `sm:`, so from the moment the 256px sidebar mounted the title column absorbed every pixel of squeeze: **139px for 52px serif, 7 line boxes, 295px tall**. Now `lg:` — measured 303px / 2 lines / 120px, and ≤2 lines at all of 390 · 430 · 640 · 760 · 768 · 800 · 880 · 1023 · 1024 · 1280 · 1440, 0 page overflow.
- **`null%` on the Delivery card** — the section guarded `percent === null`, the card did not. Fires whenever a Gantt is drawn before tasks are broken out (the normal state), and that card is the landing page of a whole-wiki client share.
- **Monitors' uptime strip** — bars are `flex-1` floored at 3px and cannot shrink; the last ~10 days were past a card that is `overflow: hidden`, so unreachable (§45.2).
- **Changelog on a phone** — the action cluster is `shrink-0` in a nowrap row; editing a release was impossible at 390px.
- **The Design System type specimen showed `Wa…`** — 117px at 768, **36px at 390**.
- **Two Design System tables were `overflow-hidden`** — 198px of columns unreachable at 390px.

**44 wiki states × 4 viewports: 0 findings, 0 console errors.**

## 4. Requests — eight defects

Found by adversarial review, all reproduced.

- **Every internal mutation was fire-and-forget.** No intake hook defines `onError`. A failed delete left the row stuck on "Delete permanently?" forever — `setConfirmDeleteId(null)` sat after an `await`. ⚠️ The **public** half of the same file did this correctly via `rowError`; the internal half never adopted it. Now one `runRowAction`/`runBatch` pair a call site cannot forget.
- A **partial batch cleared the selection wholesale**, including the rows that failed. Now clears only what completed.
- The **stage filter offered a "Closed" bucket that was always empty** — the two sets were exactly complementary.
- A **deleted-but-selected row left a stuck batch bar** whose every button was a silent no-op.
- A **>500-row import failed with the bare words "Validation failed"** after all the column mapping. The cap lived only in the route's zod schema; it is now shared, and over-long titles are shortened and **counted in the preview**.
- **Escape stranded the import modal on its success screen.**
- The **"could not read this column" tooltip never rendered** — `title` on a Heroicon lands on the `<svg>` as an attribute; SVG needs a `<title>` child.

author: mernst
body:
`BuildJDK.gather_runtime_from_jar` and its `BuildJDK24` counterpart pass the
result of `JarFile.getInputStream(ZipEntry)` straight into a
`Map<String, InputStream>`.

That method is documented to return "an input stream for reading the contents
of the specified zip file entry **or null if the zip file entry does not exist
within the jar file**", and its body returns `null` when
`verifiableEntry(ze) == null`.  It overrides `ZipFile.getInputStream`, which the
annotated JDK already declares `@Nullable`; the `JarFile` override was
unannotated, and therefore unsoundly `@NonNull`.

typetools/jdk#292 corrects that annotation, which makes the Nullness Checker
report these two call sites:

```
daikon/dcomp/BuildJDK.java:266: error: [nullness:argument] incompatible argument for parameter arg1 of Map.put.
        class_stream_map.put(entryName, is);
                                        ^
  found   : @Initialized @Nullable InputStream
  required: @Initialized @NonNull InputStream
```

Here the entry always exists, because it came from `jfile.entries()`, so this
adds an `@AssumeAssertion` documenting that.

Companion to typetools/jdk#292; the two should be merged together, or
back-to-back.  If typetools/jdk#292 lands first, `test_daikon_part1` fails on
`typetools/jdk` master until this one lands.

author: kvnlng
body:
## What this does

This implements the release procedure Kevin approved. `main` is the development branch. Releases are cut to a frozen `release/X.Y` branch, tagged `vX.Y.Z`, and published by hand. Patch fixes land on the release branch and reach `main` by `git cherry-pick -x`; a release branch is never merged into `main`. `RELEASING.md` is the procedure.

Round 2 addresses the review of `59cd616` (B1–B3, S1, N1–N3; the rulings are in the PR comments). It also merges `origin/main` at `7438a90`, which commented out `tests.yml`'s push and pull_request triggers, and it updates the text to match that and the new "Protect release tags" ruleset (N5).

### `publish.yml`: dispatch only, with the check on every run

- **Trigger.** The only trigger is `workflow_dispatch`; `release: published` is removed. Creating a GitHub Release, which Zenodo still archives, uploads nothing.
- **The tag/version check was bypassable, and now runs on every run.** The old step was `if: github.event_name == 'release'`, so a manual run to `pypi` uploaded with **no check at all**. The unconditional step "The ref must be a release tag matching the version":
  - **first refuses any target but exactly `pypi` or `testpypi`** (B1). GitHub compares expression strings, and matches environment names, case-insensitively. So `PyPI` selected the `pypi` environment and the real upload URL, while the case-sensitive script treated the same run as a rehearsal and let it upload from a branch;
  - requires the wheel's version to equal `isocenter/_version.py`'s (parsed, not imported);
  - requires a run to `pypi` to come from a `refs/tags/v*` ref, with that tag equal to both;
  - lets a TestPyPI rehearsal run from a branch, but a tag, if it runs from one, must still match.

  Values reach the script through `env:`, never `${{ }}` inside the shell.
- **Expressions.** The environment name is `${{ inputs.target }}`. The URL and `repository-url` expressions send only `pypi` to PyPI, and the build check is what makes "only `pypi`" mean exactly that string.

### `docs.yml`: the site follows the latest release tag

- **Trigger.** `push: tags: ['v*']` plus `workflow_dispatch`. The `main` branch filter and the `paths` filter are gone.
- **`guard` job** (B3). It refuses any ref that is not a `refs/tags/v*` tag, or whose tag is not the highest `v*` tag by version order. `versionsort.suffix` is set for `a`, `b` and `rc`, so `v1.0.0rc1` sorts below `v1.0.0` and does not block it (S1). The job cap is 6 against step caps of 3+1.
- **`deploy` job.** It `needs: guard` and **alone** holds the `docs-deploy` concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress`. With the group at workflow level, a run the guard would refuse joined the group first and cancelled the latest release's deploy in progress. Now such a run never reaches the group. The job cap is 22 against step caps of 19.
- **The `github-pages` environment still permits this. Checked by reading, not by running.** `docs.yml` declares no environment, and `mkdocs gh-deploy` pushes to `gh-pages` with `contents: write`. The environment's `gh-pages`-only policy governs Pages' own deployment from that branch.

### Docs and tracked procedure

- **`RELEASING.md`** (new) covers names, how changes land, cutting a release, patch releases, the documentation site, and what cannot be undone. Round 2 adds:
  - patches forward-port by cherry-pick, and a section, "Never merge a release branch into `main`", explains why (B2);
  - step 8 is an ordinary copy commit, and patch step 4's dangling reference is fixed;
  - pushing the tag deploys the docs before PyPI, so the TestPyPI rehearsal must pass before tagging (N2);
  - no CI runs on push or PR (`tests.yml` is dispatch or `workflow_call` only);
  - `v*` tags are admin-only under the ruleset.
- **`docs/developer_guide.md`** §4 summarises and links to `RELEASING.md`. The build-check text is corrected (N3), and so is the Zenodo paragraph.
- **`docs/installation.md`** no longer says releases publish from a GitHub Release.
- **CHANGELOG** has one `[Unreleased]` → `### Changed` entry.

### Tests

- **`tests/test_packaging_contract.py`**
  - The docs trigger is exactly `{"tags": ["v*"]}`.
  - `test_the_docs_deploy_refuses_any_ref_but_the_latest_release_tag` **runs the guard script** in a scratch repo. Tags are created out of version order with distinct dates, and the repo also has a non-`v` tag (N1), a branch named `v0.10.0`, and `v1.0.0rc1` followed by `v1.0.0` (S1).
  - `test_a_refused_docs_run_cannot_cancel_a_deploy` pins the job split. The jobs are exactly `{guard, deploy}`. There is no workflow-level or guard concurrency. The deploy `needs` the guard, has no `if`, and holds `cancel-in-progress`. The guard step is absent from deploy, and the guard cap exceeds its step sum.
  - `test_publishing_is_a_manual_run_with_no_event_that_uploads_by_itself` pins the trigger set, the options and default, the absence of `event_name` from the parsed workflow, the environment, both URL expressions, and `needs`.
  - `test_a_publish_run_refuses_a_ref_or_version_that_does_not_match` **runs the check script** over 15 combinations, including `PyPI` from `main`, `PYPI` from a matching tag, `pypi ` with a trailing space, `TestPyPI` from a branch, and an empty target.
  - `test_the_publish_check_parses_the_real_version_file`.
- **`tests/test_version_contract.py`**
  - The runbook test reads `RELEASING.md`.
  - `test_the_changelog_opens_with_unreleased_or_the_declared_release` checks that the top heading is `[Unreleased]` or the release `_version.py` declares. A parametrized test covers the shapes, including a merged-forward patch.
- **Red check.** The round-2 tests against `59cd616`'s workflows, on 3.12, gave the 7 expected failures.

## Verification record

**Tip SHA: `73bfbe3ab2ae06aa06b44fce80b767469bc98244`** (merge of `origin/main` `7438a90` included). Both runs used `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=<tree>` and `pytest -p no:cacheprovider -v`, with no pipe. The commit is recorded in each log header.

| | 3.12.14 (`.venv`) | 3.14.7t (`.venv314t`) |
|---|---|---|
| Tree | worktree (`git rev-parse HEAD` = tip, `git status --short` empty) | `git archive 73bfbe3` |
| `isocenter.__file__` | `…/worktrees/agent-affe90f3ae6bbb990/isocenter/__init__.py` | `…/scratchpad/relproc_314t/isocenter/__init__.py` |
| Full suite `tests/` | `4828 passed, 7 skipped in 1195.33s (0:19:55)` | `4828 passed, 7 skipped in 1224.58s (0:20:24)` |

**Mutants.** Each is an anchored `str.replace` that matches exactly once, applied to a `git archive 73bfbe3` copy and run on both interpreters. Each diff is recorded in its log. Controls on the unmutated copy: 20 passed on the workflow tests and 16 on `test_version_contract.py`, on both interpreters. **All 24 were killed on both.**

| Mutant | Killed by (each interpreter) |
|---|---|
| B1a target allowlist's refusal arm made unreachable | 5 |
| B1b `TARGET` case-folded before the allowlist | 2 (`PYPI` from a matching tag, `TestPyPI` from a branch) |
| B1c allowlist widened to case-insensitive globs | 4 |
| B2a top-heading check accepts anything | 2 |
| B2b top-heading check accepts any version | 2 |
| B3a concurrency moved back to workflow level | 1 |
| B3b `needs: guard` dropped | 1 |

body:
## Change

Submit an incremental Lean geometric-scope completion for **JSP-000926 / Erdős 1115**, proposed as **Partial Progress**, for intake and review.

For every real function `phi` tending to positive infinity, the main target constructs a nonconstant entire function of some finite order with `log M(r,f) <= C * phi(r) * (log r)^2` eventually, such that every curve continuous on `[0,infinity)` along which `|f|` tends to infinity fails to have geometric disk length `O(r)`. Curve escape is derived; no speed or differentiability assumption is imposed.

Full target: `Erdos1115.not_erdos_1115_continuousOn` in `JSP000926.CurveStatement`. Disk length is the supremum of sums of polygonal-variation lengths of finite ordered disjoint compact subarcs wholly in the open disk, with traversal multiplicity. Infinite length remains infinite. Supporting theorems prove radius monotonicity, independence from negative parameters, and finite disk length for locally rectifiable escaping curves.

The analytic construction is reused from [plby/lean-proofs at 8822f7d](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1115.lean). Its existing target uses `LipschitzWith 1` and occupation time. The new contribution proves a genuine variation lower bound directly from the alternating gates, then supplies the general continuous-curve and half-line interfaces. The existing construction is not claimed as new. Mathematics remains credited to Gol'dberg and Eremenko, and the existing formalization to Codex / GPT-5.6 Sol. The fixed source's explicit Apache-2.0 notice and the adapted argument's provenance are retained. The prerequisite is imported through a hash-checked bootstrap, not redistributed as newly authored source.

This resolves the geometric scope of the particular linear-length counterexample. It does not formalize the prescribed exact-order strengthening, Hayman's positive theorem, or the broader optimal-length question. No new mathematical discovery or global first-formalization priority is claimed. Bounded public duplicate searches, original-paper comparison and exact quantifiers are documented in the package.
