author: cspades
body: # What does this PR do ? With `leave_one_out_baseline=True` and `normalize_rewards=True`, it is possible to get an advantage explosion with a reward distribution like `[y x x x x ... ]` where `x != y`, which is caused by numerical discrepancies between the mean of the square and the square of the mean when computing the standard deviation: ``` Rewards = [0, 0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.95] mean = 0.9499999 E[x²] = 0.90250003 mean² = 0.90249985 variance = (7/6) × 1.7881393e-7 = 2.0861626e-7 std = 0.0004567453 normalized advantage (of 0) = -0.9499999 / (0.0004567453 + 1e-6) = -2075.39 ``` This is not expected, because the idea behind GRPO is that with a trivial reward distribution (leaving out the current sample, so including all the other rewards), you get NO advantage, and a trivial reward distribution should produce `std = 0`, not `std = 0.0004567453`. This suggests that the incorrect answer is incredibly wrong after normalization, when it is only really significantly wrong (i.e. the raw difference against the mean is enough of a disadvantage). You could argue that with a single outlier reward, it should be harshly punished, but I don't think it should be punished with respect to the inverse of a squared FP32 rounding error. The raw / un-normalized error should be sufficient disadvantage and isn't a function of numerical precision. We fix this by extending the normalization mask `normalize_mask = (std > 0) & ~is_trivial_distribution` so that the trivial reward distribution for the sample `y` that produces an extremely small but non-zero `std` skips normalization similar to the `std == 0` case, which intuitively guards against _precisely the same case_. Before this fix, using vLLM or Megatron-LLM on a very "easy" dataset like CLEVR where it's very common for the pre-trained model to get correct rollouts except for a single incorrect generation, we get exorbitant disadvantage that damages training loss, gradients, etc.: After this fix, we go back to normalcy: # Issues List issues that this PR closes ([syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue#linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue-using-a-keyword)): # Usage * **You can potentially add a usage example below** ```python # Add a code snippet demonstrating how to use this ``` # Before your PR is "Ready for review" **Pre checks**: - [ ] Make sure you read and followed [Contributor guidelines](/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [ ] Did you write any new necessary tests? - [ ] Did you run the unit tests and functional tests locally? author: bartekus
body:
Two things, both corpus-level, no implementation.

## Decision D-03, completed

The owner ratified `003-work-and-run-semantics`, `004-execution-adapter` and
`005-acceptance-and-evidence`. All three keep `implementation: pending`, so each
is a work order and none is a claim about code.

`registry plan` offering `003` is now the same thing as permission to build it,
which it was not for the whole of this repository's first day. That gap between
what the tool schedules and what the corpus has agreed to was the thing AGENTS.md
was written to guard, and it is now closed for `000` to `005`.

## Spec 006 proposed, and deliberately not ratified

Specs `002` to `005` each describe operator verbs and each own a library crate.
The product is therefore specified, partly implemented, and **not runnable**:
`project register` and `doctor` exist as library calls and as nothing a terminal
can invoke.

`006-command-surface` claims `crates/statecraft-cli/` and fixes:

- the command tree, with verbs joining it only as the behavior behind them
  lands, because a command that prints "not implemented" is less discoverable
  than one that does not exist;
- **a command is a binding, never a second implementation**, which the coupling
  gate can actually enforce: a rule that leaked into a command would have to be
  written into 006, where it visibly does not belong;
- a closed exit-code vocabulary separating a **finding** (1) from a **refusal**
  (2) from a **failure** (4), which is the distinction a caller scripts against;
- `--json` and human output as two renderings of one value, with the JSON one
  contractual and the human one explicitly not;
- the executable's name stated rather than inherited. `D-02` gives the package
  `statecraft-cli`; `D-01` recommends `statecraft` and is not adopted for
  naming. Left alone, Cargo would settle the question by default and nobody
  would have agreed to the answer.

It is `draft`. Ratifying it is the owner's act, as always.

## Spec 001 section 3.3 was wrong and is corrected

Its claim-vocabulary section ended with "Today this repository is specified only
... no spec but `000` is approved, and no code exists." All three clauses are
now false. A section whose whole subject is the discipline of graded claims is
the worst possible place for a stale ungraded one, so it is now a dated table
with a row per change, and the previous state stays readable rather than being
overwritten.

The current row is deliberately narrower than "002 is implemented": the grade is
*implemented for its own territory*, the evidence is named in the same sentence,
and nothing in the repository may call this product runnable until `006` exists.

**This edit is also what the coupling gate demanded, and the gate was right.**
The first push of this branch was refused with `C-001`: it changed
`docs/decisions/00-founding-decisions.md`, which spec `001` owns, with no
authoring edit to `001`. The fix is this correction, not a waiver. `001`'s own
text was wrong, and the gate found it.

## Verification

`make gate` green, `make code` green, `make verify SPEC=001` passes 9 commands.
`spec-spine couple` reports 8 paths, no drift. No waiver line is needed or
present.

AGENTS.md and the README both still described a specification-only repository
with no code. Both are corrected here.

author: lupusmalusdeviant
body:
## Worum es geht

Erster spielbarer Prototyp: Die Seele (`soul` aus dem Figuren-Pack) läuft mit WASD oder den Pfeiltasten durch eine beleuchtete Arena, die 2.5D-Kamera folgt ihr. Ein Imp auf einem Sockel feuert ein Sigil-Pattern, das beim Bauen mit `grimoire_sigilc` übersetzt und vom Interpreter `grimoire_sigil` im festen Tick ausgeführt wird. Ein Treffer beendet die Runde mit deutlicher Reaktion; nach 1,5 s beginnt sie neu. `Escape` beendet das Spiel.

Die Engine ist über den Release-Tag `v0.3.0` gepinnt. Die offenen Entscheidungen dieses PRs hat der PO am 2026-09-17 getroffen (siehe unten).

## Änderungen

- **Engine-Pin:** `grimoire`, `grimoire_exec`, `grimoire_assets` und neu `grimoire_sigilc` (Build-Abhängigkeit) auf `tag = "v0.3.0"` (Tag-Commit `b2e7369`). Der Tag enthält, wofür der Branch zwischenzeitlich Engine-`main` gepinnt hatte: `FNP_MESH` Fassung 2 (Tangenten), den Bullet-Pass (WP3.5) und den Sigil-Render-Adapter (WP5.3). Drittanbieter-Versionen unverändert, die `clippy.toml`-Kopien stimmen mit `v0.3.0` überein, beide Goldhashes unverändert.
- **`content/sigil/imp_volley.sigil`** (neu): gezielter Fächer aus fünf Orbs in `enemy.hex_magenta` (H0) alle 50 Ticks, dazwischen ein sich drehender Ring aus 14 „Reis“-Dornen in `enemy.poison_lime` (H1) alle 100 Ticks; eine Silhouette je Bullet-Typ (PRD-0003 Regeln 3 und 4). Die Namen sind so gewählt, dass die alphabetische Nummerierung von `sigilc` auf die gleichnamigen Zeilen der Bullet-Pass-Tabellen fällt (orb 0, rice 1; hex_magenta 0, poison_lime 1); ein Test prüft das gegen `bullet_silhouette`, `bullet_palette` und `map_visual`. Das Build-Skript von `fnp_content` übersetzt die Quelle und bettet die Unit ein (bis zum Asset-Compiler WP4.3, PO-Entscheid 2026-09-17).
- **`fnp_game::arena`** (neu): `ArenaGame` mit Bewegung nach PRD-0005 FR-01 (90 % der Zielgeschwindigkeit nach 3 Ticks, leichtes Nachgleiten), Arena- und Imp-Begrenzung, `AimTarget` auf die Spielerposition des laufenden Ticks, Sigil-Interpreter, spielseitiger Broadphase über `grimoire_collide::SpatialGrid`, Treffer gegen eine Kapsel (FR-03), Pause der Emitter und `ClearRequest`, Neustart nach 90 Ticks. `FiendsGame` (P0-Demo) bleibt unverändert.
- **`fnp_game::arena::present`** (neu): Arena mit Boden, Säulen, Kohlebecken, Fackeln, Mondlicht; Seele und Imp als geskinnte Figuren; Treffer-Reaktion (Figur kippt und krümmt sich, rotes Leuchten, Blinken, roter Lichtblitz), Aufstieg nach dem Neustart; Spieler-Marker-Ring zeigt die Trefferkapsel. **Bullets** ausschließlich über `grimoire::adapters::sigil_render::extract_bullets` in `StageFrame::bullets`; der Bullet-Pass zeichnet sie als Billboards auf Ebene 6 und leitet die Geschoss-Lichter selbst über `point_light_from_bullet` ab. Das Spiel baut weder Bullet-Meshes noch Bullet-Lichter.
- **`fnp_app`**: Pfad zum Pack über `--pack` oder `FNP_FIGURE_PACK`, sonst klare Meldung und Exit-Code 2 vor dem Fenster. Eigene Hauptschleife auf der Plattformschicht (Begründung unten), generisch über den Renderer, headless getestet. Am Laufende eine Zeile mit Frame-Zeiten, Spitzenwerten für Bullets und Lichter, Runde und Treffern.
- **`fnp_sim_harness`**: `run_arena`, `run_arena_with_executor`, `simulate_arena` mit Bot; Gate `tests/arena_determinism.rs` mit Goldhash `0x9001d4a1d2f7125e` (Seed 42, 3.600 Ticks) und Thread-Gate 1/2/N. Der zuerst eingefrorene Wert `0xc17457a2f7e6fb49` wurde in einem eigenen Commit erneuert (vom PO bestätigt, PO-Entscheid 2026-09-17), weil die Umbenennung der Paletten die Content-Identität der Unit ändert (Nachweis im Commit: mit der alten Unit ergibt sich exakt der alte Hash, der übrige Spielzustand ist an allen 3.600 Ticks gleich). Die Umstellung auf den Bullet-Pass selbst ändert den Hash nicht.

## Vorläufig (bewusst)

- **Sigil → Kollision spielseitig:** Der Fassaden-Adapter aus Vertrag §9.6 (`SigilCollidePlugin`) existiert noch nicht; `arena.broadphase` baut dasselbe Gitter nach derselben Regel selbst.
- **Eigene Hauptschleife:** `App::run` gibt Plugins keinen Zugriff auf den `WgpuRenderer`, `load_figure` braucht ihn aber. Die Schleife folgt der Frame-Reihenfolge der Fassade (§9, §9.3); Profiler, Overlay und Mauszielen der Fassade fehlen darin. Der Fassaden-Haken für die Asset-Registrierung ist als Folgearbeit freigegeben.
- **Keine Animation:** Ruhepose und eine gekrümmte Treffer-Pose; Imp in Bindepose.
- **Blob-Schatten statt Schattenkarte:** Geskinnte Figuren werfen noch keinen Schatten der Schattenkarte (Engine-Lücke), deshalb Preset „Low“.
- **Kein Gamepad:** Die Plattformschicht liefert keine Gamepad-Ereignisse; der linke Stick folgt mit ihr.
- Werte wie Trefferkapsel (Radius 0,28 m, Schulterstrecke 0,24 m), Geschwindigkeiten, Kamera und Lichter sind Startwerte fürs Spielgefühl, nicht abgestimmt.

## Nachweis

- Lokal (Windows): `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` und `cargo build --workspace` grün; Arena-Goldhash im Debug- und Release-Profil gleich.
- Offscreen-Lauf mit dem echten Loop (`crates/fnp_app/tests/offscreen_capture.rs`, Software-Adapter, Figuren-Pack r4, Bullet-Pass): 480 Frames, Ausweichen, Treffer, Neustart, weiterlaufen; Spitze 43 Bullets, 3.743 Bullets gezeichnet, **verworfen: 0 nicht abbildbar, 0 ungültig, 0 fremder Palettenraum**; Spitze 18 Punktlichter, davon 8 vom Renderer abgeleitete Geschoss-Lichter; 2 Treffer. Rund 65 ms je Frame auf dem CPU-Adapter (960×540, 4× MSAA, Rücklesen jedes zweiten Bildes).
- Bot-Szenario (60 s): 13 Runden, 12 Treffer, Spitze 55 Bullets.
- Fenster-Rauchtest der Release-Exe (Software-Adapter, Zweitmonitor ohne Fokus, `GRIMOIRE_EXAMPLE_MAX_FRAMES=300`, Pack r4, ohne Eingabe, mit Bullet-Pass): Pack in 0,3 s geladen (Seele 7 Teile, 20 Gelenke, 1,96 m; Imp 6 Teile, 1,06 m), 300 Frames, mittlere Frame-Zeit 97,1 ms (Spitze 1,01 s im ersten Frame), 1.613 Ticks, Spitze 24 Bullets, 1.647 Bullets gezeichnet, verworfen 0/0/0, 7 Treffer, Exit-Code 0. Auf der Grafikkarte nicht gemessen.
- Fehlerpfade: ohne Pack bzw. mit nicht vorhandenem Pfad Meldung und Exit-Code 2, kein Fenster.
- CI: Lauf 35162851580 (Kopf `47c48c6`, vor dem Bullet-Pass), Lauf 35165412835 (Kopf `6b7dfc5`, mit Bullet-Pass, Engine-`main`) und Lauf 35197999985 (Kopf `4a455dc`, Tag `v0.3.0`, `main` eingemergt) grün auf Windows, Linux und macOS; beide Goldhashes (P0 `0x527020aecf764ca7`, Arena `0x9001d4a1d2f7125e`) und der Tabellen-Abgleich der Unit stimmen auf allen drei Systemen.

## Entschieden (PO-Entscheid 2026-09-17)

1. **Engine-Release-Tag:** `v0.3.0` ist veröffentlicht; dieser PR pinnt ihn (`build(engine): bump grimoire to v0.3.0`).
2. **Arena-Goldhash** `0x9001d4a1d2f7125e`: bestätigt.
3. **Sigil-Übersetzung per Build-Skript:** angenommen bis zum Asset-Compiler (WP4.3).
4. **P0-Demo `FiendsGame`** samt Goldhash: wird nach diesem Merge in einem eigenen PR entfernt, nicht hier.
5. **Fassaden-Haken für die Asset-Registrierung** und **gemeinsamer Silhouetten-/Paletten-Katalog** für Sigil: als Folgearbeit freigegeben, nicht Teil dieses PRs. Bis zum Katalog hält der Tabellen-Test in `fnp_content` die Namen der Unit ausgerichtet.

author: ericmoore207
body:
## What this changes

Before advising on testing, I checked what's deployed: **it's up, running current `main`, and its database is empty** — no courses, no admin, nobody on it. Which exposed a gap: there was no way to create the first admin.

## The token you're planning to set wouldn't have worked

`ADMIN_REGISTRATION_TOKEN` is read by the API to decide whether `/auth/admin-register` works. **Terraform never passed it to the container.** You could have added the secret in GitHub, deployed, and still hit *"Admin registration is not configured on this server"* — with nothing to indicate why.

Now wired through: workflow → root variable → module → container environment. Empty is still the default, and empty keeps that page shut.

## And a command, for when you'd rather not leave a token lying around

```bash
python manage.py create_admin --email you@example.com --name "Your Name"
```

- Generates a password, prints it **once**, marks it must-change.
- **Safe to run twice:** promotes an existing account instead of duplicating it, and only touches the password if you pass a new one — a stray second run can't lock anyone out.
- Refuses a malformed address; says so plainly when the username is taken.

## What the token actually is — worth knowing before you set it

It's a password for *becoming an admin*. Anyone who has it can create an admin account on your platform with no approval from you. No expiry, no audit trail of its own. So the runbook says: make it long and random, use it once for yourself, **clear the secret and redeploy**, then add everyone else from Admin → Admin team where each change is recorded against a name.

## `docs/GOING-LIVE.md`

The order to do things in: the variables and where each comes from (including that `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL` must be a **verified sender** in Brevo or mail silently goes nowhere), the **Paystack webhook URL** (without it a payment stays "pending" when a student closes the tab), why **categories must exist before anyone can register**, when to switch test keys for live ones, and what each symptom on the live site means.

## Checklist

- [x] Backend changes have tests — 311 passing, 5 new
- [x] ruff clean; `terraform fmt` and `terraform validate` clean

author: kkunkunya
body:
按 `docs/design/issue-draft-group-finalize.md` §10 的落地顺序，实现前 3 个提交（服务层 + finalize 接整组）。**载荷里没有 `children` 时走的就是「1 个节点的组」，所以本 PR 合入时对外行为一字不变。**

## 三个提交

1. `refactor(issue)` — `IssueService.Create` 拆成 `createInTx` / `afterCommit`。`createInTx` 成为写 issue 行的唯一权威；既有 Go 测试全绿即证据。
2. `feat(issue)` — 新增 `IssueService.CreateGroup`：父 + N 子一个显式应用事务整组提交或整组回滚；父子关系写在应用代码里（不加外键、不加级联）；子节点挂同一事务内刚插入的根节点；project 由 `createInTx` 从父单回填。
3. `feat(issue-draft)` — `issueDraftNodeID` 推导、`issueGroupParamsFromDraft` 校验、`createIssueGroupForDraft` 的 23505 认领、finalize 接 `CreateGroup`、`completed` 分支回传整组。

## 硬约束核对

- **迁移数 = 0**：`git diff --stat origin/kun...HEAD` 里没有 `server/migrations/*`，也没有 sqlc 生成物改动（没动 `.sql`）。
- **迁移 486 一行未动**：改的是它的含义（一个对齐**节点**至多一张 issue），索引定义不变。
- **锁不跨建组**：finalize 仍是三段短事务；`LockIssueDraftInWorkspace` 的 `FOR UPDATE` 不跨越 `CreateGroup`。
- **不让一组单共用 `origin_id`**：根 `= chat_session_id`，子节点 UUIDv5 混入 `(chat_session_id, key)`，每个节点自带幂等键。
- **不改 prompt 契约、不 bump policy `Version`、不动 `packages/` 的 TS 与预览面板**。

## 验证

```
cd server && go build ./... && go vet ./...        # 通过
cd server && go test ./internal/... -count=1       # 通过（见下）
git diff --check                                   # 干净
```

`./internal/...` 全绿，除 4 个与本改动无关、在 **pristine `origin/kun` 上同样失败**的环境包（沙箱不允许 process-tree 操作）：
`internal/cli`、`internal/daemon`、`internal/daemon/execenv`、`internal/daemon/repocache`。

DB 支撑的测试跑在 `scripts/test-db.sh` 起的一次性库上（`MULTICA_TEST_DB_EXPECT_USE=1`，套件确实连上了才判绿）。

## 新增测试

服务层（`internal/service/issue_group_test.go`）：整组 4 张一起提交、尾节点失败整组回滚、配额不足一张都不建、空组拒绝。

Handler（`internal/handler/issue_draft_group_test.go`）：
- 无 `children` 的单节点结果与今天逐字段相同（含 draft 回写 `issue_id`）
- 父 + 3 子：父 origin = session，3 张子单各自不同 origin，`parent_issue_id` 全指向父单，stage 落库正确
- 同一 payload 确认两次只产生一组
- **换掉整套 children key 再确认一次仍只有一组**（§3.3 时序 B，revision 挡不住、只有根节点 id 挡得住）
- 建组后 draft 未 completed 再确认 → 认领并写回（时序 C）
- 并发 4 次确认只产生一组，两边拿到同一个 `issue_id`
- 重复 key / trim 后重复 / 缺 key / 21 张 / stage 0、-1、21 / 子单缺标题 → 400 且一张都没建
- 子单 assignee 无权 → 403 且一张都没建
- 配额不够 → 402 且一张都没建
- `issueDraftNodeID` 稳定性 + 换 session 必不同 + golden UUID 值（钉住命名空间与推导）

## 一处刻意的取舍

设计稿 §4.5 写「子单 afterCommit 按 stage 升序」。实现用的是**载荷顺序**（父单先，子单按数组顺序）：编号就是按载荷顺序分配的，`ListChildIssues` 也按 `number ASC` 读回，再排一次只会让广播顺序和这组单读出来的顺序不一致；而每个节点的 afterCommit 之间没有依赖。若评审要求严格照 §4.5，改一处 sort 即可。

## 不在本单

prompt 契约扩 `children`、policy `Version` bump、TS 类型/zod、预览面板与确认页 —— 全在 DENE-411（阶段 5 前端）。

Closes DENE-410

author: jmendivilznas
body:
## The bug

`bundleCache` charges an entry only its **value** length, so the cap it advertises does not bound what the cache actually holds. Every entry also costs its key string, a map slot and a list node.

That rounds to nothing beside a whole bundle file — which is all this cache held when it was written — and dominates completely for a short value.

Measured against a 4 MB cap:

| | entries held | accounted | actually occupied |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| before | 500,000 | 488 KB | **~54 MB** |
| after | 42,366 | 4.0 MB | ~4 MB |

Eviction never fired, because the budget never noticed them, so the map grew for the life of the process. A zero-length value — a reasonable *"the answer is nothing, don't recompute it"* entry — was free forever.

## The fix

`Put` now charges `len(key) + len(value) + cacheEntryOverhead`, applied identically on insert, on replace and on eviction.

The overhead is a flat estimate on purpose. The job is to stop the budget ignoring the cost entirely, not to model Go's allocator — being approximate and honest beats being exact and absent.

## What does not change

Nothing about the cache's behaviour for the values it holds today. `blob://` bundle bytes are large enough that adding ~64 bytes per entry to their accounting changes no eviction decision.

**The two existing tests keep their assertions verbatim.** Only their byte constants scale, because a 10-byte entry now costs ~75 rather than 10 — and they are written against `cacheEntryOverhead` rather than a fresh magic number, so they stay true if the estimate is ever revised.

## Why it is its own PR

Found while building [#5475](https://github.com/znasllc-io/memql/pull/5475), which adds a second caller that stores short values and would have hit this immediately. But this is the **cache's own contract**, not that caller's problem: it is reviewable, mergeable and revertable without it, and its tests pass with no other change on the branch.

#5475 is stacked on top of this one.
